children.translated_text: <s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>, 1
Now we shall expound the chapter called <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s> (On Long Life). // Car 1.1.1
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
To Him who has assumed three forms through the division of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
who is the source of the three <s>Vedas</s>, the three-eyed one, the lord of the three worlds — salutation! // 1
Salutation to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, by whose grace, through meritorious deeds,
the world is seen reflected in the mirror of the intellect. // 2
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Veśa</s> (Agniveśa), <s>Caraka</s>, and others — repeated salutations! // 3
To <s>Ahipati</s> (Patañjali, lord of serpents), who through his revisions of the <s>Pātañjala</s> [Yoga Sūtras], the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s>, and the <s>Caraka</s> [Saṃhitā],
removes the defects of mind, speech, and body — salutation! // 4
Following the meaning of <s>Caraka</s> as indicated by the teacher <s>Naradatta</s>,
this commentary <s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> is composed by <s>Cakradatta</s> (Cakrapāṇidatta). // 5

children.text: sabhyāḥ sadguruvāksudhāsrutiparisphītaśrutīn asmi vo nālaṃ toṣayituṃ payodapayasā nāmbhonidhis tṛpyati /
children.translated_text: O worthy assembly! I am unable to satisfy your ears, flooded with the nectar-stream of a true teacher's words — the ocean is not satisfied by rain-water.

children.text: vyākhyābhāsarasaprakāśanam idaṃ tv asmin yadi prāpyate kvāpi kvāpi kaṇo guṇasya tadasau karṇe kṣaṇaṃ dhīyatām // 6
children.translated_text: Yet if, in this illumination of the semblance of commentary-essence, some grain of merit is here and there obtained — then let it rest in the ear for a moment. // 6

children.text: iha hi dharmārthakāmamokṣaparipanthirogopaśamāya brahmaprabhṛtibhiḥ praṇītāyurvedatantreṣvativistaratvena samprati vartamānālpāyurmedhasāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ na samyagarthādhigamaḥ tadanadhigamācca tadvihitārthānāmananuṣṭhāne tathaivopaplavo rujāmiti manvānaḥ paramakāruṇiko 'trabhavān agniveśo'lpāyurmedhasāmapi suropalambhārthaṃ nātisaṃkṣepavistaraṃ kāyacikitsāpradhānam āyurvedatantraṃ praṇetum ārabdhavān // 7
children.translated_text: Here, because the <s>Āyurveda</s> treatises composed by <s>Brahmā</s> and others — for the pacification of diseases that obstruct <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> — are excessively elaborate, men of the present time, who are short-lived and of limited intellect, cannot properly comprehend their meaning. And because of non-comprehension, and the non-performance of what is prescribed therein, there is such an onslaught of diseases — thinking thus, the supremely compassionate <s>Agniveśa</s> began to compose a treatise on <s>Āyurveda</s>, primarily concerning <s>Kāyacikitsā</s> (internal medicine), neither too concise nor too elaborate, for the easy comprehension even of those of short life and limited intellect. // 7

And in that [treatise], which consists of the <s>Śloka</s>, <s>Nidāna</s>, <s>Vimāna</s>, <s>Śārīra</s>, <s>Indriya</s>, <s>Cikitsita</s>, <s>Kalpa</s>, and <s>Siddhi</s> <s>sthānas</s> (sections), about to be expounded, the principal meanings of the entire treatise are stated [first]. // 8
By the statement beginning with 'kta' etc., it should be understood that [the commentary] has shown [this]. // 9

children.text: nanu prayojanābhidhānaṃ śāstrapravṛttyarthamiti yaduktaṃ tanna yuktaṃ yato na prayojanābhidhānamātreṇa prayojanavattāvadhāraṇaṃ vipralambhakasaṃsāramocanapratipādakādiśāstreṣu prayojanābhidhāne'pi niṣprayojanatvadarśanāt // 10
children.translated_text: Objection: The statement 'the purpose is declared for the sake of undertaking the treatise' is not valid, because the mere declaration of purpose does not establish that the text is purposeful — since even in misleading texts that claim to teach liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s>, despite the declaration of purpose, purposelessness is observed. // 10

children.text: atha manyase āptaprayojanābhidhānametadato'tra yathārthatvaṃ nanu bho kathamayaṃ prayojanābhidhāyī āptaḥ tadabhihitaśāstrasya yathārthatvāditi cet hanta na yāvacchāstrasya prayojanavattāvadhāraṇaṃ na tāvacchāstrapravṛttiḥ na yāvacchāstrapravṛttir na tāvacchāstrasya yathārthatvāvadhāraṇaṃ na yāvacchāstrasya yathārthatvāvadhāraṇaṃ na tāvacchāstrasya karturāptatvamavadhāryate āptatvānavadhṛtau ca kutas tadabhihitaprayojanavattāvadhāraṇam iti cakrakamāpadyate atha manyase mā bhavatu prayojanavattāvadhāraṇam artharūpaprayojanavattāsaṃdeha eva pravartako bhaviṣyati kṛṣyādāv api hi pravṛttir arthasaṃdehādeva na hi tatra kṛṣīvalānāṃ phalalābhāvadhāraṇaṃ vidyate antarāvagrahāderapisaṃbhāvyamānatvāt nanvevamasatyapi prayojanābhidhāne saprayojananiṣprayojanaśāstradarśanācchāstratvam eva prayojanavattāsaṃdehopadarśakam astu tathāpyalaṃ prayojanābhidhānena // 11
children.translated_text: If you think: 'This declaration of purpose is by an authoritative person (<s>āpta</s>), therefore it is truthful here' — well then, how is this declarer of purpose authoritative? If you say 'because the treatise he has declared is truthful' — but as long as the purposefulness of the treatise is not established, there is no undertaking of the treatise; as long as there is no undertaking of the treatise, the truthfulness of the treatise is not established; as long as the truthfulness of the treatise is not established, the authoritativeness of the treatise's author is not determined; and when authoritativeness is not determined, how can the purposefulness declared by him be established? — thus a circular reasoning (<s>cakraka</s>) arises. If you think: 'Let there not be establishment of purposefulness — mere doubt regarding purposefulness will itself motivate' — for even in agriculture, activity proceeds from mere doubt of result, since farmers have no certainty of obtaining fruit, given the possibility of drought and such. Objection: If so, even without declaration of purpose, since one observes both purposeful and purposeless treatises, the very fact of being a treatise presents the doubt of purposefulness — then what need is there of declaring purpose? // 11

children.text: naivaṃ nahi sāmānyena prayojanasaṃdehaḥ prayojanaviśeṣārthinaṃ tathā pravartayati yathābhipretaprayojanaviśeṣaviṣayaḥ saṃdehaḥ abhipretaviśeṣaviṣayaśca saṃdeho na viśeṣaviṣayasmaraṇamantarā bhavati ato ye tāvad anavadhṛtāgniveśaprāmāṇyās teṣāṃ dhātusāmyasādhanamidaṃ śāstraṃ na vetyevam ākāraviśeṣasaṃdehotpādanārthaṃ prayojanaviśeṣābhidhānaṃ ye punaḥ paramarṣeragniveśasyādyata evāvadhṛtaprāmāṇyāsteṣāṃ tadabhihitaprayojanavattāvadhāraṇenaiva pravṛttir iti yuktaṃ prayojanābhidhānam // 12
children.translated_text: Not so. For a general doubt about purpose does not motivate one seeking a specific purpose in the same way as does a doubt concerning the specific purpose desired. And a doubt concerning a specific object does not arise without the remembrance of that specific object. Therefore, for those who have not established the authority of <s>Agniveśa</s>, the declaration of the specific purpose — 'Is this treatise a means of establishing equilibrium of the <s>dhātus</s> or not?' — is for generating doubt of that specific nature. But for those who have already established the authority of the supreme sage <s>Agniveśa</s>, their activity proceeds from the very establishment of the purposefulness declared by him — thus the declaration of purpose is proper. // 12

children.text: prayojanābhidhāyivākye tu svalpaprayatnabodhye prayojanasāmānyasaṃdehādeva pravṛttirupapannā na punaranekasaṃvatsarakleśabodhye śāstre // 13
children.translated_text: However, in the case of a statement declaring purpose — which is understood with little effort — activity is possible from a general doubt about purpose alone; but not so in the case of a treatise requiring many years of laborious study. // 13

children.text: tadevaṃ yaducyate prayojanābhidhāyivākyapravṛttāv api prayojanamabhidhātavyaṃ tathā cānavasthā iti tannirastaṃ bhavati // 14
children.translated_text: Thus the objection — 'Even in undertaking the purpose-declaring statement, a purpose must be declared, leading to infinite regress' — is refuted. // 14

children.text: athetyādi sūtre 'thaśabdo brahmādipraṇītatantreṣv alpāyurmedhasāmarthānavadhāraṇasya tathābhīṣṭadevatānamaskāraśāstrakaraṇārthagurvājñālābhayor ānantarye prayukto'pi śāstrādau svarūpeṇa maṅgalaṃ bhavatyudakāharaṇapravṛttodakumbhadarśanam iva prasthitānām // 15
children.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with 'atha' etc.: the word 'atha' indicates sequence after the prior prerequisites — namely, the inability to comprehend the <s>Āyurveda</s> treatises composed by <s>Brahmā</s> and others by those of short life and limited intellect, the salutation to the desired deity, the purpose of composing the treatise, and the obtaining of the teacher's permission. Though used for sequence, it also serves as an auspicious opening (<s>maṅgala</s>) at the beginning of a treatise, by its very form — like the sight of a full water-pot for those setting out on a journey. // 15

children.text: granthādau maṅgalasevānirastāntarāyāṇāṃ granthakartṛśrotḥṇām avighneneṣṭalābho bhavatīti yuktaṃ maṅgalopādānam // 16
children.translated_text: Those whose obstacles have been removed by the observance of auspicious rites at the beginning of a work — both author and listeners — achieve their desired goals without hindrance. Therefore the adoption of an auspicious opening is proper. // 16

children.text: athaśabdasya maṅgalatve smṛtir oṃkāraś cāthaśabdaśca dvāv etau brahmaṇaḥ purā // 17
children.translated_text: Regarding the auspiciousness of the word 'atha,' the <s>smṛti</s> states: '<s>Oṃkāra</s> and the word atha — these two formerly [issued] from <s>Brahman</s>' // 17

children.text: kaṇṭhaṃ bhittvā viniryātau tena māṅgalikāv ubhau iti // 18
children.translated_text: 'having burst forth from his throat — therefore both are auspicious.' // 18
And in other treatises too, this word 'atha' is seen as auspicious at the beginning. // 19

children.text: yathā atha śabdānuśāsanam athāto dharmaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ vai ityādau // 20
children.translated_text: As in: 'Atha [the science of] word-instruction' (<s>Vyākaraṇa</s>); 'Now, from this, we shall expound <s>dharma</s>' (<s>Mīmāṃsā</s>); etc. // 20

children.text: abhīṣṭadevatānamaskārastu granthādau śiṣṭācāraprāptaḥ paramaśiṣṭenāgniveśena kṛta eva anyathā śiṣṭācāralaṅghanena śiṣṭatvameva na syād vyākhyānāntarāyabhayaśca tathā granthāviniveśitasyāpi namaskārasya pratyavāyāpahatvācca na granthaniveśanam // 21
children.translated_text: As for the salutation to the desired deity at the beginning of the work: this is obtained through the practice of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>), and was certainly performed by <s>Agniveśa</s>, the supremely learned one — otherwise, by transgressing learned practice, he would not be learned. And [one might think] there is no need to include it in the text, since even a salutation not incorporated in the text can remove the obstacle of misfortune in exposition. // 21

children.text: yathā ca gurvājñālābhānantaram etat tantrakaraṇaṃ tathā atha maitrīparaḥ puṇyam ityādau sphuṭameva // 22
children.translated_text: That this composition of the treatise follows after obtaining the teacher's permission is quite clear from [the passage] 'atha maitrīparaḥ puṇyam...' etc. // 22

children.text: granthakaraṇe ca gurvanumatipratipādanena granthasyopādeyatā pradarśitā bhavati // 23
children.translated_text: And by demonstrating the teacher's approval for the composition, the worthiness of the treatise is established. // 23

children.text: yat punaḥ śiṣyapraśnānantaryārthatvam athaśabdasya varṇyate tanna māṃ dhinoti nahi śiṣyān puro vyavasthāpya śāstraṃ kriyate śrotṛbuddhisthīkāre tu śāstrakaraṇaṃ yuktaṃ na ca buddhisthīkṛtāḥ praṣṭāro bhavanti // 24
children.translated_text: Now, as for the interpretation that the word 'atha' indicates sequence after a student's question — that does not satisfy me, for a treatise is not composed by first arranging students before oneself. The composition of a treatise is proper when it rests in the intellect of the listener; and those in whose intellect it rests do not become questioners. // 24

children.text: ataḥśabdo 'dhikāraprāgavadhyupadarśakaḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ yad upadekṣyāmo dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ taditi yadi vā hetau yena brahmādipraṇītāyurvedatantrāṇām uktena nyāyenotsambandhatvam iva ato hetor dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāma iti yojanīyam // 25
children.translated_text: The word 'ataḥ' indicates the prior prerequisites to the topic: 'What we shall teach henceforth is the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>.' Or, [taken] in the causal sense: because the <s>Āyurveda</s> treatises composed by <s>Brahmā</s> and others are, by the reasoning stated, as if disconnected [for present readers] — therefore, for this reason, 'we shall expound the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>.' // 25

children.text: dīrghaṃjīvitīyam ityatra dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdo 'sminn astīti matvarthe adhyāyānuvākayor luk ca iti chapratyayaḥ // 26
children.translated_text: In '<s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>': the word '<s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>' is [present] in this [chapter] — the suffix 'cha' is derived by the rule 'in the sense of possessing, [the suffixes] luk etc. [apply] to chapters and <s>anuvākas</s>.' // 26

children.text: yadi vā dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdam adhikṛtya kṛto grantho 'dhyāyarūpastantrarūpo vā ityasyāṃ vivakṣāyām adhikṛtya kṛte granthe ityadhikārāt śiśukrandayamasabha ityādinā chaḥ // 27
children.translated_text: Or, [it means] a work in the form of a chapter or treatise composed with reference to the word '<s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>' — in this intended meaning, by [the rule] 'for a work composed with reference to [a topic],' the suffix 'cha' [is derived] by [the analogy of] '<s>śiśukrandayamasabha</s>' etc. // 27
The same should be understood in other similar cases. // 28

children.text: atra ca satyapi śabdāntare dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdenaiva saṃjñā kṛtā dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdasyaiva pravacanādau niveśāt praśastatvācca // 29
children.translated_text: And here, although other words [could serve as the name], the name is formed with the word '<s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>' alone, because that word is placed at the very beginning of the discourse and is auspicious. // 29

children.text: dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdo 'sminn asti iti dīrghaṃjīvitaśabdam adhikṛtya kṛto vā ityanayā vyutpattyā dīrghaṃjīvitīyaśabdas tantre 'dhyāye ca pravartanīyaḥ // 30
children.translated_text: By either derivation — 'the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s> is in this' or 'composed with reference to the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvita</s>' — the word <s>dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s> applies both to the treatise and to the chapter. // 30

children.text: tena dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāma ityanena tantraṃ prati vyākhyānapratijñā labdhā bhavati punar dīrghaṃjīvitīyam iti padam āvartyādhyāyapadasamabhivyāhṛtam adhyāyavyākhyānapratijñāṃ lambhayati // 31
children.translated_text: Therefore, by '<s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ</s>' (we shall expound the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s>), the promise to expound the treatise is obtained; and by repeating the word '<s>dīrghaṃjīvitīyam</s>' in conjunction with the word '<s>adhyāya</s>' (chapter), the promise to expound the chapter is obtained. // 31

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ cāvṛtya padasya yojanaṃ yathā apāmārgataṇḍulīye gaurave śirasaḥ śūle pīnase ityādau śirasa iti padaṃ gaurave ityanena yujyate āvṛtya śūle ityanena ca // 32
children.translated_text: And indeed, the construction of a repeated word is attested, as in '<s>Apāmārga-taṇḍulīya</s>' [chapter]: 'in heaviness, in headache, in rhinitis...' — the word 'of the head' is construed with 'heaviness' and then, being repeated, with 'pain.' // 32

children.text: ataśca yaducyate akṛtatantrapratijñasyādhyāyapratijñā ūnakāyamāneti tannirastaṃ bhavati // 33
children.translated_text: Therefore, the objection — 'a promise regarding a chapter without having made a promise regarding the treatise results in an incomplete body' — is refuted. // 33

children.text: yadi vā adhyāyapratijñaivāstu tayaiva tantrapratijñāpyarthalabdhaiva na hy adhyāyas tantravyatiriktaḥ tenāvayavavyākhyāne tantrasyāpyavayavino vyākhyā bhavatyeva yathā aṅgulīgrahaṇena devadatto'pi gṛhīto bhavati // 34
children.translated_text: Or, let the promise pertain to the chapter alone; even by that, the promise regarding the treatise is implicitly obtained. For a chapter is not separate from the treatise. Therefore, in expounding a part, the whole (the treatise) is also expounded — just as by grasping a finger, <s>Devadatta</s> [the whole person] is grasped. // 34

children.text: avayavāntaravyākhyānapratijñā tu na labhyate tāṃ tu pratyadhyāyameva kariṣyati // 35
children.translated_text: But the promise to expound other parts [chapters] is not obtained [from this]; that [promise] he will make for each chapter separately. // 35

children.text: adhyāyamiti adhipūrvādiṅaḥ iṅaśca iti karmaṇi ghañā sādhyam // 36
children.translated_text: '<s>Adhyāya</s>' (chapter) is derived: from the verb '<s>iṅ</s>' (to study) with the prefix 'adhi-' — [by the rule] 'iṅ also [takes the prefix adhi-]' — the <s>ghañ</s> suffix is applied in the sense of the object (that which is studied). // 36
Therefore: 'that which is studied' = <s>adhyāya</s>. // 37

children.text: na cānayā vyutpattyā prakaraṇacatuṣkasthānādiṣvatiprasaṅgaḥ yato yogarūḍheyam adhyāyasaṃjñādhyāyasya prakaraṇasamūhaviśeṣa eva dīrghaṃjīvitīyādilakṣaṇe paṅkajaśabdavadvartate na yogamātreṇa vartate // 38
children.translated_text: And by this derivation, there is no over-application to sections of four [chapters], <s>sthānas</s>, etc., because this designation '<s>adhyāya</s>' is <s>yogarūḍha</s> (conventionally restricted despite its etymological breadth) — it applies only to a specific collection of <s>prakaraṇas</s> characterized as <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s> etc., functioning like the word '<s>paṅkaja</s>' (born in mud = lotus), which does not apply to everything born in mud. // 38

children.text: vakṣyati hi adhikṛtyeyamadhyāyanāmasaṃjñā pratiṣṭhitā iti nāmasaṃjñā yogarūḍhasaṃjñetyarthaḥ // 39
children.translated_text: For [the text] will state: 'This designation is established with reference to [the chapters called] <s>adhyāya</s>' — meaning: the designation is a <s>yogarūḍha</s> term. // 39
Or, in the senses of instrument and location — // 40
by the <s>sūtra</s> '<s>adhyāya-nyāya-udyāva-saṃhārāḥ</s> ca' — the word <s>adhyāya</s> is established by irregular formation (<s>nipātana</s>). // 41
'That in which or by which a specific meaning is studied' = <s>adhyāya</s>. // 42
The prevention of over-application is by the reasoning already stated. // 43
'<s>Vyākhyāsyāmaḥ</s>' (we shall expound) is derived from the root '<s>khyā</s>' (to tell/declare) with the prefixes 'vi' and 'ā,' by the future tense suffix '<s>lṛṭ</s>.' // 44

children.text: cakṣiṅo hi prayoge'nicchato 'pi vyākhyātuḥ kriyāphalasambandhasya durnivāratvena svaritañita ityādinātmanepadaṃ syāditi // 45
children.translated_text: For, in the usage of the root '<s>cakṣiṅ</s>' (to tell, <s>ātmanepada</s>), even when the speaker does not desire [the fruit], since the connection between action and result is inescapable, the <s>ātmanepada</s> would apply by the rule '<s>svaritañit</s>' etc. // 45
'Vi' is [used] in the sense of distinction; and the distinctions are [those of] elaborate explanation (<s>vyāsa</s>), concise statement (<s>samāsa</s>), and such. // 46

children.text: āṅayaṃ kriyāyoge ye tu maryādāyām abhividhau vā āṅprayogaṃ manyante teṣām abhiprāyaṃ na vidmaḥ // 47
children.translated_text: The prefix 'ā' is [used] in connection with the verb. As for those who consider the use of 'ā' to be in the sense of limit or inclusion — we do not understand their view. // 47

children.text: yato maryādāyāmabhividhau cāṅaḥ prātipadikena yogaḥ syāt yathā āsamudrakṣitīśānām āpāṭalīputrād vṛṣṭo deva ityādau ihāpi ca tathā // 48
children.translated_text: Because in the senses of limit and inclusion, 'ā' would have connection with a nominal stem — as in '<s>āsamudra-kṣitīśānām</s>' (up to the ocean, of earth-lords), '<s>ā-Pāṭalīputrāt</s> (up to Pāṭaliputra) it rained,' etc. And here too it would be the same [if taken that way]. // 48

children.text: kriyāyogavirahe upasargāḥ kriyāyoge iti niyamād āṅa upasargatvaṃ na syāt tataścānupasargeṇāṅā vyavadhānād ver upasargasya prayogo na syāt // 49
children.translated_text: In the absence of connection with a verb, by the rule 'prefixes [function] in connection with verbs,' 'ā' would not have the status of a prefix; and then, due to the intervention of a non-prefix 'ā,' the use of the prefix 'vi' would not be possible. // 49

children.text: yenāvyavahitaḥ sajātīyavyavahito vā dhātor upasargo bhavati // 50
children.translated_text: For a prefix must be either immediately adjacent to the verbal root or separated [only] by another prefix of the same class. // 50

children.text: vyāṅor ubhayor apyanupasargatve tatsambandhocitabhūriprātipadikakalpanāgauravaprasaṅgaḥ syāt tasmāt kriyāyogitvam evāṅo nyāyyam // 51
children.translated_text: If both 'vi' and 'ā' were not prefixes, the cumbersomeness of having to postulate numerous nominal stems appropriate to their connection would arise. Therefore it is proper that 'ā' be [taken as] connected with the verb. // 51

children.text: atha ataḥ dīrghaṃ jīvitīyam adhyāyaṃ vi ā khyāsyāma ityaṣṭapadatvam // 52]
children.translated_text: Thus: 'atha ataḥ dīrghaṃ jīvitīyam adhyāyaṃ vi ā khyāsyāmaḥ' — this is the eight-word [analysis]. // 52]
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car 1.1.2
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: nanu kathamagniveśaḥ sakalapadārthāśeṣaviśeṣajñānavyākhyeyam āyurvedaṃ vyākhyāsyati yato na tāvad bheṣajādīnām aśeṣaviśeṣapratyakṣajñeyaḥ sarvapadārthānāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ pratyakṣāviṣayatvāt anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tu sarvapadārthāvadhāraṇaṃ duṣkarameva yata ekam eva madhu svarūpeṇa jīvayati mārayati coṣṇaṃ samaghṛtaṃ ca kaphaprakṛterhitamahitaṃ vātaprakṛteḥ anūpe sātmyamasātmyaṃ marau śīte sevyamasevyaṃ grīṣme hitam avṛddhe vṛddhe cāhitam alpaṃ guṇakaram ābādhakaram atyupayuktam āmatāṃ gatam udare upakramavirodhitvād ativibhramakaraṃ kākamācīyuktaṃ pakvanikucena ca sahopayuktaṃ maraṇāya athavā balavarṇavīryatejaupaghātāya bhavati ityevamādi tattad yuktaṃ tattacchataśaḥ karoti ata evaikasyaiva madhuno rūpaṃ yadānena prakāreṇa duradhigamaṃ tadātra kaiva kathā nikhilapadārthāśeṣaviśeṣajñānasya ajānaṃśca vyācakṣāṇaḥ kathamupādeyavacana iti kṛtvā guror āptāt pratipannaṃ pratipādayiṣyāma iti darśayan tāmimāṃ śaṅkāṃ nirācikīrṣur gurūktānuvādarūpatāṃ svagranthasya darśayannāha iti ha smāha bhagavānātreya iti // 1
children.translated_text: [{Āyurvedadīpikā}] Now, how will <s>Agniveśa</s> expound <s>Āyurveda</s>, which requires knowledge of every particular of all substances for its exposition? For firstly, the complete particularities of medicines and so forth are not knowable through direct perception, since the particularities of all substances are beyond the scope of perception. And determination of all substances through positive and negative concomitance alone is indeed difficult, since even a single substance like honey, by its own nature, can both sustain life and cause death — when hot or mixed with equal ghee, it is beneficial for one of <s>kapha</s> constitution but harmful for one of <s>vāta</s> constitution; it is wholesome in marshy lands but unwholesome in desert; it should be consumed in winter but avoided in summer; beneficial when one is not aged but harmful in old age; in small quantity it produces good effects, but when used excessively it causes disease; when it undergoes undigested state in the stomach, it causes great confusion due to contradicting treatment; combined with <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) or consumed together with ripe <s>nikuca</s> (breadfruit), it leads to death, or to the destruction of strength, complexion, virility, and vital energy — thus, each substance combined with this or that produces hundreds of such effects. Therefore, when even the nature of a single substance like honey is so difficult to ascertain in this manner, what need is there to speak of knowledge of every particular of all substances? And one who expounds without knowing — how can his words be worth accepting? Thinking thus, showing that 'we shall teach what has been received from the <s>guru</s> (teacher), who is an authority,' and wishing to dispel this doubt by demonstrating that his own treatise is in the form of a repetition of the teacher's words, he says: 'Thus indeed did the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> declare.' [1]

children.text: atra itiśabdo vakṣyamāṇārthaparāmarśakaḥ haśabdo'vadhāraṇe yathā na ha vai saśarīrasya priyāpriyayorapahatirastīti atra na heti naivetyarthaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: Here, the word <s>iti</s> refers back to the meaning about to be stated. The word <s>ha</s> is used for emphasis, as in 'there is indeed no warding off of the pleasant and unpleasant for one who has a body' — here <s>na ha</s> means 'certainly not.' [2]

children.text: atra smāha iti smaśabdaprayogena bhūtamātra eva liḍarthe laṭ sme iti laṭ na bhūtānadyatanaparokṣe ātreyopadeśasyāgniveśaṃ pratyaparokṣatvāt // 3
children.translated_text: Here, by the use of the word <s>sma</s> in <s>smāha</s>, the <s>laṭ</s> (present tense) is used in the sense of the <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense) denoting mere past action, according to the rule '<s>laṭ sme</s>' — the <s>liṭ</s> is not applicable in the sense of past action that is non-contemporary and unwitnessed, since <s>Ātreya</s>'s teaching was directly witnessed by <s>Agniveśa</s>. [3]

children.text: yathā ca bhūtamātre liḍ bhavati tathāca darśayiṣyāmaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: And we shall demonstrate how the <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense) is used in the sense of mere past action. [4]

children.text: bhagaṃ pūjitaṃ jñānaṃ tadvān yathoktam utpattiṃ pralayaṃ caiva bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim // 5
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s> means revered knowledge; one who possesses it is called <s>Bhagavān</s>. As it is said: 'He who knows the origin and dissolution of beings, their coming and going, [5]

children.text: vetti vidyāmavidyāṃ ca sa vācyo bhagavāniti yadi vā bhagaśabdaḥ samastaiśvaryamāhātmyādivacanaḥ yathoktam aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśasaḥ śriyaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: knowledge and ignorance — he is to be called <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Alternatively, the word <s>bhaga</s> denotes the totality of lordship, greatness, and so forth, as it is said: 'Of sovereignty in its entirety, of valor, of fame, of prosperity, [6]
and of knowledge and dispassion — these six constitute <s>bhaga</s>, say the learned.' [7]
Here, '<s>Ātreya</s>' means 'descendant of <s>Atri</s>'; by this, his pure lineage is indicated. [8]

children.text: atrānye varṇayanti caturvidhaṃ sūtraṃ bhavati gurusūtraṃ śiṣyasūtraṃ pratisaṃskartṛsūtram ekīyasūtraṃ ceti // 9
children.translated_text: Here, others explain that <s>sūtras</s> (aphoristic statements) are of four kinds: teacher's <s>sūtra</s> (<s>gurusūtra</s>), disciple's <s>sūtra</s> (<s>śiṣyasūtra</s>), redactor's <s>sūtra</s> (<s>pratisaṃskartṛsūtra</s>), and an individual's <s>sūtra</s> (<s>ekīyasūtra</s>). [9]

children.text: tatra gurusūtraṃ yathā naitad buddhimatā draṣṭavyam agniveśa ityādi pratisaṃskartṛsūtraṃ yathā tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ ityādi śiṣyasūtraṃ yathā naitāni bhagavan pañcakaṣāyaśatāni pūryante ityādi ekīyasūtraṃ yathā kumārasya śiraḥ pūrvamabhinirvartata iti kumāraśirā bharadvājaḥ ityādi // 10
children.translated_text: Among these, a teacher's <s>sūtra</s> is like 'This should not be viewed thus by the wise, O <s>Agniveśa</s>' and so forth. A redactor's <s>sūtra</s> is like 'The venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him' and so forth. A disciple's <s>sūtra</s> is like 'O Lord, these five hundred <s>kaṣāya</s> (decoctions) are not exhausted' and so forth. An individual's <s>sūtra</s> is like 'Because the head of a child forms first, therefore he is <s>Kumāraśiras Bhāradvāja</s>' and so forth. [10]
Therefore, the first <s>sūtra</s>, which is a declaration of exposition, belongs to the teacher alone, since the disciple <s>Agniveśa</s> has no authority to expound. [11]
And the second <s>sūtra</s> belongs to the redactor.

children.text: itiśabdena ca prakāravācinā dīrghaṃjīvitīyaṃ vyākhyāsyāma iti parāmṛśyate tenāha smeti bhūtānadyatanaparokṣa eva bhavati pratisaṃskartāraṃ pratyātreyopadeśasya parokṣatvāt // 12
children.translated_text: And by the word <s>iti</s>, which denotes manner, what is referred to is 'we shall expound the chapter on longevity (<s>Dīrghañjīvitīya</s>)'; therefore, '<s>āha sma</s>' (he said) is indeed in the sense of past action that is non-contemporary and unwitnessed, since <s>Ātreya</s>'s teaching was unwitnessed from the redactor's perspective. [12]

children.text: anena ca nyāyena tamuvāca bhagavānātreya ityādāv api liḍvidhir upapanno bhavati // 13
children.translated_text: And by this same reasoning, the use of the <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense) is justified also in passages like 'the venerable <s>Ātreya</s> said to him' and so forth. [13]

children.text: suśrute ca yathovāca bhagavān dhanvantariḥ iti pratisaṃskartṛsūtramiti kṛtvā ṭīkākṛtā liḍvidhir upapāditaḥ iti // 14
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Suśruta</s>, the commentator has justified the use of the <s>liṭ</s> in 'thus the venerable <s>Dhanvantari</s> said,' treating it as a redactor's <s>sūtra</s>. [14]

children.text: atra brūmaḥ yattāvaduktaṃ śiṣyasyāgniveśasya vyākhyānānadhikārādidaṃ guroḥ sūtraṃ tanna nahi jātyā gurutvam asti yataḥ sa evātreyaḥ svagurum apekṣya śiṣyaḥ agniveśādīn apekṣya guruḥ evamagniveśo 'pi granthakaraṇakāle svabuddhisthīkṛtāñśiṣyān prati gururiti na kaścid doṣaḥ // 15
children.translated_text: Here we say: as for the statement that this is the teacher's <s>sūtra</s> because the disciple <s>Agniveśa</s> has no authority to expound — that is not correct. For there is no teachership by birth, since the same <s>Ātreya</s> is a disciple in relation to his own teacher, and a teacher in relation to <s>Agniveśa</s> and others. Likewise, <s>Agniveśa</s> too, at the time of composing his treatise, is a teacher in relation to his own disciples whose understanding he has refined — therefore there is no fault. [15]

children.text: yatpunardvitīyasya pratisaṃskartṛsūtratayā bhūtānadyatanaparokṣe liḍvidhir upapādyate tatra vicāryaṃ kim idaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūtraṃ pūrvavākyaikatāpannaṃ na vā yadyekavākyatāpannaṃ tadā suśrute tathā vyākhyāsyāmo yathovāca dhanvantarir iti yojanīyaṃ tathāca tathā vyākhyāsyāma iti kriyaikavākyatāpannam uvācetipadaṃ na bhinnakartṛkaṃ bhavitum arhati tathā ca kuto liḍvidhiḥ atha naikatāpannaṃ tadā gaur aśvaḥ puruṣo hastītivannārthasaṃgatiḥ // 16
children.translated_text: As for the justification of the <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense) in the sense of past non-contemporary unwitnessed action by treating the second <s>sūtra</s> as a redactor's <s>sūtra</s> — here one must consider: is this second <s>sūtra</s> syntactically connected with the preceding sentence or not? If it is syntactically connected, then in the <s>Suśruta</s> one should construe it as 'we shall expound thus, as <s>Dhanvantari</s> declared,' and being syntactically connected with the verb 'we shall expound,' the word 'declared' (<s>uvāca</s>) cannot have a different agent — and then how can the <s>liṭ</s> be justified? But if it is not syntactically connected, then like 'a cow, a horse, a man, an elephant,' there is no coherence of meaning. [16]

children.text: kiṃca jatūkarṇādau pratisaṃskartṛśrutigandho 'pi nāsti tat kathaṃ nānāśrutaparipūrṇakaṇṭhaḥ śiṣyo jatūkarṇaḥ prāñjalir adhigamyovāca ityādau liḍvidhiḥ // 17
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the case of <s>Jatūkarṇa</s> and others, there is not even a trace of the redactor's voice; then how is the <s>liṭ</s> justified in passages like 'the disciple <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>, whose throat was full of diverse learning, approached with joined palms and said'? [17]

children.text: anena nyāyena carake 'pi pratisaṃskartṛsūtrapakṣe liḍvidhirnāsti tasmāccarake 'gniveśaḥ suśrute suśruta eva sūtrāṇāṃ praṇetā kvacit kiṃcidarthaṃ stotuṃ nindituṃ vākhyāyikārūpaṃ purākalpaṃ darśayan kimapi sūtraṃ gurūktānuvādarūpatayā kimapyekīyamatānuvādarūpatayā likhati pratisaṃskartā tv ayaṃ granthaṃ pūrayati tadādyagranthakartṛtayaiva // 18
children.translated_text: By this same reasoning, even in <s>Caraka</s>, on the view that these are redactor's <s>sūtras</s>, the <s>liṭ</s> is not justified. Therefore, in the <s>Caraka</s> it is <s>Agniveśa</s>, and in the <s>Suśruta</s> it is <s>Suśruta</s> himself who is the author of the <s>sūtras</s>. Sometimes, to praise or censure some point, showing a narrative from ancient times in the form of a legend, he writes some <s>sūtras</s> as repetition of the teacher's words and some as repetition of an individual's views. The redactor, however, completes this treatise, and that too in the capacity of the original author. [18]

children.text: liḍvidhistu bhūtānadyatanamātra eva chandovihito bhāṣāyāmapi varṇanīyaḥ anyathā uvāceti padaṃ jatūkarṇādau na syāt tathā ca harivaṃśe dhanyopākhyāne māmuvāca iti tathā ahamuvāca iti ca na syāt yathā sa māmuvācāmbucaraḥ kūrmo mānuṣavat svayam // 19
children.translated_text: As for the use of the <s>liṭ</s> (perfect tense), it is to be explained as merely denoting non-contemporary past action, prescribed in Vedic usage and applicable in ordinary language as well. Otherwise, the word <s>uvāca</s> (he said) would not be possible in the case of <s>Jatūkarṇa</s> and others; and similarly, in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, in the narrative of <s>Dhanya</s>, the expressions 'he said to me' and 'I said' would not be possible, as in: 'That aquatic one, the tortoise, himself spoke to me in human speech— [19]

children.text: kimāścaryaṃ mayi mune dhanyaścāhaṃ kathaṃ vibho iti tathā svyambhuvacanāt so 'haṃ vedān vai samupasthitaḥ // 20
children.translated_text: what wonder is there concerning me, O sage? And how am I blessed, O Lord?' And likewise: 'By the command of the Self-born One, I approached the <s>Vedas</s>, [20]
and he uttered these four.' [21]

children.text: yadapi iti ha smāha ityatra itiśabdena pūrvasūtraṃ parāmṛśyate tanna yena dīrghaṃjīvitīyādisūtramātrasya tadarthasya vā gurūktatvapratipādane sati naivottaratrābhidheyābhidhānena nikhilatantrasya gurūktānuvādarūpatayā karaṇaṃ śrotṛśraddhākaraṇaṃ pratipāditaṃ bhavati // 22
children.translated_text: As for the claim that in '<s>iti ha smāha</s>' the word <s>iti</s> refers back to the preceding <s>sūtra</s> — that is not correct, because by establishing only that a particular <s>sūtra</s> such as the <s>Dīrghañjīvitīya</s>, or its meaning, was spoken by the teacher, it would not be demonstrated that the entire treatise in its subsequent subject-matter and exposition is composed as a repetition of the teacher's words, which is what generates the listener's faith. [22]

children.text: bhavati tu bhāvayituṃ yathā purā vyākhyātaṃ tasmāttadeva nyāyyamiti // 23
children.translated_text: Rather, it is to be understood that it was expounded as before — therefore that alone is proper. [23]

children.text: agniveśasya vyākhyāsyāma iti bahuvacanam ekasminn apy asmadaḥ prayogādbahuvacanaprayogasya sādhutvāt sādhu hi vadanti vaktāro vayaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ iti // 24
children.translated_text: <s>Agniveśa</s>'s use of the plural in 'we shall expound' (<s>vyākhyāsyāmaḥ</s>) is because the use of the plural is correct even for a single person when using the first-person pronoun, for the grammarians say: 'It is correct to say "we shall do."' [24]

children.text: bhagavānātreya ityatra tv ekavacananirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ bhagavānityanenaivātreyasya gurorgauravasya darśitatvāt // 25]
children.translated_text: However, in '<s>Bhagavān Ātreya</s>' the singular is used, because the honorific <s>Bhagavān</s> itself already shows the greatness of the teacher <s>Ātreya</s>. [25]
Desiring long life, <s>Bharadvāja</s> approached
<s>Indra</s>, the fierce ascetic having understood him to be the refuge, the lord of the immortals. [Car 1.1.3]
For <s>Prajāpati</s> received <s>Āyurveda</s> in its entirety

children.text: jagrāha nikhilenādāv aśvinau tu punas tataḥ // Car_1,1.4
children.translated_text: as it was first taught by <s>Brahmā</s>; and then the <s>Aśvins</s> received it from him. [Car 1.1.4]
From the <s>Aśvins</s>, the venerable <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) indeed received it completely;
and <s>Bharadvāja</s>, urged by the sages, approached <s>Śakra</s>. [Car 1.1.5]
When diseases, being obstacles, arose
among embodied beings, threatening their austerities, fasting, study, celibacy, vows, and lifespans, [Car 1.1.6]
then the great sages, placing compassion for beings foremost,

children.text: sametāḥ puṇyakarmāṇaḥ pārśve himavataḥ śubhe // Car_1,1.7
children.translated_text: assembled, those of meritorious deeds, on the auspicious slopes of the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas). [Car 1.1.7]
<s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: ātreyo gautamaḥ sāṃkhyaḥ pulastyo nārado'sitaḥ // Car_1,1.8
children.translated_text: <s>Ātreya</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Asita</s>, [Car 1.1.8]
<s>Agastya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, <s>Āśvalāyana</s>,
<s>Pārikṣi</s>, <s>Bhikṣu Ātreya</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Kapiñjala</s>, [Car 1.1.9]
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Āśmarathya</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Abhijit</s>,
<s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Vārkṣi</s>, <s>Devala</s>, <s>Gālava</s>, [Car 1.1.10]
<s>Sāṃkṛtya</s>, <s>Baijavāpi</s>, <s>Kuśika</s>, <s>Bādarāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: baḍiśaḥ śaralomā ca kāpyakātyāyanāv ubhau // Car_1,1.11
children.translated_text: <s>Baḍiśa</s>, <s>Śaraloman</s>, and both <s>Kāpya</s> and <s>Kātyāyana</s>, [Car 1.1.11]
<s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, <s>Kaikaśeya</s>, <s>Dhaumya</s>, <s>Mārīca</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>,

children.text: śarkarākṣo hiraṇyākṣo lokākṣaḥ paiṅgireva ca // Car_1,1.12
children.translated_text: <s>Śarkarākṣa</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, <s>Lokākṣa</s>, and indeed <s>Paiṅgi</s>, [Car 1.1.12]
<s>Śaunaka</s>, <s>Śākuneya</s>, <s>Maitreya</s>, <s>Maimatāyani</s>,
the <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, and likewise other great sages — [Car 1.1.13]
treasuries of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, of self-restraint, and of discipline,
blazing with the splendor of their austerities, like fires being offered oblations — [Car 1.1.14]
comfortably seated there, they held this sacred discourse.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
Who are those great sages? To answer this, he says '<s>Aṅgiras</s>' and so forth. [1]

children.text: bahvṛṣīṇām atra kīrtanaṃ granthādau pāpakṣayahetutvena tathāyurvedasyaivaṃvidhamahāpuruṣasevitatvena sevyatvopadarśanārthaṃ ceti // 2
children.translated_text: The mention of many sages here at the beginning of the treatise is for the purpose of destroying sins, and also for showing that <s>Āyurveda</s>, being practiced by such great persons, is worthy of being practiced. [2]

children.text: eṣu ca madhye kecid yāyāvarāḥ kecicchālīnāḥ kecidayonijāḥ evaṃprakārāśca sarve mīlitā boddhavyāḥ // 3
children.translated_text: Among these, some are wandering ascetics (<s>yāyāvara</s>), some are householders (<s>śālīna</s>), some are of non-womb origin (<s>ayonija</s>) — all of such diverse types together should be understood. [3]

children.text: bhikṣurityātreyaviśeṣaṇaṃ vakṣyati hi tanneti bhikṣur ātreyaḥ iti // 4
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhikṣu</s>' is an epithet of <s>Ātreya</s>, for it will be stated: 'therefore <s>Bhikṣu Ātreya</s>.' [4]
'<s>Vaikhānasa</s>' is a designation derived from a particular type of observance. [5]
The <s>Vālakhilyas</s> are certain sages of small physical stature. [6]
'Treasuries' means like repositories — in the sense of being inexhaustible abodes. [7]
<s>Dama</s> (self-restraint) means the state of being controlled. [8]
'This' (<s>imām</s>) refers to what will be stated hereafter. [9]
Health is the supreme root of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). [Car 1.1.15]
Diseases are the destroyers of that and of a worthy life;
this great obstacle has arisen among human beings. [Car 1.1.16]
'What would be the means of alleviating them?' — having said this, they entered into meditation.

children.text: atha te śaraṇaṃ śakraṃ dadṛśurdhyānacakṣuṣā // Car_1,1.17
children.translated_text: Then, with the eye of meditation, they beheld <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) as their refuge. [Car 1.1.17]
He, the lord of the immortals, will declare the means of alleviation as it truly is.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: dhāraṇāddharmaḥ sa cātmasamavetaḥ kāryadarśanānumeyaḥ arthaḥ suvarṇādiḥ kāmyata ita kāmo vanitāpariṣvaṅgādiḥ mokṣaḥ saṃsāravimokṣaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is so called from 'sustaining' (<s>dhāraṇa</s>); it inheres in the self and is inferred from the observation of its effects. <s>Artha</s> (wealth) means gold and the like. <s>Kāma</s> (desire) is so called because it is desired — it refers to the embrace of women and such pleasures. <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation) is release from the cycle of existence (<s>saṃsāra</s>). [1]
Health (<s>ārogya</s>) is the equilibrium of the <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents), arising from the absence of disease. [2]
'Root' (<s>mūla</s>) means cause. [3]

children.text: uttamamiti pradhānaṃ tenārogyaṃ caturvarge pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ rogagṛhītasya kvacidapi puruṣārthe 'samarthatvād ityuktam // 4
children.translated_text: 'Supreme' means principal; thus health is the principal cause among the four aims of life (<s>caturvarga</s>), since one afflicted with disease is incapable of any human aim whatsoever — this is what is stated. [4]

children.text: tasyāpahartāra iti ārogyasyāpahartāraḥ idam eva ca rogāṇām ārogyāpaharaṇaṃ yad anarthalābhaḥ na punar utpanno rogaḥ paścād ārogyam apaharati bhāvābhāvayoḥ parasparābhāvātmakatvāt // 5
children.translated_text: 'Destroyers of that' means destroyers of health. And this destruction of health by diseases is the acquisition of harm; it is not that a disease, once arisen, subsequently destroys health, because existence and non-existence are mutually defined by the absence of each other. [5]

children.text: śreyaso jīvitasya ceti śreyovajjīvitaṃ hitatvena sukhatvena cārthe daśamahāmūlīye vakṣyamāṇaṃ tasya jīvitasyāpahartāra iti yojanīyam aśreyojīvitamahitatvena duḥkhahetutayā cānupādeyam iti kṛtvā tadapaharaṇamiha noktam // 6
children.translated_text: 'And of a worthy life' — a life that is worthy means one that is beneficial and happy, as will be described in the chapter '<s>Daśamahāmūlīya</s>'; 'destroyers of that life' is how it should be construed. A life that is unworthy, being non-beneficial and a cause of suffering, is not worth taking up — therefore its destruction is not mentioned here. [6]

children.text: atra sukhitajīvitopaghāto dharmādyupaghātenaiva labdhaḥ tena vayaṃ paśyāmaḥ śreyaḥśabdena sāmānye nābhyudayavācinā dharmādayo 'bhidhīyante jīvitaśabdena ca jīvitamātraṃ yato jīvitaṃ svarūpeṇaiva sarvaprāṇināṃ nirupādhyupādeyaṃ vacanaṃ hi ācakame ca brahmaṇa iyamātmā āśīḥ āyuṣmān bhūyāsam iti // 7
children.translated_text: Here, the harm to a happy life is already implied by the harm to <s>dharma</s> and the other aims. Therefore, we hold that the word '<s>śreyas</s>' (worthy/auspicious), in its general sense and not referring specifically to worldly prosperity, denotes <s>dharma</s> and the other aims, while the word 'life' (<s>jīvita</s>) denotes life itself — because life, in its own nature, is unconditionally worth preserving for all living beings. For the scriptural statement says: 'And <s>Brahman</s> desired: "May this self — may I live long."' [7]

children.text: yattvatyantaduḥkhagṛhītasya jīvitaṃ jihāsitaṃ tatra duḥkhasyātyantajihāsitasyānyathā hātum aśakyatvāt priyamapi jīvitaṃ tyaktum icchati na svarūpeṇa // 8
children.translated_text: As for the statement that one who is seized by extreme suffering desires to abandon life — there, because suffering which is extremely desired to be abandoned cannot be removed otherwise, one wishes to abandon even dear life; not [life] in its own essential nature. // 8
'Obstacle' (<s>antarāya</s>) should be understood as [an obstacle] to the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s> and the like. // 9
'This' (<s>ayam</s>) refers to [the obstacle] in the form of the manifestation of disease. // 10
'Of those' (<s>teṣām</s>) means: of diseases. // 11
'Refuge' (<s>śaraṇam</s>) means: protector. // 12
Because of his capacity, he is called <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). // 13

children.text: dhyānaṃ samādhiviśeṣaḥ tadupalabdhisādhanatvāccakṣur iva dhyānacakṣuḥ tena sa vakṣyati śamopāyaṃ yathāvad amaraprabhuḥ iti dhyānacakṣuṣā dadṛśuriti yojanā // 14]
children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is a particular form of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Because it is the means of attaining that [knowledge], it is called 'the eye of meditation' (<s>dhyāna-cakṣus</s>), like an eye. He will [later] say: 'The lord of the immortals will declare the means of pacification as it truly is.' Thus 'they saw with the eye of meditation' — this is the syntactic connection. // 14]

children.text: kaḥ sahasrākṣabhavanaṃ gacchet praṣṭuṃ śacīpatim // Car_1,1.18
children.translated_text: Who shall go to the abode of the Thousand-Eyed One to ask the Lord of <s>Śacī</s>? // Car_1,1.18
'Let me be employed in this purpose' — this was the first speech.
<s>Bharadvāja</s> spoke thus; therefore he was appointed by the sages. // Car_1,1.19
He, having gone to <s>Śakra</s>'s abode, [found him] situated amidst hosts of divine sages,
and saw the Slayer of <s>Bala</s>, blazing like fire. // Car_1,1.20
He, having approached and congratulated the Lord of the Gods with blessings of victory,

children.text: provāca vinayāddhīmān ṛṣīṇāṃ vākyam uttamam // Car_1,1.21
children.translated_text: spoke with humility, the wise one, the supreme message of the sages: // Car_1,1.21
'Diseases have arisen that cause fear to all living beings;
therefore tell me the means of their pacification as it truly is, O Lord of the Immortals.' // Car_1,1.22
To him the blessed Lord of a Hundred Sacrifices (<s>Śatakratu</s>) taught <s>Āyurveda</s>,
having understood his vast intellect, in few words, to that supreme sage. // Car_1,1.23
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: athaiteṣu madhye bharadvājaḥ katham indram upāgamad ityāha ka ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, how among these [sages] <s>Bharadvāja</s> approached <s>Indra</s> — this is stated beginning with 'Who' (<s>ka</s>). // 1

children.text: śacīpatim ityanena śacīsambhogavyāsaktam apyaham upāsituṃ kṣama iti bharadvājo darśayati // 2
children.translated_text: 'Lord of <s>Śacī</s>' — by this, <s>Bharadvāja</s> shows: 'I am fit to approach even one who is absorbed in the enjoyment of <s>Śacī</s>.' // 2
'In the purpose' (<s>arthe</s>) means: in the objective. // 3
'Let me be employed' (<s>niyujyeyam</s>) means: let me be engaged. // 4
'Herein' (<s>atra</s>) means: in this very stated objective. The word <s>atra</s> [functions] because [it specifies] 'in which purpose.' // 5

children.text: yathā subhikṣam ityāgataḥ yasmāt subhikṣaṃ tasmādāgata ityarthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: Just as [one says] 'he came because of abundance' — since there was abundance, therefore he came — such is the meaning. // 6

children.text: niyojita iti caurādiko ṇica na hetau // 7
children.translated_text: 'Appointed' (<s>niyojita</s>) — the causative is of the <s>curādi</s> [tenth conjugation] type, not in the sense of 'cause.' // 7

children.text: anena prakaraṇena bharadvājasyāyurvedāgame viśeṣeṇārthitvānna preraṇamiti darśitaṃ bhavati // 8
children.translated_text: By this passage it is shown that <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s going for <s>Āyurveda</s> was especially from his own eagerness, not from being urged [by others]. // 8

children.text: provāceti samyaguvāca na tu praśabdaḥ prapañcārthaḥ padairalpair ityuktatvāt // 9
children.translated_text: 'Spoke' (<s>provāca</s>) means: spoke correctly. The prefix <s>pra-</s> is not for the purpose of elaboration, since 'in few words' has been stated. // 9

children.text: kasmāt padair alpair uvācetyāha matiṃ buddhvā vipulām iti yasmād vipulamatiṃ bharadvājaṃ pratipannavān tasmāt padair alpair uvāceti bhāvaḥ matiś ca bahuviṣayatvenopacārād vipulety ucyate sā ca matiḥ śuśrūṣāśravaṇagrahaṇadhāraṇohāpohatattvābhiniveśavatīha vipulā boddhavyā // 10
children.translated_text: Why did he teach in few words? This is answered by 'having understood his vast intellect' — since he recognized <s>Bharadvāja</s> as one of vast intellect, therefore he taught in few words — such is the purport. And the intellect is called 'vast' (<s>vipulā</s>) figuratively, because of having many subjects [within its scope]. That intellect — endowed with eagerness to hear, hearing, grasping, retaining, reasoning pro and con, and dedication to truth — should here be understood as 'vast.' // 10

children.text: atra cendreṇa divyadṛśā bharadvājābhiprāyam agrata eva buddhvāyurveda upadiṣṭaḥ tena bharadvājasyendrapṛcchādīha na darśitaṃ kiṃvā bhūtam apīndrapṛcchādi granthavistarabhayād iha na likhitam // 11]
children.translated_text: And here, <s>Indra</s>, having already understood <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s intention through divine sight, taught <s>Āyurveda</s>. Therefore <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s questioning of <s>Indra</s> and the like is not shown here. Or, though <s>Indra</s>'s questioning and the like actually occurred, it is not written here out of fear of expanding the text. // 11]
The knowledge of causes, symptoms, and medicines, directed toward the healthy and the sick,

children.text: trisūtraṃ śāśvataṃ puṇyaṃ bubudhe yaṃ pitāmahaḥ // Car_1,1.24
children.translated_text: threefold in its threads, eternal, and meritorious — that which <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Brahmā) understood. // Car_1,1.24
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
What that <s>Āyurveda</s> taught in few words was like — this is stated beginning with 'cause' (<s>hetu</s>). // 1

children.text: hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānamiti hetvādīni jñāyante 'neneti hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānaṃ yāvac cāyurvedavācyaṃ tāvaddhetvādyantarbhūtam ityarthaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'Knowledge of causes, symptoms, and medicines' (<s>hetu-liṅga-auṣadha-jñānam</s>) — causes and the rest are known by means of this, therefore [it is called] 'knowledge of causes, symptoms, and medicines.' And as far as <s>Āyurveda</s> expresses, that much is included within causes and the rest — such is the meaning. // 2

children.text: hetugrahaṇena saṃnikṛṣṭaviprakṛṣṭavyādhihetugrahaṇaṃ liṅgagrahaṇena ca vyādher ārogyasya ca kṛtsnaṃ liṅgamucyate tena vyādhyārogye 'pi liṅgaśabdavācye yatastābhyāmapi hi talliṅgaṃ liṅgyata eva vakṣyati hi viṣamārambhamūlānāṃ jvara eko hi lakṣaṇam // 3
children.translated_text: By the word 'cause' (<s>hetu</s>), both proximate and remote causes of disease are grasped. By the word 'symptom' (<s>liṅga</s>), the entire symptomatology of both disease and health is stated. Thus disease and health too are denoted by the word 'symptom,' since by both of them that symptom is indeed indicated. For it will be stated: 'Of those whose origin is in irregular activity, fever alone is the defining mark.' // 3

children.text: viṣamārambhamūlādyair jvara eko nigadyate ityādi auṣadhagrahaṇena ca sarvapathyāvarodhaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: 'Of those whose origin is in irregular activity and the like, fever alone is declared' — and so on. By the word 'medicine' (<s>auṣadha</s>), all that is wholesome is included. // 4
And the body is here included within both 'cause' and 'symptom.' // 5

'Directed toward the healthy and the sick' (<s>svasthāturaparāyaṇam</s>) — the supreme, excellent path (<s>ayana</s>) for the healthy and the sick — thus [it is called] <s>svasthāturaparāyaṇam</s>. // 6

children.text: kimanyo'yaṃ hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānarūpa āyurvedo brahmabuddhādāyurvedād utānanya ityāha trisūtram ityādi // 7
children.translated_text: Is this <s>Āyurveda</s> in the form of knowledge of causes, symptoms, and medicines different from the <s>Āyurveda</s> understood by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, or is it the same? This is answered by 'threefold in its threads' (<s>trisūtram</s>) and the rest. // 7

children.text: pitāmaho'pi yaṃ trisūtraṃ bubudhe tamindraḥ provāca // 8
children.translated_text: <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Brahmā) also understood it as 'threefold in its threads' — that same [<s>Āyurveda</s>] <s>Indra</s> taught. // 8

children.text: trīṇi hetvādīni sūtryante yasmin yena vā tantrisūtram // 9
children.translated_text: Three — causes and the rest — are threaded (<s>sūtryante</s>) in which or by which — [hence] 'threefold in threads' (<s>trisūtram</s>). // 9
There, [it is called] <s>sūtra</s> (thread) because of indicating (<s>sūcanāt</s>), because of threading (<s>sūtraṇāt</s>), and because of the continuity of meaning (<s>arthasaṃtateḥ</s>). // 10

children.text: etena taṃ yathā brahmā trisūtraṃ bubudhe tathaiva hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānam indraḥ provācetyaviplutamāgamaṃ darśayati // 11
children.translated_text: By this, it is shown that just as <s>Brahmā</s> understood it as 'threefold in threads,' so too <s>Indra</s> taught the knowledge of causes, symptoms, and medicines — [thus] demonstrating the unbroken transmission (<s>aviplutam āgamam</s>). // 11
'Understood' (<s>bubudhe</s>) — not 'created' (<s>kṛtavān</s>). // 12
For this very reason it is said 'eternal' (<s>śāśvatam</s>) — meaning: permanent. // 13
And that eternality is to be explained at the end of the <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>. // 14]
He, the great-minded sage, single-mindedly,

children.text: yathāvadacirāt sarvaṃ bubudhe tanmanā muniḥ // Car_1,1.25
children.translated_text: understood quickly and fully that boundless, three-branched <s>Āyurveda</s>. // Car_1,1.25
By that [knowledge], <s>Bharadvāja</s> obtained immeasurable life, accompanied by happiness;
and that [knowledge] he taught to the sages without remainder and without excess. // Car_1,1.26
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: athoddiṣṭam āyurvedaṃ kathaṃ gṛhītavān bharadvāja ityāha so 'nantetyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, how did <s>Bharadvāja</s> receive the <s>Āyurveda</s> that was taught? This is stated beginning with 'He, the boundless' (<s>so 'nanta</s>). // 1

children.text: avidyamānāv antapārau yasyāsāv anantapāraḥ atra pāraśabdena gobalīvardanyāyenādir ucyate pāraśabdo hy ubhayor api nadīkūlayor vivakṣāvaśād vartate kiṃvā ananto mokṣaḥ pāram utkṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ yasyāyurvedasyāsāv anantapāraḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'Boundless and shore-less' (<s>anantapāra</s>) — that whose end and shore do not exist — that is <s>anantapāra</s>. Here, by the word 'shore' (<s>pāra</s>), by the logic of 'cow-and-bull' (<s>gobalīvardanyāya</s>), the beginning is [also] denoted. For the word <s>pāra</s> applies to both banks of a river according to the desired sense. Or: 'boundless' (<s>ananta</s>) is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); 'the supreme fruit' (<s>pāra</s>) which is excellent — of that <s>Āyurveda</s> — [hence] <s>anantapāra</s>. // 2

children.text: vakṣyati hi cikitsā tu naiṣṭhikī yā vinopadhām iti // 3
children.translated_text: For it will be stated: 'The ultimate therapy is that which is without support [of worldly aims].' // 3
Here 'ultimate' (<s>naiṣṭhikī</s>) means: the cause of the means to liberation. // 4

children.text: trayo hetvādayaḥ skandharūpā yasya sa triskandhaḥ skandhaśca sthūlāvayavaḥ pravibhāgo vā // 5
children.translated_text: Three — causes and the rest — being in the form of branches (<s>skandha</s>) — [hence] 'three-branched' (<s>triskandha</s>). And a branch (<s>skandha</s>) is a major division or section. // 5
He whose mind was on that very reception of <s>Āyurveda</s> — he is 'single-minded' (<s>tanmanāḥ</s>). // 6
Because of reflection (<s>manana</s>) [and] being endowed with excellence of knowledge — [he is called] 'sage' (<s>muni</s>). // 7

children.text: etena yasmādayaṃ mahāmatis tanmanāḥ muniśca tenānantapāramapyāyurvedaṃ hetvādiskandhatrayamālambanaṃ kṛtvā yathāvadacirādeva pratipannavān ityāśayaḥ // 8
children.translated_text: By this [it is meant]: since he was of great intellect, single-minded, and a sage, therefore he understood quickly and fully even the boundless <s>Āyurveda</s>, using the three branches of causes and the rest as his foundation — such is the purport. // 8
'Quickly' (<s>acirāt</s>) means: in a short time. // 9

children.text: atra ca yathā brahmā trisūtraṃ bubudhe yathā cendro hetuliṅgauṣadhajñānaṃ provāca tathaiva bharadvājo'pi triskandhaṃ taṃ bubudhe ityanenāyurvedasyāviplutāgamatvam upadarśyate tena trisūtratriskandhayor na punaruktiḥ // 10
children.translated_text: And here, just as <s>Brahmā</s> understood it as 'threefold in threads,' and just as <s>Indra</s> taught the 'knowledge of causes, symptoms, and medicines,' so too <s>Bharadvāja</s> understood it as 'three-branched' — by this, the unbroken transmission of <s>Āyurveda</s> is demonstrated. Therefore there is no redundancy between 'threefold in threads' and 'three-branched.' // 10
'By that' (<s>tena</s>) means: by the <s>Āyurveda</s> received from <s>Indra</s>. // 11
'Immeasurable' (<s>amitam</s>) means: as if immeasurable — because of being exceedingly long. // 12

children.text: āyuḥśabdaścāyuḥkāraṇe rasāyanajñāne boddhavyaḥ yenottarakālaṃ hi rasāyanopayogād ayaṃ bharadvājo'mitamāyuravāpsyati na ṛṣibhya āyurvedakathanāt pūrvaṃ rasāyanamācarati sma kiṃvā sarvaprāṇyupakārārthādhītāyurvedajanitadharmavaśāt tatkālam evāmitamāyur lebhe bharadvāja iti boddhavyam // 13
children.translated_text: The word 'life' (<s>āyus</s>) should be understood as [referring to] the cause of life, namely the knowledge of rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>). For later, through the use of <s>rasāyana</s>, this <s>Bharadvāja</s> will obtain immeasurable life — he does not practice <s>rasāyana</s> before teaching <s>Āyurveda</s> to the sages. Or: through the <s>dharma</s> born from having studied <s>Āyurveda</s> for the benefit of all beings, he obtained immeasurable life at that very time — this should be understood. // 13

children.text: tacceti śrutaṃ yadā tamiti pāṭhaḥ tadā tam āyurvedam // 14
children.translated_text: 'That' (<s>tac</s>) — what was heard. When the reading is 'that' (<s>tam</s>), [it means] 'that <s>Āyurveda</s>.' // 14
'Without remainder' (<s>anavaśeṣayan</s>) means: completely — such is the meaning. // 15
Having studied <s>Āyurveda</s>, immediately afterwards he gave it to the sages. // 16]
And the sages received from <s>Bharadvāja</s> that [<s>Āyurveda</s>] which benefits [all] creatures,
desiring long life — the <s>Veda</s> that increases lifespan. // Car_1,1.27
Those great sages saw correctly, with the eye of knowledge,

children.text: sāmānyaṃ ca viśeṣaṃ ca guṇān dravyāṇi karma ca // Car_1,1.28
children.translated_text: <s>sāmānya</s> (generality) and <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), qualities, substances, and action, // Car_1,1.28
and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). Having known these, established in the methods taught in the treatise,

children.text: lebhire paramaṃ śarma jīvitaṃ cāpyanitvaram // Car_1,1.29
children.translated_text: they obtained supreme bliss and also life without haste [i.e., long life]. // Car_1,1.29
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Desiring long life' — that is, of [all] living beings and of themselves. // 1

children.text: jñānārthaṃ jñānarūpaṃ vā cakṣur jñānacakṣuḥ tena jñānacakṣuṣā // 2
children.translated_text: An eye for the purpose of knowledge or in the form of knowledge is the 'eye of knowledge' (<s>jñāna-cakṣus</s>); with that eye of knowledge [they saw]. // 2

children.text: gṛhītena tenāyurvedena kiṃ dadṛśurityāha sāmānyaṃ cetyādi // 3
children.translated_text: Having received that <s>Āyurveda</s>, what did they see? This is answered by '<s>sāmānya</s>' and the rest. // 3

children.text: eṣāṃ cottaratra lakṣaṇaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ padārthānāṃ viśvarūpāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati tenaitat tatraiva vyākaraṇīyam // 4
children.translated_text: The definitions of these six categories (<s>padārtha</s>), which are of universal form, will [be given] later. Therefore this is to be explained there. // 4
'Those' (<s>tad</s>) refers to <s>sāmānya</s> and the rest. // 5
'The method taught in the treatise' (<s>tantroktaṃ vidhim</s>) — [the method] in the form of avoiding what is unwholesome and adopting what is wholesome. // 6
'Bliss' (<s>śarma</s>) means: happiness. // 7
'Supreme' (<s>param</s>) means: not invaded by suffering. // 8
'Without haste' (<s>anitvaram</s>) means: without rushing [i.e., long-lasting]. // 9]
Then <s>Punarvasu</s> [<s>Ātreya</s>], devoted to friendliness, [gave] the meritorious <s>Āyurveda</s>
to six disciples, out of compassion for all beings. // Car_1,1.30
<s>Agniveśa</s>, <s>Bhela</s>, <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>,
<s>Hārīta</s>, and <s>Kṣārapāṇi</s> — they received the words of that sage. // Car_1,1.31
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
With 'Then' (<s>atha</s>) and the rest, he shows the status of <s>Ātreya</s> — also known as <s>Punarvasu</s>, the disciple of <s>Bharadvāja</s> — as teacher of <s>Agniveśa</s> and the others. // 1

children.text: atra kecidbharadvājātreyayoraikyaṃ manyante tanna bharadvājasaṃjñayā ātreyasya kvacid api tantrapradeśe 'kīrtanāt hārīte cātreyādigurutayā bharadvāja uktaḥ śakrād aham adhītavān ityādinā mattaḥ punarasaṃkhyeyās trisūtraṃ triprayojanam // 2
children.translated_text: Here some hold that <s>Bharadvāja</s> and <s>Ātreya</s> are identical. That is not so, because <s>Ātreya</s> is never mentioned by the name <s>Bharadvāja</s> anywhere in the treatise. And in the <s>Hārīta</s> [Saṃhitā], <s>Bharadvāja</s> is stated as the teacher of <s>Ātreya</s> and the others, by [the passage beginning] 'I have studied from <s>Śakra</s>' and so on: 'From me, again, innumerable [learned] the threefold-threaded, three-purposed [<s>Āyurveda</s>].' // 2
'From <s>Ātreya</s> onward, the seven great sages know [it].' // 3
[The lineage runs] up to 'From <s>Ātreya</s>, the sage <s>Hārīta</s>.' // 4

children.text: vāgbhaṭena tu yaduktaṃ brahmā smṛtvāyuṣo vedaṃ prajāpatim ajigrahat // 5
children.translated_text: But what <s>Vāgbhaṭa</s> has said — '<s>Brahmā</s>, having recalled the <s>Veda</s> of life, taught <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: so 'śvinau tau sahasrākṣaṃ so 'triputrādikān munīn vā ityanenātreyasyendraśiṣyatvaṃ tadāyurvedasamutthānīyarasāyanapāde ādiśabdena vakṣyamāṇendraśiṣyatāyogāt samarthanīyam // 6
children.translated_text: he [taught] the <s>Aśvins</s>, they the Thousand-Eyed One, he the sons of <s>Atri</s> and other sages' — by this, <s>Ātreya</s>'s studentship under <s>Indra</s> [should be reconciled]. Since in the <s>Āyurveda-samutthānīya-rasāyana</s> section, the word 'and others' (<s>ādi</s>) implies <s>Indra</s>-studentship yet to be stated, it should be harmonized [with the present account]. // 6

children.text: tatra hīndreṇa punarmaharṣīṇām āyurveda upadiṣṭa iti vaktavyam // 7
children.translated_text: For there it is to be said: '<s>Indra</s> taught <s>Āyurveda</s> to the great sages again.' // 7

children.text: maitrīparo maitrīpradhānaḥ maitrī ca sarvaprāṇiṣvātmanīva buddhiḥ // 8]
children.translated_text: 'Devoted to friendliness' (<s>maitrīparaḥ</s>) — one for whom friendliness is primary. And friendliness is the [attitude of] regarding all living beings as [one regards] oneself. // 8]
There was a distinction of intellect [in him] — not another instruction from the sage;

children.text: tantrasya kartā prathamam agniveśo yato 'bhavat // Car_1,1.32
children.translated_text: therefore <s>Agniveśa</s> became the first author of the treatise. // Car_1,1.32

children.text: atha bhelādayaś cakruḥ svaṃ svaṃ tantraṃ kṛtāni ca /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhela</s> and the others also composed their respective treatises; and these compositions
they recited before <s>Ātreya</s> together with the assemblage of sages — those of good intellect. // Car_1,1.33
Hearing the threading of meanings by those of meritorious deeds,

children.text: yathāvat sūtritam iti prahṛṣṭās te 'numenire // Car_1,1.34
children.translated_text: the sages, delighted, approved [saying]: 'It has been properly threaded.' // Car_1,1.34
All of them praised those [authors], who desired the welfare of all beings,

children.text: sādhu bhūteṣvanukrośa ityuccair abruvan samam // Car_1,1.35
children.translated_text: [saying] 'Excellent is the compassion toward beings!' — they spoke aloud together. // Car_1,1.35

children.text: taṃ puṇyaṃ śuśruvuḥ śabdaṃ divi devarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: That meritorious sound was heard by the divine sages stationed in heaven;

children.text: sāmarāḥ paramarṣīṇāṃ śrutvā mumudire param // Car_1,1.36
children.translated_text: together with the gods, hearing [it] from the supreme sages, they rejoiced greatly. // Car_1,1.36

children.text: aho sādhviti nirghoṣo lokāṃs trīn anvavādayat /
children.translated_text: A cry of 'Ah, excellent!' resounded through the three worlds,
in the sky — smooth, deep, uttered by the delighted celestials. // Car_1,1.37

children.text: śivo vāyur vavau sarvā bhābhir unmīlitā diśaḥ /
children.translated_text: An auspicious wind blew; all directions were illumined with radiance;

children.text: nipetuḥ sajalāś caiva divyāḥ kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ // Car_1,1.38
children.translated_text: and divine showers of flowers, bearing water, fell. // Car_1,1.38
Then the deities of knowledge entered <s>Agniveśa</s> and the others who stood foremost —

children.text: buddhiḥ siddhiḥ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kīrtiḥ kṣamādayaḥ // Car_1,1.39
children.translated_text: Intelligence, Accomplishment, Memory, Wisdom, Steadfastness, Fame, Forbearance, and the rest. // Car_1,1.39
And those treatises of theirs, approved by the supreme sages

children.text: bhavāya bhūtasaṃghānāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ bhuvi lebhire // Car_1,1.40
children.translated_text: for the welfare of the multitude of beings, attained establishment on earth. // Car_1,1.40

children.text: hitāhitaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkham āyus tasya hitāhitam /
children.translated_text: What is beneficial and harmful, what is happiness and suffering, what is life and what is beneficial and harmful to life,

children.text: mānaṃ ca tacca yatroktam āyurvedaḥ sa ucyate // Car_1,1.41
children.translated_text: and the measure of that — where [all] this is declared, that is called <s>Āyurveda</s>. // Car_1,1.41
Life is the conjunction of body, sense-organs, mind, and self — [that which is] sustaining,

children.text: nityagaś cānubandhaś ca paryāyair āyur ucyate // Car_1,1.42
children.translated_text: Continuous (<s>nityaga</s>) and connected (<s>anubandha</s>) — by these synonyms, life (<s>āyus</s>) is spoken of. // Car_1,1.42
Of that life, the most sacred knowledge (<s>veda</s>) is deemed [so] by the knowers of knowledge,

children.text: vakṣyate yan manuṣyāṇāṃ lokayor ubhayor hitam // Car_1,1.43
children.translated_text: which will be expounded, for the benefit of human beings in both worlds. // Car_1,1.43
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s> (Ātreya),
Now we shall expound the chapter called <s>Vātakalākalīya</s> (On the Qualities and Faults of <s>Vāta</s>). // Car_1,12.1
Thus spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car_1,12.2
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: pūrvādhyāye rogāḥ svarūpamārgabāhyakāraṇabheṣajair abhihitāḥ upayuktajñānās tatkāraṇavātādayo bahuvācyatvān noktāḥ ataḥ samprati pṛthakprakaraṇe te 'bhidhīyante vātakalākalīye tatrāpi prādhānyād vāyureva prathamamucyate /
children.translated_text: In the previous chapter, diseases were described with respect to their nature, pathways, external causes, and remedies. [Although] the knowledge employed [there] is useful, <s>Vāta</s> and the other causes [of disease], being subjects of extensive discussion, were not mentioned. Therefore, now in a separate section, they are discussed — in the <s>Vātakalākalīya</s>. There too, because of its primacy, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is discussed first.

children.text: kalā guṇaḥ yaduktaṃ ṣoḍaśakalam iti akalā guṇaviruddho doṣaḥ tena vātakalākalīyo vātaguṇadoṣīya ityarthaḥ yadi vā kalā sūkṣmo bhāgas tasyāpi kalā kalākalā tasyāpi sūkṣmo bhāga ityarthaḥ // 1]
children.translated_text: <s>Kalā</s> means 'quality' — as stated in 'consisting of sixteen <s>kalās</s>.' <s>Akalā</s> means 'fault,' which is opposed to quality. Thus <s>Vātakalākalīya</s> means 'concerning the qualities and faults of <s>Vāta</s>.' Alternatively, <s>kalā</s> means a subtle part; the <s>kalā</s> of that <s>kalā</s> [is] <s>kalākalā</s> — meaning the most subtle aspect of that.

children.text: vātakalākalājñānamadhikṛtya parasparamatāni jijñāsamānāḥ samupaviśya maharṣayaḥ papracchuranyo'nyaṃ kiṃguṇo vāyuḥ kimasya prakopaṇam upaśamanāni vāsya kāni kathaṃ cainam asaṃghātavantam anavasthitam anāsādya prakopaṇapraśamanāni prakopayanti praśamayanti vā kāni cāsya kupitākupitasya śarīrāśarīracarasya śarīreṣu carataḥ karmāṇi bahiḥśarīrebhyo veti // Car_1,12.3
children.translated_text: Having taken up the knowledge of the qualities and faults of <s>Vāta</s>, the great sages, desiring to know one another's views, sat together and asked one another: 'What are the qualities of <s>Vāyu</s>? What aggravates it? What are its pacifying [factors]? And how do aggravating and pacifying [factors] aggravate or pacify it — which is without mass, unstable, and intangible? And what are the actions of [<s>Vāyu</s>] — whether aggravated or not, whether moving in the body or outside bodies — when it moves in bodies, and outside bodies?' // Car_1,12.3
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

Here, the discussion of the qualities of <s>Vāta</s> and the like, being in the form of statements by multiple sages, is for the purpose of showing the agreement of many sages, and for making the treatise conform to the conventions of doctrine, narrative, and tradition.
'Without mass' (<s>asaṃghāta</s>) means lacking an aggregate of parts, unlike <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Śleṣman</s> (Kapha).
'Unstable' (<s>anavasthita</s>) means of a moving nature.
'Intangible' (<s>anāsādya</s>) should be understood as being due to its mobility and its having non-dense constituent parts.

children.text: atrovāca kuśaḥ sāṃkṛtyāyanaḥ rūkṣalaghuśītadāruṇakharaviśadāḥ ṣaḍime vātaguṇā bhavanti // Car_1,12.4
children.translated_text: Thereupon <s>Kuśa Sāṃkṛtyāyana</s> said: 'Dry (<s>rūkṣa</s>), light (<s>laghu</s>), cold (<s>śīta</s>), harsh (<s>dāruṇa</s>), rough (<s>khara</s>), and clear (<s>viśada</s>) — these six are the qualities of <s>Vāta</s>.' // Car_1,12.4
<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

<s>Rūkṣa</s> and the others are primarily states of being; therefore, dryness and the like should be understood as qualities. Harshness (<s>dāruṇatva</s>) [means] mobility (<s>calatva</s>) — [through this,] the mobility stated in the <s>Dīrghaṃjīvitīya</s> [chapter] is accounted for. Alternatively, harshness (<s>dāruṇatva</s>) means producing hardness (<s>kāṭhinya</s>) through desiccation.

children.text: tacchrutvā vākyaṃ kumāraśirā bharadvāja uvāca evametadyathā bhagavānāha eta eva vātaguṇā bhavanti sa tv evaṃguṇair evaṃdravyair evamprabhāvaiśca karmabhirabhyasyamānair vāyuḥ prakopamāpadyate samānaguṇābhyāso hi dhātūnāṃ vṛddhikāraṇamiti // Car_1,12.5
children.translated_text: Having heard that statement, <s>Kumāraśirā Bhāradvāja</s> said: 'It is exactly so, as the venerable one says. These indeed are the qualities of <s>Vāta</s>. But <s>Vāyu</s> becomes aggravated when substances, powers, and actions of similar qualities are repeatedly applied. For the habitual use of substances of similar qualities is the cause of increase in the <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents).' // Car_1,12.5
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'<s>Kumāraśirā</s>' is a qualifier of <s>Bhāradvāja</s> — for the purpose of distinguishing him from [the] <s>Bhāradvāja</s> [who is] the teacher of <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: evamprabhāvairiti prabhāvād raukṣyādikārakair dhāvanajāgaraṇādibhiḥ prabhāvābhidhānaṃ ca karmaṇāṃ nirguṇatvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Of similar powers' (<s>evamprabhāva</s>) means [substances] that produce dryness and the like through their inherent power — such as running, wakefulness, and the like. The term 'power' (<s>prabhāva</s>) is used for actions because actions are without [explicit] qualities.
'Habitually applied' (<s>abhyasyamāna</s>) means used repeatedly.

children.text: tacchrutvā vākyaṃ kāṅkāyano vāhlīkabhiṣag uvāca evametadyathā bhagavānāha etānyeva vātaprakopaṇāni bhavanti ato viparītāni vātasya praśamanāni bhavanti prakopaṇaviparyayo hi dhātūnāṃ praśamakāraṇamiti // Car_1,12.6
children.translated_text: Having heard that statement, <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, the physician of <s>Bāhlīka</s>, said: 'It is exactly so, as the venerable one says. These indeed are the aggravators of <s>Vāta</s>. What is opposite to these constitutes the pacifying [factors] of <s>Vāta</s>. For the opposite of aggravation is the cause of pacification of the <s>dhātus</s>.' // Car_1,12.6

children.text: tacchrutvā vākyaṃ baḍiśo dhāmārgava uvāca evametadyathā bhagavānāha etānyeva vātaprakopapraśamanāni bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Having heard that statement, <s>Baḍiśa Dhāmārgava</s> said: 'It is exactly so, as the venerable one says. These indeed are the factors of aggravation and pacification of <s>Vāta</s>.

children.text: yathā hy enam asaṃghātam anavasthitamanāsādya prakopaṇapraśamanāni prakopayanti praśamayanti vā tathānuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ vātaprakopaṇāni khalu rūkṣalaghuśītadāruṇakharaviśadaśuṣirakarāṇi śarīrāṇāṃ tathāvidheṣu śarīreṣu vāyurāśrayaṃ gatvāpyāyamānaḥ prakopamāpadyate vātapraśamanāni punaḥ snigdhagurūṣṇaślakṣṇamṛdupicchilaghanakarāṇi śarīrāṇāṃ tathāvidheṣu śarīreṣu vāyur asajyamānaś caran praśāntimāpadyate // Car_1,12.7
children.translated_text: As to how the aggravating and pacifying [factors] aggravate or pacify it — which is without mass, unstable, and intangible — we shall explain thus: The aggravators of <s>Vāta</s> produce dryness, lightness, coldness, harshness, roughness, clearness, and porosity in the body-parts. In bodies of such [quality], <s>Vāyu</s>, having reached its abode and being nourished, becomes aggravated. The pacifiers of <s>Vāta</s>, on the other hand, produce unctuousness, heaviness, heat, smoothness, softness, viscosity, and denseness in the body-parts. In bodies of such [quality], <s>Vāyu</s>, not adhering [and] moving [freely], attains pacification.' // Car_1,12.7

children.text:
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}
  śarīrāṇāmiti śarīrāvayavānām /
  śuṣirakarāṇi randhrakarāṇi /
  āśrayamiti samānaguṇasthānam /
children.translated_text:
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'Of the bodies' (<s>śarīrāṇām</s>) means of the body-parts.
'Producing porosity' (<s>śuṣirakarāṇi</s>) means producing hollows.
'Abode' (<s>āśraya</s>) means a location of similar qualities.
'Being nourished' (<s>āpyāyamāna</s>) means being augmented.
The opposite of 'harsh' (<s>dāruṇa</s>) is 'soft' (<s>mṛdu</s>); the opposite of 'porous' (<s>śuṣira</s>) is 'dense' (<s>ghana</s>).
'Not adhering' (<s>asajyamāna</s>) means not remaining [in one place], i.e., with its constituent parts diminishing.

children.text: etenaitaduktaṃ bhavati yadyapi vāyunā vātakāraṇānāṃ vātaśamanānāṃ vā tathā sambandho nāsti tathāpi śarīrasambaddhais tair vātasya śarīracāriṇaḥ sambandho bhavati tataśca vātasya samānaguṇayogādvṛddhir viparītaguṇayogācca hrāsa upapanna eveti // 1]
children.translated_text: By this, the following is stated: although <s>Vāyu</s> does not directly contact the causes of <s>Vāta</s>-aggravation or <s>Vāta</s>-pacification, nevertheless, since they are connected with the body, and since <s>Vāta</s> moves in the body, a connection [exists]. Therefore, the increase of <s>Vāta</s> through conjunction with substances of similar qualities, and its decrease through conjunction with substances of opposite qualities, is well-established.

children.text: tacchrutvā baḍiśavacanam avitatham ṛṣigaṇair anumatamuvāca vāyorvido rājarṣiḥ evametat sarvam anapavādaṃ yathā bhagavānāha /
children.translated_text: Having heard the true statement of <s>Baḍiśa</s>, approved by the assembly of sages, the royal sage <s>Vāyorvida</s> said: 'It is exactly so — everything [you say] is irrefutable, as the venerable one states.

children.text: yāni tu khalu vāyoḥ kupitākupitasya śarīrāśarīracarasya śarīreṣu carataḥ karmāṇi bahiḥśarīrebhyo vā bhavanti teṣāmavayavān pratyakṣānumānopadeśaiḥ sādhayitvā namaskṛtya vāyave yathāśakti pravakṣyāmaḥ vāyustantrayantradharaḥ prāṇodānasamānavyānāpānātmā pravartakaś ceṣṭānām uccāvacānāṃ niyantā praṇetā ca manasaḥ sarvendriyāṇām udyojakaḥ sarvendriyānām abhivoḍhā sarvaśarīradhātuvyūhakaraḥ saṃdhānakaraḥ śarīrasya pravartako vācaḥ prakṛtiḥ sparśaśabdayoḥ śrotrasparśanayormūlaṃ harṣotsāhayor yoniḥ samīraṇo'gneḥ doṣasaṃśoṣaṇaḥ kṣeptā bahirmalānāṃ sthūlāṇusrotasāṃ bhettā kartā garbhākṛtīnām āyuṣo'nuvṛttipratyayabhūto bhavatyakupitaḥ /
children.translated_text: As to the actions of <s>Vāyu</s> — whether aggravated or not, whether moving in the body or outside bodies — when it moves in bodies or outside bodies, having established their parts through direct perception, inference, and authoritative instruction, and having paid homage to <s>Vāyu</s>, we shall declare them to the best of our ability: <s>Vāyu</s> is the upholder of the body-mechanism (<s>tantrayantradharaḥ</s>); it is of the nature of <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>, <s>Vyāna</s>, and <s>Apāna</s>; it is the initiator of all actions — high and low; the controller and director of the mind; the activator of all sense-organs; the conveyor of all sensory objects; the organizer of all bodily <s>dhātus</s>; the unifier of the body; the originator of speech; the fundamental nature of touch and sound; the root of the organs of hearing and touch; the source of joy and enthusiasm; the stimulator of the digestive fire; the desiccator of [excess] <s>doṣas</s>; the expeller of external waste-matter; the divider of gross and subtle channels; the fashioner of the forms of embryos; and the foundational basis of the continuance of life — when it is not aggravated.

children.text: kupitastu khalu śarīre śarīraṃ nānāvidhairvikārair upatapati balavarṇasukhāyuṣām upaghātāya mano vyāharṣayati sarvendriyāṇy upahanti vinihanti garbhān vikṛtimāpādayaty atikālaṃ vā dhārayati bhayaśokamohadainyātipralāpāñ janayati prāṇāṃścoparuṇaddhi /
children.translated_text: When aggravated, however, it afflicts the body in the body with various kinds of disorders, tending toward the destruction of strength, complexion, happiness, and lifespan; it agitates the mind; impairs all the sense-organs; destroys embryos, or causes them to become deformed, or retains them beyond the proper time; it generates fear, grief, delusion, despair, and excessive babbling; and it obstructs the vital breaths.

children.text: prakṛtibhūtasya khalvasya loke carataḥ karmāṇīmāni bhavanti tadyathā dharaṇīdhāraṇaṃ jvalanojjvālanam ādityacandranakṣatragrahagaṇānāṃ saṃtānagatividhānaṃ sṛṣṭiśca meghānām apāṃ visargaḥ pravartanaṃ srotasāṃ puṣpaphalānāṃ cābhinirvartanam udbhedanaṃ caudbhidānām ṛtūnāṃ pravibhāgaḥ vibhāgo dhātūnāṃ dhātumānasaṃsthānavyaktiḥ bījābhisaṃstāraḥ śasyābhivardhanam avikledopaśoṣaṇe avaikārikavikāraśceti /
children.translated_text: When it moves in the world in its natural state, its actions are as follows: sustaining the earth; blazing of fire; the arrangement of the continuous courses of the sun, moon, stars, and planetary bodies; the creation of clouds; the release of waters; the setting in motion of rivers; the production of flowers and fruits; the sprouting of plants; the division of seasons; the differentiation of [primary] elements (<s>dhātus</s>); the manifestation of the measure, form, and structure of the elements; the germination of seeds; the maturation of crops; [producing] freedom from decay and [proper] drying; and [producing] change without deviation.
