children.text: prakupitasya khalvasya lokeṣu carataḥ karmāṇīmāni bhavanti tadyathā śikhariśikharāvamathanam unmathanamanokahānām utpīḍanaṃ sāgarāṇām udvartanaṃ sarasāṃ pratisaraṇamāpagānām ākampanaṃ ca bhūmeḥ ādhamanam ambudānāṃ nīhāranirhrādapāṃśusikatāmatsyabhekoragakṣārarudhirāśmāśanivisargaḥ vyāpādanaṃ ca ṣaṇṇāmṛtūnāṃ śasyānāmasaṃghātaḥ bhūtānāṃ copasargaḥ bhāvānāṃ cābhāvakaraṇaṃ caturyugāntakarāṇāṃ meghasūryānalānilānāṃ visargaḥ sa hi bhagavān prabhavaścāvyayaśca bhūtānāṃ bhāvābhāvakaraḥ sukhāsukhayor vidhātā mṛtyuḥ yamaḥ niyantā prajāpatiḥ aditiḥ viśvakarmā viśvarūpaḥ sarvagaḥ sarvatantrāṇāṃ vidhātā bhāvānāmaṇuḥ vibhuḥ viṣṇuḥ krāntā lokānāṃ vāyureva bhagavāniti // Car_1,12.8
children.translated_text: When it moves in the worlds in an aggravated state, its actions are as follows: shattering the peaks of mountains; uprooting trees; churning the oceans; causing the lakes to rise up; making rivers flow backward; causing the earth to quake; driving the clouds downward; discharging mist, thunder, dust, sand, fish, frogs, serpents, alkali, blood, stones, and lightning; the destruction of the six seasons; the non-germination of crops; the affliction of beings; and the annihilation of [existing] things. For that blessed [<s>Vāyu</s>] is the origin and the imperishable [force] of all beings; the maker of existence and non-existence; the dispenser of happiness and unhappiness; Death; <s>Yama</s>; the controller; <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Aditi</s>; <s>Viśvakarman</s>; the Universal Form; all-pervading; the arranger of all systems; the atom among [all] entities; the all-pervading; <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the strider across worlds — [such] indeed is the blessed <s>Vāyu</s>. // Car_1,12.8
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: śarīrāśarīracarasyeti vātasvarūpakathanaṃ tena śarīreṣu carata iti bahiḥ śarīrebhyo veti ca punaruktaṃ na bhavati // 1
children.translated_text: 'Moving in the body and outside bodies' describes the nature of <s>Vāta</s> itself; therefore, 'moving in bodies' and 'outside bodies' are not redundant repetitions.
By saying 'parts [thereof],' [the author] indicates that a complete description is impossible due to the great extent of elaboration.
'Having established' (<s>sādhayitvā</s>) means having demonstrated.

Among the actions of <s>Vāta</s>, speech and the like are directly perceptible; the impelling of the mind and the like are inferential; the fashioning of embryonic forms and the like are knowable through authoritative tradition.

children.text: tantraṃ śarīraṃ yad uktaṃ tantrayantreṣu bhinneṣu tamo'ntyaṃ pravivikṣatām iti tadeva yantraṃ yadi vā tantrasya yantraṃ saṃdhayaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: '<s>Tantra</s>' means the body — as stated in 'when the body-mechanisms (<s>tantrayantras</s>) are broken, [the soul] seeks to enter the final darkness.' That itself is the mechanism (<s>yantra</s>); or alternatively, the mechanism of the <s>tantra</s> (body) means the joints.
'Of the nature of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the others' means having the form of <s>Prāṇa</s> and the rest.

children.text: ceṣṭāviśeṣaṇam uccāvacānāṃ vividhānām ityarthaḥ kiṃvā śubhāśubhānāmityarthaḥ // 7
children.translated_text: The qualifier of 'actions' [is] 'high and low' (<s>uccāvaca</s>) — meaning 'of various kinds'; or alternatively, meaning 'auspicious and inauspicious.'

children.text: niyantā anīpsite viṣaye pravartamānasya manasaḥ praṇetā ca manasa evepsite 'rthe // 8
children.translated_text: 'Controller' (<s>niyantā</s>) means [the controller] of the mind when it is engaged in an undesired object; 'director' (<s>praṇetā</s>) means [the director] of the mind toward a desired object.

children.text: udyojakaḥ prerakaḥ kiṃvā udyogakāraka iti pāṭhaḥ so 'pyabhinnārthaḥ // 9
children.translated_text: 'Activator' (<s>udyojaka</s>) means impeller; or the reading <s>udyogakāraka</s> [exists], which has the same meaning.

children.text: abhivoḍhevābhivoḍhā sarvendriyārthagrāhakatvena taccāsya vāyumayena sparśanendriyeṇa sarvendriyāṇāṃ vyāpakatvāt pūrvādhyāyapratipāditena nyāyena boddhavyam // 10
children.translated_text: 'Conveyor' (<s>abhivoḍhā</s>) means the grasper of all sensory objects for all sense-organs. This [capacity] of <s>Vāyu</s> is through the tactile sense-organ, which is made of <s>Vāyu</s> and pervades all sense-organs — this should be understood by the principle established in the previous chapter.
'Organizer' (<s>vyūhakara</s>) means the maker of aggregation, i.e., the maker of [bodily] structure.

children.text: prakṛtiḥ kāraṇaṃ śabdakāraṇatvaṃ ca vāyornityam ākāśānupraveśāt uktaṃ hi khādīnyabhidhāya teṣāmekaguṇaḥ pūrvo guṇavṛddhiḥ pare pare iti // 12
children.translated_text: 'Fundamental nature' (<s>prakṛti</s>) means cause. The causation of sound by <s>Vāyu</s> is constant, because of <s>Vāyu</s>'s invariable penetration into <s>Ākāśa</s> (space). For it is stated, having enumerated <s>Ākāśa</s> and the rest: 'the first has one quality; in each successive [element], there is an increase of quality.'

children.text: tathā punaruktaṃ khādīnyabhidhāya viṣṭaṃ hy aparaṃ pareṇa iti // 13
children.translated_text: And again it is stated, having enumerated <s>Ākāśa</s> and the rest: 'the latter is pervaded by the former.'

children.text: śravaṇamūlatvaṃ vāyoḥ karṇaśaṣkulīracanāviśeṣe vyāpriyamāṇatvāt mūlaṃ pradhānakāraṇam // 14
children.translated_text: The rootness of <s>Vāyu</s> with respect to hearing is because it is engaged in the particular formation of the ear-cavity. 'Root' (<s>mūla</s>) means the primary cause.
'Enthusiasm' (<s>utsāha</s>) means the mental effort toward [accomplishing] tasks.
'Source' (<s>yoni</s>) means the cause of manifestation.
'Desiccator of <s>doṣas</s>' means the desiccator of bodily moisture.
'Divider' (<s>bhettā</s>) and 'fashioner' (<s>kartā</s>) — this [occurs] at the time of the body's origination.
The word '<s>bhūta</s>' (being) here denotes essential nature.
'For the destruction' (<s>upaghātāya</s>) — this is a stop [in the sentence].

children.text: garbhāniti vikṛtim āpādayatyatikālaṃ dhārayatītyanena ca sambadhyate // 21
children.translated_text: 'Embryos' — this connects with 'causes them to become deformed' and 'retains them beyond the proper time.'
'The arrangement of the continuous courses of the sun' and the rest means the arrangement of [their] uninterrupted (<s>saṃtāna</s>) movement (<s>gati</s>).
'Of rivers' (<s>srotasām</s>) means of streams.
'Division' (<s>pravibhāga</s>) means the characteristic of being differentiated.

children.text: dhātūnāmiti pṛthivyādīnāṃ dhātavaḥ kāryadravyāṇi prastarādīni mānaṃ parimāṇaṃ saṃsthānamākṛtiḥ tayorvyaktirabhivyaktiḥ tatra kāraṇamiti yāvat // 25
children.translated_text: 'Of the elements' (<s>dhātūnām</s>) means of earth and the rest. The <s>dhātus</s> are the material substances such as stone and the like. 'Measure' (<s>māna</s>) means dimension. 'Structure' (<s>saṃsthāna</s>) means form. The 'manifestation' (<s>vyakti</s>) of these two — [<s>Vāyu</s>] is the cause thereof.
'Germination of seeds' (<s>bījābhisaṃskāra</s>) — the processing of seeds of rice and the like [means] the capacity for producing sprouts.

children.text: avikledaḥ pākakālād arvāg aviklinnatvam upaśoṣaṇaṃ ca pākena yavādīnāmārdrāṇāmeva avikledopaśoṣaṇe śasyānāmeva // 27
children.translated_text: 'Freedom from decay' (<s>avikleda</s>) means not becoming putrid before the time of ripening; and 'drying' (<s>upaśoṣaṇa</s>) means through ripening of moist [grains] such as barley and the like. Both freedom from decay and drying pertain to crops only.

children.text: avaikārikavikāreṇa sarvasminneva jagati prakṛtirūpe kāraṇatvaṃ brūte // 28
children.translated_text: By 'change without deviation' (<s>avaikārikavikāra</s>), [the author] states that <s>Vāyu</s> is the cause [of change] in the entire universe in its natural state.
'<s>Śikharī</s>' means mountain.
'<s>Anokaha</s>' means tree.
'Rising upward' (<s>udvartana</s>) means upward movement.
'Flowing backward' (<s>pratisaraṇa</s>) means reverse movement.

children.text: visarjanaṃ visargaḥ sa ca pṛthaṅnīhārādibhiḥ sambadhyate nīhāraḥ śiśirasamūhaḥ nirhrādo meghaṃ vinā garjitam aśaniḥ vajrabhedo'gniḥ // 33
children.translated_text: 'Discharge' (<s>visarga</s>) — this connects separately with mist and the rest. '<s>Nīhāra</s>' means a mass of cold [moisture]. '<s>Nirhrāda</s>' means thunder without clouds. '<s>Aśani</s>' means a type of thunderbolt-fire.
'Non-germination' (<s>asaṃghāta</s>) means non-production or non-growth.
'Affliction' (<s>upasarga</s>) means the occurrence of epidemics and the like.
In 'clouds, sun...' and so on, 'discharge' (<s>visarga</s>) means creation.

children.text: vāyur iha devatārūpo'bhipretaḥ tena tasya bhūtalacaturyugāntakarānilakaraṇamaviruddham evaṃ yadanyad apy anupapadyamānaṃ vāyos tadapi devatārūpatvenaiva samādheyam // 37
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Vāyu</s> is intended in the form of a deity; therefore, his role as the agent of destruction at the end of the four <s>yugas</s> on earth is not contradictory. Likewise, whatever else appears inexplicable regarding <s>Vāyu</s> should also be resolved through his nature as a deity. // 37

children.text: samprati sāmānyena punaḥ kupitākupitasya vāyoḥ svarūpamucyate sa hi bhagavānityādi // 38
children.translated_text: Now the nature of <s>Vāyu</s>, both in its aggravated and non-aggravated states, is stated in general terms, beginning with 'He is indeed the Blessed One,' etc. // 38
<s>Prabhava</s> means 'cause.' // 39
<s>Avyaya</s> means 'imperishable.' // 40
This connects with the following word '<s>bhūtānām</s>' (of beings). // 41
The distinctions such as <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), <s>Yama</s>, and others should be understood from the <s>Āgama</s> (scripture). // 42

children.text: sarvatantrāṇāṃ sarvakarmaṇāṃ tantraśabdaḥ karmavacano'pyasti yaduktaṃ vastistantrāṇāṃ karmaṇāmityarthaḥ // 43]
children.translated_text: Of all <s>tantras</s> — of all procedures; the word <s>tantra</s> is also used in the sense of procedure, as stated: '<s>vasti</s>-<s>tantras</s>' means 'of the procedures' — this is the meaning. // 43]

children.text: tacchrutvā vāyorvidavaco marīciruvāca yadyapyevam etat kimarthasyāsya vacane vijñāne vā sāmarthyamasti bhiṣagvidyāyāṃ bhiṣagvidyām adhikṛtyeyaṃ kathā pravṛtteti // Car_1,12.9
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of the knower of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Marīci</s> said: 'Even if this is so, what capacity does the statement or knowledge of this have in the science of medicine? This discussion has been undertaken with reference to the science of medicine.' // Car_1,12.9

children.text: vāyorvida uvāca bhiṣak pavanam atibalam atiparuṣam atiśīghrakāriṇam ātyayikaṃ cen nānuniśāmyet sahasā prakupitam atiprayataḥ kathamagre'bhirakṣitumabhidhāsyati prāgevainam atyayabhayāt vāyoryathārthā stutir api bhavatyārogyāya balavarṇavivṛddhaye varcasvitvāyopacayāya jñānopapattaye paramāyuḥprakarṣāya ceti // Car_1,12.10
children.translated_text: The knower of <s>Vāyu</s> said: 'If a physician does not carefully observe <s>Pavana</s> (Wind), which is exceedingly powerful, exceedingly harsh, exceedingly swift in action, and of an urgent nature, when it has suddenly become aggravated — being extremely vigilant — how will he be able to protect [the patient] further? Therefore, even the praise of <s>Vāyu</s> according to his true nature serves, out of fear of danger: for health, for the increase of strength and complexion, for vitality, for nourishment, for the attainment of knowledge, and for the greatest extension of lifespan.' // Car_1,12.10

children.text: marīciruvāca agnireva śarīre pittāntargataḥ kupitākupitaḥ śubhāśubhāni karoti tadyathā paktimapaktiṃ darśanamadarśanaṃ mātrāmātratvam ūṣmaṇaḥ prakṛtivikṛtivarṇau śauryaṃ bhayaṃ krodhaṃ harṣaṃ mohaṃ prasādam ityevamādīni cāparāṇi dvaṃdvānīti // Car_1,12.11
children.translated_text: <s>Marīci</s> said: '<s>Agni</s> (Fire) alone, residing within the body as <s>Pitta</s>, whether aggravated or not, produces auspicious and inauspicious [effects], namely: digestion and indigestion, vision and blindness, proper and improper degree of [bodily] heat, natural and abnormal complexion, courage and fear, anger and joy, delusion and clarity — and other such pairs of opposites.' // Car_1,12.11
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: pittāntargata iti vacanena śarīre jvālādiyuktavahniniṣedhena pittoṣmarūpasya vahneḥ sadbhāvaṃ darśayati na tu pittādabhedaṃ pitte nāgnimāndyasya grahaṇyadhyāye vakṣyamāṇatvāt tathā pittaharasya sarpiṣo'gnivardhanatvenoktatvāt // 1
children.translated_text: By saying 'residing within <s>Pitta</s>,' he shows the existence of fire in the form of the heat of <s>Pitta</s>, while negating fire with flames and the like in the body. But this does not mean non-difference from <s>Pitta</s>, since weakness of fire (<s>agnimāndya</s>) in <s>Pitta</s> will be stated in the chapter on <s>Grahaṇī</s>, and since ghee, which alleviates <s>Pitta</s>, is said to increase <s>Agni</s>. // 1

children.text: paktimapaktimiti avikṛtivikṛtibhedena pācakasyāgneḥ karma darśanādarśane netragatasyālocakasya ūṣmaṇo mātrāmātratvaṃ varṇabhedau ca tvaggatasya bhrājakasya bhayaśauryādayo hṛdayasthasya sādhakasya rañjakasya tu bahiḥsphuṭakāryādarśanād udāharaṇaṃ na kṛtam // 2]
children.translated_text: Digestion and indigestion are the functions of the digestive fire (<s>Pācaka</s>), through the distinction of normal and abnormal states. Vision and blindness belong to the <s>Ālocaka</s> [fire] located in the eyes. The proper and improper degree of heat and the distinctions of complexion belong to the <s>Bhrājaka</s> [fire] in the skin. Fear, courage, and the like belong to the <s>Sādhaka</s> [fire] in the heart. No example is given for the <s>Rañjaka</s> [fire], since its external manifest effects are not seen. // 2]

children.text: tacchrutvā marīcivacaḥ kāpya uvāca soma eva śarīre śleṣmāntargataḥ kupitākupitaḥ śubhāśubhāni karoti tadyathā dārḍhyaṃ śaithilyamupacayaṃ kārśyam utsāhamālasyaṃ vṛṣatāṃ klībatāṃ jñānamajñānaṃ buddhiṃ mohamevamādīni cāparāṇi dvaṃdvānīti // Car_1,12.12
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Marīci</s>'s words, <s>Kāpya</s> said: '<s>Soma</s> (Moon) alone, residing within the body as <s>Śleṣman</s> (Kapha), whether aggravated or not, produces auspicious and inauspicious [effects], namely: firmness and looseness, nourishment and emaciation, energy and laziness, virility and impotence, knowledge and ignorance, intelligence and delusion — and other such pairs of opposites.' // Car_1,12.12
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
<s>Soma</s> means the deity of water; alternatively, the moon. // 1]

children.text: tacchrutvā kāpyavaco bhagavān punarvasurātreya uvāca sarva eva bhavantaḥ samyag āhur anyatraikāntikavacanāt sarva eva khalu vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ prakṛtibhūtāḥ puruṣamavyāpannendriyaṃ balavarṇasukhopapannam āyuṣā mahatopapādayanti samyagevācaritā dharmārthakāmā iva niḥśreyasena mahatā puruṣamiha cāmuṣmiṃś ca loke vikṛtāstvenaṃ mahatā viparyayeṇopapādayanti kratavas traya iva vikṛtimāpannā lokamaśubhenopaghātakāla iti // Car_1,12.13
children.translated_text: Hearing <s>Kāpya</s>'s words, the Blessed <s>Punarvasu Ātreya</s> said: 'All of you have spoken correctly, except for your one-sided statements. Indeed, <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Śleṣman</s>, when in their natural state, endow a person with unimpaired senses, strength, complexion, happiness, and a long lifespan — just as the three aims of life — <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Artha</s>, and <s>Kāma</s> — when properly pursued, lead to the greatest good for a person both in this world and the next. But when vitiated, they bring about great adversity — like the three [ritual] fires when they become impure, which afflict the world with inauspiciousness until the time of destruction.' // Car_1,12.13

children.text: tadṛṣayaḥ sarva evānumenire vacanamātreyasya bhagavato'bhinananduś ceti // Car_1,12.14
children.translated_text: Thereupon all the sages agreed with the words of the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s> and applauded them. // Car_1,12.14
Having heard <s>Ātreya</s>'s words, all of them agreed;
the sages applauded, as the gods [applaud] the words of <s>Indra</s>. // Car_1,12.15

children.text: guṇāḥ ṣaḍ dvividho hetur vividhaṃ karma yat punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Six qualities, a twofold cause, and various actions further;

children.text: vāyoścaturvidhaṃ karma pṛthak ca kaphapittayoḥ // Car_1,12.16
children.translated_text: four kinds of action of <s>Vāyu</s>, and separately those of <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>. // Car_1,12.16
The views of the great sages and the view of <s>Punarvasu</s> —

children.text: kalākalīye vātasya tat sarvaṃ saṃprakāśitam // Car_1,12.17
children.translated_text: all that has been revealed in the [chapter called] <s>Kalākalīya</s> concerning <s>Vāta</s>. // Car_1,12.17
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>, 12
Now we shall expound the chapter called <s>Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya</s>. // Car_1,26.1
Thus indeed spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car_1,26.2
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

Having described one aspect of the beneficial and harmful, the <s>Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya</s>, which treats <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>vīrya</s> (potency), and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), is stated for the purpose of knowing the entirety of beneficial and harmful substances. // 1

children.text: tatrāpi vipākādīnāmapi rasenaiva prāyo lakṣaṇīyatvādrasaprakaraṇam ādau kṛtam // 2]
children.translated_text: Moreover, since <s>vipāka</s> and the rest are mostly to be understood through <s>rasa</s> alone, the section on <s>rasa</s> is presented first. // 2]
<s>Ātreya</s> and <s>Bhadrakāpya</s>, and <s>Śākunteya</s> likewise,
<s>Pūrṇākṣa</s> the <s>Maudgalya</s>, and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> the <s>Kauśika</s>, // Car_1,26.3

children.text: yaḥ kumāraśirā nāma bharadvājaḥ sa cānaghaḥ /
children.translated_text: and he who is named <s>Kumāraśirā</s>, the sinless son of <s>Bharadvāja</s>,

children.text: śrīmān vāyorvidaścaiva rājā matimatāṃ varaḥ // Car_1,26.4
children.translated_text: the illustrious knower of <s>Vāyu</s>, and the king, best of the intelligent, // Car_1,26.4
<s>Nimi</s> the king of <s>Videha</s>, and <s>Baḍiśa</s> of great wisdom,
and <s>Kāṅkāyana</s> the <s>Bāhlīka</s>, best of the physicians of <s>Bāhlīka</s> — // Car_1,26.5
these great sages, advanced in learning and age, masters of themselves,
assembled in the delightful forest of <s>Caitraratha</s>, desiring to deliberate. // Car_1,26.6
Of them, seated there, this meaningful discourse
took place — of those who knew the truth — on the determination of <s>rasa</s> and food. // Car_1,26.7
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
By establishing the preliminary objections (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) through the views of the sages, the final doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>) is established for the instruction of students. // 1

children.text: rasenāhāraviniścayo rasāhāraviniścayaḥ kiṃvā ayaṃ rasaviniścayaḥ tathā paraṃ cāto vipākānām ityādirāhāraviniścayaḥ // 2]
children.translated_text: 'The determination of food through <s>rasa</s>' (<s>rasāhāraviniścaya</s>) — or alternatively, 'this is the determination of <s>rasa</s>' and 'henceforth from <s>vipāka</s>, etc.' constitutes 'the determination of food.' // 2]

children.text:
eka eva rasa ityuvāca bhadrakāpyaḥ yaṃ pañcānām indriyārthānām anyatamaṃ jihvāvaiṣayikaṃ bhāvamācakṣate kuśalāḥ sa punarudakādananya iti /
dvau rasāv iti śākunteyo brāhmaṇaḥ chedanīya upaśamanīyaśceti /
trayo rasā iti pūrṇākṣo maudgalyaḥ chedanīyopaśamanīyasādhāraṇā iti /
catvāro rasā iti hiraṇyākṣaḥ kauśikaḥ svādurhitaśca svādur ahitaś cāsvādur hitaścāsvādur ahitaśceti /
pañca rasā iti kumāraśirā bharadvājaḥ bhaumaudakāgneyavāyavyāntarikṣāḥ /
children.translated_text:
'There is only one <s>rasa</s>,' said <s>Bhadrakāpya</s> — 'that which the learned call the one, among the objects of the five senses, which is the object of the tongue; and it is none other than water.'
'There are two <s>rasas</s>,' said <s>Śākunteya</s> the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — 'the depleting and the pacifying.'
'There are three <s>rasas</s>,' said <s>Pūrṇākṣa Maudgalya</s> — 'the depleting, the pacifying, and the common [to both].'
'There are four <s>rasas</s>,' said <s>Hiraṇyākṣa Kauśika</s> — 'the pleasant-beneficial, the pleasant-harmful, the unpleasant-beneficial, and the unpleasant-harmful.'
'There are five <s>rasas</s>,' said <s>Kumāraśirā Bhāradvāja</s> — 'the earthy, the watery, the fiery, the airy, and the ethereal.'
'There are six <s>rasas</s>,' said the royal sage, the knower of <s>Vāyu</s> — 'the heavy, the light, the cold, the hot, the unctuous, and the dry.'
'There are seven <s>rasas</s>,' said <s>Nimi</s> of <s>Videha</s> — 'sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent, and alkaline.'
'There are eight <s>rasas</s>,' said <s>Baḍiśa Dhāmārgava</s> — 'sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent, alkaline, and indeterminate.'

children.text: aparisaṃkhyeyā rasā iti kāṅkāyano vāhlīkabhiṣak āśrayaguṇakarmasaṃsvādaviśeṣāṇām aparisaṃkhyeyatvāt // Car_1,26.8
children.translated_text: 'The <s>rasas</s> are innumerable,' said <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, the physician of <s>Bāhlīka</s> — 'because the distinctions of substrate, quality, action, and flavor are innumerable.' // Car_1,26.8
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
'There is only one' and so on. // 1
'Of the sense-objects' — the genitive is in the partitive sense. // 2

children.text: anyatamam iti ekam anyaśabdo hy ayamekavacanaḥ yathānyo dakṣiṇena gato 'nya uttareṇa eka ityarthaḥ tam appratyayaśca svārthikaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: '<s>Anyatama</s>' means 'one'; the word <s>anya</s> here is singular in number, as in 'one went south, another went north' — meaning 'one.' The suffix <s>-tama</s> is used in its own sense [without intensifying]. // 3
'Object of the tongue' means 'graspable by the tongue.' // 4
Even the absence of <s>rasa</s> is perceived by the tongue; hence he says '<s>bhāva</s>' (positive entity). // 5

children.text: udakādananya iti rasodakayor ekatvakhyāpanārthaṃ pūrvapakṣatvād aduṣṭam // 6
children.translated_text: 'None other than water' — this is a preliminary objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) for proclaiming the identity of <s>rasa</s> and water, and being a <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, it is not flawed. // 6
And this <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> follows the doctrine of <s>Kapila</s>. // 7

children.text: hi rasatanmātraṃ gandhatanmātram ityādivacanena guṇāvyatiriktaṃ dravyamiti bruvate // 8
children.translated_text: For they say — by statements such as 'the <s>tanmātra</s> of <s>rasa</s>, the <s>tanmātra</s> of smell,' etc. — that substance is non-different from quality. // 8
'Depleting' means causing reduction (<s>apatarpaṇa</s>). // 9
'Pacifying' means nourishing (<s>bṛṃhaṇa</s>). // 10

children.text: sādhāraṇa ityāgneyasaumyasāmānyād ubhayor api laṅghanabṛṃhaṇayoḥ kartā parasparavirodhādakartā vā // 11
children.translated_text: 'Common' means possessing common effects — due to the generality of fiery and watery [natures], it is the agent of both reduction and nourishment, or the non-agent of both, due to mutual opposition. // 11

children.text: svāduriti abhīṣṭaḥ hita iti āyatāv anapakārī // 12
children.translated_text: 'Pleasant' means desired; 'beneficial' means not causing harm over time. // 12

children.text: āśrīyata ityāśrayo dravyaṃ guṇāḥ snigdhagurvādayaḥ karma dhātuvardhanakṣapaṇādi saṃsvādaḥ rasānām avāntarabhedaḥ eṣāṃ viśeṣāṇāṃ bhedānām ityarthaḥ // 13
children.translated_text: That which is depended upon (<s>āśrīyate</s>) is the substrate (<s>āśraya</s>), i.e., the substance (<s>dravya</s>). The qualities are unctuousness, heaviness, and the like. The action is the increase or diminution of <s>dhātus</s>. The flavor (<s>saṃsvāda</s>) is the sub-distinction of <s>rasas</s>. 'Of the distinctions of these' means 'of their varieties' — this is the meaning. // 13

children.text: tatra dravyabhedād ādhārabhedenāśritasyāpi rasasya bhedo bhavati āśrayo hi kāraṇaṃ kāraṇabhedācca kāryabhedo 'vaśyaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ // 14
children.translated_text: There, due to the difference of substance, i.e., due to the difference of substrate, there is a difference even in <s>rasa</s> which depends [on the substrate]. For the substrate is the cause, and from the difference of the cause, there necessarily arises a difference in the effect — this is the meaning. // 14
The distinctions of qualities such as heaviness, etc., and the distinctions of actions are also produced by <s>rasa</s> alone. // 15

children.text: tataś ca kāryabhedādavaśyaṃ kāraṇabheda iti pūrvapakṣābhiprāyaḥ // 16
children.translated_text: And therefore, from the difference of effects, there must necessarily be a difference of causes — this is the intention of the preliminary objection. // 16

children.text: saṃsvādabhedastu ekasyām api madhurajātāv ikṣukṣīraguḍādigataḥ pratyakṣameva bhedo dṛśyate sa tu saṃsvādabhedaḥ svasaṃvedya eva yaduktam ikṣukṣīraguḍādīnāṃ mādhuryasyāntaraṃ mahat // 17
children.translated_text: But the distinction of flavor: even within the single class of sweet, one directly perceives a distinction in the flavor of sugarcane, milk, <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), and the like. That distinction of flavor is self-evident, as stated: 'Great is the internal difference of sweetness among sugarcane, milk, jaggery, and the like; // 17
yet that distinction cannot be described even by <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of speech).' // 18]

children.text: ṣaḍeva rasā ityuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ punarvasuḥ madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭutiktakaṣāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There are exactly six <s>rasas</s>,' said the Blessed <s>Ātreya Punarvasu</s> — 'sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, and astringent.'

children.text: teṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ rasānāṃ yonirudakaṃ chedanopaśamane dve karmaṇī tayor miśrībhāvāt sādhāraṇatvaṃ svādvasvādutā bhaktiḥ hitāhitau prabhāvau pañcamahābhūtavikārās tv āśrayāḥ prakṛtivikṛtivicāradeśakālavaśāḥ teṣvāśrayeṣu dravyasaṃjñakeṣu guṇā gurulaghuśītoṣṇasnigdharūkṣādyāḥ kṣaraṇāt kṣāraḥ nāsau rasaḥ dravyaṃ tadanekarasasamutpannam anekarasaṃ kaṭukalavaṇabhūyiṣṭham anekendriyārthasamanvitaṃ karaṇābhinirvṛttam avyaktībhāvastu khalu rasānāṃ prakṛtau bhavatyanurase 'nurasasamanvite vā dravye aparisaṃkhyeyatvaṃ punas teṣām āśrayādīnāṃ bhāvānāṃ viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvānna yuktam ekaiko 'pi hy eṣām āśrayādīnāṃ bhāvānāṃ viśeṣān āśrayate viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt na ca tasmād anyatvam upapadyate parasārasaṃsṛṣṭabhūyiṣṭhatvānna caiṣām abhinirvṛtter guṇaprakṛtīnām aparisaṃkhyeyatvaṃ bhavati tasmānna saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ rasānāṃ karmopadiśanti buddhimantaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Of those six <s>rasas</s>, the source (<s>yoni</s>) is water. Depleting and pacifying are the two actions; from their combination arises the common [effect]. Pleasant and unpleasant are [matters of] preference. Beneficial and harmful are the potencies (<s>prabhāva</s>). The substrates are modifications of the five great elements, subject to the considerations of natural state and altered state, place, and time. In those substrates, called substances (<s>dravya</s>), the qualities are heaviness, lightness, coldness, hotness, unctuousness, dryness, and the like. <s>Kṣāra</s> (alkaline) corrodes — it is not a <s>rasa</s>; it is a substance produced from many <s>rasas</s>, possessing many <s>rasas</s>, predominantly pungent and salty, endowed with the objects of many senses, and produced through [artificial] processing. But the indeterminate (<s>avyakta</s>) is indeed what belongs to the natural state of <s>rasas</s> — in a subordinate <s>rasa</s> or in a substance possessing a subordinate <s>rasa</s>. And their innumerability — based on the innumerability of the distinctions of substrates and other factors — is not valid; for each <s>rasa</s> takes on the distinctions of substrates and other factors due to the innumerability of those distinctions, and one cannot therefore establish its otherness [from the six], since they are mixed and predominated by one another. Nor does the innumerability of the qualities whose nature is [to arise from <s>rasas</s>] occur [independently]. Therefore the wise do not teach the action of mixed <s>rasas</s>.'

children.text: taccaiva kāraṇamapekṣamāṇāḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ rasānāṃ paraspareṇāsaṃsṛṣṭānāṃ lakṣaṇapṛthaktvam upadekṣyāmaḥ // Car_1,26.9
children.translated_text: 'And for that very reason, looking to the causes, we shall teach the distinct characteristics of the six <s>rasas</s>, unmixed with one another.' // Car_1,26.9
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
He states the final doctrine through the words of <s>Punarvasu</s>, beginning with 'exactly six,' etc. // 1
He addresses the position of the unity of <s>rasa</s>, etc., stated in the preliminary objections, beginning with 'Of those six,' etc. // 2

children.text: yoniḥ ādhārakāraṇaṃ kāryakāraṇayośca bhedāt siddha udakādrasabhedaḥ pratyakṣa eveti bhāvaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: <s>Yoni</s> means the foundational cause (<s>ādhārakāraṇa</s>); and since cause and effect are different, the difference of <s>rasa</s> from water is established — it is directly perceived — this is the purport. // 3

children.text: kṣitivyatiriktam udakameva yathā rasayonistathā rasanārtho rasastasya ityādau vivṛtameva dīrghaṃjīvitīye // 4
children.translated_text: Water, distinct from earth, is the source of <s>rasa</s> — just as the meaning of <s>rasa</s> and its sense-object has already been explained in the [chapter] <s>Dīrghañjīvitīya</s>. // 4

children.text: tayormiśrībhāvāditi karmaṇor amūrtayor miśrībhāvānupapattau tadādhārayor dravyayor miśrībhāvāditi boddhavyam // 5
children.translated_text: 'From their combination' — since the combination of actions, which are formless, is impossible, it should be understood as 'from the combination of the substances that are their substrates.' // 5
'Common' means having a connection with common effects. // 6
<s>Bhakti</s> means 'desire' or 'preference.' // 7

children.text: tena yo yamicchati sa tasya svādurasvāduritara iti puruṣāpekṣau dharmau na rasabhedakāryāv ityarthaḥ // 8
children.translated_text: Therefore, he who desires a particular [taste] — for him it is pleasant; for another it is unpleasant — thus these two properties depend on the person, and are not [properties] that differentiate <s>rasa</s> — this is the meaning. // 8

children.text: pañcamahābhūtetyādau tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe tena āśrayā eva na rasā ityarthaḥ // 9
children.translated_text: In the passage beginning with 'five great elements,' etc., the word <s>tu</s> is used in the restrictive sense; therefore [the meaning is that] the substrates alone [vary], not the <s>rasas</s>. // 9

children.text: kiṃbhūtā bhaumādayo bhūtavikārā āśrayā ityāha prakṛtivikṛtivicāradeśakālavaśā iti vaśaśabdo 'dhīnārthaḥ sa ca prakṛtyādibhiḥ pratyekaṃ yojyaḥ // 10
children.translated_text: What kind are the earthy and other modifications of the elements [that serve as] substrates? — he answers with 'subject to the considerations of natural state and altered state, place, and time.' The word <s>vaśa</s> means 'dependent upon'; and it should be connected individually with natural state (<s>prakṛti</s>) and the rest. // 10

children.text: tatra prakṛtivaśā yathā mudgāḥ kaṣāyā madhurāśca santaḥ prakṛtyā laghavaḥ etaddhi lāghavaṃ na rasavaśaṃ tathāhi sati kaṣāyamadhuratvād gurutvaṃ syāt vikṛtivaśaṃ ca vrīher lājānāṃ laghutvaṃ tathā saktusiddhapiṇḍakānāṃ ca gurutvaṃ vicāraṇā vicāro dravyāntarasaṃyoga ityarthaḥ tena vicāraṇāvaśaṃ yathā madhusarpiṣī saṃyukte viṣaṃ tathā viṣaṃ cāgadasaṃyuktaṃ svakāryavyatiriktakāryakāri deśo dvividho bhūmir āturaśca tatra bhūmau śvetakāpotī valmīkādhirūḍhā viṣaharī tathā himavati bheṣajāni mahāguṇāni bhavanti śarīradeśe yathā sakthimāṃsād gurutaraṃ skandhakroḍaśiraspadām ityādi kālavaśaṃ tu yathā mūlakamadhikṛtyoktaṃ tadbālaṃ doṣaharaṃ vṛddhaṃ tridoṣaṃ tathā yathartupuṣpaphalam ādadīta ityādi // 11
children.translated_text: Among those, [lightness] due to nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) is as follows: <s>mudgas</s> (green gram), being astringent and sweet, are light by nature — this lightness is not due to taste. For if [lightness were] taste-dependent, then because of being astringent and sweet, there would be heaviness. And [lightness] due to modification (<s>vikṛti</s>): the lightness of parched rice (<s>lājas</s>) [made] from rice; likewise the heaviness of cakes prepared from barley-flour. 'Examination' (<s>vicāraṇā</s>) means investigation, i.e., combination with another substance. Thus, [change] due to examination: as honey and ghee when combined [become] poison; likewise poison combined with an antidote acts contrary to its own [normal] effect. 'Region' (<s>deśa</s>) is twofold: the land and the patient. Of these, regarding land: <s>śvetakāpotī</s> growing upon an anthill is poison-destroying. Likewise, in the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas), medicines are of great potency. Regarding the bodily region: thigh-meat is heavier than that of the shoulder, chest, head, and feet — and so on. And [change] due to time (<s>kāla</s>): as stated regarding the radish — 'when young it destroys <s>doṣas</s>; when old it [aggravates] all three <s>doṣas</s>.' Likewise: 'one should gather seasonal flowers and fruits' — and so on. // 11

children.text: atra caikaprakaraṇoktā ye 'nuktās te cakārāt svabhāvādiṣvevāntarbhāvanīyāḥ // 12
children.translated_text: And here, those [factors] mentioned in one section [but] not mentioned [in this list] should be included within 'nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>) and the other [categories] by means of the word 'ca' (and). // 12

children.text: yaduktaṃ caraḥ śarīrāvayavāḥ svabhāvo dhātavaḥ kriyāḥ // 13
children.translated_text: As has been stated: 'locomotion, bodily parts, nature, <s>dhātus</s> (tissues), actions, // 13

children.text: liṅgaṃ pramāṇaṃ saṃskāro mātrā cāsmin parīkṣyate iti // 14
children.translated_text: signs, measure, processing, and quantity — these are to be examined in this [context].' // 14

children.text: tatra caraśarīrāvayavadhātūnāṃ deśena grahaṇaṃ mātrā vicāre praviśati śeṣaṃ svabhāve tathā rasavimāne vakṣyamāṇaṃ cātrāpraviṣṭam āhāraviśeṣāyatanam antarbhāvanīyaṃ yathāsambhavam // 15
children.translated_text: Among these, locomotion, bodily parts, and <s>dhātus</s> are subsumed under 'region' (<s>deśa</s>); 'quantity' (<s>mātrā</s>) falls within 'examination' (<s>vicāra</s>); the remainder falls within 'nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>). And what will be stated in the <s>Rasavimāna</s> that does not fall here — the 'special domain of food' (<s>āhāraviśeṣāyatana</s>) — should be included as appropriate. // 15

children.text: snigdharūkṣādyā ityatrādigrahaṇenānuktā api tīkṣṇamṛdvādayo na rasāḥ kiṃtu dravyaguṇāḥ pṛthageveti darśayati // 16
children.translated_text: By the word 'ādi' (etc.) in 'unctuous, dry, etc.' (<s>snigdha-rūkṣa-ādi</s>), it is shown that even unmentioned [qualities] like sharp (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>), mild (<s>mṛdu</s>), etc. are not tastes but rather qualities of substances — separately [from taste]. // 16

children.text: kṣaraṇāt adhogamanakriyāyogāt kṣāro dravyaṃ nāsau rasaḥ rasasya hi niṣkriyasya kriyānupapannetyarthaḥ // 17
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣāra</s> (alkali) — from 'kṣaraṇa' meaning the action of flowing downward — is a substance, not a taste. For taste, being without action (<s>niṣkriya</s>), cannot be connected with action — this is the meaning. // 17

children.text: kṣaraṇaṃ ca kṣārasya pānīyayuktasyādhogamanena vadanti hi laukikāḥ kṣāraṃ srāvayāmaḥ iti śāstraṃ ca chittvā chittvāśayāt kṣāraḥ kṣaratvāt kṣārayatyadhaḥ iti // 18
children.translated_text: And the 'flowing' (<s>kṣaraṇa</s>) of <s>kṣāra</s> is [understood as] its downward movement when combined with water. For people in common usage say: 'we filter the alkali.' And the treatise [says]: 'having cut and cut from the receptacle, the alkali flows; because it flows, it makes [things] flow downward.' // 18

children.text: hetvantaram āha dravyaṃ tadanekarasotpannam iti anekarasebhyo muṣkakāpāmārgādibhya utpannam anekarasotpannaṃ yataś cānekarasotpannam ata evānekarasaṃ kāraṇaguṇānuvidhāyitvāt kāryaguṇasyeti bhāvaḥ // 19
children.translated_text: He states another reason: 'it is a substance, produced from multiple tastes.' Produced from multiple-tasted [substances] such as <s>muṣkaka</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, etc. — [it is called] 'produced from multiple tastes.' And since it is produced from multiple tastes, therefore it has multiple tastes — because the qualities of the effect conform to the qualities of the cause — this is the meaning. // 19
He states the very fact of its multiple-tastedness: 'predominantly pungent and salty.' // 20
By the word 'predominantly' (<s>bhūyiṣṭha</s>) he shows that there is a connection with other non-predominant tastes. // 21
He states another reason: 'endowed with multiple sense-objects.' // 22

children.text: kṣāro hi sparśena gandhena cānvitaḥ tena dravyaṃ rase hi guṇe na sparśo nāpi gandha iti bhāvaḥ // 23
children.translated_text: For <s>kṣāra</s> is endowed with touch and smell. Therefore it is a substance — for in taste, which is a quality, there is neither touch nor smell — this is the meaning. // 23

children.text: hetvantaramāha karaṇābhinirvṛttamiti karaṇena bhasmaparisrāvaṇādinābhinirvṛttaṃ kṛtam ityarthaḥ na raso 'nena prakāreṇa kriyata iti bhāvaḥ // 24
children.translated_text: He states another reason: 'produced by means of an instrument.' Produced — i.e., made — by means of an instrument such as filtering of ashes and the like — this is the meaning. A taste is not made in this manner — this is the meaning. // 24
He refutes the view of 'indistinct taste' (<s>avyaktarasa</s>): 'indistinctness' (<s>avyaktībhāva</s>) etc. // 25

children.text: avyaktībhāva ityabhūtatadbhāve cvipratyayena rasānāṃ madhurādīnāṃ vyaktānām eva kvacidādhāre 'vyaktatvaṃ nānyo madhurādibhyo 'vyaktarasa ityarthaḥ // 26
children.translated_text: 'Indistinctness' (<s>avyaktībhāva</s>) — by the <s>cvi</s>-suffix in the sense of 'becoming what it was not before' — means that the distinct [tastes] sweet and so on become indistinct in a certain substrate; there is no 'indistinct taste' other than sweet etc. — this is the meaning. // 26
'Of tastes' (<s>rasānām</s>) means of the six — sweet and so on. // 27
'In the original' (<s>prakṛtau</s>) etc. // 28
'In the original' (<s>prakṛtau</s>) means in the cause — i.e., in water. // 29

children.text: avyaktatvaṃ ca rasasāmānyamātropalabdhir madhurādiviśeṣaśūnyā sā ca jale bhavati yata uktaṃ jalaguṇakathane suśrute vyaktarasatā rasadoṣaḥ iti ihāpi ca avyaktarasaṃ ca iti vakṣyati loke'pi cāvyaktarasaṃ dravyamāsvādya vaktāro vadanti jalasyevāsya raso na kaścin madhurādir vyakta iti // 30
children.translated_text: And 'indistinctness' means the apprehension of mere taste-in-general, devoid of specific [distinctions] like sweet etc. — and this occurs in water. As stated in <s>Suśruta</s> in the section on the qualities of water: 'distinctness of taste is a fault of taste.' And here too it will be said: 'and of indistinct taste.' In common usage too, people tasting a substance of indistinct taste say: 'its taste is like water — no particular [taste] such as sweet etc. is distinct.' // 30
And the non-apprehension of specific [tastes] like sweet etc. is due to their not having arisen. // 31

children.text: yathā dūrād avijñāyamānaviśeṣavarṇe vastuni rūpasāmānyapratītir bhavati na śuklatvādiviśeṣabuddhiḥ tathānurase 'vyaktībhāvo bhavati pradhānaṃ vyaktaṃ rasamanugato 'vyaktatvenetyanurasaḥ yathā veṇuyave madhure kaṣāyo 'nurasaḥ // 32
children.translated_text: Just as when the specific color of an object is not discernible from a distance, there is a cognition of mere color-in-general but not a specific cognition of whiteness etc. — so in a secondary taste (<s>anurasa</s>), there is indistinctness. The predominant [taste] is distinct; the one that follows it has indistinctness — hence [it is called] <s>anurasa</s> (secondary taste). As in bamboo-rice (<s>veṇuyava</s>), which is sweet, astringent is the secondary taste. // 32

children.text: yaduktaṃ rūkṣaḥ kaṣāyānuraso madhuraḥ kaphapittahā iti // 33
children.translated_text: As has been stated: 'dry, with astringent as secondary taste, sweet, it destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.' // 33

children.text: anurasasamanvita iti sarvānurasayukte yathā viṣe vacanaṃ hi uṣṇam anirdeśyarasam ityādi // 34
children.translated_text: 'Endowed with secondary taste' (<s>anurasasamanvita</s>) means endowed with all secondary tastes, as the statement about poison: 'hot, of indescribable taste' and so on. // 34

children.text: kiṃvā aṇurasasamanvite iti pāṭhas tena aṇurasenaikena maricena śarkarāpānake kaṭutvam avyaktaṃ syāt // 35
children.translated_text: Or the reading is 'endowed with minute taste' (<s>aṇurasamanvite</s>), whereby with a single minute [quantity of] pepper in a sugar-drink, pungency would be indistinct. // 35
He refutes the view of 'innumerability': 'not innumerable' (<s>aparī</s>) etc. // 36

children.text: teṣāmiti rasānām aparisaṃkhyeyatvaṃ na yuktam āśrayādīnāṃ bhāvānāmiti āśrayaguṇakarmasaṃsvādānām viśeṣāparisaṃkhyeyatvāditi āśrayādibhedasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt // 37
children.translated_text: The innumerability of tastes is not justified because of the [supposed] innumerability of their substrates and other entities (<s>bhāvas</s>) — i.e., because of the innumerability of the distinctions among substrate, quality, action, and flavor (<s>āśrayaguṇakarmasaṃsvāda</s>). // 37
Here he states the reason: 'even a single one' etc. // 38

children.text: eṣāmāśrayaguṇakarmasaṃsvādānāṃ viśeṣān ekaiko 'pi madhurādir āśrayate na ca tasmād āśrayādibhedād anyatvam āśritasya madhurāder bhavati // 39
children.translated_text: Among these — substrate, quality, action, and flavor — even a single [taste] such as sweet etc. resides in [various] distinctions. Yet from that distinction of substrate etc., no otherness of the sweet etc. that resides [therein] arises. // 39

children.text: evaṃ manyate yadyapi śālimudgaghṛtakṣīrādayo madhurasyāśrayā bhinnāḥ tathāpi tatra madhuratvajātyākrānta eka eva raso bhavati balākākṣīrakārpāsādiṣu śuklavarṇa iva // 40
children.translated_text: The view is thus: although the substrates of sweet — rice, green gram, ghee, milk, etc. — are different, nevertheless what is there is one single taste, pervaded by the universal 'sweetness' — like the white color in cranes, milk, cotton, etc. // 40

children.text: tathā guṇānāṃ gurupicchilasnigdhādīnāmanyatve 'pi karmaṇāṃ vā rasādivardhanāyurjananavarṇakaratvādīnāṃ bhinnatve satyapi na madhurarasasyānyatvaṃ yata eka eva madhuras tattadguṇayukto bhavati tatkarmakārī ceti ko virodhaḥ // 41
children.translated_text: Likewise, even though qualities such as heaviness, sliminess, unctuousness, etc. differ, or even though actions such as increasing taste, generating longevity, producing complexion, etc. differ — there is no otherness of the sweet taste, because the one sweet [taste] possesses those respective qualities and performs those actions. So what contradiction is there? // 41

children.text: tathā madhurasyāvāntarāsvādabhede 'pi madhuratvajātyanatikramaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇāvāntarabhede yathā kṛṣṇatvānatikramaḥ // 42
children.translated_text: Likewise, even though there is difference in the sub-varieties of flavor within sweet, there is no transgression of the universal 'sweetness' — just as in the sub-varieties of black color, there is no transgression of blackness. // 42

children.text: nanu maivaṃ bhavatv aparisaṃkhyeyatvaṃ rasānāṃ parasparasaṃyogāt tu ya āsvādaviśeṣaḥ sa kāryaviśeṣakaro 'pi na hi yanmadhurāmlena kriyate tanmadhureṇa vāmlena vā śakyam atastena parasparasaṃyogenāparisaṃkhyeyatvaṃ bhaviṣyatītyāha parasparetyādi // 43
children.translated_text: Objection: Let it not be that there is innumerability of tastes [in themselves], but there is a specific flavor from mutual combination [of tastes], and that is productive of specific effects. For what is done by sweet-and-sour [combined] cannot be done by sweet alone or by sour alone. Therefore, through mutual combination there would be innumerability — to this he says 'mutual' (<s>paraspara</s>) etc. // 43

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭam iti bhāve ktaḥ tena parasparasaṃsargabhūyiṣṭhatvād eṣāṃ madhurādīnām abhinirvṛtterna guṇaprakṛtīnām asaṃkhyeyatvam iti yojanā ayamarthaḥ yadyapi rasāḥ parasparasaṃsargeṇātibhūyasā yuktāḥ santo 'bhinirvṛttā dvirasādau dravye bhavanti tathāpi na teṣāṃ guṇā gurulaghvādayaḥ prakṛtayo vā madhurādīnāṃ yā yā āyuṣyatvarasābhivardhakatvādyās tā asaṃkhyeyā bhavanti kiṃtu ya eva madhurādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ guṇāḥ prakṛtayaśca uddiṣṭāsta eva miśrā bhavanti // 44
children.translated_text: 'Combined' (<s>saṃsṛṣṭam</s>) — the <s>kta</s>-suffix in the sense of the state [of being combined]. Thus: although these sweet etc. [tastes] are produced in great abundance through mutual combination, being present in dual-taste etc. substances, nevertheless their qualities (heaviness, lightness, etc.) and their natural properties (those of sweet etc., such as promoting longevity, increasing <s>rasa</s>, etc.) do not become innumerable; rather, the very qualities and natural properties that are enumerated for sweet etc. individually — those same ones exist in the mixture. // 44

children.text: kiṃvā guṇaprakṛtīnāmiti madhurādiṣaḍguṇasvarūpāṇām ityarthaḥ tena rasasya rasāntarasaṃsarge doṣāṇāmiva doṣāntarasaṃsarge rasānāṃ nāparisaṃkhyeyatvam ityarthaḥ // 45
children.translated_text: Or, 'of qualities and natures' (<s>guṇaprakṛtīnām</s>) means of the essential nature of the six qualities sweet etc. Thus: just as in the combination of one <s>doṣa</s> with another <s>doṣa</s>, the <s>doṣas</s> do not become innumerable, so too tastes [do not become innumerable] when combined with other tastes. // 45

children.text: prakṛtiśabdena karma vocyate tena guṇakarmaṇām ityarthaḥ // 46
children.translated_text: By the word 'nature' (<s>prakṛti</s>), action is meant; thus the meaning is 'of qualities and actions.' // 46
The sub-variety of flavor within sweet etc. should also be understood as produced by mutual combination. // 47

children.text: yata eva heto rasānāṃ saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ nānye guṇakarmaṇī bhavataḥ ata eva saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ rasānāṃ pṛthakkarma śāstrāntare 'pi noktam ityāha tasmād ityādi // 48
children.translated_text: Because of this very reason — that the qualities and actions of combined tastes are not different — therefore, even in other treatises, the separate action of combined tastes has not been stated. To this he says 'therefore' (<s>tasmāt</s>) etc. // 48

children.text: karmaśabdeneha gauravalāghavādikārakā gurutvādayo rasaraktādijananādayaś cāpi boddhavyāḥ // 49
children.translated_text: By the word 'action' (<s>karma</s>) here, one should understand the qualities of heaviness, lightness, etc. that produce effects, as well as [actions such as] generating blood, <s>rasa</s>, etc. // 49

children.text: na kevalam anyaśāstrakārai rasānāṃ saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ karma nopadiṣṭaṃ kiṃtu vayamapi nopadekṣyāma ityāha taccaivetyādi // 50
children.translated_text: Not only have other treatise-makers not taught the action of combined tastes, but we too shall not teach it — to this he says 'that very same' (<s>taccaiva</s>) etc. // 50
'That very same is the reason' — meaning that even in mutual combination, tastes do not have additional qualities or actions. // 51
'Separateness by definition' means the separateness of the definition. // 52

children.text: tatra lakṣyate yena tallakṣaṇam atastu madhuro rasaḥ ityādinā granthena tathā snehanaprīṇanahlādana ityādinā ca yadvācyaṃ tat sarvaṃ gṛhyate // 53
children.translated_text: There, 'definition' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) is that by which [something] is defined. Thus, by the text 'sweet taste is...' etc. and by 'unctifying, satisfying, gladdening' etc. — all that is to be stated is included. // 53

children.text: kiṃvā lakṣaṇaśabdena madhuro rasa ityādigranthavācyaṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate pṛthaktvaṃ ca rasabhedajñānārthaṃ yad vakṣyati snehanaprīṇana ityādi tad gṛhyate // 54]
children.translated_text: Or, by the word 'definition,' the definition expressed by the text 'sweet taste is...' etc. is meant; and 'separateness' — what will be stated for the purpose of knowing the distinction of tastes, such as 'unctifying, satisfying' etc. — that is included. // 54]

children.text: agre tu tāvad dravyabhedam abhipretya kiṃcid abhidhāsyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: But first, intending [to discuss] the distinction of substances, we shall state something.

children.text: sarvaṃ dravyaṃ pāñcabhautikamasminnarthe taccetanāvadacenaṃ ca tasya guṇāḥ śabdādayo gurvādayaś ca dravāntāḥ karma pañcavidhamuktaṃ vamanādi // Car_1,26.10
children.translated_text: All substance is composed of the five elements (<s>pāñcabhautika</s>). In this regard, that [substance is] either sentient or insentient. Its qualities are sound (<s>śabda</s>) and the rest, as well as heaviness (<s>guru</s>) and the rest up to fluidity (<s>drava</s>). Action is fivefold, as stated — emesis and the rest. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.10
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'But first' etc.

children.text: raseṣu vācyeṣu dravyabhedam abhipretya pratipādanīyatayā parigṛhya rasānāṃ dravyajñānādhīnajñānatvād dravyābhidhānam agre kṛtam ityarthaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: While tastes are [yet] to be discussed, intending the distinction of substances — i.e., having accepted [it] as requiring exposition — because the knowledge of tastes depends on the knowledge of substances, the discussion of substances has been placed first — this is the meaning. // 1

children.text: kiṃciditi āyurvedopayogidravyasvarūpaṃ na sarvam aprasaṅgadoṣād iti bhāvaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'Something' (<s>kiṃcit</s>) — [means only] the essential nature of substance relevant to <s>Āyurveda</s>, not everything, lest there be the fault of irrelevance — this is the meaning. // 2
'All substance' means substance [considered] as effect (<s>kārya-dravya</s>). // 3
'In this regard' (<s>asminn arthe</s>) — in this section (<s>prakaraṇa</s>). // 4

children.text: dravāntā iti vacanena pūrvoktān viṃśatiguṇān āha // 5
children.translated_text: By the expression 'up to fluidity' (<s>dravānta</s>), he refers to the twenty qualities previously stated. // 5

children.text: atra ca paratvāparatvādīnām ihānabhidhānena cikitsāyāṃ paratvādīnām aprādhānyaṃ darśayati ye 'pi tatrāpi yuktisaṃyogaparimāṇasaṃskārābhyāsā atyarthacikitsopayogino 'pi na te pārthivādidravyāṇāṃ śabdādivat sāṃsiddhikāḥ kiṃ tarhy ādheyāḥ ata iha naisargikaguṇakathane noktāḥ // 6
children.translated_text: And here, by not mentioning 'superiority' (<s>paratva</s>), 'inferiority' (<s>aparatva</s>), and the like here, he shows that in medical treatment, <s>paratva</s> etc. are not predominant. Even those [factors] like reasoning (<s>yukti</s>), combination (<s>saṃyoga</s>), measure (<s>parimāṇa</s>), processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and habituation (<s>abhyāsa</s>), though very useful in treatment, are not innate (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>) to earthy etc. substances in the way sound etc. are, but rather superimposed (<s>ādheya</s>). Therefore they are not mentioned here in the discussion of natural qualities. // 6
'As stated' — in the <s>Apāmārgatanḍulīya</s> [chapter]. // 7
And this is stated as predominant; therefore <s>bṛṃhaṇa</s> (nourishment) etc. should also be understood. // 8]

children.text: tatra dravyāṇi gurukharakaṭhinamandasthiraviśadasāndrasthūlagandhaguṇabahulāni pārthivāni tānyupacayasaṃghātagauravasthairyakarāṇi dravasnigdhaśītamandamṛdupicchilarasaguṇabahulāny āpyāni tāny upakledasnehabandhaviṣyandamārdavaprahlādakarāṇi uṣṇatīkṣṇasūkṣmalaghurūkṣaviśadarūpaguṇabahulāny āgneyāni tāni dāhapākaprabhāprakāśavarṇakarāṇi laghuśītarūkṣakharaviśadasūkṣmasparśaguṇabahulāni vāyavyāni tāni raukṣyaglānivicāravaiśadyalāghavakarāṇi mṛdulaghusūkṣmaślakṣṇaśabdaguṇabahulāny ākāśātmakāni tāni mārdavasauṣiryalāghavakarāṇi // Car_1,26.11
children.translated_text: Among those, substances that are predominantly earthy (<s>pārthiva</s>) are rich in the qualities: heavy, rough, hard, slow, stable, clear, dense, gross, and smell. They produce accumulation, compactness, heaviness, and stability. Substances that are predominantly watery (<s>āpya</s>) are rich in the qualities: fluid, unctuous, cold, slow, soft, slimy, and taste. They produce moistening, unctuousness, binding, flowing, softening, and refreshment. Substances that are predominantly fiery (<s>āgneya</s>) are rich in the qualities: hot, sharp, subtle, light, dry, clear, and color/form. They produce burning, digestion, luster, illumination, and complexion. Substances that are predominantly airy (<s>vāyavya</s>) are rich in the qualities: light, cold, dry, rough, clear, subtle, and touch. They produce dryness, weariness, movement, clarity, and lightness. Substances that are predominantly ethereal (<s>ākāśātmaka</s>) are rich in the qualities: soft, light, subtle, smooth, and sound. They produce softness, porosity, and lightness. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.11
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: bahulaśabdo gurvādibhiḥ pratyekaṃ sambadhyate kiṃvā gandhenaiva yato gandhaguṇabahulā pṛthivyeva bhavati ata eva dravyāntaralakṣaṇe 'pi vaiśeṣikaguṇo 'nta eva paṭhyate rasaguṇabahulāni ityādi tena tatrāpi rasādibhir eva bahulaśabdo yojyaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: The word 'predominantly' (<s>bahula</s>) is connected with each [quality] individually — heavy etc. Or, [it connects] with smell alone, since only earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is predominantly characterized by the quality of smell. For this very reason, even in the definition of other substances, the distinctive (<s>vaiśeṣika</s>) quality is read at the end — 'predominantly [rich in] taste-quality' etc. Thus, there too the word 'predominantly' (<s>bahula</s>) should be connected with taste etc. alone. // 1
Although all effect-substances are composed of the five elements, one should understand [their classification as] earthy etc. by the preponderance of earth etc. // 2
'Compactness' (<s>saṃghāta</s>) means hardness; 'stability' (<s>sthairya</s>) means immovability. // 3
'Binding' (<s>bandhana</s>) means mutual joining; 'refreshment' (<s>prahlāda</s>) means satisfaction of body and senses. // 4
'Subtle' (<s>sūkṣma</s>) means flowing through subtle channels. // 5

children.text: prabhā varṇaprakāśinī dīptiḥ yaduktaṃ varṇamākrāmati chāyā prabhā varṇaprakāśikā ityādi // 6
children.translated_text: 'Luster' (<s>prabhā</s>) means that which illuminates color — radiance. As stated: 'shadow encroaches upon color; luster illuminates color' — and so on. // 6
<s>Vicaraṇa</s> means <s>vicāra</s> (investigation), i.e., movement — this is the meaning. // 7
<s>Sauṣirya</s> means abundance of cavities. // 8

children.text: atrākāśabāhulyaṃ dravyasya pṛthivyādibhūtāntarālpatvena bhūrivyaktākāśatvena ca jñeyaṃ yadeva bhūriśuṣiraṃ tannābhasaṃ kiṃvā ākāśaguṇabahulatvena nābhasaṃ dravyam ityucyate // 9]
children.translated_text: Here, the abundance of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) in a substance should be understood as due to the paucity of other elements such as <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), and due to the preponderance of manifest space. That which has many cavities is said to be of the nature of <s>ākāśa</s> (space). Or alternatively, a substance is called <s>nābhasa</s> (spatial) because it has an abundance of the qualities of <s>ākāśa</s>. // 9]

children.text: anenopadeśena nānauṣadhibhūtaṃ jagati kiṃcid dravyam upalabhyate tāṃ tāṃ yuktim arthaṃ ca taṃ tam abhipretya // Car_1,26.12
children.translated_text: By this instruction, there is no substance in the world that is not a potential medicine, considering this or that method and this or that purpose. // Car 1.26.12
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> (commentary)]

children.text: aneneti pratiniyatadravyaguṇopadeśena yat pārthivādi dravyaṃ yadguṇaṃ tadguṇe dehe saṃpādye tad bheṣajaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: 'By this' means by the instruction on the specific qualities of specific substances — whatever <s>pārthiva</s> (earthly) or other substance possesses whatever quality, when that quality is to be produced in the body, that [substance] becomes a medicine — this is the meaning. // 1

children.text: tacca pārthivādi dravyaṃ na sarvathā na ca sarvasmin vyādhau bheṣajamityāha tāṃ tāṃ yuktim ityādi // 2
children.translated_text: And that <s>pārthiva</s> or other substance is not a medicine in all respects nor in every disease — this he states with 'this or that method' and so on. // 2

children.text: yuktim iti upāyam arthamiti prayojanam abhipretyeti adhikṛtya tena kenacidupāyena kvacit prayojane kiṃcid dravyamauṣadhaṃ bhavati na sarvatra // 3
children.translated_text: 'Method' means technique; 'purpose' means objective; 'considering' means taking into account. Thus, by some particular technique, for some particular objective, some substance becomes a medicine — not universally. // 3

children.text: tena yaducyate vairodhikānāṃ sarvadāpathyatvena nānauṣadhaṃ dravyam iti vaco virodhi tanna bhavati vairodhikāni hi saṃyogasaṃskāradeśakālādyapekṣāṇi bhavanti vairodhikasaṃyogādyabhāve tu pathyānyapi kvacit syuḥ // 4
children.translated_text: Therefore, the statement that substances which are mutually incompatible (<s>vairodhika</s>) are always unwholesome and hence there is no substance that is not medicine — this is not contradictory. For incompatible combinations depend on combination, processing, place, time, and so forth. In the absence of incompatible combination etc., even those may sometimes be wholesome. // 4

children.text: yānyapi sarvadāpi svabhāvādeva viṣamandakādīnyapathyāni tānyapy upāyayuktāni kvacit pathyāni bhavanti yathā udare viṣasya tilaṃ dadyāt ityādi // 5
children.translated_text: Even those substances such as poison, <s>mandaka</s>, and others that are always unwholesome by their very nature — even those, when combined with [proper] methods, sometimes become wholesome, as stated: 'In [the disease of] <s>udara</s> (abdominal enlargement), one should give a sesame-measure of poison,' and so on. // 5

children.text: yattu tṛṇapāṃśuprabhṛtīni nopayujyante ato na tāni bheṣajānītyucyate tanna teṣāmapi bheṣajasvedādyupāyatvena bheṣajatvāt // 6]
children.translated_text: As for the objection that substances like grass and dust are not used and therefore are not medicines — that is not so, because even those are medicines, being employable as means for herbal steam-bath treatments and the like. // 6]

children.text: na tu kevalaṃ guṇaprabhāvādeva dravyāṇi kārmukāṇi bhavanti dravyāṇi hi dravyaprabhāvād guṇaprabhāvād dravyaguṇaprabhāvāc ca tasmiṃstasmin kāle tattadadhikaraṇam āsādya tāṃ tāṃ ca yuktimarthaṃ ca taṃ tamabhipretya yat kurvanti tat karma yena kurvanti tadvīryaṃ yatra kurvanti tadadhikaraṇaṃ yadā kurvanti sa kālaḥ yathā kurvanti sa upāyaḥ yat sādhayanti tat phalam // Car_1,26.13
children.translated_text: But substances are not efficacious solely by the power of their qualities. For substances [act] by the power of the substance itself, by the power of qualities, or by the power of both substance and quality; in this or that time, reaching this or that substrate, and considering this or that method and purpose — what they do is the action (<s>karma</s>); that by which they do it is the potency (<s>vīrya</s>); where they do it is the substrate (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>); when they do it is the time (<s>kāla</s>); the manner in which they do it is the technique (<s>upāya</s>); and what they accomplish is the result (<s>phala</s>). // Car 1.26.13
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: pārthivādidravyāṇāṃ gurukharādiguṇayogād bheṣajatvam uktaṃ tena guṇaprabhāvādeva bheṣajaṃ syāditi śaṅkāṃ nirasyann āha na tu kevalam ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: It was stated that <s>pārthiva</s> and other substances become medicines by association with qualities like heaviness, roughness, etc. Dispelling the doubt that medicines would operate solely by the power of qualities, he says 'But not solely...' and so on. // 1

children.text: dravyaprabhāvād yathā dantyā virecakatvaṃ tathā maṇīnāṃ viṣādihantṛtvam ityādi // 2
children.translated_text: 'By the power of the substance' — for example, the purgative property of <s>Dantī</s> (Baliospermum), and the capacity of gems to counteract poisons, and so on. // 2

children.text: guṇaprabhāvādyathā jvare tiktako rasaḥ śīte 'gnir ityādi // 3
children.translated_text: 'By the power of quality' — for example, in fever the bitter taste [is effective]; in cold, fire [i.e., heat is effective], and so on. // 3

children.text: dravyaguṇaprabhāvād yathā kṛṣṇājinasyoparīti atrāpi kṛṣṇatvaṃ guṇo'jinaṃ ca dravyamabhipretaṃ yathā vā maṇḍalair jātarūpasya tasyā eva payaḥ śṛtam tatra maṇḍalaguṇayuktasyaiva jātarūpasya kārmukatvam // 4
children.translated_text: 'By the power of substance and quality together' — for example, 'upon a black antelope skin' — here too, blackness is the quality and the antelope skin is the substance intended. Or as with 'circular [discs] of gold, boiled in its own milk' — there the efficacy belongs to gold endowed with the quality of circularity. // 4
He states 'how they act' with 'in this or that...' and so on. // 5

children.text: tāṃ tāṃ yuktimāsādyeti tāṃ tāṃ yojanāṃ prāpya // 6
children.translated_text: 'Reaching this or that method' means attaining this or that combination. // 6

children.text: yat kurvantītyādāv udāharaṇaṃ yathā śirovirecanadravyāṇi yacchirovirecanaṃ kurvanti tac chirovirecanaṃ karma yenoṣṇatvādikāraṇena śirovirecanaṃ kurvanti tadvīryaṃ vīryaṃ śaktiḥ sā ca dravyasya guṇasya vā yatra śirovirecanaṃ kurvanti tadadhikaraṇaṃ śiraḥ nānyatrādhikaraṇe śirovirecanadravyaṃ prabhavatītyarthaḥ yadeti vasantādau śirogauravādiyukte ca kāle etenākāle śīte śirovirecanaṃ stabdhatvānna kārmukaṃ kiṃtu svakāla eva yathā yena prakāreṇa pradhamanāvapīḍanādinā tathā prasāritāṅgamuttānaṃ śayane saṃstarāstṛte // 7
children.translated_text: An example for 'what they do' and so forth: just as substances for nasal purgation perform nasal cleansing — that nasal cleansing is the action (<s>karma</s>); that by which, through the cause of heat etc., they perform nasal purgation is the potency (<s>vīrya</s>), i.e., the power, and that is [the power] either of the substance or of the quality; where they perform nasal purgation is the substrate — the head, meaning that a nasal purgation substance is not effective at any other substrate. 'When' means in spring etc., and at a time when there is heaviness of the head etc. — by this it is implied that in the wrong season, in cold, nasal purgation is not efficacious due to stiffness; rather [it is effective] only in its proper season. 'How' means by the method of insufflation, compression, etc., as described: 'Having the limbs extended, lying face up on a well-spread bed, // 7

children.text: īṣat pralambaśirasaṃ saṃveśya cāvṛtekṣaṇam ityādinā vidhinā kurvanti sa upāyaḥ yat sādhayanti śirogauravaśūlādyuparamaṃ tat phalaṃ phalam uddeśyam // 8
children.translated_text: with head slightly lowered, having covered the eyes' — by such procedure they act; this is the technique. 'What they accomplish' — the cessation of heaviness of the head, headache, etc. — that is the result. The result is the objective. // 8

children.text: karma kāryaṃ sādhanam uddeśyaṃ phalaṃ sādhyaṃ yathā yāganiṣpādyo dharmaḥ kāryatayā karma tajjanyastu svargādir uddeśyaḥ phalam evaṃ vamanādiṣvapi karmādhikaraṇādyunneyam // 9]
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is the effect, the means; the objective (<s>uddeśya</s>) is the result, what is to be accomplished. Just as <s>dharma</s> (merit) produced by a sacrifice is the effect in the nature of action, while heaven etc. produced thereby is the objective result — similarly in emesis etc., action, substrate, and the rest should be inferred. // 9]

children.text: bhedaś caiṣāṃ triṣaṣṭividhavikalpo dravyadeśakālaprabhāvād bhavati tam upadekṣyāmaḥ // Car_1,26.14
children.translated_text: And the varieties of these are of sixty-three kinds, arising from the influence of substance, place, and time. We shall teach that. // Car 1.26.14
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: samprati dravyam abhidhāya vikṛtānāṃ rasānām eva bhedam āha bhedaś caiṣām ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, having described the substance, he states the varieties of the modified <s>rasas</s> (tastes) themselves with 'And the varieties of these...' and so on. // 1

children.text: prabhāvaśabdo dravyadeśakālaiḥ pratyekaṃ yujyate tatra dravyaprabhāvād yathā somaguṇātirekān madhuraḥ ityādi deśaprabhāvād yathā himavati drākṣādāḍimādīni madhurāṇi bhavantyanyatrāmlānītyādi kālaprabhāvādyathā bālāmraṃ sakaṣāyaṃ taruṇamamlaṃ pakvaṃ madhuraṃ tathā hemante oṣadhyo madhurā varṣāsv amlā ityādi // 2
children.translated_text: The word 'influence' (<s>prabhāva</s>) applies individually to substance, place, and time. Thus, by the influence of substance — for example, due to the predominance of the qualities of <s>Soma</s> (moon), 'sweet' etc. By the influence of place — for example, in the <s>Himālaya</s>, grapes and pomegranates are sweet, but elsewhere sour, etc. By the influence of time — for example, an unripe mango is astringent, a young one is sour, and a ripe one is sweet. Likewise, in winter, herbs are sweet; in the rainy season, sour, and so on. // 2

children.text: agnisaṃyogādayo ye 'nye rasahetavas te 'pi kāle dravye vāntarbhāvanīyāḥ // 3]
children.translated_text: Other causes of taste such as contact with fire, etc. should be subsumed under time or substance. // 3]
Sweet, combined separately with sour and the rest,

children.text: yānti pañcadaśaitāni dravyāṇi dvirasāni tu // Car_1,26.15
children.translated_text: and sour with each of the remaining [tastes] — these substances with two tastes number fifteen. // Car 1.26.15
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He states the varieties with 'Sweet...' and so on. // 1

children.text: tatra svādoramlādiyogāt pañca śeṣair iti āditvenopayuktād anyaiḥ tenāmlasya lavaṇādiyogāc catvāri evaṃ lavaṇasya kaṭvādiyogāt trīṇi kaṭukasya tiktakaṣāyayogād dve tiktasya kaṣāyayogād ekam evaṃ pañcadaśa dvirasāni // 2]
children.translated_text: Thus, from the combination of sweet with sour etc., five; 'with the rest' means with the others beyond the one mentioned first. So, from sour with salt etc., four. Similarly, from salt with pungent etc., three. From pungent with bitter and astringent, two. From bitter with astringent, one. Thus fifteen substances with two tastes. // 2]
Sweet separately combined with sour etc., the combination with the rest is separate;

children.text: madhurasya tathāmlasya lavaṇasya kaṭos tathā // Car_1,26.16
children.translated_text: and similarly for sour, salt, and pungent. // Car 1.26.16
Substances with three tastes, in proper order, are stated to be twenty. //
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He states the three-taste [combinations] with 'Separately...' and so on. // 1

children.text: madhurasyāmlādirasacatuṣṭayena pṛthag ityekaikaśo yuktasya śeṣairlavaṇādibhir yogo bhavati tatra madhurasyāmlayuktasya śeṣalavaṇādiyogāc catvāri tathā madhurasya lavaṇayuktasya kaṭvādiyogāt trīṇi tathā kaṭuyuktasya tiktādiyogād dve tathā tiktayuktasya kaṣāyayogād ekam evaṃ madhureṇādisthitena daśa // 2
children.translated_text: Sweet, placed first, separately combined with each of the four tastes beginning with sour — [then] the combination 'with the rest,' i.e., with salt etc. Thus: sweet combined with sour, combined with the rest — salt, etc. — gives four. Sweet combined with salt, combined with pungent, etc. — three. Sweet combined with pungent, combined with bitter, etc. — two. Sweet combined with bitter, combined with astringent — one. Thus, with sweet as the initial element, ten. // 2

children.text: evamamlasyādisthitasya lavaṇayuktasya kaṭvādiyogāt trīṇi tathā kaṭukayuktasya śeṣābhyāṃ yogād dve evaṃ tiktayuktasya kaṣāyayogād ekam evam amlasya ṣaṭ // 3
children.translated_text: Similarly, for sour placed first: sour combined with salt, combined with pungent, etc. — three. Sour combined with pungent, combined with the remaining two — two. Sour combined with bitter, combined with astringent — one. Thus for sour, six. // 3

children.text: anenaiva nyāyena lavaṇasya trīṇi kaṭoś caikameva evaṃ militvā trirasāni viṃśatiḥ // 4]
children.translated_text: By the same principle, for salt — three; for pungent — only one. Thus combined, the three-taste [substances] are twenty. // 4]

children.text: vakṣyante tu catuṣkeṇa dravyāṇi daśa pañca ca // Car_1,26.17
children.translated_text: And with four [tastes] combined, the substances are fifteen. // Car 1.26.17
Sweet and sour together, combined separately with salt etc.,
and the rest combined separately, by the count of four-taste [combinations]. // Car 1.26.18
Sweet and salt together, likewise separately with pungent etc.,

children.text: yuktau śeṣaiḥ pṛthagyogaṃ yātaḥ svādūṣaṇau tathā // Car_1,26.19
children.translated_text: the remaining pairs combined separately — and sweet and pungent likewise. // Car 1.26.19
Sour and salt combined together, with pungent etc. separately,

children.text: yātaḥ śeṣaiḥ pṛthagyogaṃ śeṣairamlakaṭū tathā // Car_1,26.20
children.translated_text: combined separately with the rest — and sour and pungent likewise. // Car 1.26.20
Bitter and salt, and pungent combined together with astringent. //
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: catūrase svādvamlāv ādisthitau lavaṇādibhir ekaikaśyena yuktau śeṣaiḥ kaṭvādibhir yogāt ṣaḍ bhavanti // 1
children.translated_text: For the four-taste [combinations]: sweet and sour placed first, combined individually with salt etc., combined with pungent etc. — six result. // 1

children.text: svādulavaṇau sahitau ādisthitau kaṭvādibhiriti kaṭutiktābhyāṃ pṛthagyuktau śeṣair iti tiktakaṣāyābhyāṃ teneha bahuvacanaṃ jātau boddhavyam evaṃ trīṇi // 2
children.translated_text: 'Sweet and salt together, placed first' — combined separately with pungent and bitter, 'with the rest' meaning bitter and astringent — hence here the plural form 'became' should be understood. Thus three. // 2
'Sweet and pungent likewise' — by this, the form sweet-pungent-bitter-astringent is one. // 3
In 'with pungent etc.' also, the plural form 'became' [is used]. // 4

children.text: amlalavaṇau saṃyuktau kaṭunā sahitau śeṣābhyāṃ yogād dve tathāmlalavaṇau tiktayuktau śeṣayogād ekam // 5
children.translated_text: 'Sour and salt combined, together with pungent, combined with the rest' — two. 'Sour and salt combined with bitter, combined with the rest' — one. // 5
'Sour and pungent likewise' — by this, the form sour-pungent-bitter-astringent is one. // 6
'Combined with...' and so on gives one. // 7
Thus fifteen four-taste [combinations]. // 8]
And five-taste [substances] are said to be six, by the exclusion of one each. // Car 1.26.21

children.text: ṣaṭ caivaikarasāni syur ekaṃ ṣaḍrasameva tu /
children.translated_text: And single-taste [substances] are six; and there is one with all six tastes. //
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'By exclusion' means by omission. // 1

children.text: atra ca rasānāṃ guṇatvenaikasmin dravye samavāyo yogaśabdenocyate // 2]
children.translated_text: And here, the co-inherence of tastes as qualities in one substance is expressed by the word 'combination.' // 2]
Thus sixty-three varieties of substances have been declared by the count of tastes. // Car 1.26.22
But the sixty-three would be innumerable, due to the [additional] classification of tastes and sub-tastes;

children.text: rasāstaratamābhyāṃ tāṃ saṃkhyām atipatanti hi // Car_1,26.23
children.translated_text: for tastes exceed that number through degrees of more and less. // Car 1.26.23
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: rasasaṃsargasya prakārāntareṇāsaṃkhyeyatām āha triṣaṣṭiḥ syād ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: He states the innumerability of taste-combinations by another method with 'The sixty-three would be...' and so on. // 1
'Sub-taste' (<s>anurasa</s>) will be explained hereafter. // 2

children.text: atra ca triṣaṣṭyātmakarase rasānurasakalpanā nāsti kevale madhurādau tadabhāvāt tena yathāsambhavaṃ saptapañcāśatsaṃyogaviṣayaṃ rasānurasakalpanaṃ jñeyam // 3
children.translated_text: Here, the classification of taste and sub-taste does not apply to the sixty-three as a whole, since in a single taste like sweet etc. alone, there is no [sub-taste]. Hence the taste-sub-taste classification should be understood as applicable to the fifty-seven combinations. // 3
Alternatively, even in a single taste, there exists an unexpressed sub-taste. // 4

children.text: prakārāntareṇāpy asaṃkhyeyatām āha rasās taratamābhyām ityādi // 5
children.translated_text: He states the innumerability by yet another method with 'tastes, through degrees of more and less...' and so on. // 5
Through the distinctions of sweet, sweeter, sweetest, etc., the innumerability of tastes arises — this is the purport. // 6

children.text: kiṃvā rasānurasatvenaiva yāsaṃkhyeyatā tatraivāyaṃ hetuḥ rasās taratamābhyāmityādiḥ // 7]
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the innumerability that arises through the principle of taste and sub-taste itself — for that very [innumerability], the reason is 'tastes, through degrees of more and less...' and so on. // 7]
The combinations are fifty-seven, but the classification is sixty-three-fold;
among tastes, this has been devised by taste-theorists due to their suitability. // Car 1.26.24
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: evamasaṃkhyeyatve'pi triṣaṣṭividhaiva kalpanā cikitsāvyavahārārtham ihācāryaiḥ kalpitetyāha saṃyogā ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Even though innumerable, only the sixty-three-fold classification has been devised by the teachers here for the purpose of therapeutic practice — this he states with 'The combinations...' and so on. // 1

children.text: tatra yogyatvād iti tatra svasthāturahitacikitsāprayoge 'natisaṃkṣepavistararūpatayā hitatvād ityarthaḥ // 2]
children.translated_text: 'Due to their suitability' means due to their being beneficial in a form that is neither excessively concise nor elaborate, in application to the treatment of the healthy and the afflicted — this is the meaning. // 2]

children.text: kvacideko rasaḥ kalpyaḥ saṃyuktāś ca rasāḥ kvacit /
children.translated_text: Sometimes a single taste should be prescribed, and sometimes combined tastes,
by a physician desiring success, having considered the <s>doṣas</s> (humors), medicines, and the like. // Car 1.26.25
Substances with two tastes and more, or combined tastes, the wise

children.text: rasān ekaikaśo vāpi kalpayanti gadān prati // Car_1,26.26
children.translated_text: prescribe individually, taste by taste, for [various] diseases. // Car 1.26.26
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He states that very therapeutic application with 'Sometimes...' and so on. // 1
Here, by the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the inclusion of unmentioned factors such as place, time, strength, and so forth [is intended]. // 2

children.text: etadeva saṃyuktāsaṃyuktarasakalpanaṃ bhinnarasadravyamelakād vānekarasaikadravyaprayogād ekarasadravyaprayogādvā bhavatīti darśayannāha dravyāṇītyādi // 3
children.translated_text: Showing that this very prescription of combined and uncombined tastes arises either from the blending of substances of different tastes, or from the use of a single substance with multiple tastes, or from the use of a single-taste substance — he says 'Substances...' and so on. // 3

children.text: dvirasādīni utpattisiddhadvirasatrirasādīni dvirasaṃ yathā kaṣāyamadhuro mudgaḥ trirasaṃ yathā madhurāmlakaṣāyaṃ ca viṣṭambhi guru śītalam // 4
children.translated_text: 'With two tastes and more' means those intrinsically possessing two tastes, three tastes, etc. A two-taste [substance], for example: <s>Mudga</s> (green gram) which is astringent and sweet. A three-taste [substance], for example: 'Sweet, sour, and astringent — it is constipating, heavy, and cold.' // 4

children.text: pittaśleṣmaharaṃ bhavyam ityādi catūrasas tilaḥ yad uktaṃ snigdhoṣṇamadhuras tiktaḥ kaṣāyaḥ kaṭukas tilaḥ pañcarasaṃ tv āmalakaṃ harītakī ca śivā pañcarasā ityādivacanāt vyaktaṣaḍrasaṃ tu dravyam ihānuktaṃ viṣaṃ tv avyaktaṣaḍrasasaṃyuktaṃ hārīte tv eṇamāṃsaṃ vyaktaṣaḍrasasaṃyuktam uktam // 5
children.translated_text: [The statement] 'it removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>' etc. — sesame has four <s>rasas</s> (tastes), as stated: 'Sesame is unctuous, hot, sweet, bitter, astringent, and pungent.' <s>Āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), however, has five <s>rasas</s>, and <s>Harītakī</s> too is said to have five <s>rasas</s>. But a substance possessing all six <s>rasas</s> manifestly is not mentioned here. Poison, however, possesses the six <s>rasas</s> in an unmanifest form. In <s>Hārīta</s>'s [text], however, <s>eṇa</s>-deer meat is said to possess all six <s>rasas</s> manifestly. // 5
Thus, by combining substances having two <s>rasas</s> and so forth, one obtains the use of two <s>rasas</s> etc. // 6

children.text: tathā saṃyuktāṃśca rasāniti ekaikarasādidravyamelakāt saṃyuktān rasān ekaikaśaḥ kalpayanti prayojayanti // 7
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'combined <s>rasas</s>' means: from the mixture of substances having one <s>rasa</s> each etc., they prepare and apply the combined <s>rasas</s> one by one. // 7

children.text: gadān pratīti prādhānyena tena svasthavṛtte 'pi boddhavyaṃ kiṃvā dvirasādibhedo gada eva svasthe tu sarvarasaprayoga eva yaduktaṃ samasarvarasaṃ sātmyaṃ samadhātoḥ praśasyate iti // 8
children.translated_text: 'For diseases' [is stated] primarily; therefore it should be understood [to apply] to the regimen of the healthy as well. Or, the distinction of two <s>rasas</s> etc. applies only in disease; for the healthy, the application of all <s>rasas</s> is [proper], as stated: 'For one of balanced <s>dhātus</s>, habituation to all <s>rasas</s> equally is commended.' // 8

children.text: evaṃ ca vyākhyāne sati kvacideko rasa ityādinā samamasya na paunaruktyam // 9
children.translated_text: And with this explanation, there is no redundancy with the [earlier passage] 'sometimes one <s>rasa</s>' etc. // 9

children.text: kiṃvā kvacid eko rasaḥ ityādinā svamatam uktam atraivārthe dravyāṇi dvirasādīni ityādinācāryāntarasammatiṃ darśayati ata evānyācāryāntarābhiprāyeṇa kalpayantītyuktaṃ tena na paunaruktyam // 10]
children.translated_text: Or, by 'sometimes one <s>rasa</s>' etc., his own view is stated; here, by 'substances having two <s>rasas</s>' etc., he shows the opinion of other teachers. Therefore the word 'they prepare' is used [to indicate another view]. Hence there is no redundancy. // 10]
He who knows the varieties of <s>rasas</s> (tastes) and who knows the varieties of <s>doṣas</s> —

children.text: na sa muhyed vikārāṇāṃ hetuliṅgopaśāntiṣu // Car_1,26.27
children.translated_text: he is not confused regarding the causes, symptoms, and treatments of diseases. // Car 1.26.27
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He states the fruit of knowledge of <s>rasas</s>: 'He who...' etc. // 1

children.text: atra rasavikalpajñānādeva vyādhihetudravyajñānaṃ kṛtsnamavaruddhaṃ rasajñānenaiva prāyaḥ sakaladravyaguṇasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt // 2
children.translated_text: Here, from the knowledge of varieties of <s>rasas</s> alone, the entire knowledge of disease-causing substances is comprehended, since nearly all properties of substances will be stated through <s>rasa</s>-knowledge alone. // 2

children.text: doṣavikalpajñānācca liṅgajñānaṃ yāvaddhi liṅgaṃ tat sarvaṃ doṣavikalpasambaddham // 3
children.translated_text: And from the knowledge of <s>doṣa</s>-varieties, the knowledge of symptoms [is obtained], since all symptoms are connected with <s>doṣa</s>-varieties. // 3

children.text: rasadoṣavikalpajñānāt tu bheṣajajñānaṃ yato rasataḥ svarūpajñānaṃ bheṣajadravyasya doṣataśca bheṣajaprayogaviṣayavijñānam // 4
children.translated_text: From the knowledge of <s>rasa</s> and <s>doṣa</s>-varieties, the knowledge of medicine [is obtained], since from <s>rasa</s> comes the knowledge of the intrinsic nature of medicinal substances, and from <s>doṣas</s> comes the knowledge of the field of application of medicine. // 4
