children.translated_text: And one should not ask: 'Why are there exactly three <s>vipākas</s> and not bitter, etc. as well?' — because this is simply the nature of the elements (<s>bhūtasvabhāva</s>), by which only three — sweet, etc. — exist; and the natures of the elements are not to be questioned. // 22

children.text: nanu yaśca rasaviparītaḥ pāko yathā lavaṇasya madhuraḥ tiktakaṣāyayoś ca kaṭuḥ sa ucyatāṃ yastu samānaguṇo madhurasya madhuro'mlasyāmlaḥ kaṭukasya vā kaṭukaḥ tatkathane kiṃ prayojanaṃ yato rasaguṇair eva tatra vipākaguṇo'pi jñāsyate // 23
children.translated_text: Now, as for the <s>vipāka</s> that is contrary to the <s>rasa</s> — such as the sweet [<s>vipāka</s>] of salt and the pungent [<s>vipāka</s>] of bitter and astringent — let that be stated; but as for one whose quality is the same [as the <s>rasa</s>] — such as the sweet [<s>vipāka</s>] of sweet, the sour of sour, or the pungent of pungent — what is the purpose of stating it, since the <s>vipāka</s> quality would be known from the <s>rasa</s> qualities themselves? // 23

children.text: naivaṃ yena lavaṇādivad visadṛśarasāntarotpādaśaṅkānirārāsārtham api tatrānuguṇo'pi vipāko vaktavya eva vipākajaśca rasa āhārapariṇāmānte bhavati prākṛtastu raso vipākaviruddhaḥ pariṇāmakālaṃ varjayitvā jñeyaḥ tena pippalyāḥ kaṭukarasatvam ādau kaṇṭhasthaśleṣmakṣapaṇamukhaśodhanādikartṛtvena saprayojanaṃ madhuravipākatvaṃ tu pariṇāmena vṛṣyatvādijñāpanena saprayojanam // 24
children.translated_text: This is not so, because — just as in the case of salt etc., to dispel the doubt of a dissimilar <s>rasa</s> arising [as <s>vipāka</s>] — even the concordant <s>vipāka</s> must indeed be stated. Moreover, the <s>rasa</s> born of <s>vipāka</s> occurs at the end of the transformation of food, while the natural <s>rasa</s>, contrary to the <s>vipāka</s>, should be understood [as operating] except during the period of transformation. Thus, the pungent <s>rasa</s> nature of long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>) has its purpose initially in clearing the phlegm adhering to the throat, cleansing the mouth, etc.; while its sweet <s>vipāka</s> nature has its purpose through the transformation, in indicating its aphrodisiac property, etc. // 24

children.text: tathā yatra vipākasya rasāḥ samānaguṇatayānuguṇā bhavanti tatra balavat kāryaṃ bhavati viparyaye tu durbalam iti jñeyam // 25
children.translated_text: Similarly, where the <s>rasas</s> are concordant with the <s>vipāka</s> by having the same qualities, there the effect is strong; in the opposite case, it is weak — this should be understood. // 25

children.text: etacca pākatrayaṃ dravyaniyataṃ tena grahaṇyadhyāye vakṣyamāṇāhārāvasthāpākādbhinnam eva tatra hy aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣāmeva rasānām avasthāvaśāt trayaḥ pākā vācyāḥ annasya bhuktamātrasya ṣaḍrasasya prapākataḥ ityādinā granthena // 26]
children.translated_text: And this threefold <s>vipāka</s> is substance-specific; therefore it is indeed different from the stage-wise digestion of food (<s>āhārāvasthāpāka</s>) that will be described in the chapter on <s>Grahaṇī</s>. For there, without distinction, for all <s>rasas</s>, three stages of digestion are to be stated, as per the passage: 'Of food just eaten, having all six <s>rasas</s>, through the initial digestion...' and so on. // 26]
Soft, sharp, heavy, light, unctuous, dry, hot, and cold —
some hold <s>vīrya</s> (potency) to be eightfold; some hold it to be twofold. // Car_1,26.64

children.text: śītoṣṇamiti vīryaṃ tu kriyate yena yā kriyā /
children.translated_text: 'Cold and hot' — <s>vīrya</s> is that by which an action is performed;

children.text: nāvīryaṃ kurute kiṃcit sarvā vīryakṛtā kriyā // Car_1,26.65
children.translated_text: nothing acts without <s>vīrya</s>; all action is brought about by <s>vīrya</s>. // Car_1,26.65
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
He states the characteristics of <s>vīrya</s> according to one view, with 'soft,' etc. // 1
Both of these views proceed on the basis of the technical definition (<s>pāribhāṣikī</s>) of <s>vīrya</s>. // 2

children.text: vaidyake hi rasavipākaprabhāvavyatirikte prabhūtakāryakāriṇi guṇe vīryamiti saṃjñā tenāṣṭavidhavīryavādimate picchilaviśadādayo guṇā na rasādiviparītaṃ kāryaṃ prāyaḥ kurvanti tena teṣāṃ rasādyupadeśenaiva grahaṇaṃ mṛdvādīnāṃ tu rasādyabhibhāvakatvamasti yathā pippalyāṃ kaṭurasakāryaṃ pittakopanamabhibhūya tadgate mṛduśītavīrye pittameva śamayatīti tathā kaṣāye tiktānurase mahati pañcamūle tatkāryaṃ vātakopanam abhibhūyoṣṇena vīryeṇa tadviruddhaṃ vātaśamanameva kriyate tathā madhure'pīkṣau śītavīryatvena vātavṛddhir ityādi // 3
children.translated_text: For in medicine, the quality that is distinct from <s>rasa</s>, <s>vipāka</s>, and <s>prabhāva</s> and that produces abundant effects receives the designation <s>vīrya</s>. Therefore, in the view of eightfold <s>vīrya</s>, qualities like slimy (<s>picchila</s>), clear (<s>viśada</s>), etc. generally do not produce effects contrary to <s>rasa</s> and the rest, and hence they are subsumed under the teaching of <s>rasa</s>, etc. But qualities such as soft (<s>mṛdu</s>), etc. have the power to override <s>rasa</s> and the rest — as, for example, in long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>), the pungent <s>rasa</s> effect of aggravating <s>Pitta</s> is overridden, and by the soft and cold <s>vīrya</s> residing in it, <s>Pitta</s> itself is pacified. Similarly, in the great <s>Pañcamūla</s> [decoction], which is astringent with a predominantly bitter sub-taste, its [expected] effect of aggravating <s>Vāta</s> is overridden, and by its hot <s>vīrya</s>, the opposite — the pacification of <s>Vāta</s> — is effected. Likewise, even in sweet sugarcane (<s>ikṣu</s>), due to its cold potency, <s>Vāta</s> is increased, etc. // 3

children.text: yaduktaṃ suśrute etāni khalu vīryāṇi svabalaguṇotkarṣād rasam abhibhūyātmakarma darśayanti ityādi // 4
children.translated_text: As stated in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'These potencies (<s>vīryas</s>), by the superiority of their own strength and qualities, override the <s>rasa</s> and manifest their own action' — and so on. // 4

children.text: śītoṣṇavīryavādimataṃ tv agnīṣomīyatvāj jagataḥ śītoṣṇayoreva prādhānyājjñeyam // 5
children.translated_text: The view of those who hold that potency (<s>vīrya</s>) is [only] hot and cold should be understood from the fact that the world is of the nature of <s>Agni</s> (fire) and <s>Soma</s> (moon), and hot and cold alone are predominant. // 5
And it is said —
Though a substance has manifold nature, the two great forces — <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> —
like the manifest and unmanifest universe, it never exceeds. // 6

children.text: etacca matadvayam apyācāryasya paribhāṣāsiddhamanumatameva yenottaratra rasavīryavipākānāṃ sāmānyaṃ yatra lakṣyate ityādau pāribhāṣikam eva vīryaṃ nirdekṣyati // 7
children.translated_text: And both these views are approved by the teacher as established by technical convention, since later he will define <s>vīrya</s> in the technical sense in the passage 'Where a commonality of <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>vīrya</s> (potency), and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect) is observed...' and so on. // 7

children.text: pāribhāṣikavīryasaṃjñāparityāgena tu śaktiparyāyasya vīryasya lakṣaṇamāha vīryaṃ tv ityādi // 8
children.translated_text: Without abandoning the technical designation of <s>vīrya</s>, he states the definition of <s>vīrya</s> as a synonym of <s>śakti</s> (power) with '<s>Vīrya</s> indeed...' and so on. // 8
<s>Vīrya</s> means <s>śakti</s> (power). // 9

children.text: yeneti rasena vā vipākena vā prabhāvena vā gurvādiparādibhirvā guṇairyā kriyā tarpaṇahlādanaśamanādirūpā kriyate tasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ tad rasādi vīryam // 10
children.translated_text: 'By which' — whether by <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), <s>prabhāva</s> (specific potency), or by qualities such as heaviness etc. and other attributes — whatever action of the nature of nourishment, refreshment, alleviation, and the like is performed — in that action, that <s>rasa</s> etc. is the <s>vīrya</s> (potency). // 10

children.text: ata evoktaṃ suśrute yena kurvanti tadvīryam iti // 11
children.translated_text: Hence it is stated in the <s>Suśruta</s> [Saṃhitā]: 'That by which [substances] act is the <s>vīrya</s>.' // 11

children.text: atraiva lokaprasiddhām upapattim āha nāvīryam ityādi // 12
children.translated_text: He states the commonly known reasoning with 'No powerless [substance]...' and so on. // 12
'Powerless' (<s>avīrya</s>) means incapable — this is the meaning. // 13
'Made by potency' (<s>vīryakṛta</s>) means made by one possessing potency — 'made by the potent.' // 14]
<s>Rasa</s> (taste) [is perceived] at the contact of substances; <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect) by the completion of action;
<s>vīrya</s> (potency) is perceived from the time of cohabitation [with the body] and from [the moment of] contact. // Car 1.26.66
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: rasādīnāmekadravyaniviṣṭānāṃ bhedena nārthaṃ lakṣaṇamāha raso nipāta ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: He states the distinguishing characteristics of <s>rasa</s> etc. which are situated in a single substance, with '<s>Rasa</s> at contact...' and so on. // 1
'Contact' (<s>nipāta</s>) means conjunction with the organ of taste. // 2

children.text: karmaniṣṭhayeti karmaṇo niṣṭhā niṣpattiḥ karmaniṣṭhā kriyāparisamāptiḥ rasopayoge sati yo 'ntyāhārapariṇāmakṛtaḥ karmaviśeṣaḥ kaphaśukrābhivṛddhyādilakṣaṇaḥ tena vipāko niścīyate // 3
children.translated_text: 'By the completion of action' — <s>niṣṭhā</s> means completion; 'completion of action' means the conclusion of the process. When <s>rasa</s> is employed, the particular action produced by the final transformation of food — characterized by the increase of <s>kapha</s>, <s>śukra</s> (reproductive tissue), and the like — by that, <s>vipāka</s> is ascertained. // 3

children.text: adhīvāsaḥ sahāvasthānaṃ yāvad adhīvāsāditi yāvaccharīranivāsāt etacca vipākātpūrvaṃ nipātāccordhvaṃ jñeyam // 4
children.translated_text: 'Cohabitation' (<s>adhīvāsa</s>) means dwelling together; 'from the time of cohabitation' means from the time of residence in the body. This should be understood as being after [the perception of] <s>rasa</s> and before <s>vipāka</s>, and [also] from the moment of contact onward. // 4

children.text: nipātācceti śarīrasaṃyogamātrāt tena kiṃcid vīryam adhīvāsād upalabhyate yathānūpamāṃsāder uṣṇatvaṃ kiṃcic ca nipātādeva labhyate yathā marīcādīnāṃ tīkṣṇatvādi kiṃcic ca nipātādhīvāsābhyāṃ yathā marīcādīnāmeva // 5
children.translated_text: 'From contact' means from mere conjunction with the body. Thus some <s>vīrya</s> is perceived from cohabitation — as the heat of marsh-meat etc.; some is perceived from contact itself — as the sharpness of pepper etc.; and some from both contact and cohabitation — as in the case of pepper itself. // 5

children.text: etena rasaḥ pratyakṣeṇaiva vipākastu nityaparokṣaḥ tatkāryeṇānumīyate vīryaṃ tu kiṃcidanumānena yathā saindhavagataṃ śaityam ānūpamāṃsagataṃ vā auṣṇyaṃ kiṃcic ca vīryaṃ pratyakṣeṇaiva yathā rājikāgatam auṣṇyaṃ ghrāṇena picchilaviśadasnigdharūkṣādayaḥ cakṣuḥsparśanābhyāṃ niścīyanta iti vākyārthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: By this [it is implied that] <s>rasa</s> is [known] by direct perception alone; <s>vipāka</s>, however, is always imperceptible and is inferred from its effects; <s>vīrya</s> is partly [known] by inference — as the coldness in rock salt or the heat in marsh-meat — and partly by direct perception — as the heat in mustard [perceived] by the nose; viscous, clear, unctuous, dry, and such [qualities] are ascertained by the eye and touch — this is the meaning of the passage. // 6

children.text: etacca vīryaṃ sahajaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca jñeyam // 7
children.translated_text: And this <s>vīrya</s> should be understood as both innate (<s>sahaja</s>) and acquired (<s>kṛtrima</s>). // 7

children.text: etacca yathāsambhavaṃ gurulaghvādiṣu vīryeṣu lakṣaṇaṃ jñeyam // 8
children.translated_text: This definition should be understood as applicable to <s>vīryas</s> such as heaviness, lightness, etc., as the case may be. // 8
'Of substances' means of substances being employed. // 9
And this definition of <s>vīrya</s> pertains only to <s>vīrya</s> in the technical sense. // 10]
Where a commonality of <s>rasa</s> (taste), <s>vīrya</s> (potency), and <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect) is observed,

children.text: viśeṣaḥ karmaṇāṃ caiva prabhāvastasya sa smṛtaḥ // Car_1,26.67
children.translated_text: yet there is a difference in actions — the specific potency (<s>prabhāva</s>) of that [substance] is what is remembered. // Car 1.26.67
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He states the definition of <s>prabhāva</s> with '<s>Rasa</s>, <s>vīrya</s>...' and so on. // 1
'Commonality' means similarity. // 2
'Difference of actions' means of purgative action and the like residing in <s>Dantī</s> and similar [substances].

children.text: sāmānyaṃ lakṣyata ityanena rasādikāryatvena yannāvadhārayituṃ śakyate kāryaṃ tat prabhāvakṛtam iti sūcayati ata evoktaṃprabhāvo 'cintya ucyate rasavīryavipākakāryatayācintya ityarthaḥ // 3]
children.translated_text: 'Where commonality is observed' — by this he indicates that the effect which cannot be accounted for by the operation of <s>rasa</s> etc. is produced by <s>prabhāva</s>. Hence it is said: '<s>Prabhāva</s> is called inconceivable' — inconceivable as an effect of <s>rasa</s>, <s>vīrya</s>, and <s>vipāka</s>, this is the meaning. // 3]
<s>Citraka</s> (Plumbago) is held to be pungent [in taste], pungent in <s>vipāka</s>, and hot in <s>vīrya</s>;
similarly <s>Dantī</s> (Baliospermum) — yet it purges a person by <s>prabhāva</s>. // Car 1.26.68
Poison and antidotes to poison — <s>prabhāva</s> is the cause there;
and that which moves both upward and downward [in the body] — that is empowered by <s>prabhāva</s>. // Car 1.26.69
The manifold actions of gems that are to be worn —

children.text: tat prabhāvakṛtaṃ teṣāṃ prabhāvo'cintya ucyate // Car_1,26.70
children.translated_text: those are produced by <s>prabhāva</s>; the <s>prabhāva</s> of those is said to be inconceivable. // Car 1.26.70
<s>Vipāka</s>, <s>vīrya</s>, and <s>prabhāva</s> have been properly illustrated;

children.text: kiṃcidrasena kurute karma vīryeṇa cāparam // Car_1,26.71
children.translated_text: a substance performs some action by <s>rasa</s>, and another by <s>vīrya</s>; // Car 1.26.71

children.text: dravyaṃ guṇena pākena prabhāveṇa ca kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: some by quality, some by <s>vipāka</s>, and some by <s>prabhāva</s>;
<s>vipāka</s> overrides <s>rasa</s>, <s>vīrya</s> overrides both, and <s>prabhāva</s> overrides all. // Car 1.26.72
When there is equality of strength among <s>rasa</s> etc. — this [refers to] innate strength. //
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: asyaiva durabhigamatvād udāharaṇāni bahūnyāha kaṭuka ityādinā // 1
children.translated_text: Because of the difficulty of grasping this, he gives many examples with 'Pungent...' and so on. // 1
'Similarly' means having qualities the same as <s>Citraka</s>. // 2
'Poison-destroying as stated' — that is, from the passage beginning 'tooth-poison [from bites] is the root,' etc. // 3

children.text: ūrdhvānulomikamiti yugapad ubhayabhāgaharaṃ kiṃvā ūrdhvaharaṃ tathānulomaharaṃ ca // 4
children.translated_text: 'Moving both upward and downward' means simultaneously eliminating [waste] in both directions; or alternatively, that which moves upward and also that which moves downward. // 4
'Manifold actions' means the destruction of poison, alleviation of pain, etc. // 5

children.text: etaccodāharaṇamātraṃ tena jīvanamedhyādidravyasya rasādyacintyaṃ sarvaṃ prabhāva iti jñeyam // 6
children.translated_text: These are merely examples. Therefore, all that is inconceivable through <s>rasa</s> etc. in substances having life-giving, intellect-enhancing, and similar [effects] should be understood as <s>prabhāva</s>. // 6

children.text: prabhāvaśceha dravyaśaktir abhipretā sā ca dravyāṇāṃ sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ dantītvādiyuktā vyaktireva yataḥ śaktirhi svarūpameva bhāvānāṃ nātiriktaṃ kiṃciddharmāntaram evaṃ pradeśāntaroktaguṇaprabhāvādiṣvapi vācyam yathoktaṃ dravyāṇi hi dravyaprabhāvādguṇaprabhāvām ityādi // 7
children.translated_text: And <s>prabhāva</s> here is intended as the power of the substance. That is the <s>sāmānya-viśeṣa</s> (universal-particular) of substances — the very individuality endowed with <s>Dantī</s>-ness, etc. For power (<s>śakti</s>) is indeed the very nature of things, not some additional, distinct attribute. The same should be said regarding quality-power etc. as mentioned elsewhere, as stated: 'Substances [act] by the power of the substance, by the power of quality...' and so on. // 7

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ dantyādiḥ svarūpata eva virecayati tena kimiti jalādyupahatā dantī na virecayatīti pratibandhakābhāvaviśiṣṭasyaiva prabhāvasya kāraṇatvāt jalopahatāyāṃ dantyāṃ jalopaghātaḥ pratibandhaka ityādyanusaraṇīyam // 8
children.translated_text: And one should not say that <s>Dantī</s> purges by its very nature [alone], for why then does <s>Dantī</s> damaged by water not purge? Because it is the <s>prabhāva</s> qualified by the absence of obstruction that is the cause. In <s>Dantī</s> damaged by water, the water-damage is the obstruction — this and similar points should be followed. // 8

children.text: naiyāyikaśaktivāde yā ca viṣasya viṣaghnatve upapattir uktā ūrdhvādhogāmitvavirodhalakṣaṇā sāntarbhāgatvāt prabhāvād eva bhavati // 9
children.translated_text: And the reasoning stated in the <s>Naiyāyika</s> (logician's) theory of power regarding the poison-destroying property of [anti-poison substances] — characterized by the contradiction of upward and downward movement — that too arises from <s>prabhāva</s> alone, being included within it. // 9
Similarly, the same should be said regarding the attribution of earthiness etc. in the case of upward-and-downward movement and the like. // 10]
I shall henceforth teach the knowledge for recognizing the six tastes. // Car 1.26.73
By unctuous nourishment, refreshment, and softness, the sweet taste is perceived;
and when present in the mouth, it pervades the mouth and seems to coat it. // Car 1.26.74
From setting the teeth on edge, from salivation of the mouth, from perspiration, from stimulation of the mouth,
and from a burning sensation in the throat and mouth — upon tasting, one should declare it the sour taste. // Car 1.26.75
That which, dissolving, produces moisture, fluidity, and softness in the mouth

children.text: yaḥ śīghraṃ lavaṇo jñeyaḥ sa vidāhānmukhasya ca // Car_1,26.76
children.translated_text: quickly — that should be known as the salt taste, and also from the burning of the mouth. // Car 1.26.76
That which agitates the tastes upon contact and seems to prick,

children.text: vidahanmukhanāsākṣi saṃsrāvī sa kaṭuḥ smṛtaḥ // Car_1,26.77
children.translated_text: burning the mouth, nose, and eyes, causing discharge — that is remembered as pungent. // Car 1.26.77

children.text: pratihanti nipāte yo rasanaṃ svadate na ca /
children.translated_text: That which, upon contact, repels the tongue and does not taste pleasant —
that is the bitter taste, which produces clarity, dryness, and refreshment in the mouth. // Car 1.26.78
The taste which produces clarity, astringency, and numbness in the tongue,

children.text: badhnātīva ca yaḥ kaṇṭhaṃ kaṣāyaḥ sa vikāsyapi // Car_1,26.79
children.translated_text: and which seems to constrict the throat — that is the astringent taste, and it also causes a sense of expansion. // Car 1.26.79
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'That by which it is recognized' — <s>vijñāna</s> means definition, this is the meaning. // 1
'Dissolving' (<s>pralīyan</s>) means becoming liquefied. // 2
'Causing discharge' (<s>saṃsrāvī</s>) means that which makes [things] flow. // 3

children.text: vikāsīti hṛdayavikasanaśīla uktaṃ hi suśrute hṛdayaṃ pīḍayati iti // 4]
children.translated_text: 'Causing expansion' (<s>vikāsī</s>) means tending to expand the heart; as stated in the <s>Suśruta</s>: 'It oppresses the heart.' // 4]

children.text: evamuktavantaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca bhagavan śrutametadavitatham arthasampadyuktaṃ bhagavato yathāvad dravyaguṇakarmādhikāre vacaḥ paraṃ tv āhāravikārāṇāṃ vairodhikānāṃ lakṣaṇam anatisaṃkṣepeṇopadiśyamānaṃ śuśrūṣāmaha iti // Car_1,26.80
children.translated_text: When the blessed <s>Ātreya</s> had thus spoken, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: 'Blessed one! This speech of yours on the topic of substance, quality, and action has been heard — it is truthful, endowed with completeness of meaning, and properly [expressed]. But I desire to hear the definition of the incompatible variants of food, taught without excessive brevity.' // Car 1.26.80
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Now, intending to speak about incompatible food, he says 'Thus...' and so on. // 1

children.text: śarīradhātuvirodhaṃ kurvantīti vairodhikāḥ lakṣyate vairodhikamaneneti lakṣaṇaṃ vairodhikābhidhāyako grantha eva // 2
children.translated_text: 'Incompatible' (<s>vairodhika</s>) — they produce antagonism to the bodily tissues (<s>dhātus</s>). 'Definition' (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) — the text which describes the incompatible [foods]. // 2
'Whatever provokes the <s>doṣas</s>...' and so on — this should be understood as the definition of incompatibility. // 3]

children.text: tam uvāca bhagavān ātreyaḥ dehadhātupratyanīkabhūtāni dravyāṇi dehadhātubhirvirodham āpadyante parasparaguṇaviruddhāni kānicit kānicit saṃyogāt saṃskārād aparāṇi deśakālamātrādibhiś cāparāṇi tathā svabhāvādaparāṇi // Car_1,26.81
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: 'Substances that are antagonistic to the bodily tissues come into conflict with the bodily tissues. Some are mutually antagonistic in their qualities; some [become incompatible] through combination; others through processing; and yet others through place, time, measure, and similar factors; and others again by their very nature.' // Car 1.26.81
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: dehadhātupratyanīkabhūtānīti dehadhātūnāṃ rasādīnāṃ vātādīnāṃ ca prakṛtisthānāṃ pratyanīkasvarūpāṇi // 1
children.translated_text: 'Antagonistic to the bodily tissues' means having a nature opposed to the bodily tissues — the <s>rasas</s> (nutrient fluids), <s>Vāta</s> and the other [<s>doṣas</s>] in their natural state. // 1

children.text: virodhamāpadyanta iti dehadhātūnāṃ virodhamācaranti dūṣayantīti yāvat // 2
children.translated_text: 'Come into conflict' means they practice opposition to the bodily tissues — that is, they vitiate them. // 2

children.text: yathābhūtāni dravyāṇi dehadhātubhirvirodhamāpadyante tadāha parasparaviruddhāni kānicid ityādi // 3
children.translated_text: He states how substances come into conflict with the bodily tissues with 'Mutually antagonistic...' and so on. // 3

children.text: tatra parasparaguṇaviruddhāni yathā na matsyān payasābhyavaharet ubhayaṃ hy etad ityādinoktāni // 4
children.translated_text: Thus, mutually antagonistic in qualities — as stated in 'One should not eat fish together with milk, for both of these...' etc. // 4

children.text: saṃyogaviruddhaṃ yathā tadeva nikucaṃ pakvaṃ na māṣa ityādinoktaṃ yat saṃskārādiviruddhaguṇakathanaṃ vinā sāhityamātreṇa viruddham ucyate tat saṃyogaviruddham // 5
children.translated_text: Incompatible by combination — as stated in 'That same <s>Nikuca</s>, when ripe, not with <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram)...' etc. That which is stated as incompatible merely by being taken together, without specifying incompatible qualities through processing etc. — that is incompatibility by combination. // 5

children.text: matsyapayasos tu yadyapi sahopayogo viruddhatvenoktaḥ tathāpyasau guṇaviruddhatvena kathita iti guṇavirodhakasyaivodāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: As for fish and milk, although their joint consumption is stated as incompatible, since this is described as due to incompatibility of qualities, it is an example of quality-incompatibility alone.

children.text: virodhaśca viruddhaguṇatve satyapi kvacid eva dravyaprabhāvād bhavati tena ṣaḍrasāhāropayoge madhurāmlayor viruddhaśītoṣṇavīryayor virodho nodbhāvanīyaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: And incompatibility, even when there are incompatible qualities, arises only in some cases due to the specific power (<s>prabhāva</s>) of the substance. Therefore, when consuming food with all six tastes, the incompatibility of sweet and sour which have opposed cold and hot potencies should not be raised [as an objection]. // 6

children.text: saṃskārato viruddhaṃ yathā na kapotān sarṣapatailabhṛṣṭān ityādi // 7
children.translated_text: Incompatible by processing — as in 'Pigeons fried in mustard oil should not [be eaten],' etc. // 7
'Place' is of two kinds: land and body. // 8

children.text: tatra bhūmiviruddhaṃ yathā tadeva bhasmapāṃśuparidhvastam kiṃvā yat kiṃcidagocarabhṛtaṃ taddeśaviruddhaṃ śarīraviruddhaṃ yathā uṣṇārtasya madhu maraṇāya // 9
children.translated_text: Thus, land-incompatibility — as in 'That which is covered with ash and dust'; or whatever is fed in an unfamiliar region — that is place-incompatibility. Body-incompatibility — as in 'Honey is death for one suffering from heat.' // 9
Time-incompatibility — as in 'Stale <s>Kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum) is death.' // 10
Measure-incompatibility — as in 'Honey and <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) in equal measure are death.' // 11
By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the inclusion of incompatibility by <s>doṣa</s>-constitution and the like [is meant]. // 12
Naturally incompatible — as poison. // 13]

children.text: tatra yānyāhāramadhikṛtya bhūyiṣṭham upayujyante teṣām ekadeśaṃ vairodhikam adhikṛtyopadekṣyāmaḥ na matsyān payasā sahābhyavaharet ubhayaṃ hy etanmadhuraṃ madhuravipākaṃ mahābhiṣyandi śītoṣṇatvādviruddhavīryaṃ viruddhavīryatvācchoṇitapradūṣaṇāya mahābhiṣyanditvānmārgoparodhāya ca // Car_1,26.82
children.translated_text: Among those [substances] which are mostly employed in connection with food, we shall teach a portion with reference to incompatibility. One should not eat fish together with milk, for both of these are sweet, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, greatly productive of excessive secretion (<s>abhiṣyanda</s>); being cold and hot [respectively], they are of incompatible potency; and because of incompatible potency, they cause vitiation of the blood; and because of their great tendency to produce excessive secretion, they cause obstruction of channels. // Car 1.26.82

children.text: tanniśamyātreyavacanamanu bhadrakāpyo 'gniveśam uvāca sarvāneva matsyān payasā sahābhyavahared anyatraikasmāc cilicimāt sa punaḥ śakalī lohitanayanaḥ sarvato lohitarājī rohitākāraḥ prāyo bhūmau carati taṃ cet payasā sahābhyavaharenniḥsaṃśayaṃ śoṇitajānāṃ vibandhajānāṃ ca vyādhīnāmanyatamamathavā maraṇaṃ prāpnuyāditi // Car_1,26.83
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of <s>Ātreya</s>, <s>Bhadrakāpya</s> said to <s>Agniveśa</s>: 'One may eat all fish with milk except one — the <s>Cilicima</s>. That [fish] is flat-bodied (<s>Śakalī</s>), red-eyed, with red stripes all over, resembling the <s>Rohita</s> fish, and mostly moves on land. If one eats that with milk, one would undoubtedly contract one or other of the diseases arising from blood or those arising from obstruction, or else death.' // Car 1.26.83
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'With reference to incompatibility' means regarding incompatibility. // 1

children.text: śītoṣṇatvāditi payaḥ śītam uṣṇavīryāśca matsyāḥ śeṣaṃ madhuratvādi samānam // 2
children.translated_text: 'Cold and hot' — milk is cold, and fish have hot potency. The rest — sweetness etc. — is common [to both]. // 2
And this is incompatible by the specific power (<s>prabhāva</s>) of the substance alone. // 3

children.text: sa punaḥ śakalī ityādinā nāndiniḥ iti khyāto matsya ucyate // 4]
children.translated_text: By 'That flat-bodied one' and so on, the fish known as <s>Nāndinī</s> is meant. // 4]

children.text:
neti bhagavānātreyaḥ sarvāneva matsyānna payasā sahābhyavaharedviśeṣatastu cilicimaṃ sa hi mahābhiṣyanditvāt sthūlalakṣaṇatarān etān vyādhīn upajanayatyāmaviṣam udīrayati ca /
grāmyānūpaudakapiśitāni ca madhutilaguḍapayomāṣamūlakabisair virūḍhadhānyairvā naikadhyamadyāt tanmūlaṃ hi bādhiryāndhyavepathujāḍyakalamūkatāmaiṇmiṇyam athavā maraṇamāpnoti /
na pauṣkaraṃ rohiṇīkaṃ śākaṃ kapotān vā sarṣapatailabhraṣṭān madhupayobhyāṃ sahābhyavaharet tanmūlaṃ hi śoṇitābhiṣyandadhamanīpravicayāpasmāraśaṅkhakagalagaṇḍarohiṇīnām anyatamaṃ prāpnotyathavā maraṇamiti /
na mūlakalaśunakṛṣṇagandhārjakasumukhasurasādīni bhakṣayitvā payaḥ sevyaṃ kuṣṭhābādhabhayāt /
na jātukaśākaṃ na nikucaṃ pakvaṃ madhupayobhyāṃ sahopayojyam etaddhi maraṇāyāthavā balavarṇatejovīryoparodhāyālaghuvyādhaye ṣāṇḍhyāya ceti /
tadeva nikucaṃ pakvaṃ na māṣasūpaguḍasarpirbhiḥ sahopayojyaṃ vairodhikatvāt /
tathāmrāmrātakamātuluṅganikucakaramardamocadantaśaṭhabadarakośāmrabhavyajāmbavakapitthatintiḍīkapārāvatākṣoḍapanasanālikeradāḍimāmalakānyevaṃprakārāṇi cānyāni dravyāṇi sarvaṃ cāmlaṃ dravamadravaṃ ca payasā saha viruddham /
tathā kaṅguvanakamakuṣṭhakakulatthamāṣaniṣpāvāḥ payasā saha viruddhāḥ /
padmottarikāśākaṃ śārkaro maireyo madhu ca sahopayuktaṃ viruddhaṃ vātaṃ cātikopayati /
hāridrakaḥ sarṣapatailabhṛṣṭo viruddhaḥ pittaṃ cātikopayati /
pāyaso manthānupāno viruddhaḥ śleṣmāṇaṃ cātikopayati /
upodikā tilakalkasiddhā heturatīsārasya /
balākā vāruṇyā saha kulmāṣairapi viruddhā saiva śūkaravasāparibhṛṣṭā sadyo vyāpādayati /
mayūramāṃsam eraṇḍasīsakāvasaktam eraṇḍāgnipluṣṭam eraṇḍatailayuktaṃ sadyo vyāpādayati /
hāridrakamāṃsaṃ hāridrasīsakāvasaktaṃ hāridrāgnipluṣṭaṃ sadyo vyāpādayati tadeva bhasmapāṃśuparidhvastaṃ sakṣaudraṃ sadyo maraṇāya /
children.translated_text:
'No,' said the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>. 'One should not consume any fish with milk, and especially not the <s>cilicima</s> fish, for due to its highly fluid-producing nature, it generates these diseases characterized by corpulence, and it provokes toxic indigestion (<s>āmaviṣa</s>).'
'One should not eat the flesh of village, marshy, or aquatic [animals] together with honey, sesame, jaggery, milk, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), radish, <s>bisa</s> (lotus stalk), or sprouted grains all at once — for from that root [cause], one obtains deafness, blindness, tremor, stupor, stammering, nasal speech, or else death.'
'One should not consume <s>pauṣkara</s> or <s>rohiṇīka</s> greens, or pigeons roasted in mustard oil, together with honey and milk — for from that root [cause], one obtains hemorrhagic overflow, vessel-spreading, epilepsy, <s>śaṅkhaka</s>, throat-goiter, <s>rohiṇī</s>, or else death.'
'One should not consume milk after eating radish, garlic, <s>kṛṣṇagandhā</s>, <s>arjaka</s>, <s>sumukha</s>, <s>surasa</s>, and the like — out of fear of affliction from leprosy.'
'<s>Jātuka</s>-greens and ripe <s>nikuca</s> (breadfruit) should not be consumed together with honey and milk — for this causes death, or else obstruction of strength, complexion, luster, and virility, and a chronic disease, and impotence.'
'That same ripe <s>nikuca</s> should not be consumed together with <s>māṣa</s>-soup, jaggery, or ghee, because of its incompatibility.'
'Likewise, mango, <s>amrātaka</s>, citron, <s>nikuca</s>, <s>karamarda</s>, plantain, <s>dantaśaṭha</s>, jujube, <s>kośāmra</s>, quince, <s>jāmbava</s>, wood-apple, tamarind, <s>pārāvata</s>, walnut, jackfruit, coconut, pomegranate, <s>āmalaka</s>, and other substances of this kind — and all sour [substances], both liquid and non-liquid — are incompatible with milk.'
'Likewise, foxtail millet, wild rice (<s>vanaka</s>), <s>makuṣṭhaka</s>, horse-gram, <s>māṣa</s>, and <s>niṣpāva</s> (flat beans) are incompatible with milk.'
'<s>Padmottarikā</s>-greens consumed together with sugar-based <s>maireya</s> (liquor) and honey are incompatible and greatly aggravate <s>vāta</s>.'
'<s>Hāridraka</s> (a bird) roasted in mustard oil is incompatible and greatly aggravates <s>pitta</s>.'
'Milk-rice with <s>mantha</s> (a stirred drink) as after-drink is incompatible and greatly aggravates <s>kapha</s>.'
'<s>Upodikā</s> (basella) cooked with sesame-paste is a cause of dysentery.'
'<s>Balākā</s> (crane) with <s>vāruṇī</s> (liquor) is incompatible, and also with <s>kulmāṣa</s> (barley-gruel); the same [crane] fried in pig-fat kills immediately.'
'Peacock-flesh placed on a castor-wood spit, roasted on castor-fire, or mixed with castor-oil kills immediately.'
'<s>Hāridraka</s>-flesh placed on a turmeric-wood spit or roasted on turmeric-fire kills immediately; the same [flesh] dusted with ash and taken with honey [causes] immediate death.'

children.text: matsyanistālanasiddhāḥ pippalyastathā kākamācī madhu ca maraṇāya /
children.translated_text: Fish cooked in <s>nistālana</s> (rendered fat) [together with] long-pepper, and <s>kākamācī</s> (nightshade) with honey — [cause] death.

children.text: madhu coṣṇam uṣṇārtasya ca madhu maraṇāya /
children.translated_text: And hot honey, and honey [taken by] one afflicted by heat — [cause] death.

children.text: madhusarpiṣī samadhṛte cāntarikṣaṃ samadhṛtaṃ madhu puṣkarabījaṃ madhu pītvoṣṇodakaṃ bhallātakoṣṇodakaṃ takrasiddhaḥ kampillakaḥ paryuṣitā kākamācī aṅgāraśūlyo bhāsaśceti viruddhāni /
children.translated_text: Honey and ghee taken in equal measure, and rainwater taken in equal measure, honey [with] lotus-seed, honey followed by hot water, <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking-nut) [followed by] hot water, <s>kampillaka</s> cooked in buttermilk, stale <s>kākamācī</s>, and meat of <s>bhāsa</s> (vulture) roasted on charcoal — these are incompatible.
Thus this has been declared in response to the question. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.84
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Flesh of village [animals] etc. is incompatible even with any one of honey etc. // 1
'Stammering' (<s>kalamūkatā</s>) means indistinct speech. // 2

children.text: pauṣkarādīnāṃ madhupayobhyāṃ sahābhyavahāro viruddhaḥ pauṣkaraṃ puṣkaratratrarūpaṃ śākaṃ rohiṇī kaṭurohiṇī // 3
children.translated_text: The consumption of <s>pauṣkara</s> etc. together with honey and milk is incompatible. <s>Pauṣkara</s> is the greens of <s>puṣkaratrā</s>-type; <s>rohiṇī</s> is <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>. // 3
'Vessel-spreading' (<s>dhamanīpraticaya</s>) means knotty swelling of the veins. // 4
'<s>Jātu</s>-greens' means bamboo leaves. // 5

children.text: vairodhikatvādityanena prakaraṇalabdhasyāpi vairodhikatvasya punarabhidhānaṃ sāmānyoktaṣāṇḍhyādivyādhikartṛtopadarśanārtham evamanyatrāpi sāmānye'pi vairodhikatvamātrābhidhāne vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: By [saying] 'because of incompatibility,' the re-statement of incompatibility already obtained from the context is for the purpose of showing the specific diseases like impotence etc. produced by [that] incompatibility. Similarly, elsewhere too, even in a general [statement] where only incompatibility is mentioned, this should be said.

children.text: tathāmletyādau amlagrahaṇena labdhānāpy amlāmrātakādīnām abhidhānaṃ viśeṣavirodhasūcanārtham // 6
children.translated_text: In 'likewise sour...' etc., the mention of <s>amrātaka</s> etc. — already obtained by the word 'sour' — is for the purpose of indicating specific incompatibilities. // 6

children.text: sarvagrahaṇenaiva dravādravāmle prāpte punardravādravavacanaṃ sarvaśabdasya dravādravāmlakārtsnyārthatāpratiṣedhārthaṃ bhavati hi prakaraṇād ekadeśe 'pi sarvavyapadeśaḥ yathā sarvān bhojayediti kiṃvā sarvagrahaṇam amlavipākānāṃ vrīhyādīnāṃ grahaṇārtham // 7
children.translated_text: Even though liquid and non-liquid sour [substances] are obtained by the word 'all' alone, the repeated mention of 'liquid and non-liquid' is to prevent [the interpretation] that the word 'all' means the totality of liquid and non-liquid sour [substances] — for from context, even a partial [collection] receives the designation 'all,' as in 'he should feed all.' Or, the word 'all' is for the inclusion of those like rice etc. that are sour in post-digestive effect (<s>vipāka</s>). // 7

children.text: payaseti tṛtīyayeva sahārthe labdhe punaḥ sahetyabhidhānaṃ kevalāmlādiyuktasyaiva virodhitopadarśanārthaṃ tena amlapayaḥsaṃyoge guḍādisaṃyoge sati viruddhatvaṃ na dugdhāmrādīnām // 8
children.translated_text: 'With milk' — even though the meaning 'together with' is obtained by the third case-ending alone, the repeated mention of 'together with' is for showing that incompatibility pertains only to that which is combined with sour alone etc. Thus, in a combination of sour and milk, when there is also a combination with jaggery etc., there is no incompatibility — [i.e.,] not of milk-mango etc. [when combined with other things]. // 8
<s>Vanaka</s> means <s>vanakodrava</s> (wild rice). // 9
<s>Padmottarikā</s> means <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower). // 10
'Sugar-based' (<s>śārkara</s>) is a qualifier of <s>maireya</s>. // 11

children.text: vātaṃ cātikopayatīti vacanena pittakaphāv alpaṃ kopayatīti bodhayati evaṃ pittaṃ cātikopayati kaphaṃ cātikopayatītyetayorapi vācyam // 12
children.translated_text: By the statement 'greatly aggravates <s>vāta</s>,' it indicates that it aggravates <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> slightly. Similarly should be stated for 'greatly aggravates <s>pitta</s>' and 'greatly aggravates <s>kapha</s>.' // 12
<s>Hāridraka</s> is the bird known as <s>haritāla</s> (green pigeon). // 13

children.text: balākā vāruṇyā saha viruddhā tathā kulmāṣaiśca balākā viruddhā // 14
children.translated_text: <s>Balākā</s> (crane) is incompatible with <s>vāruṇī</s> (liquor), and also <s>balākā</s> is incompatible with <s>kulmāṣa</s> (barley-gruel). // 14

children.text: eraṇḍasīsakāvasaktamiti eraṇḍakāṣṭhāvasaktaṃ sīsako hi bhaṭitrakaraṇakāṣṭham ucyate // 15
children.translated_text: 'Placed on a castor-wood spit' (<s>eraṇḍasīsakāvasakta</s>) means placed on castor wood; for <s>sīsaka</s> means the wood used for making a spit. // 15
'The same' (<s>tadeva</s>) means <s>hāridraka</s>-flesh. // 16

children.text: matsyā nistālyante pacyante yasmin tanmatsyanistālanaṃ kiṃvā nistālanaṃ vasā jatūkarṇe'pyuktaṃ matsyavasā siddhāḥ pippalyaḥ iti // 17
children.translated_text: '<s>Matsyanistālana</s>' — that in which fish are rendered (cooked), i.e., that is the rendered fat of fish. Or <s>nistālana</s> means fat. As stated in <s>Jatūkarṇa</s> too: 'long-peppers cooked in fish-fat.' // 17
'<s>Kākamācī</s> and honey' — this is combination-incompatibility. // 18
<s>Bhāsa</s> means the domestic fowl (<s>goṣṭhakukkuṭa</s>). // 19]

children.text: yat kiṃcid doṣamāsrāvya na nirharati kāyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever food-substance, having provoked the <s>doṣas</s>, does not expel [them] from the body,
all of that conduces to harm. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.85
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
For the purpose of including unmentioned incompatibles, he says 'whatever' etc. // 1
'That which is consumed' (<s>āhāra</s>) — medicine too [is included]. // 2
'Having provoked the <s>doṣas</s>' — having generated the <s>doṣas</s> in an unsettled form — 'does not expel [them].' // 3

children.text: anena vamanavirecanadravyāṇi nirākaroti tāni hi doṣānāsrāvya nirharanti // 4]
children.translated_text: By this he excludes emetic and purgative substances, for those, having provoked the <s>doṣas</s>, do expel them. // 4]
And also that which [is incompatible] by region, time, digestive fire, quantity, habituation, <s>vāta</s> and the other [<s>doṣas</s>],
by processing, by potency, by the constitution of the bowels, and by [considerations of] condition and sequence — // <s>Car</s>_1,26.86
by [rules of] avoidance and treatment, by cooking, and also by combination —

children.text: viruddhaṃ tacca na hitaṃ hṛtsampadvidhibhiśca yat // Car_1,26.87
children.translated_text: that which is incompatible, that is not beneficial, and that which is contrary to satisfaction and proper procedure — // <s>Car</s>_1,26.87
Incompatible by region, for instance: dry, sharp, etc. medicines
being consumed in an arid land; unctuous, cold, etc. [medicines] in a marshy land. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.88
Incompatible by time: the consumption of cold, dry, etc. [substances]

children.text: śīte kāle tathoṣṇe ca kaṭukoṣṇādisevanam // Car_1,26.89
children.translated_text: in cold weather; likewise the consumption of pungent, hot, etc. [substances] in hot [weather]. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.89
Incompatible with [digestive] fire — likewise food and drink [that are incompatible] with the four types [of digestive fire].
Honey and ghee in equal measure — that is incompatible by quantity. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.90
For one habituated to pungent, hot, etc. — the consumption of sweet, cold, etc.

children.text: yattatsātmyaviruddhaṃ tu viruddhaṃ tv anilādibhiḥ // Car_1,26.91
children.translated_text: That is incompatibility by habituation; and incompatible with <s>vāta</s> and the other [<s>doṣas</s>] — // <s>Car</s>_1,26.91
— is that food, medicine, or treatment that is incompatible with the habitual consumption of like-quality [substances].
Incompatible by processing is that food which becomes like poison. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.92
As indeed peacock-flesh placed on a castor-wood spit.

children.text: viruddhaṃ vīryato jñeyaṃ vīryataḥ śītalātmakam // Car_1,26.93
children.translated_text: Incompatibility by potency should be known: that which is cold in potency, // <s>Car</s>_1,26.93
that is consumed together with a substance of hot potency.
And for one of harsh bowels (<s>krūrako���ṭha</s>) — [food that is] very little, of mild potency, and non-purgative; // <s>Car</s>_1,26.94

children.text: mṛdukoṣṭhasya guru ca bhedanīyaṃ tathā bahu /
children.translated_text: for one of soft bowels — heavy, purgative, and likewise abundant —
this is incompatibility by bowel-constitution; and [there is] incompatibility by condition: // <s>Car</s>_1,26.95
for one engaged in exertion, sexual activity, and exercise — food that aggravates <s>vāta</s>;
for one who is sleepy, sluggish, and lazy — food that aggravates <s>kapha</s>. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.96
And that which one eats without having voided feces and urine, and that which one who is not hungry [eats],
and that [eaten by] one excessively overcome by hunger — that is incompatibility by sequence. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.97
Incompatible by [rules of] avoidance: having consumed pork and the like,

children.text: sevetoṣṇaṃ ghṛtādīṃśca pītvā śītaṃ niṣevate // Car_1,26.98
children.translated_text: one then consumes hot [substances]; or having drunk ghee and the like, one consumes cold [substances]. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.98
And incompatible by cooking: that which is cooked with spoiled or bad fuel,
or that which is with uncooked rice, or excessively cooked, or burnt.

children.text: saṃyogato viruddhaṃ tadyathāmlaṃ payasā saha // Car_1,26.99
children.translated_text: Incompatible by combination — as sour [substances] together with milk. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.99
That which is displeasing to the mind — that is called incompatible with the heart.

children.text: sampadviruddhaṃ tadvidyād asaṃjātarasaṃ tu yat // Car_1,26.100
children.translated_text: That should be known as incompatible by quality (<s>sampad</s>) which has not developed its taste, // <s>Car</s>_1,26.100
or in which the taste has passed, or in which the taste has deteriorated.

children.text: jñeyaṃ vidhiviruddhaṃ tu bhujyate nibhṛte na yat /
children.translated_text: That which is not eaten in a secluded [manner] should be known as incompatible by procedure —
such food, consumed [improperly], becomes incompatible. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.101
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: yaccāpi deśakālāgnītyādigranthaṃ kecit paṭhanti sa ca vyakta eva // 1]
children.translated_text: Some read the text 'and also by region, time, fire...' etc. — and that is indeed self-explanatory. // 1]
Of impotence, blindness, herpes, dropsy,
boils, insanity, fistula-in-ano,
fainting, intoxication, distension, throat-obstruction, anemia, toxic indigestion,

children.text: saṃtānadoṣasya tathaiva mṛtyor viruddhamannaṃ pravadanti hetum // Car_1,26.103
children.translated_text: leucoderma, leprosy, malabsorption syndrome, edema, acid-dyspepsia, fever, rhinitis,
defect of progeny, and likewise death — incompatible food is declared to be the cause. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.102–103
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'Impotence' (<s>ṣāṇḍhya</s>) means the state of being a eunuch. // 1

children.text: etacca vairodhikakathanaṃ viśeṣavacanena bādhyate tena laśunasya kṣīreṇa pānaṃ kvacin na virodhi yaduktaṃ sādhayecchuddhaśuṣkasya laśunasya catuṣpalam // 3
children.translated_text: 'Defect of progeny' (<s>saṃtānadoṣa</s>) means having still-born children and the like. // 2

children.text: kṣīrodake'ṣṭaguṇite kṣīraśeṣaṃ ca pāyayet tathā mūlakasvarasaṃ kṣīram ityādiprayogeṣūnneyam // 4
children.translated_text: And this statement of incompatibility is overridden by specific [authoritative] statements. Thus, drinking garlic with milk is sometimes not incompatible — as stated: 'One should cook four <s>palas</s> of clean dried garlic

children.text: kiṃvā anekadravyasaṃyogād atra virodhinām avirodhaḥ virodhimātrasaṃyoga eva virodhī bhavati // 5
children.translated_text: in eight times [its quantity of] milk and water, and give [the patient] to drink until only the milk remains.' Likewise in formulations such as 'radish-juice with milk' etc., this should be inferred. // 4

children.text: yattu madhuna uṣṇena vamanena saṃyuktasya satyapi madanaphalādidravyasaṃyoge 'virodhārthamuktam apakvagamanādi tanmadhuno dravyāntarasaṃyoge 'pyuṣṇasambandhatve virodhitvopadarśanārthaṃ yato viṣānvayaṃ madhu viṣasya coṣṇavirodhi // 6
children.translated_text: Or, due to the combination of multiple substances, there is non-incompatibility of [otherwise] incompatible [substances]; incompatibility exists only when there is a combination of the incompatible alone.

children.text: laśunādīnāṃ tu dravyāntarāsaṃyoge satyeva melako viruddha iti śāstravacanādunnīyate // 7]
children.translated_text: As for what is said regarding honey — that even in the presence of combination with <s>madanaphala</s> etc. substances, honey combined with hot emesis [remains] incompatible, and that 'undigested passage' etc. [results] — that is for showing that even in honey's combination with other substances, incompatibility remains when there is a connection with heat, since honey follows the nature of poison, and poison is incompatible with heat. // 6

children.text: eṣāṃ khalvapareṣāṃ ca vairodhikanimittānāṃ vyādhīnāmime bhāvāḥ pratikārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: But for garlic etc., it is inferred from the text of the treatise that the combination is incompatible only when there is no combination with other substances. // 7]

children.text: tadyathā vamanaṃ virecanaṃ ca tadvirodhināṃ ca dravyāṇāṃ saṃśamanārtham upayogaḥ tathāvidhaiśca dravyaiḥ pūrvam abhisaṃskāraḥ śarīrasyeti // Car_1,26.104
children.translated_text: For these diseases caused by incompatible [foods], and for others too, these are the remedial measures:

Namely: emesis and purgation, and the use of substances antagonistic to those incompatible [foods] for the purpose of pacification, and prior conditioning of the body with such substances. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.104

children.text: vamanaṃ śamanaṃ caiva pūrvaṃ vā hitasevanam // Car_1,26.105
children.translated_text: Purging, emesis, pacification, and prior consumption of wholesome [substances]
counteract diseases born of incompatible food. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.105
And through habituation, through small quantity, for one with strong digestive fire, for a young person,
for those who are unctuous, exercised, and strong — the incompatible becomes ineffective. // <s>Car</s>_1,26.106
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'Antagonistic to those' means those that destroy impotence etc. // 1
'With such [substances]' means those [substances] that are antagonistic to diseases born of incompatible food. // 2
'Prior conditioning' (<s>abhisaṃskāra</s>) means the nourishing of the body through constant use. // 3
Or, 'with such' means with rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) treatments. // 4
And this should be understood as the treatment for a disease not yet arisen (<s>anāgatābādhacikitsita</s>). // 5]
Whatever views the great sages held in determining tastes,
substances [classified] by qualities and actions, the count of substances based on taste, // <s>Car</s>_1,26.107

children.text: parādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ ca lakṣaṇāni pṛthakpṛthak // Car_1,26.108
children.translated_text: the cause of the enumeration of tastes, the characteristics of taste and sub-taste,

children.text: pañcātmakānāṃ ṣaṭtvaṃ ca rasānāṃ yena hetunā /
children.translated_text: and the individual characteristics of the qualities like superiority etc., // <s>Car</s>_1,26.108
and by what reason the five-elemental tastes are six,

children.text: ṣaṇṇāṃ rasānāṃ ṣaṭtve ca savibhaktā vibhaktayaḥ /
children.translated_text: and by what excess of quality tastes become upward-moving or downward-moving, // <s>Car</s>_1,26.109
The general rule and the exception regarding the qualities and actions of substances; // Car 1.26.110
the superior, inferior, and middling status of <s>rasas</s> with respect to heaviness etc.;
the distinguishing marks of <s>pāka</s> (post-digestive effect) and <s>prabhāva</s> (specific potency); the determination of the number of <s>vīryas</s> (potencies); // Car 1.26.111
the individual characteristics of the six <s>rasas</s> when tasted;

children.text: yadyadvirudhyate yasmādyena yatkāri caiva yat // Car_1,26.112
children.translated_text: what is incompatible with what, and from what [reason]; and what produces what [effect]; // Car 1.26.112
and the medicine for diseases caused by incompatibilities —
all this the sage declared in the <s>Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya</s> [chapter]. // Car 1.26.113

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne ātreyabhadrakāpyīyo nāma ṣaḍviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ // Car_1,26.114
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named <s>Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya</s>, in the <s>Ślokasthāna</s> of the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and revised by <s>Caraka</s>. // Car 1.26.114
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: saṃgrahe dravyasaṃkhyā rasāśrayā iti bhedaścaiṣām ityādinā rasasaṃkhyā hi paramārthato dravyasaṃkhyaiva nirguṇatvād rasānām iti bhāvaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: In the summary, 'the number of substances is based on <s>rasas</s>' — and 'the distinctions of these' etc. — means: the number of <s>rasas</s> is in reality the number of substances, since <s>rasas</s> are without [independent] qualities. This is the purport. // 1

children.text: kāraṇaṃ rasasaṃkhyāyā iti rasānāṃ tatra yogyatvād ityādinā vibhaktayo bhedaḥ tatra madhura ityādinā // 2
children.translated_text: 'The cause of the number of <s>rasas</s>' — means: by 'the suitability of <s>rasas</s> therein' etc.; the divisions [are stated] by 'there, sweet' etc. // 2

children.text: uddeśo dravyāṇāṃ śītaṃ vīryeṇa ityādinā apavādo dravyāṇāṃ madhuraṃ kiṃcit ityādinā // 3]
children.translated_text: The general rule (<s>uddeśa</s>) regarding substances is [stated] by 'cold in potency' etc.; the exception (<s>apavāda</s>) regarding substances by 'some sweet [substance]' etc. // 3]
[{Commentary on CS}
Now we shall expound the chapter on the regimen of food and drink (<s>Annapānavidhi</s>). // Car 1.27.1
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car 1.27.2
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: samprati sāmānyenoktānāṃ guṇakarmabhyāṃ prativyaktyanuktānāṃ prativyaktiprāya upayogidravyasya viśiṣṭaguṇakarmakathanārtham annapānavidhir adhyāyo'bhidhīyate // 1
children.translated_text: Now, the chapter <s>Annapānavidhi</s> is stated for the purpose of describing the specific qualities and actions of each individual useful substance — those which were stated generally with respect to their qualities and actions but not [described] individually. // 1
Here, the 'cha' suffix that has arisen undergoes deletion (<s>luk</s>). // 2

children.text: atrānne kāṭhinyasāmānyāt khādyaṃ pāne ca dravatvasāmānyāllehyam avaruddhaṃ jñeyam // 3
children.translated_text: Here, under 'food' (<s>anna</s>), by similarity of hardness, what is to be chewed (<s>khādya</s>) is included; and under 'drink' (<s>pāna</s>), by similarity of fluidity, what is to be licked (<s>lehya</s>) is included. // 3

children.text: annapānaṃ vidhīyate viśiṣṭaguṇakarmayogitayā pratipādyate 'nenetyannapānavidhiḥ dravyāṇāṃ guṇakarmakathanam eva cānnapānavidhiḥ yatastaddhi jñātvānnapānaṃ vidhīyate // 4]
children.translated_text: 'Food and drink are regulated' — means: they are taught as possessing specific qualities and actions. '<s>Annapānavidhi</s>' is thus the description of the qualities and actions of substances; for it is by knowing these that food and drink are [properly] regulated. // 4]

children.text: iṣṭavarṇagandharasasparśaṃ vidhivihitamannapānaṃ prāṇināṃ prāṇisaṃjñakānāṃ prāṇamācakṣate kuśalāḥ pratyakṣaphaladarśanāt tadindhanā hy antaragneḥ sthitiḥ tat sattvam ūrjayati taccharīradhātuvyūhabalavarṇendriyaprasādakaraṃ yathoktamupasevyamānaṃ viparītamahitāya sampadyate // Car_1,27.3
children.translated_text: Food and drink that are of desirable color, smell, taste, and touch, and that are prepared according to proper rules — the skilled call these the very life (<s>prāṇa</s>) of living beings (those designated as <s>prāṇins</s>), because their results are directly perceived. For the maintenance of the internal fire depends on them as fuel; they invigorate <s>sattva</s> (the mind); and they produce clarity of the bodily <s>dhātu</s>-array, strength, complexion, and the senses — when consumed as prescribed. When consumed contrarily, they lead to harm. // Car 1.27.3
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
What does that food and drink accomplish? He states: 'of desirable' etc. // 1

children.text: iṣṭamiti abhimataṃ hitaṃ ca kiṃvā iṣṭaṃ priyaṃ hitaṃ tu vidhivihitaśabdenaiva prāpyate // 2
children.translated_text: 'Desirable' means agreeable and beneficial. Or, 'desirable' means pleasing; 'beneficial' is obtained through the word '<s>vidhivihita</s>' (prepared according to rules) itself. // 2

children.text: vidhir vakṣyamāṇarasavimāne tadetadāhāravidhānam ityādigranthavācyaḥ tathendriyopakramaṇīye nāratnapāṇiḥ ityādinoktaṃ vidhānaṃ tena vidhinā vihitaṃ vidhivihitam // 3
children.translated_text: The 'rule' (<s>vidhi</s>) is to be stated in the forthcoming <s>Rasavimāna</s> [chapter]: 'This is the regimen of diet' etc.; likewise in the <s>Indriyopakramaṇīya</s>: 'Not <s>Ratnapāṇi</s>' etc. — the regulation stated there. 'Regulated by that rule' = <s>vidhivihita</s>. // 3
Among color etc., sound is not mentioned because sound is generally absent in food and drink. // 4

children.text: varṇādiṣu yadyat prathamam annapāne gṛhyate tattat pūrvam uktam // 5
children.translated_text: Among color etc., whichever is perceived first in food and drink is mentioned first. // 5

children.text: rasastu sparśasya paścādgṛhyamāṇo'pi prādhānyakhyāpanārthaṃ sparśasyāgre kṛtaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: But taste, though perceived after touch, is placed before touch in order to indicate its pre-eminence. // 6

children.text: prāṇinām ityanenaiva labdhe'pi prāṇisaṃjñakānām iti vacanaṃ sthāvaraprāṇipratiṣedhārthaṃ vṛkṣādayo hi vanaspatisattvānukāropadeśācchastre prāṇina uktāḥ na tu loke prāṇisaṃjñakāḥ kiṃtarhi jaṅgamā eva // 7
children.translated_text: Though 'of living beings' (<s>prāṇin��m</s>) already conveys [the meaning], the additional phrase 'those designated as <s>prāṇins</s>' is for excluding stationary living beings (plants). For trees etc. are called <s>prāṇins</s> in the scriptures due to the figurative teaching of sentience in plants; but in common usage they are not designated as <s>prāṇins</s> — rather, only mobile beings are. // 7

children.text: iha ca manuṣyasyaivādhikṛtatve'pi sāmānyena sakalaprāṇiprāṇahetutayāhārakathanaṃ manuṣavyatirikte'pi prāṇinyāhārasya prāṇajanakatvopadarśanārtham // 8
children.translated_text: And here, though only human beings are the primary subject, the general statement that food is the cause of life for all beings serves to show that food produces life even in beings other than humans. // 8
'Life' (<s>prāṇa</s>) — because it is the cause of life-breath, like 'ghee is longevity.' // 9

children.text: atha kathaṃ tat prāṇamācakṣata ityāha pratyakṣaphaladarśanāditi // 10
children.translated_text: Now, how do they call it 'life'? He answers: 'because its results are directly perceived.' // 10

children.text: pratyakṣeṇaiva hy āhāraṃ vidhinā kurvatāṃ prāṇā anuvartanta iti tathā nirāhārāṇāṃ prāṇā nahy avatiṣṭhanta iti dṛśyata ityarthaḥ // 11
children.translated_text: For it is directly perceived that life-breaths continue for those who take food according to proper rules; and that life-breaths do not persist for those without food. This is the meaning. // 11

children.text: pratyakṣaśabdaś ceha sphuṭapramāṇe vartate yataḥ prāṇānām annakāryatvam anumānagamyameva // 12
children.translated_text: And the word 'directly perceived' (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) here refers to clear evidence, since the fact that life-breaths are an effect of food is actually knowable by inference. // 12

children.text: ānnakāryatva eva prāṇānāṃ hetumāha tadindhanā hītyādinā // 13
children.translated_text: He states the reason for life-breaths being effects of food: 'for the maintenance of the internal fire depends on them as fuel' etc. // 13

children.text: yasmād antaragnisthitiś cānnapānahetunā agnisthitiśca prāṇahetuḥ tato'nnaṃ prāṇā iti bhāvaḥ uktaṃ hi balam ārogyamāyuśca prāṇāścāgnau pratiṣṭhitāḥ // 14
children.translated_text: Since the maintenance of the internal fire is caused by food and drink, and the maintenance of fire is the cause of life — therefore food is life. This is the purport. For it is said: 'Strength, health, longevity, and life-breaths are established in fire (<s>agni</s>).' // 14

children.text: kiṃvā pūrvamannapānasya prāṇahetutvamuktaṃ tadindhanā hītyādināgnihetutvaṃ varṇyate // 15
children.translated_text: Or, first the causation of life by food and drink was stated; [now] by 'for the maintenance... as fuel' etc., its causation of fire is described. // 15
'Invigorates <s>sattva</s>' means: it produces mental strength. // 16
'<s>Dhātu</s>-array' means the aggregate of <s>dhātus</s> (bodily tissues). // 17
'Contrarily' means consumed not according to rules. // 18]
Therefore, O <s>Agniveśa</s>, for the purpose of understanding what is wholesome and unwholesome, we shall teach you the regimen of food and drink in its entirety.

children.text: tat svabhāvād udaktaṃ kledayati lavaṇaṃ viṣyandayati kṣāraḥ pācayati madhu saṃdadhāti sarpiḥ snehayati kṣīraṃ jīvayati māṃsaṃ bṛṃhayati rasaḥ prīṇayati surā jarjarīkaroti sīdhur avadhamati drākṣāsavo dīpayati phāṇitamācinoti dadhi śophaṃ janayati piṇyākaśākaṃ glapayati prabhūtāntarmalo māṣasūpaḥ dṛṣṭiśukraghnaḥ kṣāraḥ prāyaḥ pittalam amlam anyatra dāḍimāmalakāt prāyaḥ śleṣmalaṃ madhuram anyatra madhunaḥ purāṇācca śāliṣaṣṭikayavagodhūmāt prāyastikaṃ vātalamavṛṣyaṃ cānyatra vegāgrāmṛtāpaṭolapattrāt prāyaḥ kaṭukaṃ vātalam avṛṣyaṃ cānyatra pippalīviśvabheṣajāt // Car_1,27.4
children.translated_text: By its very nature: water moistens; salt causes discharge; alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>) promotes digestion; honey unites [tissues]; ghee produces unctuousness; milk sustains life; meat nourishes; broth (<s>rasa</s>) satisfies; wine (<s>surā</s>) makes [tissues] flaccid; <s>sīdhu</s> (fermented liquor) scrapes [tissues]; grape-wine (<s>drākṣāsava</s>) kindles [digestion]; jaggery (<s>phāṇita</s>) accumulates [<s>doṣas</s>]; curd generates swelling; <s>piṇyāka</s>-vegetable (sesame-cake greens) causes lassitude; <s>māṣa</s>-bean soup produces much internal waste and destroys vision and semen; alkali is generally <s>pitta</s>-producing; sour [substances] are [<s>pitta</s>-producing] except for pomegranate and <s>āmalaka</s>; sweet is generally <s>śleṣma</s>-producing, except for honey and old [preparations of] <s>ś��li</s> rice, <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, barley, and wheat; bitter is generally <s>vāta</s>-producing and non-aphrodisiac, except for <s>vegāgrā</s>, <s>amṛtā</s> (Tinospora), <s>paṭola</s>, and its leaf; pungent is generally <s>vāta</s>-producing and non-aphrodisiac, except for long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>) and ginger (<s>viśvabheṣaja</s>). // Car 1.27.4
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: annapānaṃ vidhīyate yena taṃ vidhiṃ dravyaguṇakarmarūpaṃ tathā caraśarīrāvayavādirūpaṃ cākhilena kārtsnyenopadekṣyāmaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: We shall teach the regimen in its entirety — that is, in the form of qualities and actions of substances, as well as the forms of living body-parts etc. — by which food and drink are regulated. // 1

children.text: yadyapi ceha dravyaṃ prati prati guṇakarmabhyāṃ na nirdekṣyati vakṣyati hi annapānaikadeśo'yamuktaḥ prāyopayogikaḥ iti tathāpyanuktānām api dravyāṇāṃ caraśarīrāvayavādyupadeśena tathā pūrvādhyāyoktapārthivādidravyaguṇakarmakathanena ca tadvidhānamapyuktaṃ bhavatītyata uktamakhileneti vakṣyati hi yathā nānauṣadhaṃ kiṃcid deśajānāṃ vaco yathā // 2
children.translated_text: Although he will not describe every substance individually with its qualities and actions — for he will state: 'This is only a partial [description] of food and drink, stated as generally applicable' — nevertheless, even for unmentioned substances, through the teaching of living body-parts etc. and through the description of qualities and actions of earthly etc. substances stated in the previous chapter, their regulation too is [implicitly] stated. Therefore he says 'in entirety.' For [the text] will state: 'There is nothing that is not medicine among things born of the land...' // 2

children.text: dravyaṃ tu tattathā vācyamanuktamiha yad bhavet tathā caraḥ śarīrāvayavāḥ ityādi kiṃvā vidhiśabdo 'śitapītalīḍhakhāditaprakāravācī tena cāśitādayaḥ sarva evākhilena vācyaḥ tatkāraṇabhūtāni tu dravyāṇi raktaśālyādīnyekadeśenoktāni ato vakṣyati annapānaikadeśo'yamuktaḥ iti // 3
children.translated_text: 'But that substance which is unmentioned here should be described accordingly' — and 'living [body], body-parts' etc. Or, the word '<s>vidhi</s>' (regimen) refers to the modes of eating, drinking, licking, and chewing. By this, all [modes] — eating etc. — are to be stated in entirety; but the substances that are their causes — red rice etc. — are stated only partially. Therefore [the text] will say: 'This is only a partial [description] of food and drink.' // 3

children.text: annapāne ca vaktavye yaddravyaṃ prāya upayujyate tasya sāmānyaguṇamabhidhāya vargasaṃgraheṇa guṇamupadekṣyati // 4
children.translated_text: And in [the matter of] food and drink to be discussed, having first stated the general quality of the substance that is mostly used, he will teach its qualities through class-wise grouping. // 4

children.text: udakābhidhānaṃ cāgre kṛtam udakasyānne pāne ca vyāpriyamāṇatvāt // 5
children.translated_text: And water is described first because water is involved in both food and drink. // 5

children.text: tad ityudāharaṇaṃ kiṃvā sa svabhāvo yasya sa tatsvabhāvaḥ tasmāt kledanasvabhāvād ityarthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: 'That' is an illustration. Or: 'that whose nature is such' — i.e., by its nature of moistening. // 6

children.text: yadyapi udakamāśvāsakarāṇāṃ jalaṃ stambhanānām ityuktaṃ tathāpīhānuktakledanakarmābhidhānārthaṃ punarucyate // 7
children.translated_text: Although 'water is among life-giving [substances]' and 'water is among astringents' has been stated, here it is stated again for the purpose of declaring the moistening action [which was] unstated [before]. // 7

children.text: iha jalalavaṇādīnāṃ yat karmocyate tatteṣāmitarakarmabhyaḥ pradhānaṃ jñeyam agryādhikāre tu tatkarmakartṛdravyāntarapraśastatā jñeyā // 8
children.translated_text: The action stated here for water, salt, etc. should be known as their predominant action over their other actions. In the <s>Agrya</s> chapter, however, the excellence of other substances performing that same action should be known. // 8

children.text: kṣāraḥ pacantamagniṃ pācayati tena pācayatīti hetau ṇic // 9
children.translated_text: 'Alkali promotes digestion' — it causes the fire to digest; therefore the causative (<s>ṇic</s>) is [used] in the sense of causation. // 9

children.text: snehayatītyādau tu tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe iti ṇic // 10
children.translated_text: In 'produces unctuousness' etc., the causative is by [the rule] 'he does that, he declares that.' // 10
'Unites' means it joins together separated skin, flesh, etc. // 11
'<s>Rasa</s>' (broth) here means meat-broth. // 12

children.text: prīṇayatīti kṣīṇān puṣṇāti na tv atibṛhattvaṃ karoti tena māṃsakarmaṇā bṛṃhaṇena samaṃ naikyam // 13
children.translated_text: 'Satisfies' means it nourishes the depleted without producing excessive bulkiness; therefore it is not identical with 'nourishing,' which is the action of meat. // 13

children.text: jarjarīkarotīti ślathamāṃsādyupacayaṃ karoti yad uktaṃ hārīte surā jarjarīkarotyasṛṅmedobāhulyāt iti tathā hy atraivoktaṃ surā kṛśānāṃ puṣṭyartham iti // 14
children.translated_text: 'Makes flaccid' means it produces a lax accumulation of flesh etc. As stated in <s>Hārīta</s>: 'Wine makes [tissues] flaccid due to abundance of blood and fat.' And here too it is stated: 'Wine is for the nourishment of the emaciated.' // 14

children.text: avadhamayatīti vilikhatītyarthaḥ anekārthatvād dhātūnāṃ vacanaṃ hi lekhanaḥ śītarasikaḥ iti tathā hārīte 'pyuktaṃ sīdhur avadhamayati vāyvagniprabodhanāt iti // 15
children.translated_text: 'Scrapes' means 'scratches' — due to the multiple meanings of verbal roots. For the statement is: '[<s>sīdhu</s> is] scraping, cooling, [and] pleasant.' And in <s>Hārīta</s> too: '<s>Sīdhu</s> scrapes due to awakening <s>vāyu</s> and <s>agni</s>.' // 15

children.text: ācinoti doṣān iti śeṣaḥ tantrāntaravacanaṃ hi vātapittakaphāṃstasmādācinoti ca phāṇitam iti // 16
children.translated_text: 'Accumulates' — supply '<s>doṣas</s>.' For the statement in another treatise is: 'Therefore jaggery accumulates <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.' // 16

children.text: piṇyākaḥ tilakalkaḥ nighaṇṭukāras tv āha piṇyāko haritaśigruḥ // 17
children.translated_text: <s>Piṇyāka</s> is sesame-paste. The lexicographer, however, says: '<s>Piṇyāka</s> is the green <s>śigru</s> (moringa).' // 17
'Causes lassitude' means it causes diminishment of vigor. // 18

children.text: prabhūtāntarmalasya purīṣasya kartā prabhūtāntarmalaḥ yadyapi māṣo bahumalaḥ iti vakṣyati tathāpi māṣavikṛteḥ sūpasyeha guṇakathanaṃ tena na punaruktaṃ na cāvaśyaṃ prakṛtidharmo vikṛtimanugacchati yataḥ saktūnāṃ siddhapiṇḍikā gurvī eva bhavati tasmān māṣavikṛtāv api malavṛddhidarśanārtham etadabhidhānam // 19
children.translated_text: 'Producer of much internal waste' — [means] the producer of [much] fecal matter. Although it will be stated 'beans produce much waste,' here the quality of the preparation (<s>vikṛti</s>) — namely soup — is being stated, so there is no repetition. And it is not necessarily the case that the properties of the raw substance follow into its preparations, since prepared balls of <s>saktus</s> (parched grain) become heavy. Therefore, to show that waste-increase exists even in a bean preparation, this is stated. // 19

children.text: kṣārasya pācanatvaṃ guṇo'bhihitaḥ iha tu dṛṣṭiśukraghnatvaṃ doṣa iti pṛthagucyate // 20
children.translated_text: The digestive property of alkali has been stated as a quality; here, its destruction of vision and semen is stated as a defect — hence it is mentioned separately. // 20
'Generally <s>pitta</s>-producing' — means specifically: sour is more <s>pitta</s>-producing than others — salty and pungent. // 21

children.text: evamanyatrāpi prāyaḥśabdo viśeṣārtho vācyaḥ kiṃvā prāyaḥśabdo'mlena sambadhyate // 22
children.translated_text: Likewise in other cases too, the word 'generally' (<s>prāyaḥ</s>) should be understood as indicating specificity. Or, the word 'generally' is construed with 'sour.' // 22

children.text: atra pittam ādāv amlajanyatayoktaṃ doṣaprādhānyasyāniyatatvāt uktaṃ hi na te pṛthak pittakaphānilebhya iti tathā samapittānilakaphā iti kiṃvā pittoṣmā vahniḥ sa cehānnapānapacane pradhānaṃ yaduktaṃ yadannaṃ dehadhātvojobalavarṇādipoṣakam // 23
children.translated_text: Here, <s>pitta</s> is mentioned first because of being generated by sour [taste] — since the predominance of <s>doṣas</s> is not fixed. For it is stated: 'They are not separate from <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>vāta</s>'; and 'having equal <s>pitta</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.' Or: <s>pitta</s>-heat is fire, and fire is predominant in the digestion of food and drink, as stated: 'That food which nourishes the bodily <s>dhātus</s>, vitality, strength, complexion, etc. — // 23

children.text: tatrāgnir hetur āhārān nahy apakvād rasādayaḥ iti teneha vahnikāraṇapittajanakam evādāv ucyate yataśca pittajanakamagre vaktavyam ato rasapradhānamapi madhuro nādāv uktaḥ // 24
children.translated_text: therein fire is the cause; for <s>rasas</s> etc. [do not arise] from undigested [food].' Therefore, that which generates <s>pitta</s>, the cause of fire, is stated first. And because the <s>pitta</s>-generator must be stated first, even sweet — though predominant among <s>rasas</s> — is not stated first. // 24

children.text: madhuna iti vicchedapāṭhena navānavasya madhunaḥ kaphākartṛtvaṃ darśayati // 25
children.translated_text: 'Of honey' — by reading with a break, it shows that fresh honey does not produce <s>kapha</s>. // 25

children.text: iha ca ṣaḍrasasyaiva kathanametattrayeṇaiva anuktānāṃ lavaṇatiktakaṣāyāṇām api pākadvārā grahaṇāt yato lavaṇaḥ pākāt prāyo madhuraḥ tiktakaṣāyau kaṭukau pākato bhavataḥ // 26
children.translated_text: And here, only the six <s>rasas</s> are being discussed through these three [— sour, sweet, and bitter —]; the unmentioned salty, bitter, and astringent are also included through [their] post-digestive [effects], since salty becomes predominantly sweet after digestion, and bitter and astringent become pungent after digestion. // 26

children.text: prāyaḥ sarvaṃ tiktam ityādistu grantho hārītīyaḥ iha kenāpi pramādāl likhitaḥ // 27]
children.translated_text: The passage 'generally everything bitter...' etc. is from <s>Hārīta</s>'s [text]; here it has been written by someone's error. // 27]
Hereafter, we shall explain the food-substances by class-wise grouping. // Car 1.27.5
The classes of husk-grains (<s>śūkadhānya</s>), legumes (<s>śamīdhānya</s>), meats, vegetables, and fruits;
herbs (<s>harita</s>), wines (<s>madya</s>), waters, milk-products (<s>gorasa</s>), sugarcane-products (<s>ikṣuvikāra</s>); // Car 1.27.6
ten [classes], and two additional classes of prepared foods and food-accessories —
we shall describe [them] with their <s>rasas</s> (tastes), <s>vīryas</s> (potencies), <s>vipākas</s> (post-digestive effects), and <s>prabhāvas</s> (specific potencies). // Car 1.27.7
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
The grouping of food-substances such as husk-grains etc. by class is the 'class-wise grouping.' // 1
In 'tastes, potencies' etc., <s>prabhāva</s> (specific potency) is read separately because it applies to fewer [cases]. // 2

children.text: rasādinirdeśaśca yathāyogyatayā jñeyaḥ tena na sarvadravye sarvarasādyabhidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati // 3
children.translated_text: And the indication of <s>rasas</s> etc. should be understood as applying to each [substance] as appropriate; therefore not every <s>rasa</s> etc. will be stated for every substance. // 3

children.text: atra śūkadhānyam ādāv āhārapradhānatvāt śūkavanti dhānyāni śūkadhānyāni // 4]
children.translated_text: Here, husk-bearing grains (<s>śūkadhānya</s>) are [discussed] first because of the primacy of food. Grains that possess husks are 'husk-bearing grains.' // 4]
<s>Raktaśāli</s> (red rice), <s>Mahāśāli</s> (great rice), <s>Kalama</s>, <s>Śakunāhṛta</s> (bird-brought),

children.text: tūrṇako dīrghaśūkaś ca gauraḥ pāṇḍukalāṅgulau // Car_1,27.8
children.translated_text: <s>Tūrṇaka</s>, <s>Dīrghaśūka</s> (long-awned), <s>Gaura</s> (white), <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, and <s>Kalāṅgula</s>, // Car_1,27.8
<s>Sugandhaka</s> (fragrant), <s>Lohavāla</s>, <s>Sārivākhya</s>, <s>Pramodaka</s>,

children.text: pataṃgas tapanīyaśca ye cānye śālayaḥ śubhāḥ // Car_1,27.9
children.translated_text: <s>Pataṃga</s>, <s>Tapanīya</s> (golden), and whatever other auspicious <s>śāli</s> rices [there are] — // Car_1,27.9
[they are] cold in taste and in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), sweet, with little wind [aggravation],
producing compact and scant feces, unctuous, bulk-promoting, and semen-promoting. // Car_1,27.10
<s>Raktaśāli</s> is the best among them — it destroys thirst and removes the three wastes (<s>malas</s>);
<s>Mahāśāli</s> [ranks] next to it, <s>Kalama</s> next to that, and the rest thereafter. // Car_1,27.11
<s>Yavaka</s>, <s>Hāyana</s>, <s>Pāṃsuvāpya</s>, <s>Naiṣadhaka</s>, and the like —
imitate the <s>śāli</s> rices in both their virtues and faults. // Car_1,27.12
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: iha ca dravyanāmāni nānādeśaprasiddhāni tena nāmajñāne sāmarthyaṃ tathābhūtaṃ nāstyevānyeṣām api ṭīkākṛtāṃ tena deśāntaribhyo nāma prāyaśo jñeyaṃ yattu pracarati gauḍe tal likhiṣyāmo 'nyadeśaprasiddhaṃ ca kiṃcit // 1
children.translated_text: Here, the names of substances are well-known in various regions. Therefore, others — even other commentators — do not have the full competence to know the names. Hence the names should mostly be known from [people of] other regions. Whatever is current in <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal), that we shall write — and also some [names] well-known in other regions. // 1
<s>Kalama</s> is well-known by its own name in <s>Vedāgrahāras</s> (Brahmin settlements). // 2
<s>Śakunāhṛta</s> is well-known by the name <s>Vakra</s> in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. // 3
<s>Raktaśāli</s> is well-known [everywhere]. // 4
<s>Mahāśāli</s> is well-known in <s>Magadha</s>. // 5

children.text: atra ca śālirhaimantikaṃ dhānyaṃ ṣaṣṭikādayaśca graiṣmikāḥ vrīhayaḥ śāradā iti vyavasthā // 6
children.translated_text: And here the arrangement is: <s>śāli</s> is a winter grain; <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> and the like are summer [grains]; <s>vrīhi</s> rices are autumnal. // 6
The property of <s>Raktaśāli</s> etc. of producing compact feces, despite being sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, is due to <s>prabhāva</s> (inherent potency) alone. // 7

children.text: mahāṃstasyānviti raktaśāleranu tena raktaśāliguṇā mahāśāler manāgalpāḥ evaṃ tasyānu kalama ityatrāpi vācyam // 8
children.translated_text: '<s>Mahāśāli</s> [ranks] next to it' — meaning next to <s>Raktaśāli</s>; thus the qualities of <s>Mahāśāli</s> are slightly less than those of <s>Raktaśāli</s>. The same should be said regarding '<s>Kalama</s> next to that.' // 8
'To that' refers to <s>Mahāśāli</s>. // 9

children.text: tataḥ pare iti śakunāhṛtādayaḥ uttarottaramalpaguṇā ityarthaḥ // 10
children.translated_text: 'The rest thereafter' means <s>Śakunāhṛta</s> and the others — each successively of lesser quality. // 10

children.text: guṇāguṇair iti śālīnāṃ raktaśālyādīnāṃ ye guṇās tṛṣṇāghnatvatrimalāpahatvādayaḥ teṣām aguṇais tadguṇaviparītair doṣair yavakādayo 'nukāraṃ kurvanti tataśca yavakās tṛṣṇātrimalādikarā iti // 11
children.translated_text: 'In virtues and faults' — the 'virtues' of the <s>śāli</s> rices like <s>Raktaśāli</s> etc. are the qualities of thirst-destruction, removal of the three <s>malas</s>, and so forth; the 'faults' (<s>aguṇa</s>) — the defects opposite to those virtues — are imitated by <s>Yavaka</s> and the like. Thus <s>Yavaka</s>s cause thirst, the three <s>malas</s>, and so on. // 11
And the word 'quality' (<s>guṇa</s>) here is in the sense of praise. // 12]
Cold, unctuous, not heavy, sweet, destroying all three <s>doṣas</s>, firm in nature —

children.text: ṣaṣṭikaḥ pravaro gauraḥ kṛṣṇagaurastato'nu ca // Car_1,27.13
children.translated_text: <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice) is the best; <s>Gaura</s> (white [ṣaṣṭika]) and <s>Kṛṣṇagaura</s> [rank] next to it. // Car_1,27.13
<s>Varaka</s>, <s>Uddālaka</s>, <s>Cīna</s>, <s>Śārada</s>, <s>Ujjvala</s>, <s>Dardura</s>,
<s>Gandhana</s>, and <s>Kuruvinda</s> — differ from <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> only slightly in qualities. // Car_1,27.14
Sweet and sour in <s>vipāka</s>, <s>vrīhi</s> (autumn rice) is <s>Pitta</s>-producing and heavy;

children.text: bahupurīṣoṣmā tridoṣas tv eva pāṭalaḥ // Car_1,27.15
children.translated_text: it produces abundant feces and heat; but <s>Pāṭala</s> [rice] aggravates all three <s>doṣas</s>. // Car_1,27.15
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: ṣaṣṭikaguṇe 'kārapraśleṣād agururiti boddhavyaṃ mātrāśitīye ṣaṣṭiko laghuḥ paṭhitaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: In the qualities of <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s>, 'not heavy' (<s>aguru</s>) should be understood from the elision of the vowel; in the <s>Mātrāśitīya</s> [chapter], <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> is read as 'light.' // 1
'Next to it' — [meaning] of slightly lesser quality than the white <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s>. // 2

children.text: varakoddālakādayaḥ ṣaṣṭikaviśeṣāḥ kecit kudhānyāni varakādīni vadanti // 3
children.translated_text: <s>Varaka</s>, <s>Uddālaka</s>, and the like are varieties of <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s>. Some call <s>Varaka</s> and the like inferior grains (<s>kudhānya</s>). // 3
'<s>Vrīhi</s>' is the name for the autumnal quick-ripening grain. // 4
<s>Pāṭala</s> is a variety of <s>vrīhi</s>. // 5

children.text: tantrāntare'pi paṭhyate tridoṣastveva pāṭalaḥ iti suśrute pāṭalaśabdenaitadvyatirikto dhānyaviśeṣo jñeyaḥ tena tadguṇakathanena neha virodhaḥ // 6]
children.translated_text: In other treatises too it is read: '<s>Pāṭala</s> indeed aggravates all three <s>doṣas</s>.' In <s>Suśruta</s>, by the word '<s>Pāṭala</s>' a different grain variety should be understood. Therefore, the description of its qualities [there] does not contradict [what is said] here. // 6]
Together with <s>Koradūṣa</s>, <s>Śyāmāka</s> (millet) is astringent-sweet, light,
wind-producing, destroyer of <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>, cold, constipating, and desiccating. // Car_1,27.16
<s>Hastiśyāmāka</s>, <s>Nīvāra</s> (wild rice), <s>Toyaparṇī</s>, <s>Gavedhuka</s>,
<s>Praśāntikā</s>, <s>Ambhaḥśyāmāka</s>, <s>Lauhitya</s>, <s>Aṇupriyaṅgu</s>, // Car_1,27.17
<s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Jhiṇṭī</s>, <s>Garmūṭī</s>, <s>Varukā</s>, <s>Varaka</s>, likewise
<s>Śibira</s>, <s>Utkaṭa</s>, and <s>Jūrṇāhva</s> — are similar to <s>Śyāmāka</s> in qualities. // Car_1,27.18
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
<s>Koradūṣa</s> and the like are varieties of inferior grains (<s>kudhānya</s>). // 1

children.text: koradūṣaḥ kodravaḥ koradūṣasya kevalasya śleṣmapittaghnatvaṃ tena yaduktaṃ raktapittanidāne yadā janturyavakoddālakakoradūṣaprāyāṇy annāni bhuṅkte ityādinā pittakartṛtvaṃ koradūṣasya tat tatraivoktaniṣpāvakāñjikādiyuktasya saṃyogamahimnā boddhavyam // 2
children.translated_text: <s>Koradūṣa</s> is <s>Kodrava</s> (Kodo millet). The <s>Kapha</s>-and-<s>Pitta</s>-destroying property belongs to <s>Koradūṣa</s> alone. Therefore, what is stated in the chapter on the etiology of bleeding disorders — 'when a person eats food consisting mainly of <s>Yavaka</s>, <s>Uddālaka</s>, and <s>Koradūṣa</s>' — attributing <s>Pitta</s>-causing property to <s>Koradūṣa</s> — that should be understood there as due to the power of combination with <s>Niṣpāva</s>, <s>Kāñjika</s>, and the like mentioned in that context. // 2
<s>Śyāmāka</s> and the like are also varieties of grass-grains (<s>tṛṇadhānya</s>). // 3

children.text: hastiśyāmākaḥ śyāmākabheda eva nīvāra uḍikā gavedhuko ghuluñcaḥ sa grāmyāraṇyabhedena dvividhaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: <s>Hastiśyāmāka</s> is a variety of <s>Śyāmāka</s> itself. <s>Nīvāra</s> is <s>Uḍikā</s>. <s>Gavedhuka</s> is <s>Ghuluñca</s> — it is of two kinds: cultivated and wild. // 4

children.text: praśāntikā uḍikaiva sthalajā raktaśūkā ambhaḥśyāmākā jalajā oḍikā loke ḍe ityucyate priyaṅguḥ kāṅganī iti prasiddhā // 5
