children.translated_text: <s>Praśāntikā</s> is the same as <s>Uḍikā</s> growing on dry land, with red husks. <s>Ambhaḥśyāmāka</s> is the aquatic <s>Oḍikā</s>, known in common speech as <s>Ḍe</s>. <s>Priyaṅgu</s> is well-known as <s>Kāṅganī</s>. // 5

children.text: mukundo vākasatṛṇa iti varukaḥ śaṇabījaṃ varakaḥ śyāmabījaṃ śibiras tīrabhuktau siddhaka ityucyate jūrṇāhvo jonāra iti khyātaḥ // 6]
children.translated_text: <s>Mukunda</s> is <s>Vākasatṛṇa</s>. <s>Varuka</s> is hemp-seed. <s>Varaka</s> is <s>Śyāmabīja</s> (dark seed). <s>Śibira</s> is called <s>Siddhaka</s> in the <s>Tīrabhukti</s> region. <s>Jūrṇāhva</s> is well-known as <s>Jonāra</s> (sorghum). // 6]
Dry, cold, not heavy, sweet, producing abundant wind and feces — [such is] barley (<s>yava</s>);
firmness-producing, with an astringent secondary taste, strengthening, and destroyer of <s>Kapha</s> disorders. // Car_1,27.19
Dry, with an astringent secondary taste, sweet, destroyer of <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>,
destroyer of fat, worms, and poison, and strengthening — bamboo-grain (<s>veṇuyava</s>) is considered [thus]. // Car_1,27.20
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: yavasya gurorapi bahuvātatvaṃ rūkṣatvāt kiṃvā suśrute yavo laghuḥ paṭhitaḥ tenātrāpyagururiti mantavyaṃ balyaśca srotaḥśuddhikaratvāt prabhāvādvā // 1
children.translated_text: Barley's property of producing abundant wind despite being heavy is due to its dryness. Or, in <s>Suśruta</s>, barley is read as 'light'; therefore here too 'not heavy' should be understood. And it is 'strengthening' because of its property of purifying the channels — or through <s>prabhāva</s>. // 1

children.text: asya ca śītamadhurakaṣāyatvenānuktamapi pittahantṛtvaṃ labhyata eva tena suśrute kaphapittahantā ityuktamupapannam // 2]
children.translated_text: Its <s>Pitta</s>-destroying property, though not explicitly stated, is obtained from its being cold, sweet, and astringent. Therefore, what is stated in <s>Suśruta</s> — 'it destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>' — is appropriate. // 2]
Healing, wind-destroying, wheat (<s>godhūma</s>) is sweet and cooling,

children.text: jīvano bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ snigdhaḥ sthairyakaro guruḥ // Car_1,27.21
children.translated_text: life-giving, bulk-promoting, aphrodisiac, unctuous, firmness-producing, and heavy. // Car_1,27.21
<s>Nāndīmukhī</s> and <s>Madhūlī</s> are sweet, unctuous, and cooling.

children.text: ityayaṃ śūkadhānyānāṃ pūrvo vargaḥ samāpyate // Car_1,27.22
children.translated_text: Thus this first group of husk-bearing grains (<s>śūkadhānya</s>) is concluded. // Car_1,27.22
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: godhūmasya svāduśītasnigdhādiguṇopayogāc chleṣmakartṛtvaṃ bhavatyeva ata eva suśrute śleṣmakara ityuktam // 1
children.translated_text: Wheat's <s>Kapha</s>-producing property arises from the combination of its sweet, cold, unctuous, and similar qualities. Therefore, what is stated in <s>Suśruta</s> — '<s>Kapha</s>-producing' — is appropriate. // 1

children.text: yattu vasante kaphapradhāne yavagodhūmabhojanaḥ ityuktaṃ tat purāṇagodhūmābhiprāyeṇa purāṇaśca godhūmaḥ kaphaṃ na karotītyuktam eva prāyaḥ śleṣmalaṃ madhuram ityādinā granthenātraivādhyāye // 2
children.translated_text: As for the statement 'in spring, when <s>Kapha</s> is predominant, one should eat barley and wheat' — that is with reference to aged wheat. And it has been stated that aged wheat does not produce <s>Kapha</s> — in this very chapter, by the text 'what is sweet is generally <s>Kapha</s>-producing' and so on. // 2
<s>Nandīmukhī</s> is a kind of barley; <s>Madhūlī</s> is a variety of wheat. // 3
'Thus here' — // 3
'Thus' (<s>iti</s>) is in the sense of 'in this manner.' // 4

children.text: samāpta iti vaktavye samāpyata iti yat karoti tena jñāpayati yat bahudravyatvān nāyaṃ samāpto gaṇaḥ kiṃtu yathā kathaṃcit prasiddhaguṇakathanena samāpyate // 5
children.translated_text: Where 'is concluded' (<s>samāpta</s>) should be said, by saying 'is being concluded' (<s>samāpyate</s>) [the author] indicates that this group is not [fully] concluded because of the large number of substances, but is somehow concluded through the description of qualities of the well-known [ones]. // 5

children.text: evamanyatrāpi ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ samāpyata ityādau vyākhyeyam // 6]
children.translated_text: The same should be explained elsewhere too — in 'the sixth group is being concluded' and the like. // 6]

children.text: kaṣāyamadhuro rūkṣaḥ śītaḥ pāke kaṭur laghuḥ /
children.translated_text: Astringent-sweet, dry, cold, pungent in <s>vipāka</s>, light,

children.text: viśadaḥ śleṣmapittaghno mudgaḥ sūpyottamo mataḥ // Car_1,27.23
children.translated_text: clear, destroyer of <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s> — <s>Mudga</s> (green gram) is considered the best among pulse-foods (<s>sūpya</s>). // Car_1,27.23

children.text: vṛṣyaḥ paraṃ vātaharaḥ snigdhoṣṇo madhuro guruḥ /
children.translated_text: Supremely aphrodisiac, wind-destroying, unctuous, hot, sweet, heavy,

children.text: balyo bahumalaḥ puṃstvaṃ māṣaḥ śīghraṃ dadāti ca // Car_1,27.24
children.translated_text: strengthening, producing abundant waste — <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram) quickly gives virility. // Car_1,27.24
<s>Rājamāṣa</s> (cowpea) is laxative, appetizing, destroyer of <s>Kapha</s>, semen, and sour-<s>Pitta</s>;

children.text: tatsvādurvātalo rūkṣaḥ kaṣāyo viśado guruḥ // Car_1,27.25
children.translated_text: it is sweet like that [<s>Māṣa</s>], wind-producing, dry, astringent, clear, and heavy. // Car_1,27.25
Hot, astringent, sour in <s>vipāka</s>, destroyers of <s>Kapha</s>, semen, and wind —
<s>Kulattha</s> (horse gram) is constipating, and beneficial in cough, hiccup, dyspnea, and hemorrhoids. // Car_1,27.26
Sweet, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, constipating, dry, and cold —
<s>Makuṣṭhaka</s> (moth bean) is recommended in bleeding disorders (<s>raktapitta</s>), fever, and the like. // Car_1,27.27
<s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea), <s>Masūra</s> (lentil), <s>Khaṇḍikā</s>, together with <s>Hareṇu</s> —
[are] light, cold, sweet, with an astringent [taste], and desiccating. // Car_1,27.28
They are recommended in [conditions of] <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>, in soups, and in poultices;

children.text: teṣāṃ masūraḥ saṃgrāhī kalāyo vātalaḥ param // Car_1,27.29
children.translated_text: among them, <s>Masūra</s> (lentil) is constipating, and <s>Kalāya</s> (pea) is especially wind-producing. // Car_1,27.29
Unctuous, hot, sweet, bitter, astringent, and pungent — [such is] sesame (<s>tila</s>);

children.text: tvacyaḥ keśyaśca balyaśca vātaghnaḥ kaphapittakṛt // Car_1,27.30
children.translated_text: beneficial for the skin, good for the hair, strengthening, wind-destroying, and producing <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s>. // Car_1,27.30
Sweet, cold, heavy, strength-reducing, and of a desiccating nature,

children.text: sasnehā balibhir bhojyā vividhāḥ śimbijātayaḥ // Car_1,27.31
children.translated_text: slightly unctuous, to be eaten with [proper] preparation — [such are] the various species of legumes (<s>śimbi</s>). // Car_1,27.31

children.text: śimbī rūkṣā kaṣāyā ca koṣṭhe vātaprakopinī /
children.translated_text: The [generic] legume (<s>śimbī</s>) is dry and astringent, wind-aggravating in the bowels,

children.text: na ca vṛṣyā na cakṣuṣyā viṣṭabhya ca vipacyate // Car_1,27.32
children.translated_text: neither aphrodisiac nor good for the eyes, and digests after causing distension. // Car_1,27.32
<s>Āḍhakī</s> (pigeon pea) destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Pitta</s> [but is] wind-producing; [it] destroys <s>Kapha</s> and <s>Vāta</s> [in certain forms].
<s>Avalguja</s> and <s>Iḍagaja</s> [likewise]; <s>Niṣpāva</s> (flat bean) aggravates wind and <s>Pitta</s>. // Car_1,27.33
The fruits of <s>Kākāṇḍa</s>, <s>Ūmā</s> (flax), and <s>Ātmaguptā</s> should be indicated as [having properties] like <s>Māṣa</s>.
This second group — the pod-bearing grains (<s>śamīdhānya</s>) — has been declared by the great sage. // Car_1,27.34
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
Among the pod-bearing grains to be discussed in the <s>śamīdhānya</s> group, <s>Mudga</s> (green gram) is described [first] because of its primacy as a grain. // 1
'Pulse-food' (<s>sūpya</s>) means suitable for soup — [i.e.,] pod-bearing grain. The best among those is 'the best pulse-food' (<s>sūpyottama</s>). // 2

children.text: vṛṣya ityādimāṣaguṇe snigdhoṣṇamadhuratvādiguṇayogādeva vātaharatve labdhe punastadabhidhānaṃ viśeṣavātahantṛtvapratipādanārtham evamanyatrāpyevaṃjātīye vyākhyeyam // 3
children.translated_text: In the qualities of <s>Māṣa</s> beginning with 'aphrodisiac' — since its wind-destroying property is already obtained from the conjunction of qualities such as unctuousness, heat, sweetness, etc., the re-statement is for the purpose of indicating its especially [potent] wind-destroying capacity. The same should be explained similarly elsewhere in such cases. // 3
'Virility' (<s>puṃstva</s>) means semen. // 4

children.text: śīghramiti vacanena śukrasrutikaratvalakṣaṇamapi vṛṣyatvaṃ māṣasya darśayati śukrasrutikaraṃ ca vṛṣyaśabdenocyata eva vacanaṃ hi śukrasrutikaraṃ kiṃcit kiṃcit śukravivardhanam // 5
children.translated_text: By the word 'quickly,' [the author] shows that the aphrodisiac quality of <s>Māṣa</s> is characterized by causing the flow of semen. And the causing of semen-flow is indeed denoted by the word 'aphrodisiac' (<s>vṛṣya</s>). For the text states: 'Some [substances] cause the flow of semen; some augment semen; // 5

children.text: srutivṛddhikaraṃ kiṃcittrividhaṃ vṛṣyamucyate iti tadevaṃ sampūrṇavṛṣyatvaṃ māṣe boddhavyam // 6
children.translated_text: some cause both flow and augmentation — the aphrodisiac is said to be threefold.' Thus, the complete threefold aphrodisiac quality should be understood in <s>Māṣa</s>. // 6

children.text: rājamāṣaguṇakathane tatsvāduriti māṣavatsvāduḥ kiṃvā rūkṣaścetyādi pāṭhāntaram // 7
children.translated_text: In the statement of the qualities of <s>Rājamāṣa</s>, 'sweet like that' means sweet like <s>Māṣa</s>. Or alternatively, the reading 'dry etc.' is a variant. // 7

children.text: uṣṇa ityādinā kulatthaguṇaḥ kulatthaśca śuklakṛṣṇacitralohitabhedena caturvidho bhavati tathā grāmyavanyabhedena ca dvividho'pi ata eva tantrāntare vanyaḥ kulatthastadvacca viśeṣān netraroganut ityuktam // 8
children.translated_text: By 'hot' and so on, the qualities of <s>Kulattha</s> [are stated]. <s>Kulattha</s> is of four kinds: white, black, variegated, and red. It is also of two kinds: cultivated and wild. Therefore, in other treatises it is stated: 'Wild <s>Kulattha</s>, and its varieties — [are] especially curative of eye-diseases.' // 8
<s>Makuṣṭaka</s> is well-known as <s>Moṭha</s>. // 9
<s>Caṇaka</s> (chickpea) is well-known. // 10
<s>Khaṇḍikā</s> is the triangular pea (<s>tripuṭakalāya</s>). <s>Hareṇu</s> is the round pea (<s>vartulakalāya</s>). // 11
'<s>Kalāya</s> is wind-producing' — [this refers to] the triangular pea. // 12

children.text: tilaguṇo yadyapi viśeṣeṇa noktaḥ tathāpi pradhāne kṛṣṇatile jñeyaḥ uktaṃ hi suśrute tileṣu sarveṣvasitaḥ pradhāno madhyaḥ sito hīnatarās tato'nye iti // 13
children.translated_text: The qualities of sesame, although not stated with specificity, should be understood as pertaining primarily to black sesame. For it is stated in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'Among all sesame seeds, the black is primary; the white is middling; and the others are inferior.' // 13
'Various species of legumes' means [those with] varieties such as black, yellow, red, white, and <s>Kuśimbī</s> legumes. // 14
'The legume is dry' etc. — some [manuscripts] read [this verse]. // 14
'<s>Āḍhakī</s> is <s>Tuvarī</s> (pigeon pea), wind-producing' — this is a sentence-break. // 15
'<s>Kapha</s>-and-<s>Vāta</s>-destroying' is the quality of the seeds of <s>Avalguja</s> and <s>Iḍagaja</s>. // 16
<s>Niṣpāva</s> is <s>Valla</s> (flat bean). // 17

children.text: kākāṇḍaḥ śūkaraśimbiḥ umā atasī ūrṇāṃpāṭhapakṣe tasyaivorṇā // 18
children.translated_text: <s>Kākāṇḍa</s> is <s>Śūkaraśimbi</s> (pig-legume). <s>Ūmā</s> is flax (<s>Atasī</s>). In the reading <s>Ūrṇā</s>, it refers to its fiber. // 18

children.text: śamīdhānyavarga ityatra śamī śimbiḥ tadantargataṃ dhānyam // 19]
children.translated_text: In '<s>śamīdhānya</s>-group' — <s>śamī</s> means pod; the grain contained within it [is <s>śamīdhānya</s>]. // 19]
Cow, donkey, mule, camel, horse, leopard, lion, bear, monkey,
wolf, tiger, hyena, mongoose, cat, mouse, // Car_1,27.35
<s>Lopāka</s> (jackal), <s>Jambuka</s> (fox), hawk, <s>Vāntāda</s> (vulture-type), <s>Cāṣa</s> (blue jay), crow,
<s>Śaśaghnī</s> (hare-killer/eagle), honey-eater, <s>Bhāsa</s> (kite), vulture, owl, sparrow, // Car_1,27.36
<s>Dhūmikā</s> (smoky hawk), <s>Kurara</s> (osprey) — these are the 'seizing' (<s>prasaha</s>) animals and birds.
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
After pulse-foods, the meat group is discussed because of the primacy of meat as a condiment [to rice]. // 1

children.text: kharaḥ gardabhaḥ aśvataraḥ vegasaraḥ sa cāśvāyāṃ kharājjātaḥ dvīpī citravyāghraḥ ṛkṣaḥ bhallūkaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: '<s>Khara</s>' is donkey. '<s>Aśvatara</s>' is <s>Vegasara</s> (mule) — it is born from a donkey upon a mare. '<s>Dvīpī</s>' is the spotted tiger (leopard). '<s>Ṛkṣa</s>' is bear. // 2

children.text: vṛkaḥ kukkurānukārī paśuśatruḥ tarakṣuḥ vyāghrabhedaḥ taraccha iti khyātaḥ babhruḥ atilomaśaḥ kukkuraḥ parvatopakaṇṭhe bhavati kecid bṛhannakulam āhuḥ // 3
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛka</s> (wolf) imitates dogs and is an enemy of cattle. <s>Tarakṣu</s> is a variety of tiger, known as <s>Taraccha</s> (hyena). <s>Babhru</s> is an exceedingly hairy dog found near mountains; some call it the large mongoose. // 3
<s>Lopāka</s> is a small jackal with a large tail. // 4
<s>Śyena</s> (hawk) is a well-known bird. // 5
<s>Vāntāda</s> (the vomit-eater) is the dog. // 6

Those that devour by force (<s>prasahya</s>) are named <s>prasaha</s> (predatory). // Car_1,27.53
The hole-dwellers (<s>bhūśaya</s>) are so called from dwelling in burrows; the marshy (<s>ānūpa</s>), from inhabiting marshy regions;
the aquatic (<s>jalaja</s>), from living in water; the water-roaming (<s>jalecara</s>), from moving in water. // Car_1,27.54
The land-born (<s>sthalaja</s>) are called dry-land (<s>jāṅgala</s>) animals, as they roam in arid regions;

children.text: prasahā dvividhā māṃsādā vyāghraśyenādayaḥ tathā amāṃsādāśca gavādayaḥ tena māṃsādānāṃ viśeṣamāha prasahānām ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: The predatory (<s>prasaha</s>) animals are of two kinds: meat-eaters like the tiger, hawk, etc., and non-meat-eaters like cattle, etc. Therefore, he states the special [property] of meat-eaters with 'of the predatory,' etc. // 1
By the word 'chronic' (<s>jīrṇa</s>), he shows the long-standing nature of hemorrhoids and the like. // 2

children.text: pratudā ityatra tathā jāṅgalā ityatra cakāro luptanirdiṣṭaḥ // 3

'Where <s>Kapha</s> follows' — this is the point of division [in the sentence]. // 4]
Goat meat (<s>āja</s>) is not excessively cold, heavy, or unctuous; it is non-vitiating of the <s>doṣas</s>. // Car_1,27.61
Due to its similarity to the bodily tissues, it is non-obstructive and nourishing.
Sheep meat (<s>āvika</s>), being sweet and cold, is heavy and nourishing. // Car_1,27.62
In the classification, goats and sheep are not fixed [in any one category], because of their mixed grazing habits.

'Due to similarity to the bodily tissues' means due to its resemblance to human flesh. // 1

children.text: etena śītagurusnigdhatvena yuktam apyājamāṃsaṃ śarīradhātusāmyāt kaphaṃ na karotītyuktaṃ bhavati // 2

children.translated_text: But in the chapter on the etiology of bleeding disorders (<s>Raktapitta</s>), the statement 'pork, buffalo...' etc. — the production of bleeding by sheep meat should be understood only when combined with other substances. // 4
'In the classification' means in the eightfold classification of <s>prasaha</s>, etc. // 5

children.text: miśragocaratvāditi kadācidanūpasevanāt kadācid dhanvasevanāt kadācid ubhayasevanād ajāvyor aniścitayonitvam ityarthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: 'Due to mixed grazing habits' means that goats and sheep sometimes frequent marshy areas, sometimes arid regions, and sometimes both — hence their classification is undetermined. // 6

children.text: atra aniścite iti yoniviśeṣaṇaṃ kiṃvā ajā ca avī ca ete aniścite // 7
children.translated_text: Here, 'undetermined' qualifies the classification. Alternatively, 'goat and sheep — these [are] undetermined.' // 7

children.text: nanu yadyevaṃ tadā tittirirapi dhanvānūpasevanānna viṣkiragaṇe paṭhanīyaḥ // 8
children.translated_text: Now, [one may object]: if so, then the francolin (<s>tittiri</s>) too, since it frequents both arid and marshy areas, should not be listed in the <s>viṣkira</s> (gallinaceous) group. // 8

children.text: naivaṃ tittirijātiviśeṣasya dhanvānūpayor niyamena niṣevaṇād guṇaniyamaḥ pāryate kartum avyajayostu niyamo'yaṃ nāsti yataḥ kecidajāvī dhanvamātracare keciccānūpamātracare keciccobhayamātracare tena tayor niyamacarakṛto yonibhedaḥ kartuṃ na pāryate // 9]
children.translated_text: Not so, because the francolin as a specific species invariably frequents either the arid or marshy [but not mixed] — hence a fixed rule of properties can be made. But for goats and sheep this fixity does not exist, since some goats and sheep graze only in arid areas, some only in marshy areas, and some in both — therefore no classification based on fixed grazing habit can be established for them. // 9]
Of the meats that have been described in general terms, individually by their own properties, // Car_1,27.63
the special [properties] of some will be taught, due to their distinctive quality-characteristics.
For vision, hearing, intelligence, digestive fire, age, complexion, voice, and lifespan, // Car_1,27.64
the peacock is the most beneficial; it is strengthening, alleviates <s>Vāta</s>, and increases flesh and semen.
[The meats of the first five groups are] heavy, hot, unctuous, and sweet; they promote voice, complexion, and strength. // Car_1,27.65
Swans (<s>haṃsa</s>) are said to be nourishing, promoting semen, and destroying <s>vāta</s> (wind);
they are unctuous, hot, aphrodisiac, nourishing, and voice-promoting. // Car_1,27.66
Strength-giving and supremely <s>vāta</s>-destroying, the foot-armed [birds, i.e., roosters] are sudorific;
the partridge is heavy, hot, and sweet — not excessively so — because it frequents both arid and marshy regions. // Car_1,27.67
The partridge (<s>tittiri</s>) quickly pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s> in which wind predominates;
grey partridges (<s>kapiñjala</s>) are recommended in disorders of <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> associated with blood, // Car_1,27.68
and in conditions of mild <s>vāta</s> — because of their coldness, sweetness, and lightness.
Quails (<s>lāva</s>) are astringent and sweet, light, and fire-kindling; // Car_1,27.69
they pacify the combined [derangement of all three] <s>doṣas</s> and are pungent in post-digestive effect.

children.text: godhā vipāke madhurā kaṣāyakaṭukā rase // Car_1,27.70
children.translated_text: The monitor lizard (<s>godhā</s>) is sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, astringent and pungent in taste; // Car_1,27.70
it pacifies <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is nourishing, and strength-increasing.

children.text: śallako madhurāmlaśca vipāke kaṭukaḥ smṛtaḥ // Car_1,27.71
children.translated_text: The porcupine (<s>śallaka</s>) is sweet and sour, and is said to be pungent in <s>vipāka</s>; // Car_1,27.71
it destroys <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, and removes cough and dyspnea.
Astringent, clear, cold, and suppressing hemorrhagic disorders (<s>raktapitta</s>), // Car_1,27.72
sweet in <s>vipāka</s> — [such are] domestic pigeons (<s>kapota</s>).
Somewhat lighter than them are wild pigeons (<s>kapota</s>). // Car_1,27.73
They are cold, astringent, and produce scanty urine.
Parrot-meat (<s>śuka-māṃsa</s>) is astringent and sour, dry and cold in <s>vipāka</s>; // Car_1,27.74
it is beneficial in consumption, cough, and wasting — astringent, light, and appetizing.
Sparrows (<s>caṭaka</s>) are sweet, unctuous, and increase strength and semen; // Car_1,27.75
they pacify combined <s>doṣa</s>-derangement and pacify <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: kaṣāyo viśado rūkṣaḥ śītaḥ pāke kaṭurlaghuḥ // Car_1,27.76
children.translated_text: Astringent, clear, dry, cold, pungent in <s>vipāka</s>, and light — // Car_1,27.76
the hare (<s>śaśa</s>) is sweet and recommended in combined <s>doṣa</s>-derangement with wind as the least [deranged].

children.text: madhurā madhurāḥ pāke tridoṣaśamanāḥ śivāḥ // Car_1,27.77
children.translated_text: Sweet, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, pacifying all three <s>doṣas</s>, auspicious, // Car_1,27.77
light, binding of feces and urine, and cold — so are declared the spotted deer (<s>eṇa</s>).
Boar-meat (<s>varāha</s>) is unctuous, nourishing, aphrodisiac, fatigue-destroying, <s>vāta</s>-removing, // Car_1,27.78
strength-giving, appetizing, sudorific, and heavy.
Beef (<s>gavya</s>) is [useful] in pure <s>vāta</s> conditions, in nasal catarrh, in intermittent fever, // Car_1,27.79
and is beneficial in dry cough, fatigue, excessive digestive fire, and muscle-wasting.

children.text: snigdhoṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ vṛṣyaṃ māhiṣaṃ guru tarpaṇam // Car_1,27.80
children.translated_text: Buffalo-meat (<s>māhiṣa</s>) is unctuous, hot, sweet, aphrodisiac, heavy, and satiating; // Car_1,27.80
it produces firmness, largeness of body, vigor, and also sleep.

children.text: gurūṣṇā madhurā balyā bṛṃhaṇāḥ pavanāpahāḥ // Car_1,27.81
children.translated_text: Fish (<s>matsya</s>) are heavy, hot, sweet, strength-giving, nourishing, and <s>vāta</s>-removing; // Car_1,27.81
they are unctuous, aphrodisiac, and declared to be highly <s>doṣa</s>-producing —
because of feeding on moss and sprouts, and because of avoidance of sleep. // Car_1,27.82
The <s>Rohita</s> fish is appetizing, light in digestion, and of great strength;
complexion-promoting, <s>vāta</s>-destroying, aphrodisiac, eye-promoting, and strength-increasing. // Car_1,27.83
The turtle (<s>kūrma</s>) is said to promote intellect and memory, is wholesome and consumption-destroying;
rhinoceros-meat (<s>khaḍga-māṃsa</s>) is secretion-producing, strength-giving, and said to be sweet; // Car_1,27.84
it is unctuous, nourishing, complexion-promoting, fatigue-destroying, and <s>vāta</s>-removing.
The eggs of <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> geese, <s>Cakora</s> partridges, domestic chickens (<s>dakṣa</s>), peacocks, // Car_1,27.85

children.text: caṭakānāṃ ca yāni syur aṇḍāni ca hitāni ca /
children.translated_text: and sparrows — these are [declared] beneficial

children.text: kṣīṇaretaḥsu kāseṣu hṛdrogeṣu kṣateṣu ca // Car_1,27.86
children.translated_text: for those with depleted semen, in coughs, in heart diseases, and in consumption. // Car_1,27.86
They are sweet, non-irritating, and immediately strength-giving.
For nourishing the body, no other food excels meat. // Car_1,27.87
Thus is declared this third class — that of meats.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Of some' (<s>keṣāṃcit</s>) refers to the forthcoming peacock and the like. // 1
'Because of the distinction of qualities' means: because of possessing distinguished qualities. // 2

children.text: mayūrasya gurutvasnigdhatvaṃ vartakādigaṇapaṭhitatvenaiva labdhaṃ sat punarucyate viśeṣārtham // 3
children.translated_text: The heaviness and unctuousness of the peacock, already obtained by its being listed in the <s>vartaka</s> (quail) and similar group, is stated again for the purpose of specification. // 3

children.text: evamanyatrāpi gaṇoktaguṇakathanena labdhasya punaḥ kathane vyākhyeyam // 4
children.translated_text: Similarly elsewhere too, when a quality already obtained by group-statement is stated again, it should be explained [as being for specification]. // 4
'Foot-armed' (<s>caraṇāyudha</s>) means the rooster. // 5

children.text: dhanvānūpaniṣevaṇāditi hetukathanena ya eva dhanvānūpaniṣevī tittiriḥ sa eva yathoktaguṇa iti jñeyam // 6
children.translated_text: 'Because it frequents both arid and marshy regions' — by stating the reason, it should be understood that only that partridge which frequents both arid and marshy regions has the stated qualities. // 6

children.text: evamanye 'pi ye gavādayo dhanvānūpaniṣeviṇas te 'pi tittirisamānaguṇā bhavanti tittiristu viśeṣeṇeti tittiriḥ sākṣāduktaḥ // 7
children.translated_text: Similarly, other [birds] too — like the <s>gava</s> (bustard) and others — that frequent both arid and marshy regions also have qualities similar to the partridge. But the partridge is stated directly because of its special [excellence]. // 7

children.text: kiṃvā tittirereva evaṃguṇatve dhanvānūpaniṣevaṇaṃ hetuḥ nānyatra gavāder anūpadeśāder iti jñeyam // 8
children.translated_text: Or: that frequenting both arid and marshy regions is the reason for the partridge's having such qualities — [this reasoning does] not [apply] elsewhere to the <s>gava</s> and others from marshy regions, etc. — this should be understood. // 8
'Domestic pigeons' (<s>kapotā gṛhavāsinaḥ</s>) means: <s>pārāvata</s> (tame doves). // 9

children.text: caṭakā madhurā ityādi kecit paṭhantyeva ye tu na paṭhanti teṣāṃ mate caṭakasya pratudasāmānyaguṇalabdhaṃ vṛṣyatvaṃ tṛptiṃ caṭakamāṃsānāṃ gatvā yo 'nupibet payaḥ ityādivṛṣyaprayogādeva labhyate // 10
children.translated_text: 'Sparrows are sweet' etc. — some include this reading; but those who do not read it — in their view, the aphrodisiac property of sparrow-meat, obtained through the general [classification] as a <s>pratuda</s> (pecking bird), is obtained specifically from the aphrodisiac preparation [stated as]: 'Having eaten sparrow-meat and saturated, if one drinks milk...' and so on. // 10

children.text: mayūrādīnāṃ tu bahavo guṇā gaṇoktaguṇādhikā iti pṛthak pāṭhaḥ kṛtaḥ // 11
children.translated_text: But since the peacock and others have many qualities additional to those of the group-statement, a separate reading is given. // 11

children.text: māṃsaṃ bṛṃhaṇānām ityanenaivāgryādhikāravacanena māṃsasya bṛṃhaṇatve labdhe śarīrabṛṃhaṇe nānya ityādivacanaṃ prakaraṇaprāptatvena tathā tasyaivārthasya dārḍhyārthaṃ ca jñeyam // 12]
children.translated_text: Since the nourishing property of meat is already obtained by the statement in the <s>agrya</s> (foremost) section — 'Meat is the foremost among nourishing [foods]' — the statement 'No other food excels meat for nourishing the body' should be understood as arising from the context and for the purpose of reinforcing that very meaning. // 12]
<s>Pāṭhā</s>, <s>Śuṣā</s>, <s>Śaṭī</s> [-vegetable], <s>Vāstuka</s> (chenopodium), and <s>Suniṣaṇṇaka</s> — // Car_1,27.88
one should know [these] to be astringent, tri-<s>doṣa</s>-destroying; but <s>Vāstuka</s> loosens the bowels.
<s>Kākamācī</s> (Solanum nigrum) pacifies the three <s>doṣas</s>, is aphrodisiac, and a rejuvenative; // Car_1,27.89
it is neither excessively hot nor cold in potency, is purgative, and destroys skin diseases.
<s>Rājakṣavaka</s> vegetable is tri-<s>doṣa</s>-pacifying and light; // Car_1,27.90
it is astringent and especially recommended for those suffering from disorders of the intestines (<s>grahaṇī</s>) and hemorrhoids.

children.text: kālaśākaṃ tu kaṭukaṃ dīpanaṃ garaśophajit // Car_1,27.91
children.translated_text: <s>Kālaśāka</s> is pungent, appetizing, and destroys chronic poisoning and swelling; // Car_1,27.91
the <s>Kālāya</s> vegetable is said to be light, hot, <s>vāta</s>-aggravating, and dry.

children.text: dīpanī coṣṇavīryā ca grāhiṇī kaphamārute // Car_1,27.92
children.translated_text: <s>Cāṅgerī</s> (sorrel) is appetizing, of hot potency, and astringent — recommended in <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> [disorders]; // Car_1,27.92
it is also beneficial in intestinal disorders and hemorrhoids.

children.text: madhurā madhurā pāke bhedinī śleṣmavardhanī // Car_1,27.93
children.translated_text: <s>Upodikā</s> is sweet, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, purgative, and <s>kapha</s>-increasing; // Car_1,27.93

children.text: vṛṣyā snigdhā ca śītā ca madaghnī cāpyupodikā /
children.translated_text: it is aphrodisiac, unctuous, cold, and also intoxication-destroying.
<s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus) is dry, intoxication-and-poison-destroying, and recommended for those with hemorrhagic disorders; // Car_1,27.94
it is sweet, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>, and cooling.
<s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> (Centella), <s>Vetrāgra</s> (cane-shoots), <s>Kucelā</s>, <s>Vanatiktaka</s> (forest-bitter), // Car_1,27.95
<s>Karkoṭaka</s>, <s>Avalguja</s>, <s>Paṭola</s> (pointed gourd), <s>Śakulādanī</s>,
<s>Vṛṣapuṣpa</s> flowers, <s>Śārṅgeṣṭā</s>, <s>Kembūka</s>, together with <s>Kaṭhillaka</s>, // Car_1,27.96
<s>Nāḍī</s>, <s>Kalāya</s> (pea), <s>Gojihvā</s>, <s>Vārtāka</s> (eggplant), <s>Tilaparṇikā</s>,

children.text: kaulakaṃ kārkaśaṃ naimbaṃ śākaṃ pārpaṭakaṃ ca yat // Car_1,27.97
children.translated_text: <s>Kaulaka</s>, <s>Kārkaśa</s>, <s>Naimba</s> (neem-vegetable), and whatever is <s>Pārpaṭaka</s> vegetable — // Car_1,27.97
[all these] are <s>kapha</s>-and-<s>pitta</s>-destroying, bitter, cold, and pungent in <s>vipāka</s>.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
Vegetables too are taught immediately after [meats] because they serve as side-dishes. // 1
'<s>Śuṣā</s>' is <s>Kāsamarda</s> (Cassia occidentalis). // 2
'<s>Śaṭī</s>' is well-known by its own name. // 3
'<s>Vāstuka</s>' is <s>Ṭaṅka-vāstuka</s>. // 4

children.text: nātyuṣṇaśītavīryeti noṣṇatvaṃ prakarṣaprāptamasyā nāpi śītatvam ityarthaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: 'Neither excessively hot nor cold in potency' means: its hotness is not extreme, nor is its coldness — such is the meaning. // 5

children.text: yattu suśrute tiktā kākamācī vātaṃ śamayati uṣṇavīryatvāt ityuktaṃ tadvīryavādimatena ata eva dravyaguṇe suśrute'pi nātyuṣṇaśītā ityevameva paṭhitam // 6
children.translated_text: As for what is said in the <s>Suśruta</s> — '<s>Kākamācī</s> is bitter and pacifies <s>vāta</s> because of its hot potency' — that is from the standpoint of the potency-theorist. Therefore, in the <s>Suśruta</s> too, in the substance-qualities [section], it is read exactly as 'neither excessively hot nor cold.' // 6
'<s>Rājakṣavaka</s>' is <s>Dugdhikā</s> (Euphorbia). // 7

children.text: kālaśākaṃ kāliyā iti khyātaṃ kālākhyam iti kālaśākam evocyate punaḥ anye tu kālāyam iti paṭhanti // 8
children.translated_text: '<s>Kālaśāka</s>' is what is known as '<s>Kāliyā</s>'; what is called '<s>Kāla</s>' is <s>Kālaśāka</s> itself stated again. Others read '<s>Kālāyam</s>.' // 8
'<s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>' is what is known as '<s>Maṇimaṇī</s>.' // 9
'<s>Kucelā</s>' is a variety of <s>Akarṇaviddhikā</s>. // 10
'<s>Vanatiktaka</s>' is <s>Pathyasundara</s>. // 11
'<s>Avalguja</s>' is <s>Bālgujī</s>. // 12
'<s>Śakulādanī</s>' is <s>Kaṭurohiṇī</s>. // 13
'<s>Śārṅgeṣṭā</s>' is <s>Kākatiktā</s>. // 14
'<s>Kaṭhillaka</s>' is <s>Punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia). // 15
'<s>Nāḍī</s>' is <s>Nāḍīca</s>. // 16
'<s>Kalāya</s>' is the round <s>Kalāya</s> (pea). // 17
'<s>Tilaparṇikā</s>' is <s>Hulahulikā</s>. // 18
'<s>Gojihvā</s>' is <s>Dārvīpattrikā</s>. // 19

children.text: kulakaḥ kāravellakaḥ kecit tu kulakaṃ paṭolabhedam āhuḥ // 20
children.translated_text: '<s>Kulaka</s>' is <s>Kāravellaka</s> (bitter gourd). Some say <s>Kulaka</s> is a variety of <s>Paṭola</s>. // 20
'<s>Karkaśa</s>' is a small <s>Karkoṭaka</s>. // 21]

children.text: sarvāṇi sūpyaśākāni phañjī cillī kutumbakaḥ // Car_1,27.98
children.translated_text: All pulse-vegetables, <s>Phañjī</s>, <s>Cillī</s>, <s>Kutumbaka</s>, // Car_1,27.98
and all <s>Āluka</s> tubers with their leaves, and <s>Kuṭiñjara</s>,
<s>Śaṇa</s> (hemp) and <s>Śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) flowers, <s>Karbudāra</s>, <s>Suvarcalā</s>, // Car_1,27.99
<s>Niṣpāva</s> (flat bean), <s>Kovidāra</s>, <s>Pattūra</s>, <s>Cuccuparṇikā</s>,

children.text: kumārajīvo loṭṭākaḥ pālaṅkyā māriṣas tathā // Car_1,27.100
children.translated_text: <s>Kumārajīva</s>, <s>Loṭṭāka</s>, <s>Pālaṅkyā</s> (spinach), and <s>Māriṣa</s> (Amaranthus), // Car_1,27.100
<s>Kalamba</s>, <s>Nālikā</s>, <s>Āsūrya</s> (mustard-greens), <s>Kusumbha</s> (safflower) and <s>Vṛkadhūmaka</s>,

children.text: lakṣmaṇā ca prapunnāṭo nalinīkā kuṭherakaḥ // Car_1,27.101
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, <s>Prapunnāṭa</s>, <s>Nalinīkā</s>, <s>Kuṭheraka</s>, // Car_1,27.101

children.text: loṇikā yavaśākaṃ ca kuṣmāṇḍakam avalgujam yātukaḥ śālakalyāṇī triparṇī pīluparṇikā // Car_1,27.102
children.translated_text: <s>Loṇikā</s> (purslane), <s>Yavaśāka</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍaka</s> (pumpkin-greens), <s>Avalguja</s>, <s>Yātuka</s>, <s>Śālakalyāṇī</s>, <s>Triparṇī</s>, <s>Pīluparṇikā</s> — // Car_1,27.102

children.text: śākaṃ guru ca rūkṣaṃ ca prāyo viṣṭabhya jīryati /
children.translated_text: [this class of] vegetable is heavy and dry, and mostly causes distension in digestion;

children.text: madhuraṃ śītavīryaṃ ca purīṣasya ca bhedanam // Car_1,27.103
children.translated_text: it is sweet, cold in potency, and purgative. // Car_1,27.103
When steamed, squeezed of its juice, and enriched with fat — it is recommended.
The flowers of <s>Śaṇa</s> (hemp), <s>Kovidāra</s>, <s>Karbudāra</s>, and <s>Śālmali</s> (silk-cotton) — // Car_1,27.104

children.text: puṣpaṃ grāhi praśastaṃ ca raktapitte viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: are astringent and especially recommended in hemorrhagic disorders (<s>raktapitta</s>).
The shoots of banyan, <s>Udumbara</s> (cluster fig), <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>Plakṣa</s> (wavy-leaved fig), and lotus — // Car_1,27.105
are astringent, styptic, cold, and beneficial for those with <s>pitta</s>-diarrhea.
<s>Vatsādanī</s> destroys <s>vāyu</s> (wind); <s>Gaṇḍīra</s> and <s>Citraka</s> [destroy] <s>kapha</s>; // Car_1,27.106

children.text: śreyasī bilvaparṇī ca bilvapattraṃ tu vātanut /
children.translated_text: <s>Śreyasī</s>, <s>Bilvaparṇī</s>, and <s>Bilva</s>-leaf remove <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: bhaṇḍī śatāvarīśākaṃ balā jīvantikaṃ ca yat // Car_1,27.107
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaṇḍī</s>, <s>Śatāvarī</s>-vegetable, <s>Balā</s>, and <s>Jīvantikā</s> — // Car_1,27.107
and of <s>Parvaṇī</s> and <s>Parvapuṣpī</s> — are said to destroy <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
The [vegetables] of <s>Lāṅgalakī</s> and <s>Uruvūka</s> are light, loosen the feces, and bitter; // Car_1,27.108
and the vegetable of <s>Tilavetasa</s> and of <s>Pañcāṅgula</s> — // Car_1,27.109
are <s>vāta</s>-aggravating, pungent-bitter-sour, and promoting downward movement.
<s>Kausumbha</s> (safflower-greens) are dry, sour, hot, <s>kapha</s>-destroying, and <s>pitta</s>-increasing.

children.text: trapusairvārukaṃ svādu guru viṣṭambhi śītalam // Car_1,27.110
children.translated_text: <s>Trapusa</s> (cucumber) and <s>Ervāruka</s> (Armenian cucumber) are sweet, heavy, obstructing digestion, and cooling; // Car_1,27.110

children.text: mukhapriyaṃ ca rūkṣaṃ ca mūtralaṃ trapusaṃ tv ati /
children.translated_text: <s>Trapusa</s> is pleasing to the mouth, dry, and especially diuretic;
ripe <s>Ervāruka</s> removes burning, thirst, lassitude, and distress. // Car_1,27.111
Bottle-gourds (<s>Alābū</s>) loosen the bowels and are dry, cold, and heavy;
<s>Cirbhaṭa</s> and <s>Ervāruka</s> are similar, but those two are especially beneficial for loosening bowels. // Car_1,27.112
Ripe <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> (ash-gourd), with alkali, is sweet-sour and light;
it promotes the flow of urine and feces and destroys all <s>doṣas</s>. // Car_1,27.113
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Pulse-vegetables' (<s>sūpya-śākāni</s>) are <s>Māṣaparṇī</s> and the like. // 1
'<s>Phañjī</s>' is <s>Brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā</s>. // 2
'<s>Cillī</s>' is <s>Gauḍa-vāstuka</s>. // 3
'<s>Kutumbaka</s>' is <s>Droṇapuṣpikā</s> (Leucas). // 4
'<s>Āluka</s>' refers to <s>Piṇḍāluka</s> and the like. // 5
'<s>Karbudāra</s>' is <s>Kāñcana</s> (golden shower tree). // 6
'<s>Suvarcalā</s>' is <s>Sūryabhaktikā</s>; some say it is <s>Phappuka</s>. // 7
'<s>Pattūra</s>' is <s>Śāliñca</s>. // 8
'<s>Cuccuparṇikā</s>' is a variety of <s>Nāḍīca</s>. // 9
'<s>Kumārajīva</s>' is <s>Jīvaśāka</s>. // 10
'<s>Loṭṭāka</s>' is <s>Loṭṭā-māriṣa</s>. // 11
'<s>Nālikā</s>' is <s>Go-nāḍīca</s>. // 12
'<s>Āsurī</s>' is <s>Rājikā</s> (mustard) or <s>Maṇḍaka</s>. // 13
'<s>Vṛkadhūmaka</s>' is <s>Bhūmiśirīṣa</s>. // 14
'<s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>' is well-known by its own name. // 15
'<s>Nalinī</s>' is the lotus-stalk (<s>padma-mṛṇāla</s>); in the alternative reading '<s>Nīlinī</s>', [it is] <s>Buhnā</s>. // 16
'<s>Yavaśāka</s>' is <s>Kṣetra-vāstuka</s> (field-chenopodium). // 17
'<s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>' is <s>Sarpacchattra</s> (serpent-umbrella). // 18
'<s>Avalguja</s>' here is a variety of <s>Avalguja</s>. // 19
'<s>Yātuka</s>' is the white <s>Śālaparṇī</s>. // 20
'<s>Śālakalyāṇī</s>' is a variety of <s>Śāliñca</s>. // 21
'<s>Triparṇī</s>' is <s>Haṃsapādikā</s> (goose-foot). // 22
'<s>Pīluparṇikā</s>' is <s>Moraṭaka</s>. // 23
'<s>Gaṇḍīra</s>' is <s>Śamaṭha</s>. // 24
'<s>Bilvaparṇī</s>' is <s>Bilvārjaka</s>. // 25
'<s>Bhaṇḍī</s>' is well-known by its own name. // 26
'<s>Parvaṇī</s>' is <s>Parvaśāka</s>. // 27
'<s>Parvapuṣpī</s>' is <s>Kukkuṭī</s>. // 28
'<s>Pañcāṅgula</s>' is <s>Citrairanḍa</s> (variegated castor). // 29
'<s>Ervāruka</s>' is <s>Rājakarkaṭī</s> (snake-cucumber). // 30

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍakaṃ suśrute bālyādyāvasthābhedena paṭhitaṃ tad apyaviruddham eva yato bālamadhyayos tatra pittaharatvaṃ kaphakaratvaṃ coktaṃ tadapīha pittottare kaphottare saṃnipāte boddhavyam // 31]
children.translated_text: <s>Kūṣmāṇḍaka</s> (ash gourd) has been described in <s>Suśruta</s> with distinctions based on stages such as young etc.; that too is not contradictory, since there the properties of alleviating <s>pitta</s> (bile) and increasing <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) are stated for the young and middle stages — this should be understood here as referring to <s>sannipāta</s> (combined disorder) with predominance of <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> respectively. [31]

children.text: kelūṭaṃ ca kadambaṃ ca nadīmāṣakam aindukam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kelūṭa</s>, <s>kadamba</s>, <s>nadīmāṣaka</s> (river bean), and <s>ainduka</s> —

children.text: viśadaṃ guru śītaṃ ca samabhiṣyandi cocyate // Car_1,27.114
children.translated_text: are clear, heavy, cooling, and are said to be moderately viscous. [Car 1.27.114]
<s>Utpala</s> (lotus) flowers are astringent and alleviate <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders);
likewise, <s>tālapralamba</s> (palm sprout) relieves chest wounds and pain. [Car 1.27.115]
<s>Kharjūra</s> (date) and <s>tālaśasya</s> (palmyra fruit pulp) alleviate <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders) and <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption).
<s>Tarūṭa</s> (lotus root), <s>bisa</s> (lotus stalk), <s>śālūka</s> (lotus tuber), <s>krauñcādana</s>, and <s>kaśeruka</s> (water chestnut) — [Car 1.27.116]
<s>śṛṅgāṭaka</s> (water caltrop) and <s>aṅkaloḍya</s> — are heavy, cause distension, and are cooling.
The stalks of <s>kumuda</s> (white water lily) and <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), along with their flowers and fruits, are known to be — [Car 1.27.117]
cooling, sweet and astringent, and they aggravate <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind).
The <s>pauṣkara</s> (lotus rhizome) is astringent, slightly constipating, and is said to alleviate <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). [Car 1.27.118]
The seed of <s>pauṣkara</s> (lotus) is sweet in both taste and post-digestive effect,

children.text: balyaḥ śīto guruḥ snigdhastarpaṇo bṛṃhaṇātmakaḥ // Car_1,27.119
children.translated_text: strength-giving, cooling, heavy, unctuous, nourishing, and of a bulk-promoting nature. [Car 1.27.119]
<s>Muñjātaka</s> (a northern tuber) alleviates <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is sweet, an excellent aphrodisiac,

children.text: jīvano bṛṃhaṇo vṛṣyaḥ kaṇṭhyaḥ śasto rasāyane // Car_1,27.120
children.translated_text: life-sustaining, bulk-promoting, aphrodisiac, beneficial for the throat, and recommended as a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). [Car 1.27.120]
The tuber of <s>vidārī</s> (Pueraria tuberosa) is strength-giving, diuretic, sweet, and cooling.

children.text: amlikāyāḥ smṛtaḥ kando grahaṇyarśohito laghuḥ // Car_1,27.121
children.translated_text: The tuber of <s>amlikā</s> (tamarind) is said to be beneficial for <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue) and <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), and is light. [Car 1.27.121]
It is not excessively hot, destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), is astringent, and is recommended in <s>madātyaya</s> (alcoholic intoxication).
The mustard-plant vegetable (<s>sārṣapa śāka</s>) is said to aggravate all three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) and cause retention of stool and urine. [Car 1.27.122]
Similarly, <s>raktanāla</s> (red-stemmed variety) is the same, but is particularly dry and sour.
Similarly, <s>piṇḍāluka</s> (a type of yam) should be known; being a tuber, it is palatable.
Except for <s>sarpacchattraka</s> (serpent-hood mushroom), there are many other varieties of mushrooms. [Car 1.27.123]

children.text: śītāḥ pīnasakartryaśca madhurā gurvya eva ca /
children.translated_text: They are cooling, cause nasal congestion, are sweet, and indeed heavy.
This is the fourth group of vegetables, comprising leafy vegetables, tubers, and fruits. [Car 1.27.124]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: kelūṭe hārītavacanaṃ kelūṭaṃ svādu viṭapaṃ tatkandaḥ svāduśītalaḥ iti // 1
children.translated_text: Regarding <s>kelūṭa</s>, <s>Hārīta</s>'s statement is: '<s>kelūṭa</s> has a sweet stalk; its tuber is sweet and cooling.' [1]

children.text: kadambaṃ kadambikāṃ vadanti kecit tu svalpakadambakam āhuḥ // 2
children.translated_text: <s>Kadamba</s> — some call it <s>kadambikā</s>; others say it is the small <s>kadamba</s>. [2]
<s>Nadīmāṣaka</s> is known as <s>udīmānaka</s>. [3]
<s>Ainduka</s> is <s>nikṣāra</s> (alkali-free plant). [4]
<s>Tālapralamba</s> means the sprout of the <s>tāla</s> (palmyra palm). [5]
By the word <s>śasya</s> here, the pith of the crown is meant. [6]
<s>Tarūṭa</s> is the tuber of <s>kahlāra</s> (white lotus). [7]
<s>Krauñcādana</s> is <s>dhiñculikā</s>. [8]
By the word <s>kaśeruka</s>, both <s>ciñcoḍakā</s> and <s>rājakaśeruka</s> (royal water chestnut) are included. [9]
<s>Aṅkāloḍya</s> is the tuber of the small <s>utpala</s> (lotus). [10]
<s>Muñjātaka</s> is a tuber from the northern regions (<s>Uttarāpatha</s>). [11]
<s>Amlikā</s> (tamarind) is a small shrub, mostly found in <s>Kāmarūpa</s> and similar regions. [12]
<s>Sarpacchattra</s> is a mushroom shaped like a serpent's hood. [13]
The other varieties of mushrooms should be known as the many kinds that grow on cow dung, straw, and similar substrates. [14]

children.text: pattrakandaphalāśraya iti prādhānyena tena puṣpādyāśrayatvam api śākavargasya jñeyam // 15]
children.translated_text: 'Comprising leaves, tubers, and fruits' indicates predominance; it should be understood that the vegetable group also includes those based on flowers and other parts. [15]
Thirst, burning sensation, fever, dyspnea, <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), chest wounds, and consumption,
<s>vātapitta</s> (disorders of wind and bile), <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of <s>vāta</s>), hoarseness, and <s>madātyaya</s> (alcoholic intoxication), [Car 1.27.125]
bitter taste in the mouth, dryness of the mouth, and cough — it quickly removes all these. <s>Mṛdvīkā</s> (grape/raisin) is bulk-promoting, aphrodisiac, sweet, unctuous, and cooling. [Car 1.27.126]

children.text: mṛdvīkā bṛṃhaṇī vṛṣyā madhurā snigdhaśītalā // Car_1,27.126
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛdvīkā</s> (grape/raisin) is bulk-promoting, aphrodisiac, sweet, unctuous, and cooling. [Car 1.27.126]

children.text: madhuraṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ kharjūraṃ guru śītalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Kharjūra</s> (date) is sweet, bulk-promoting, aphrodisiac, heavy, and cooling.

children.text: kṣaye'bhighāte dāhe ca vātapitte ca taddhitam // Car_1,27.127
children.translated_text: It is beneficial in <s>kṣaya</s> (consumption), injury, burning sensation, and disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile). [Car 1.27.127]

children.text: tarpaṇaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ phalgu guru viṣṭambhi śītalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Phalgu</s> (fig, Ficus hispida) is nourishing, bulk-promoting, heavy, constipating, and cooling.

children.text: parūṣakaṃ madhūkaṃ ca vātapitte ca śasyate // Car_1,27.128
children.translated_text: <s>Parūṣaka</s> (Grewia asiatica) and <s>madhūka</s> (Madhuca indica) are recommended in disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile). [Car 1.27.128]

children.text: madhuraṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ balyam āmrātaṃ tarpaṇaṃ guru /
children.translated_text: <s>Āmrāta</s> (hog plum, Spondias pinnata) is sweet, bulk-promoting, strength-giving, nourishing, and heavy,

children.text: sasnehaṃ śleṣmalaṃ śītaṃ vṛṣyaṃ viṣṭabhya jīryati // Car_1,27.129
children.translated_text: unctuous, phlegm-producing, cooling, aphrodisiac, and is digested slowly causing heaviness. [Car 1.27.129]
Ripe <s>tālaśasya</s> (palmyra fruits) and <s>nārikela</s> (coconut) fruits —
are bulk-promoting, unctuous, cooling, strength-giving, and sweet. [Car 1.27.130]
<s>Bhavya</s> (Dillenia indica) is sweet, sour, and astringent, constipating, heavy, and cooling,
it aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), is astringent, and cleanses the mouth. [Car 1.27.131]
Sour varieties of <s>parūṣaka</s> (Grewia asiatica), <s>drākṣā</s> (grape), <s>badara</s> (jujube), and <s>āruka</s> (peach),
as well as <s>karkandhu</s> (wild jujube) and <s>nikuca</s> (Artocarpus lakoocha), aggravate <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm). [Car 1.27.132]
A fully ripe <s>āruka</s> (peach) is not excessively hot, heavy, predominantly sweet, palatable,
bulk-promoting, quickly digested, and does not greatly vitiate the <s>doṣas</s> (humors). [Car 1.27.133]

children.text: dvividhaṃ śītamuṣṇaṃ ca madhuraṃ cāmlameva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Pārāvata</s> (a fruit from <s>Kāmarūpa</s>) is of two kinds — cooling and heating, sweet and sour respectively;
it is heavy, should be known to cause loss of appetite and destroy digestive fire. [Car 1.27.134]
<s>Kāśmarya</s> (Gmelina arborea) fruit is said to have properties only slightly different from <s>bhavya</s>,
and similarly, <s>tūda</s> has properties only slightly different from sour <s>parūṣaka</s>. [Car 1.27.135]
<s>Ṭaṅka</s> (a fruit from <s>Kāśmīra</s>) is astringent-sweet, causes <s>vāta</s> (wind), is heavy, and cooling.

children.text: kapitthamāmaṃ kaṇṭhaghnaṃ viṣaghnaṃ grāhi vātalam // Car_1,27.136
children.translated_text: Unripe <s>kapittha</s> (wood apple, Limonia acidissima) is harmful to the throat, destroys poison, is astringent, and aggravates <s>vāta</s> (wind). [Car 1.27.136]
Being sweet, sour, and astringent, and fragrant, it promotes relish;

children.text: paripakvaṃ ca doṣaghnaṃ viṣaghnaṃ grāhi gurvapi // Car_1,27.137
children.translated_text: when fully ripe, it destroys the <s>doṣas</s> (humors), counteracts poison, is astringent, though heavy. [Car 1.27.137]

children.text: bilvaṃ tu durjaraṃ pakvaṃ doṣalaṃ pūtimārutam /
children.translated_text: Ripe <s>bilva</s> (Aegle marmelos) is difficult to digest, vitiates the <s>doṣas</s> (humors), and causes foul-smelling flatulence.
When young, it is unctuous, hot, sharp, kindles digestion, and overcomes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind). [Car 1.27.138]
Unripe <s>āmra</s> (mango) causes <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders); half-ripe mango increases <s>pitta</s> (bile);
ripe <s>āmra</s> (mango) conquers <s>vāyu</s> (wind) and promotes flesh, semen, and strength. [Car 1.27.139]
<s>Jāmbava</s> (java plum, Syzygium cumini) is predominantly astringent and sweet, heavy, constipating, and cooling,

children.text: jāmbavaṃ kaphapittaghnaṃ grāhi vātakaraṃ param // Car_1,27.140
children.translated_text: it destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is astringent, and exceedingly aggravates <s>vāta</s> (wind). [Car 1.27.140]
<s>Badara</s> (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba) is sweet, unctuous, laxative, and overcomes <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: tacchuṣkaṃ kaphavātaghnaṃ pitte na ca virudhyate // Car_1,27.141
children.translated_text: when dried, it destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), and does not antagonize <s>pitta</s> (bile). [Car 1.27.141]
<s>Simbitikā</s> fruit is astringent-sweet, cooling, and astringent.

children.text: gāṅgerukī karīraṃ ca bimbī todanadhanvanam // Car_1,27.142
children.translated_text: <s>Gāṅgerukī</s>, <s>karīra</s> (caper), <s>bimbī</s>, <s>todana</s>, and <s>dhanvana</s> — [Car 1.27.142]
are sweet with an astringent component, cooling, and alleviate <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm).

children.text: sampakvaṃ panasaṃ mocaṃ rājādanaphalāni ca // Car_1,27.143
children.translated_text: Fully ripe <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit, Artocarpus heterophyllus), <s>moca</s> (banana, Musa paradisiaca), and <s>rājādana</s> (Mimusops hexandra) fruits — [Car 1.27.143]
are sweet with an astringent component, unctuous, cooling, and heavy.
Due to their astringency, clarity, and fragrance, they promote relish. [Car 1.27.144]
<s>Lavalī</s> fruit is suitable as a condiment, pleasing to the heart, and aggravates <s>vāta</s> (wind).

children.text: nīpaṃ śatāhvakaṃ pīlu tṛṇaśūnyaṃ vikaṅkatam // Car_1,27.145
children.translated_text: <s>Nīpa</s> (Anthocephalus cadamba), <s>śatāhvaka</s>, <s>pīlu</s> (Salvadora persica), <s>tṛṇaśūnya</s> (screwpine, Pandanus), and <s>vikaṅkata</s> — [Car 1.27.145]
<s>prācīnāmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry of the eastern variety) — all these destroy the <s>doṣas</s> (humors) and remove aversion to food.
<s>Aiṅguda</s> (Balanites aegyptiaca) is bitter-sweet, unctuous, hot, and overcomes <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind). [Car 1.27.146]
<s>Tinduka</s> (Diospyros embryopteris) destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile), is astringent, sweet, and light.
One should know that <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry, Emblica officinalis) possesses all tastes except salty. [Car 1.27.147]
It is dry, sweet, astringent, and supremely alleviates <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile).
<s>Vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica) destroys disorders arising from <s>rasa</s> (chyle), <s>asṛk</s> (blood), <s>māṃsa</s> (muscle), and <s>medas</s> (fat) tissues. [Car 1.27.148]
It cures hoarseness, expectoration of <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), and diseases of <s>pitta</s> (bile);

children.text: amlaṃ kaṣāyamadhuraṃ vātaghnaṃ grāhi dīpanam // Car_1,27.149
children.translated_text: it is sour, astringent-sweet, destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), is astringent, and kindles the digestive fire. [Car 1.27.149]
<s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate, sweet variety) is unctuous, hot, pleasing to the heart, and does not antagonize <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile).
The <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate) that is dry and sour, however, aggravates <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>vāta</s> (wind). [Car 1.27.150]
Among these, the sweet <s>dāḍima</s> (pomegranate), which alleviates <s>pitta</s> (bile), is the best.

children.text: vṛkṣāmlaṃ grāhi rūkṣoṣṇaṃ vātaśleṣmaṇi śasyate // Car_1,27.151
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> (Garcinia indica, kokum) is astringent, dry, hot, and is recommended in disorders of <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm). [Car 1.27.151]
The ripe fruit of <s>amlikā</s> (tamarind) has properties only slightly different from that.

children.text: guṇais tair eva saṃyuktaṃ bhedanaṃ tv amlavetasam // Car_1,27.152
children.translated_text: <s>Amlavetasa</s> (Garcinia pedunculata) possesses those same properties but is additionally laxative. [Car 1.27.152]
In colic, loss of appetite, constipation, weak digestive fire, disorders from alcohol,

children.text: hikkāśvāse ca kāse ca vamyāṃ varcogadeṣu ca // Car_1,27.153
children.translated_text: hiccup, dyspnea, cough, vomiting, and diseases of the stool — [Car 1.27.153]
in all those arising from <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), it is prescribed.
The filaments of <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron, Citrus medica) are light; the rest of it is the opposite. [Car 1.27.154]
Without its rind, <s>karcūra</s> (a citrus variety) promotes appetite, kindles digestion, is pleasing to the heart, and fragrant.
<s>Karcūra</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind), and is beneficial in dyspnea, hiccup, and hemorrhoids. [Car 1.27.155]
<s>Nāgaraṅga</s> (orange, Citrus sinensis) fruit is sweet, slightly sour, pleasing to the heart, and promotes relish for food;
it is difficult to digest, pacifies <s>vāta</s> (wind), and is heavy. [Car 1.27.156]
<s>Vātāma</s> (almond), <s>abhiṣuka</s> (pistachio), <s>akṣoṭa</s> (walnut), <s>mukūlaka</s>, and <s>nikocaka</s> —
are heavy, hot, unctuous, sweet, and together with <s>urumāṇa</s> (a nut variety), they give strength. [Car 1.27.157]
They alleviate <s>vāta</s> (wind), are bulk-promoting, aphrodisiac, and increase <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile).

children.text: priyālameṣāṃ sadṛśaṃ vidyādauṣṇyaṃ vinā guṇaiḥ // Car_1,27.158
children.translated_text: <s>Priyāla</s> (Buchanania lanzan, charoli) should be known to have similar properties to these, except for the heating quality. [Car 1.27.158]
<s>Śleṣmātaka</s> (Cordia dichotoma) fruit is phlegm-producing, sweet, cooling, and heavy.
<s>Cāṅkoṭa</s> fruit is phlegm-producing, heavy, constipating, and destroys digestive fire. [Car 1.27.159]

children.text: gurūṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ rūkṣaṃ keśaghnaṃ ca śamīphalam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śamī</s> (Prosopis cineraria) fruit is heavy, hot, sweet, dry, and destroys hair.
<s>Kārañja</s> (Pongamia pinnata) causes distension but does not antagonize <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm). [Car 1.27.160]
<s>Āmrātaka</s> (hog plum), <s>dantaśaṭha</s>, sour <s>karamardaka</s> (Carissa carandas),
and <s>airāvataka</s> — one should know them to cause <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders). [Car 1.27.161]

children.text: vātaghnaṃ dīpanaṃ caiva vārtākaṃ kaṭu tiktakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vārtāka</s> (eggplant/brinjal) is pungent, bitter, destroys <s>vāta</s> (wind), and kindles digestion.
<s>Parpaṭakī</s> fruit should be known as aggravating <s>vāta</s> (wind) and destroying <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>pitta</s> (bile). [Car 1.27.162]
<s>Ākṣikī</s> fruit is sour, alleviates <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), but aggravates <s>vāta</s> (wind).

The fruits of <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig, Ficus religiosa), <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig, Ficus racemosa), <s>plakṣa</s> (Ficus lacor), and <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan, Ficus benghalensis) — [Car 1.27.163]
are sweet with a sour post-digestive effect, and alleviate <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm).
are astringent, sweet, and sour, aggravate <s>vāta</s> (wind), and are heavy. [Car 1.27.164]
The stone of <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking nut, Semecarpus anacardium) is comparable to fire; its flesh is sweet and cooling.
This fifth group of fruits has been described, containing those most commonly used. [Car 1.27.165]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
He describes the fruit group because some fruits are also used like vegetables. [1]
<s>Mṛdvīkā</s> (grape) is mentioned first because of the excellence of its properties. [2]
<s>Phalgu</s> is <s>audumbara</s> (fig of Ficus racemosa). [3]

children.text: madhūkaśabdena samānaguṇatvāt phalaṃ kusumaṃ ca jñeyam // 4
children.translated_text: By the word <s>madhūka</s>, because of similarity of properties, both the fruit and the flower should be understood. [4]
<s>Parūṣaka</s> here should be understood as the sweet variety of <s>parūṣaka</s>. [5]

children.text: āmrātam āmaḍā iti khyātamāmraphalasadṛśam iti candrikā etacca dvividhaṃ madhuramamlaṃ ca atra madhurasyaiva guṇaḥ amlasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt // 6
children.translated_text: <s>Āmrāta</s> is known as <s>āmaḍā</s>, resembling a mango fruit — so says the <s>Candrikā</s>. It is of two kinds: sweet and sour. Here only the properties of the sweet variety are given, since the sour variety will be described later. [6]

children.text: tālaśasyānīti tālaphalāni yathā harītakīnāṃ śasyāni ityatra phalameva śasyam ucyate // 7
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaśasyāni</s> means palmyra fruits, just as in the expression 'the <s>śasya</s> (produce) of <s>harītakī</s>,' the fruit itself is called <s>śasya</s>. [7]
<s>Siddhāni</s> means ripened; thus ripe palmyra is meant. [8]
<s>Bhavya</s> is the <s>karamaraṅga</s> (star fruit) according to some; others say it is the <s>akṣa</s>-sized fruit of the <s>saṃhitā</s>. [9]
<s>Āruka</s> is well-known in <s>Kārtikeyapura</s>. [10]

children.text: karkandhūḥ śṛgālabadarī karkandhūnikucayor vicchidya pāṭhena nityaṃ pittaśleṣmakartṛtvaṃ tayor darśayati // 11
children.translated_text: <s>Karkandhu</s> is <s>śṛgālabadarī</s> (wild jujube). By separating <s>karkandhu</s> and <s>nikuca</s> in the reading, their property of always aggravating <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm) is demonstrated. [11]

children.text: parūṣakādīnāṃ tu madhurāmlabhedena dvirūpāṇāṃ ya eva parūṣakādayo 'mlāsta eva pittaśleṣmakarā iti // 12
children.translated_text: Among <s>parūṣaka</s> and other fruits that exist in two forms — sweet and sour — those that are sour are the ones that aggravate <s>pitta</s> (bile) and <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm). [12]
<s>Pārāvata</s> is well-known in <s>Kāmarūpa</s>. [13]

children.text: atra yo madhuraḥ sa śītaḥ yaścāmlaḥ sa uṣṇa iti jñeyam // 14
children.translated_text: Here, the sweet variety should be understood as cooling, and the sour variety as heating. [14]

children.text: evaṃ rasanirdeśenaiva vīrye labdhe'pi punarvīryākhyānamamlasyāmalakasya śītatādarśanād boddhavyam // 15
children.translated_text: Thus, even though the potency is already known from the indication of taste, the separate mention of potency should be understood from the fact that sour <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry) is cooling — [showing that taste does not always determine potency]. [15]
<s>Ṭaṅka</s> is well-known in <s>Kāśmīra</s>. [16]
'Ripe' (<s>siddha</s>) means ripened over time. [17]
The description of the properties of <s>kapittha</s> (wood apple), <s>bilva</s> (bael), and <s>āmra</s> (mango) at different stages is because they are used in all stages. [18]
<s>Badara</s> (jujube) refers to the medium-sized variety, for that alone is sweet. [19]
<s>Gāṅgeruka</s> is the fruit of <s>nāgabalā</s> (Grewia hirsuta). [20]
<s>Karīra</s> is a tree of arid regions. [21]
<s>Todana</s> is a variety of <s>dhanvana</s>. [22]
<s>Rājādana</s> is <s>kṣīrī</s> (the milky tree, Mimusops hexandra). [23]

children.text: avadaṃśakṣamamiti lavalīphalaṃ prāśya dravyāntare rucir bhavati // 24
children.translated_text: 'Suitable as a condiment' (<s>avadaṃśakṣama</s>) means that after eating <s>lavalī</s> fruit, relish arises for other foods. [24]
<s>Nīpa</s> is <s>kadambaka</s> (Anthocephalus cadamba). [25]
<s>Śatāhvaka</s> fruit is known as <s>seha</s>. [26]
<s>Pīlu</s> is from the northern regions (<s>Uttarāpatha</s>). [27]
<s>Tṛṇaśūnya</s> is the fruit of <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine, Pandanus odoratissimus). [28]
<s>Prācīnāmalaka</s> is <s>pānīyāmalaka</s> (the aquatic gooseberry). [29]
<s>Tinduka</s> is the <s>Kendu</s> (Diospyros). // 30

children.text: dāḍimaguṇe kaphapittāvirodhīti amladāḍimaṃ pittāvirodhi madhuraṃ tu kaphāvirodhi evaṃ ca tridoṣaharatvamasyopapannaṃ yad uktaṃ suśrute dvividhaṃ tattu vijñeyaṃ madhuraṃ cāmlameva ca // 31
children.translated_text: In the [description of] the qualities of <s>Dāḍima</s> (pomegranate), 'not incompatible with <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>' — the sour pomegranate is not incompatible with <s>pitta</s>, while the sweet one is not incompatible with <s>kapha</s>. Thus its property of subduing all three <s>doṣas</s> is established. As stated in the <s>Suśruta</s>: 'It should be known as of two kinds — sweet and sour. // 31
The sweet destroys all three <s>doṣas</s>; the sour removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.' // 32
<s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> is <s>Mahārdrakam</s> (Garcinia). // 33
<s>Amlikā</s> is <s>Tintiḍī</s> (tamarind). // 34

children.text: śeṣamiti tvaṅmāṃsam ato'nyatheti guru kiṃvā śūle 'rucāv ityādyuktakesaraguṇaviparītam // 35
children.translated_text: 'The rest' means the skin and flesh. 'Otherwise' means [it is] heavy; or alternatively, [the properties are] opposite to those of the saffron-like filaments mentioned in '[useful for] colic, loss of appetite,' etc. // 35
<s>Vātāma</s> and the rest are from the northern region (<s>Uttarāpatha</s>). // 36
This <s>Priyāla</s> (Buchanania) is well-known in <s>Magadha</s>. // 37
<s>Dantaśaṭha</s> is <s>Jambīra</s> (citron); some call it <s>Amloṭa</s>. // 38

children.text: ihāmrātakamamlaṃ grāhyaṃ pūrvaṃ tu madhuramāmrātakam uktam // 39
children.translated_text: Here the sour <s>Āmrātaka</s> (hog-plum) should be understood; the sweet <s>Āmrātaka</s> was mentioned earlier. // 39
<s>Karamarda</s> (Carissa) is of two kinds: cultivated and wild. // 40
<s>Airāvata</s> is the <s>Amlātaka</s> (Spondias); or alternatively, <s>Nāgaraṅga</s> (orange). // 41

children.text: vārtākaṃ dakṣiṇāpathe phalavat khādyate yad goṣṭhavārtākasaṃjñakaṃ tasyeha guṇaḥ kiṃvā phalavadasiddhasyaiva vārtākasyopayojyasyāyaṃ guṇaḥ // 42
children.translated_text: As for <s>Vārtāka</s> (eggplant) — in the southern region it is eaten as a fruit, which is called <s>Goṣṭhavārtāka</s>; the qualities here pertain to that. Or alternatively, these are the qualities of <s>Vārtāka</s> itself when used without being cooked. // 42
<s>Ākṣikī</s> is a creeper; its fruit is <s>Ākṣika</s>. // 43
<s>Anupāki</s> is known as <s>Anuyā</s>. // 44
'Equal to fire' — because it produces blisters and the like. // 45]
Appetizing, digestive-stimulant, aphrodisiac — fresh ginger is the universal medicine;
its juice is prescribed in conditions of <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s> (kapha), and constipation. // Car 1.27.166
Appetizing, digestive-stimulant, sharp, fragrant, mouth-cleansing —
<s>Jambīra</s> (citron) destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, kills worms, and digests food. // Car 1.27.167
When young, [<s>Mūlaka</s> (radish)] destroys the <s>doṣas</s>; when mature, it produces all three <s>doṣas</s> [but] removes <s>vāta</s>;

children.text: snigdhasiddhaṃ viśuṣkaṃ tu mūlakaṃ kaphavātajit // Car_1,27.168
children.translated_text: when cooked with oil, it is dry — [such] <s>Mūlaka</s> conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>. // Car 1.27.168
Destroying hiccup, cough, poison, dyspnea, and pain in the sides —
<s>Surasa</s> (basil) produces <s>pitta</s>, destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and eliminates foul odor. // Car 1.27.169
<s>Yavānī</s> (ajwain), <s>Arjaka</s> (white basil), <s>Śigru</s> (drumstick), <s>Śāleya</s> (fennel), and <s>Mṛṣṭaka</s> (mustard) —
these are pleasant to the heart and palatable, but they disturb <s>pitta</s>. // Car 1.27.170
<s>Gaṇḍīra</s> (red variety), <s>Jalapippalī</s> (water pepper), <s>Tumburu</s> (prickly ash), and <s>Śṛṅgaverikā</s> —
these are sharp, hot, pungent, dry, and they destroy <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>. // Car 1.27.171
<s>Bhūstṛṇa</s> (lemongrass) destroys virility, is pungent, dry, hot, and cleanses the mouth;
<s>Kharāhvā</s> (black cumin) destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and alleviates bladder disease and pain. // Car 1.27.172
<s>Dhānyaka</s> (coriander), <s>Ajagandhā</s> (wild bishop's weed), and <s>Sumukha</s> — these are appetizing,
fragrant, not excessively pungent, and they do not disturb the <s>doṣas</s>. // Car 1.27.173
<s>Gṛñjanaka</s> (a type of onion) is astringent, sharp, and beneficial for <s>vāta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, and hemorrhoids;

children.text: svedane'bhyavahāre ca yojayet tam apittinām // Car_1,27.174
children.translated_text: it should be used in fomentation and as food for those not afflicted with <s>pitta</s>. // Car 1.27.174
<s>Palāṇḍu</s> (onion) produces <s>śleṣman</s> and destroys <s>vāta</s>, but does not remove <s>pitta</s>;
it is suitable as food, strengthening, heavy, aphrodisiac, and appetizing. // Car 1.27.175
Destroying worms, skin diseases, and <s>kilāsa</s> (leucoderma), removing <s>vāta</s>, destroying tumors —

children.text: snigdhaścoṣṇaśca vṛṣyaśca laśunaḥ kaṭuko guruḥ // Car_1,27.176
children.translated_text: <s>Laśuna</s> (garlic) is unctuous, hot, aphrodisiac, pungent, and heavy. // Car 1.27.176

children.text: śuṣkāṇi kaphavātaghnāny etāny eṣāṃ phalāni ca /
children.translated_text: When dried, these destroy <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; and these are the fruits of these [herbs].

children.text: haritānāmayaṃ caiṣa ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ samāpyate // Car_1,27.177
children.translated_text: This sixth group of fresh herbs (<s>harita</s>) is hereby concluded. // Car 1.27.177
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: haritānām apyārdrakādīnāṃ phalavadagnipākam antareṇa bhojanasya prāk paścāccopayogāt phalam anu haritakathanaṃ phalebhyastu paścādabhidhānaṃ haritasya tṛptyanādhāyakatvāt // 1
children.translated_text: The discussion of fresh herbs like fresh ginger etc. following fruits — since, like fruits, they are consumed before and after meals without [requiring] cooking on fire — and the statement of fresh herbs after fruits is because fresh herbs do not produce satiation. // 1
'Fresh' (<s>ārdraka</s>) is specified to distinguish it from dried ginger (<s>Śuṇṭhī</s>); the qualities of dried ginger will be stated in the group of food accessories. // 2
<s>Jambīra</s> is a variety of <s>Parṇāsa</s>; the <s>Jambīra</s> fruit is fragrant. // 3
'When young, it destroys the <s>doṣas</s>' — in the young stage, when the taste is undeveloped, it destroys all three <s>doṣas</s>. // 4

children.text: tantrāntaravacanaṃ hi yāvaddhi cāvyaktarasānvitāni navaprarūḍhāni ca mūlakāni bhavanti tāvallaghudīpanāni pittānilaśleṣmaharāṇi caiva // 5
children.translated_text: For the statement in other treatises says: 'As long as radishes are newly sprouted and of undeveloped taste, so long they are light, digestive-stimulant, and they destroy <s>pitta</s>, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>śleṣman</s>.' // 5

children.text: vṛddhaṃ tridoṣamiti tadevapravṛddham enāmeva mūlakāvasthām abhipretya coktaṃ mūlakaṃ kandānāmapathyatve prakṛṣṭatamam iti mārutāpahaṃ snigdhasiddhamiti sāmānyena bālaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca // 6
children.translated_text: 'Mature produces all three <s>doṣas</s>' — that same [radish] when fully grown. It is with reference to this very mature state of radish that it is said: 'Radish is the worst among the tubers as unwholesome.' 'Removes <s>vāta</s> when cooked in oil' — this applies generally to both the young and the old [radish]. // 6

children.text: śuṣkāṇi kaphavātaghnānyetāni iti vakṣyamāṇagranthenaiva śuṣkakasya kaphavātahantṛtve labdhe punarvacanaṃ prakarṣaprāptyartham // 7
children.translated_text: 'When dried, these destroy <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>' — although the quality of the dried [herbs] is already established by the forthcoming passage, the repetition is for the purpose of indicating special excellence. // 7

children.text: pūtigandhaheti śarīrasya tathā vyañjanārthaṃ māṃsasya ca pūtigandhatāṃ hanti // 8
children.translated_text: 'Eliminates foul odor' — it destroys the foul odor of the body as well as that of meat, for the purpose of flavoring. // 8
<s>Arjaka</s> is white <s>Parṇāsa</s> (basil). // 9

children.text: śigruḥ viṭapaśobhāñjanaḥ śāleyaś cāṇakyamūlaṃ marau prasiddhaṃ kiṃvā śāleyam iti misteyaṃ pāṭakaprasiddhaṃ vacanaṃ hi cāṇakyamūlamisteye śāleyābhikhyayā jaguḥ iti mṛṣṭakaṃ rājikā // 10
children.translated_text: <s>Śigru</s> is the tree-beautifying <s>Śobhāñjana</s> (Moringa). <s>Śāleya</s> is <s>Cāṇakyamūla</s>, well-known in the desert region. Or alternatively, <s>Śāleya</s> is <s>Misteya</s> (a type of fennel), well-known in <s>Pāṭaka</s>. For the statement says: 'They call <s>Cāṇakyamūla</s> by the name <s>Śāleya</s> in <s>Misteya</s>.' <s>Mṛṣṭaka</s> is <s>Rājikā</s> (mustard). // 10

children.text: gaṇḍīro dvividho raktaḥ śuklaśca tatra yo raktaḥ sa hi kaṭutvena haritavarge paṭhyate yastu śuklo jalajaḥ sa śākavarge paṭhita iti naikasya vargadvaye pāṭhaḥ // 11
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṇḍīra</s> is of two kinds — red and white. The red one is listed in the fresh herb group due to its pungency. The white one, being aquatic, is listed in the vegetable group. Thus the same [plant] is not listed in two groups. // 11
<s>Jalapippalī</s> (water pepper) grows in water and has a pepper-like form. // 12

children.text: śṛṅgaverī gojihvikā kiṃvā ārdrakākṛtiḥ śṛṅgaverī yaduktaṃ śṛṅgaveravad ākṛtyā śṛṅgaverīti bhāṣitā // 13
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgaverī</s> is <s>Gojihvikā</s> (ox-tongue plant); or it has a form like fresh ginger (<s>Ārdraka</s>). As stated: 'Having a form like <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, it is called <s>Śṛṅgaverī</s>.' // 13
'Having a form like <s>Kustumburu</s> (coriander seed), they call it <s>Tumburūṇi</s>.' // 14
<s>Bhūstṛṇa</s> (lemongrass) is <s>Gandhatṛṇa</s> (fragrant grass). // 15
<s>Kharāhvā</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇajīraka</s> (black cumin). // 16
<s>Ajagandhā</s> is <s>Vanayavānī</s> (wild bishop's weed). // 17
<s>Sumukha</s> is a variety of <s>Parṇāsa</s>. // 18

children.text: ayaṃ ca dhānyakādīnām ārdrāṇāṃ guṇaḥ śuṣkāṇāṃ tv āhārayogigaṇe kāravī kuñcikā ityādinā guṇaṃ nirdekṣyati // 19
children.translated_text: And these are the qualities of <s>Dhānyaka</s> (coriander) etc. when fresh. The qualities of the dried [forms] will be stated in the food-accessory group with '<s>Kāravī</s>, <s>Kuñcikā</s>' etc. // 19
<s>Gṛñjanaka</s> is a type of <s>Palāṇḍu</s> (onion) with small stems and leaves. // 20
'These' means those mentioned in the fresh herb group. // 21

children.text: śuṣkāṇītyādinā yadyapi śuṣkāṇām api śuṇṭhīprabhṛtīnāṃ guṇa ukto bhavati tathāpi viśeṣaguṇāntarakathanārthaṃ punastadabhidhānam āhārasaṃyogivarge bhaviṣyatīti na paunaruktyam // 22]
children.translated_text: Although by 'When dried...' etc. the qualities of the dried forms such as <s>Śuṇṭhī</s> (dried ginger) etc. have also been stated, nevertheless the repetition [later] for the purpose of stating additional specific qualities in the food-accessory group — this is not redundancy. // 22]
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
Now we shall explain the chapter called <s>Vividhāśitapītīya</s> (On the Variety of Foods and Drinks Consumed). // Car 1.28.1
Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car 1.28.2
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: pūrvādhyāye annaṃ prāṇāḥ ityuktaṃ tadyena prakāreṇānnaṃ prāṇahetur bhavati tadabhidhānārthaṃ vividhāśitapītīyo 'bhidhīyate // 1
children.translated_text: In the previous chapter, it was said: 'Food is life.' The chapter <s>Vividhāśitapītīya</s> is taught for the purpose of explaining the manner in which food becomes the cause of life. // 1
This too is a name with reference to the meaning. // 2]

children.text: vividham aśitaṃ pītaṃ līḍhaṃ khāditaṃ jantorhitam antaragnisaṃdhukṣitabalena yathāsvenoṣmaṇā samyagvipacyamānaṃ kālavad anavasthitasarvadhātupākam anupahatasarvadhātūṣmamārutasrotaḥ kevalaṃ śarīramupacayabalavarṇasukhāyuṣā yojayati śarīradhātūn ūrjayati ca /
children.translated_text: The variety of food that is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed — when it is beneficial to the creature, when its strength has been kindled by the internal fire (<s>Agni</s>), when it is being properly digested by its own respective heat, [when the body is] like time in the unceasing digestion of all tissues, with the heat, wind (<s>mārutas</s>), and channels of all tissues unimpaired — it endows the entire body with nourishment, strength, complexion, and happiness-giving longevity, and it invigorates the bodily tissues.
For the tissues, being sustained by tissue-food, follow [their] natural constitution. // Car 1.28.3
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'Variety...' and so on. // 1

children.text: vividhamiti anenāśitādīnāmavāntarabhedaṃ darśayati aśitādiṣu yo yaḥ prāya upayujyate sa pūrvam uktaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'Variety' — by this he shows the sub-categories of things eaten etc. Whichever among eaten etc. is most commonly used is mentioned first. // 2

children.text: jantor hitam iti vacanam ahitasyāśitāder balavarṇādikartṛtvābhāvāt // 3
children.translated_text: 'Beneficial to the creature' — this qualification is because unhealthy food does not produce strength, complexion, etc. // 3

children.text: antaragninā jāṭhareṇa vahninā saṃdhukṣitaṃ balaṃ yasya tenāntaragnisaṃdhukṣitabalena // 4
children.translated_text: 'With strength kindled by the internal fire' — by the internal, i.e., gastric fire, whose strength has been ignited. // 4

children.text: yathāsvenoṣmaṇeti pṛthivyādirūpāśitādeyasya ya ūṣmā pārthivāgnyādirūpastena vacanaṃ hi bhaumāpyāgneyavāyavyāḥ pañcoṣmāṇaḥ sanābhasāḥ // 5
children.translated_text: 'By its own respective heat' — of the food eaten etc. in the form of earth etc., the heat which is of the nature of earthly fire etc. For the statement says: 'The five heats — earthy, watery, fiery, airy — along with the spatial one, // 5

children.text: pañcāhāraguṇān svān svān pārthivādīn pacanti hi iti // 6
children.translated_text: digest each their own respective food qualities — earthly and the rest.' // 6
'Being properly digested' — the food etc. // 7

children.text: kiṃvā yathāsvenoṣmaṇeti yasya rudhirāder ya ūṣmā dhātvagnirūpastena samyagvipacyamānamaśitādi rasatām āpannaṃ yadā raktādidhātūn pratipadyate tadā raktādyūṣmaṇaiva pacyate evaṃ vipacyamānamaśitādi śarīramupacayādinā yojayatyūrjayati vardhayatīti yojanā // 8
children.translated_text: Alternatively, 'by its own respective heat' — the heat of blood etc., which is the tissue-fire, by that. When food etc. that has attained the state of nutrient essence (<s>rasa</s>) reaches the blood and other tissues, it is digested by the heat of blood etc. itself. Food etc. being thus digested endows the body with nourishment etc. and invigorates, i.e., strengthens — this is the construction. // 8
What kind of body? — this he states with 'like time...' and so on. // 9

children.text: yathā kālo nityagatvenānavasthitaḥ tathānavasthitaḥ aviśrāntaḥ sarvadhātūnāṃ pāko yasmin śarīre tattathā etena sarvadā svāgnipākakṣīyamāṇadhātoḥ śarīrasyāśitādinopacayādiyojanam upapannamiti darśayati yadi hi pākakṣīyamāṇaṃ śarīraṃ na syāttadā svataḥ siddhe upacayādau kimaśitādi kuryād iti bhāvaḥ // 10
children.translated_text: As time is of perpetual motion and never-resting, so is the digestion of all tissues in that body — unceasing. By this he shows that the endowment of the body with nourishment etc. by food is justified because the body's tissues are constantly being depleted by their own digestive fire. For if the body were not being depleted by digestion, then — nourishment being self-evident — what would food etc. accomplish? This is the purport. // 10

children.text: kiṃvā kālavadityaśitādiviśeṣaṇaṃ tena yathoktakālakṛtam aśitādītyarthaḥ akālabhojanasyopacayādyakārakatvāt // 11
children.translated_text: Alternatively, 'like time' qualifies the food etc. — meaning food etc. consumed at the proper time. Because food eaten at the wrong time does not produce nourishment etc. // 11

children.text: tathā anavasthitasarvadhātupākamityetadapi aśitādiviśeṣaṇaṃ tena anavasthitaḥ sarvadhātuṣu pāko yasyāśitādestattathā etena kvacidapi dhātau sthagitasyāśitāde rasarūpasya pākavigamanān nopacayādir bhavatīti darśayati // 12
children.translated_text: Likewise 'with unceasing digestion of all tissues' also qualifies the food etc. — meaning that food etc. in which digestion is unceasing in all tissues. By this he shows that if food etc. in the form of nutrient essence is obstructed in any tissue and its digestion does not proceed, then nourishment etc. does not occur. // 12

children.text: etacca vyākhyānaṃ nātisundaram asyārthasya anupahatetyādiśarīraviśeṣaṇenaiva labdhatvāt punaḥ śarīraviśeṣaṇam anupapannam // 13
children.translated_text: This interpretation is not entirely elegant, since the meaning is already obtained from the qualification of the body with 'with unimpaired...' etc.; a further qualification of the body would be unfitting. // 13

children.text: anupahatetyādi anupahatāni sarvadhātūnām ūṣmamārutasrotāṃsi yasya tattathā yadā hi eko 'pi dhātupācako'gnirupahataḥ māruto vā dhātupoṣakarasavāhī vyānarūpaḥ kvacid upahato bhavati tathā sroto vā dhātupoṣakarasavaham upahataṃ syāt tadā aśitādikaṃ dhātūnām avardhakatvānnopacayādikārakam iti bhāvaḥ // 14
children.translated_text: 'With unimpaired...' etc. — when the heat, wind, and channels of all tissues are unimpaired. For when even one tissue-digesting fire is impaired, or the wind (<s>Vyāna</s>) that carries tissue-nourishing essence is impaired somewhere, or the channel carrying tissue-nourishing essence is impaired — then food etc. does not augment the tissues and therefore does not produce nourishment etc. This is the purport. // 14

children.text: kevalamiti kṛtsnaṃ śarīraṃ kiṃvā kevalamiti adharmarahitam adharmayukte hi śarīre viphalamaśitādi bhavatīti // 15
children.translated_text: 'Entire' (<s>kevala</s>) means the whole body. Or, '<s>kevala</s>' means 'free from <s>adharma</s>' (demerit) — for in a body associated with <s>adharma</s>, food etc. becomes fruitless. // 15

children.text: nanu śarīradhātūnāṃ prakṛtisthitānāṃ svata evopacayādyasti tat kimaśitādinā kriyata ityāha dhātavo hītyādi // 16
children.translated_text: Objection: The bodily tissues in their natural state inherently possess nourishment etc.; so what does food etc. accomplish? He addresses this with 'For the tissues...' and so on. // 16

children.text: dhāturāhāro yeṣāṃ te dhātvāhārāḥ dhātavo rasādayo nityaṃ kṣīyamāṇā aśitādijanitadhātvāhārā eva santaḥ paraṃ svāsthyamanuvartante nānyathetyarthaḥ // 17]
children.translated_text: 'Tissue-food' — those whose food is the tissues; <s>dhātvāhāras</s> (tissue-foods). The tissues — <s>rasa</s> (nutrient fluid) etc. — constantly undergoing depletion, subsisting only on the tissue-food generated by food etc., maintain health — not otherwise. This is the meaning. // 17]

children.text:
tatrāhāraprasādākhyo rasaḥ kiṭṭaṃ ca malākhyam abhinirvartate /
kiṭṭāt svedapurīṣavātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ karṇākṣināsikāsyalomakūpaprajananamalāḥ keśaśmaśrulomanakhādayaś cāvayavāḥ puṣyanti /
puṣyanti tv āhārarasād rasarudhiramāṃsamedo'sthimajjaśukraujāṃsi pañcendriyadravyāṇi dhātuprasādasaṃjñakāni śarīrasaṃdhibandhapicchādayaś cāvayavāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therein, from the food, a nutrient essence called <s>rasa</s> (chyle) and waste called <s>kiṭṭa</s> (refuse) are produced. From the waste — sweat, feces, <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Kapha</s>, and the waste products of the ears, eyes, nose, mouth, and hair-follicles — and the body parts like head-hair, beard, body-hair, nails, etc. are nourished. But from the nutrient essence of food — <s>rasa</s> (chyle), <s>rudhira</s> (blood), <s>māṃsa</s> (flesh), <s>medas</s> (fat), <s>asthi</s> (bone), <s>majjā</s> (marrow), <s>śukra</s> (reproductive tissue), and <s>ojas</s> (vital essence), the substances of the five sense-organs, called the refined products of the tissues, and body parts like joint-bindings, lubricants, etc. are nourished.

children.text: te sarva eva dhātavo malākhyāḥ prasādākhyāśca rasamalābhyāṃ puṣyantaḥ svaṃ mānamanuvartante yathāvayaḥśarīram /
children.translated_text: All these tissues — both those called waste and those called refined products — being nourished by the nutrient essence and the waste, maintain their proper measure according to age and body.

children.text: evaṃ rasamalau svapramāṇāvasthitāv āśrayasya samadhātordhātusāmyam anuvartayataḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the nutrient essence and waste, remaining in their proper measure, maintain the equilibrium of tissues in the body whose tissues are balanced.

children.text: nimittatastu kṣīṇavṛddhānāṃ prasādākhyānāṃ dhātūnāṃ vṛddhikṣayābhyām āhāramūlābhyāṃ rasaḥ sāmyam utpādayatyārogyāya kiṭṭaṃ ca malānāmevameva /
children.translated_text: And due to specific causes, for tissues called refined products that have become diminished or increased, the nutrient essence produces equilibrium through increase and decrease, [both of] which are rooted in food — [this leads to] health.
