And the waste does the same for the waste products.

children.text: svamānātiriktāḥ punarutsargiṇaḥ śītoṣṇaparyāyaguṇaiś copacaryamāṇā malāḥ śarīradhātusāmyakarāḥ samupalabhyante // Car_1,28.4
children.translated_text: Furthermore, the waste products, when exceeding their proper measure, tending to be expelled, and being treated with alternating cold and hot qualities, are found to be the agents of tissue-equilibrium in the body. // Car 1.28.4
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He states that which is the food of the tissues with 'Therein...' and so on. // 1
'Therein' means in [things] eaten etc. // 2
The construction is: '<s>rasa</s> (nutrient essence) and <s>kiṭṭa</s> (waste) are produced.' // 3

children.text: āhāraprasāda ityākhyā yasya sa tathā prasādaḥ sāraḥ // 4
children.translated_text: 'Food-essence' (<s>āhāraprasāda</s>) — that whose name is thus — '<s>prasāda</s>' means the essential portion. // 4
'Waste' (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) is the non-essential portion. // 5

children.text: kiṭṭād iti kiṭṭāṃśāt tena annādyaḥ kiṭṭāṃśas tato mūtrapurīṣe bhavato vāyuśca rasāt pacyamānānmalaḥ kaphaḥ evamādi grahaṇyadhyāye vakṣyamāṇam anusartavyaṃ vakṣyati hi /
children.translated_text: 'From waste' means from the waste-portion. Thus, the waste-portion of food [gives rise to] urine and feces, and <s>vāta</s> too; the waste of <s>rasa</s> being digested is <s>kapha</s> — and so on, what will be stated in the <s>Grahaṇī</s> chapter should be followed. For it will be stated:
The waste of food is feces and urine; of <s>rasa</s> — <s>kapha</s>; of blood —

children.text: pittaṃ māṃsasya svamalo malaḥ svedastu medasaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: <s>pitta</s>; of flesh — its own waste; and of fat — sweat. // 6

children.text: syāt kiṭṭaṃ keśalomāsthno majjñaḥ sneho'kṣiviṭ tvacām /
children.translated_text: The waste of hair-on-head and body-hair is bone; of marrow — the unctuous [secretion] of the eyes, skin-moisture, etc.
By the word 'ādi' (etc.), eye-unctuousness and so on should be included. // 8

children.text: yadyapi ca vāto'naśanād apyupalabhyate tathāpi rūkṣakiṭṭādibhojanamalāṃśād apyutpadyata eveti kiṭṭādvātotpattiryuktaiva na cāyaṃ niyamo yanmalādevotpadyata iti vyāyāmādavagāhāderapi ca vātādisadbhāvāt // 9
children.translated_text: Although <s>vāta</s> is observed even from fasting [i.e., without food], nevertheless it is also produced from the waste-portion of dry, waste-predominant food; so the production of <s>vāta</s> from waste is indeed justified. And there is no strict rule that [<s>vāta</s>] is produced only from waste, since <s>vāta</s> etc. also arise from exercise, bathing, and the like. // 9
'Generation' (<s>prajanana</s>) means the reproductive organ. // 10
He states what is nourished by <s>rasa</s> with 'They nourish' etc. // 11
'Substances of the five senses' (<s>pañcendriyadravyāṇi</s>) means earth and the other [elements] which are the causes of the sense-organs — smell etc. // 12
'Called tissue-essence' (<s>dhātuprasādasaṃjñaka</s>) — he shows that the sense-organs are produced only by the extremely pure tissue-essence. // 13
'Binds the body' (<s>śarīraṃ badhnāti</s>) — hence [it is called] 'body-binding' — by means of ligaments, veins, and the like. // 14
By the word 'ādi' (etc.), menstrual blood, breast-milk, and the like are included. // 15

children.text: atrāhārarasād raktādipoṣaṇe kecid bruvate yat raso raktarūpatayā pariṇamati raktaṃ ca māṃsarūpatayā evaṃ māṃsādayo 'pyuttarottaradhāturūpatayā pariṇamanti // 16
children.translated_text: Here, regarding the nourishment of blood etc. by the food-<s>rasa</s>, some say that <s>rasa</s> transforms into the form of blood, and blood transforms into the form of flesh — thus flesh and the rest also transform successively into the form of the next higher tissue. // 16

children.text: atrāpi ca pakṣe kecid bruvate kṣīrād yathā sarvātmanā dadhi bhavati tathā kṛtsno raso raktaṃ bhavati evaṃ raktādayo'pi māṃsādirūpā bhavanti // 17
children.translated_text: And in this view too, some say: just as milk becomes curd in its entirety, so the entire <s>rasa</s> becomes blood. Likewise, blood etc. also become flesh etc. in form. // 17

children.text: anye tv āhuḥ kedārīkulyānyāyena rasasya dhātupoṣaṇaṃ tatrānnādutpanno raso dhāturūpaṃ rasamadhigamya kiyatāpyaṃśena taṃ rasaṃ vardhayati aparaśca rasarāśistatra gataḥ san śoṇitagandhavarṇayuktatvācchoṇitam iva bhūtvā kiyatāpi śoṇitasamānenāṃśena dhāturūpaṃ śoṇitaṃ puṣṇāti śeṣaśca bhāgo māṃsaṃ yāti tatrāpi śoṇitavadvyavasthā tathā medaḥprabhṛtiṣvapīti // 18
children.translated_text: Others however say: the nourishment of tissues by <s>rasa</s> follows the principle of irrigation-channels (<s>kedārīkulyā-nyāya</s>). In this [view], the <s>rasa</s> produced from food, having reached the tissue-form <s>rasa</s>, nourishes that <s>rasa</s> with a certain portion. And another mass of <s>rasa</s>, having gone there, being endowed with the smell and color of blood, becoming as if blood, nourishes the tissue-form blood with a portion similar to blood. And the remaining portion goes to flesh — and there too the arrangement is as with blood. Likewise for fat and the rest also. // 18

children.text: ata eva ca mukhyārtho 'yaṃ grantho bhavati yathā /
children.translated_text: And for this very reason, the following text has its primary meaning:

children.text: rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsaṃ māṃsānmedastato'sthi ca /
children.translated_text: From <s>rasa</s> [arises] blood, from that flesh, from flesh fat, from that bone,

children.text: asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukrādgarbhaḥ prasādajaḥ // 19
children.translated_text: from bone marrow, from that semen, from semen the embryo — born of the essence. // 19

children.text: iti tathā hārīte'pyuktaṃ rasaḥ saptāhādarvāk parivartamānaḥ śvetakapotaharitahāridrapadmakiṃśukālaktakarasaprakhyaś cāyaṃ yathākramaṃ divasaparivartād varṇaparivartam āpadyamānaḥ pittoṣmoparāgācchoṇitatvam āpadyate iti tathā suśrute 'pyuktaṃ sa khalvāpyo rasa ekaikasmin dhātau trīṇi trīṇi kalāsahasrāṇi pañcadaśa ca kalā avatiṣṭhate evaṃ māsena rasaḥ śukrībhavati iti // 20
children.translated_text: And likewise it is stated in <s>Hārīta</s>: '<s>Rasa</s>, transforming within seven days, appearing like white, pigeon-gray, green, yellow, lotus-colored, <s>kiṃśuka</s>-red, and lac-juice [in color] — undergoing color-transformation day by day in sequence — by the coloring action of <s>pitta</s>-heat, attains the state of blood.' And likewise it is stated in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'That watery <s>rasa</s> remains in each tissue for three thousand and fifteen <s>kalās</s> — thus in a month, <s>rasa</s> becomes semen.' // 20

children.text: anye tv āhuḥ khalekapotanyāyenāyam annarasaḥ pṛthak pṛthag dhātumārge gataḥ san rasādīn poṣayati na tv asya dhātupoṣako rasabhāgo dhātvantareṇa samaṃ sambandham apyanubhavati rasādipoṣakāni srotāṃsyuttarottaraṃ sūkṣmamukhāni dīrghāṇi ca tenaiva rasapoṣakarasabhāgo rasamārgacāritvād rasaṃ poṣayati evaṃ rasapoṣaṇakālād uttarakālaṃ raktapoṣako rasabhāgo raktaṃ poṣayati tathā śoṇitapoṣaṇakālād uttarakālaṃ māṃsapoṣako rasabhāgo māṃsaṃ poṣayati vidūrasūkṣmamārgacāritvāt evaṃ medaḥprabhṛtipoṣaṇe'pi jñeyam // 21
children.translated_text: Others however say: by the principle of the threshing-floor pigeons (<s>khalekapota-nyāya</s>), this food-<s>rasa</s>, having gone separately into each tissue-pathway, nourishes <s>rasa</s> and the rest; but the portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes a tissue does not even experience a connection with another tissue. The channels nourishing <s>rasa</s> and the rest have progressively finer openings and are longer. Therefore the portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes <s>rasa</s> — because it travels through the <s>rasa</s>-pathway — nourishes <s>rasa</s>. Likewise, at a time after the time of <s>rasa</s>-nourishment, the blood-nourishing portion of <s>rasa</s> nourishes blood. Likewise, at a time after blood-nourishment, the flesh-nourishing portion of <s>rasa</s> nourishes flesh — because it travels through a distant, subtle pathway. The same should be understood for the nourishment of fat and the rest. // 21

children.text: tena rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsam ityāder ayam artho yatra rasapuṣṭikālād uttarakālaṃ raktaṃ jāyate tathā raktapuṣṭikālād uttarakālaṃ māṃsaṃ prajāyate ityādi // 22
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning of 'from <s>rasa</s> [arises] blood, from that flesh' etc. is this: blood arises at a time after the time of <s>rasa</s>-nourishment, and flesh arises at a time after the time of blood-nourishment — and so on. // 22
The statements of <s>Suśruta</s> and <s>Hārīta</s> too should be explained in this way. // 23

children.text: yacca raktaṃ vibaddhamārgatvān māṃsādīnna prapadyate iti rājayakṣmaṇi vakṣyati taddhṛdayacāriśoṇitābhiprāyeṇa na tu poṣakaśoṇitābhiprāyeṇa // 24
children.translated_text: And as for what will be stated in [the section on] <s>rājayakṣman</s> — that blood, because its pathway is obstructed, does not proceed to flesh etc. — that is intended with reference to the blood circulating in the heart, not with reference to the nourishing blood. // 24

children.text: kiṃca pariṇāmapakṣe vṛṣyaprayogasya raktādirūpatāpattikrameṇāticireṇa śukraṃ bhavatīti kṣīrādayaśca sadya eva vṛṣyā dṛśyante khalekapotapakṣe tu vṛṣyotpanno rasaḥ prabhāvācchīghrameva śukreṇa sambaddhaḥ san tatpuṣṭiṃ karotīti yuktaṃ tathā rasaduṣṭau satyāṃ pariṇāmapakṣe tajjanmanāṃ śoṇitādīnāṃ sarveṣāmeva duṣṭiḥ syāt duṣṭakāraṇajātatvāt // 25
children.translated_text: Moreover, in the transformation view, an aphrodisiac preparation would produce semen only after a very long time — since it must undergo the successive stages of becoming blood etc. — yet milk and the like are seen to be aphrodisiac immediately. In the threshing-floor pigeon view, however, the <s>rasa</s> produced by the aphrodisiac, by its inherent potency (<s>prabhāva</s>), quickly becomes connected with semen and promotes its nourishment — this is reasonable. Likewise, when <s>rasa</s> is vitiated, in the transformation view, all — blood etc. — that are born from it would necessarily be vitiated, since they are born from a vitiated cause. // 25

children.text: khalekapotapakṣe tu yaddhātupoṣako rasabhāgo duṣṭaḥ sa eva duṣyati na sarve taditareṣāmaduṣṭakāraṇatvāt tathā medovṛddhau satyāṃ bhūrikāraṇatvenāsthnāpi bhūyasā bhavitavyaṃ dṛśyate ca bhūrimedasa itaradhātuparikṣayaḥ vacanaṃ ca medasvino meda evopacīyate na tathetare dhātavaḥ iti evamādi pariṇāmavāde dūṣaṇam // 26
children.translated_text: In the threshing-floor pigeon view, however, only that portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes a [particular] tissue and is vitiated — only that becomes vitiated, not all — because the other [portions] do not have a vitiated cause. Likewise, when fat is increased, bone too should increase abundantly, since [fat] is its abundant cause. But what is observed is that in one with abundant fat, the other tissues diminish. And the statement is: 'In one who has excess fat, only fat accumulates, not the other tissues likewise.' Such and similar [arguments] constitute the refutation of the transformation theory. // 26

children.text: eṣu ca pakṣeṣu sarvātmapariṇāmavādo viruddha eva yena sarvātmapariṇāme tricaturopavāsenaiva nīrasatvāccharīrasya maraṇaṃ syāt māsopavāse kevalaṃ śukramayaṃ śarīraṃ syāt // 27
children.translated_text: And among these views, the total-transformation theory is indeed contradicted — for if there were total transformation, then after merely three or four fasts, death would occur due to the body being without <s>rasa</s>; and after a month's fast, the body would be composed entirely of semen. // 27

children.text: kedārīkulyānyāyas tu tulyabala eva khalekapotanyāyena yato yad uktaṃ vṛṣyaprabhāvaṃ prati tat kedārīkulyāpakṣe'pi prabhāvādeva śīghraṃ raktādidhātūnabhigamya śukraṃ janayiṣyati vṛṣyaṃ yathā khalekapotapakṣe'pi prabhavāditi // 28
children.translated_text: The irrigation-channel principle, however, is of equal strength with the threshing-floor pigeon principle, because what was said regarding the potency of aphrodisiacs — in the irrigation-channel view too, the aphrodisiac will by its potency quickly reach the blood and other tissues and generate semen, just as in the threshing-floor pigeon view [it does so] by its potency. // 28

children.text: yattu rasaduṣṭau śoṇitadūṣaṇaṃ tanna bhavati dhātubhūtaśoṇitāṃśapoṣakasya rasabhāgasyāduṣṭatvāt iti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // 29
children.translated_text: And as for [the objection that] when <s>rasa</s> is vitiated, blood should be vitiated — that does not apply, because the portion of <s>rasa</s> that nourishes the tissue-form blood-portion is not vitiated — this is the same as the previous [argument]. // 29

children.text: atrāpi hi pakṣe na sarvo raso dhāturūpaśoṇitatām āpadyate kiṃ tarhi kaścideva śoṇitasamāno bhāgaḥ śeṣastu śoṇitasthānagatatvena kiṃcicchoṇitasamānavarṇāditvācca śoṇitam ucyate anena nyāyena medovṛddhau satyāmasthivṛddhir api nirastā yato na medasā asthi poṣyate api tarhi medaḥsthānagatenaiva rasena medo'nukāriṇā // 30
children.translated_text: For in this view too, not all <s>rasa</s> transforms into the tissue-form blood; rather, only a certain portion similar to blood [does so], while the remainder, being located in the place of blood and being somewhat similar to blood in color etc., is called 'blood.' By this principle, when fat is increased, the increase of bone too is precluded — because bone is not nourished by fat, but rather by <s>rasa</s> that has gone to the place of fat and resembles fat. // 30

children.text: evamanayoḥ pakṣayormahājanādṛtatvena tulyanyāyatvena ca naikamapi niścitaṃ buddhivibhavānna pakṣabalābalam atra na kaścit kāryavirodha ityuparamyate // 31
children.translated_text: Thus, since these two views are equally respected by the learned and have equal logical force, neither one is conclusively [established]. By the power of intellect, neither the strength nor the weakness of either view [can be determined] — there is no contradiction with [observed] effects here — so we desist. // 31

children.text: nanvāhārarasādayaḥ puṣyantīti vadatā dhāturasādāhārarasotpādaḥ pṛthak svīkriyate tataśca tasya kiṃ sthānaṃ kiṃvā pramāṇam iti kimiti noktam ucyate na tasyāhārotkarṣāpakarṣāv evaṃvidhau utkarṣāpakarṣasya niścitapramāṇatvābhāvāt sthānaṃ tu dhamanya eva // 32
children.translated_text: Objection: By saying 'food-<s>rasa</s> and the rest nourish,' the generation of food-<s>rasa</s> from tissue-<s>rasa</s> is accepted as separate — so what is its location and what is its measure? Why is this not stated? Reply: Its excess and deficiency are not of such a kind — because there is no fixed measure for excess and deficiency. And its location is in the vessels (<s>dhamanīs</s>) alone. // 32

children.text: poṣakāhārarasasya tasya ca pṛthagrasādidhātubhyaḥ pradeśāntaragrahaṇaṃ na kriyate rasādikāraṇarūpatayā rasādigrahaṇenaiva grahaṇāt // 33
children.translated_text: And for that nourishing food-<s>rasa</s>, no separate apprehension as distinct from <s>rasa</s> etc. tissues is made — because it is included in the [concept of] <s>rasa</s> etc. [themselves], in its capacity as the cause of <s>rasa</s> etc. // 33

children.text: atra yadyapyojaḥ saptadhātusārarūpaṃ tena dhātugrahaṇenaiva labhyate tathāpi prāṇadhāraṇakartṛtvena pṛthak paṭhitaṃ ye tu śukrajanyamoja icchanti teṣāmaṣṭamo dhāturojaḥ syāditi pakṣe cātideśaṃ kṛtvā vakṣyati rasādīnāṃ śukrāntānāṃ yat paraṃ tejaḥ tat khalvojaḥ iti // 34
children.translated_text: Here, although <s>ojas</s> is of the nature of the essence of the seven tissues and is thus obtainable by the term 'tissue' itself, it is read separately because of its role as the sustainer of life. And for those who hold that <s>ojas</s> is born from semen — in the view that <s>ojas</s> would be the eighth tissue — he will state by way of analogy: 'That supreme splendor of <s>rasa</s> and the rest up to semen — that indeed is <s>ojas</s>.' // 34

children.text: upapāditapoṣaṇānāṃ dhātumalānāṃ prakṛtyanuvidhānam upasaṃharati te sarva ityādi // 35
children.translated_text: He concludes the conformity to nature of the tissue-wastes whose nourishment has been established, with 'All those' etc. // 35

children.text: malākhyā api svedamūtrādayaḥ svamānāvasthitā dehadhāraṇāddhātavo bhavantītyuktaṃ dhātavo malākhyā iti // 36
children.translated_text: Even those called wastes — sweat, urine, etc. — when established in their own measure, become tissues [i.e., they support the body] by virtue of sustaining the body. Thus it is said: 'tissues called wastes.' // 36

children.text: yathāvayaḥśarīram iti yasmin vayasi bālyādau yādṛśaṃ mānaṃ dhātūnāṃ tādṛśaṃ puṣyantaḥ tathā yasmin śarīre prakṛtyā dīrghe hrasve kṛśe vā sthūle vā yādṛśaṃ mānaṃ dhātūnāṃ tādṛśaṃ puṣyanta iti yojanā // 37
children.translated_text: 'According to age and body' — the meaning is: in whatever age — childhood etc. — whatever is the measure of tissues, they nourish them to that extent; likewise in whatever body — naturally tall or short, thin or corpulent — whatever is the measure of tissues, they nourish them to that extent. // 37

children.text: evam ityādau svapramāṇāvasthitāv iti anatiriktāv anyūnau ca // 38
children.translated_text: In 'thus' etc., 'established in their own measure' means neither excessive nor deficient. // 38

children.text: āśrayasyeti śarīrasya yathāvatpakvau sarvāśrayaṃ paścāddhamanībhiḥ prapadyete sarvaśarīram ityarthaḥ // 39
children.translated_text: 'Of the substrate' means of the body. 'When properly digested' — afterwards through the vessels they reach the entire substrate, i.e., the entire body — this is the meaning. // 39
'Of one with balanced tissues' means of one with balanced <s>rasa</s> etc. and balanced sweat, urine, etc. // 40
'By cause' (<s>nimittataḥ</s>) etc. // 41
By 'by cause,' he excludes increase and decrease that are causeless — i.e., that are in the form of prognostic signs. // 42

children.text: vṛddhikṣayābhyām āhāramūlābhyām iti yathāsaṃkhyaṃ vṛddhakṣīṇāhārakṛtābhyām etenāhāraviśeṣakṛtavṛddhikṣayo rasaḥ sāmyaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // 43
children.translated_text: 'By increase and decrease rooted in food' — in order: produced by excessive and diminished food. By this [it means that] the <s>rasa</s> whose increase and decrease are caused by specific foods creates equilibrium — this is the meaning. // 43

children.text: dhātusāmyasyārogyatve siddhe'pi yadārogyāyeti brūte tena prākṛtadhātūnāṃ kṣayeṇa vātivṛddhyā vā sāmyaṃ nirākaroti asya sāmyasya rogakartṛtvād eva // 44
children.translated_text: Even though the health-producing [nature] of tissue-equilibrium is established, the reason he says 'for health' is to exclude the equilibrium [that results from] the decrease of natural tissues or their excessive increase — since such equilibrium is itself a cause of disease. // 44

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ ca malānāmevam eveti yathā rasastathā kiṭṭamapyārogyāya malānāṃ sāmyaṃ pratipāditarasakrameṇa karoti // 45
children.translated_text: And the waste (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) similarly — just as <s>rasa</s> [promotes health], so too waste promotes health by creating equilibrium of the wastes through the established sequence of <s>rasa</s>. // 45
He states another treatment for increased wastes with 'in their own measure' etc. // 46

children.text: utsargo bahirniḥsaraṇaṃ saṃśodhanarūpameṣāṃ śāstroktamasti utsargaṃ vā vahantītyutsargiṇaḥ // 47
children.translated_text: 'Excretion' (<s>utsarga</s>) means external expulsion — in the form of purification as taught in the treatises. Or, 'those that carry out excretion' (<s>utsargiṇaḥ</s>) — [i.e., the substances that effect excretion]. // 47
He states another treatment for increased wastes with 'cold, hot' etc. // 48

children.text: paryayaḥ viparyayaḥ tena śītoṣṇaviparītaguṇair ityarthaḥ tena śītasamutthe male uṣṇaṃ tathoṣṇasamutthe śītamupacāro bhavati // 49
children.translated_text: 'Alternation' (<s>paryaya</s>) means reversal. Thus: 'with qualities opposite to cold and hot' — this is the meaning. Thus, for a waste arising from cold, the remedy is hot; likewise for one arising from heat, the remedy is cold. // 49

children.text: ādiśabdaś cātra luptanirdiṣṭaḥ tena snigdharūkṣādīnāmapi viparītaguṇānāṃ grahaṇam // 50
children.translated_text: And the word 'ādi' (etc.) here is employed with an implied [qualifier]. Thus, the inclusion of opposite qualities such as unctuous and dry etc. is [intended]. // 50

children.text: kiṃvā paryayaguṇā dvaṃdvaguṇāḥ snigdharūkṣamṛdutīkṣṇādayaḥ taiśca yathāyogyatayopacaryamāṇā iti jñeyam // 51
children.translated_text: Or, 'alternating qualities' means paired qualities — unctuous-and-dry, soft-and-sharp, etc. And [the wastes] should be treated with these appropriately — this should be known. // 51

children.text: etena vṛddhamalānāṃ trividho 'pyupakramo nidānavarjanaśodhanaśamanarūpa ukto bhavati tatra nidānavarjanaṃ vṛddhamale malavṛddhihetvāhāraparityāgād alpamalāhāropayogād vā boddhavyaṃ saṃśodhanaṃ ca utsargiṇa ityanenoktaṃ śamanaṃ ca śītoṣṇetyādi granthenoktam // 52]
children.translated_text: By this, a threefold approach to increased wastes is stated — consisting of avoidance of causes, purification, and pacification. Among these, avoidance of causes in the case of increased waste should be understood as the abandonment of food that causes waste-increase, or the use of food that is low in waste. Purification is stated by [the word] 'those that excrete.' And pacification is stated by the text 'cold, hot' etc. // 52]
For those tissues — called both waste and essence — the channels (<s>srotas</s>) are the pathways and openings.
They fill the tissues according to their respective divisions, each to its own.
Thus this body originates from what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed.
And diseases in this body originate from what is eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed.
The specifics of wholesome and unwholesome use — these are the producers of good and bad [health] outcomes. // <s>Car</s>_1,28.5
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: ayanāni ca tāni mukhāni cetyayanamukhāni atra āyāntyanenetyayanāni mārgāṇi mukhāni tu yaiḥ praviśanti etena malānāṃ dhātūnāṃ ca yadevāyanaṃ tadeva praveśamukhamiti nānyena praveśo nānyena ca gamanam ityuktaṃ bhavati // 1
children.translated_text: 'Pathway-openings' (<s>ayanamukhāni</s>) — pathways (<s>ayana</s>) are that through which [substances] travel, i.e., routes; openings (<s>mukhāni</s>) are those through which [substances] enter. By this it is stated that for the wastes and tissues, the pathway itself is the opening of entry — there is no entry by one [route] and movement by another. // 1
And the channel-openings and pathways of <s>rasa</s> etc. are named after their respective [tissues]. // 2

children.text: kiṃvā ayanasya gamanasya mukhāni mārgāṇi tena ayanamukhāni gatimārgāṇītyarthaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: Or, 'openings of passage' — i.e., pathways of movement; thus 'pathway-openings' means routes of movement — this is the meaning. // 3

children.text: tāni ca srotāṃsi malaprasādapūritāni dhātūn yathāsvamiti yadyasya poṣyaṃ tacca tat pūrayati // 4
children.translated_text: And those channels, filled with waste and essence, fill the tissues 'each to its own' — i.e., whatever is to be nourished by whatever, that fills that. // 4

children.text: yathāvibhāgeneti yasya dhātoryo vibhāgaḥ pramāṇaṃ tenaiva pramāṇena pūrayati tādṛkpramāṇānyeva puṣyanti nādhikanyūnānītyarthaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: 'According to their respective divisions' means: it nourishes with the very measure that is the division (proportion) of each tissue — meaning, it promotes those of exactly such measure, neither excessive nor deficient. // 5

children.text: etacca prakṛtisthānāṃ karma vikṛtānāṃ tu nyūnātiriktadhātukaraṇam astyeveti boddhavyam // 6
children.translated_text: And this [proportion-maintaining function] is the action of tissues in their natural state; for tissues in a disturbed state, the production of deficient or excessive tissue does indeed occur — this should be understood. // 6

children.text: uktaṃ cānyatra srotasā ca yathāsvena dhātuḥ puṣyati dhātunā iti // 7
children.translated_text: And it is stated elsewhere: 'And through each channel, the tissue is nourished by [the preceding] tissue.' // 7
He concludes with 'Thus' and so on. // 8
How is there the production — from what is eaten etc. — of the mutually opposed [pair of] body and diseases that damage the body? This he answers with 'Wholesome and unwholesome' and so on. // 9

children.text: hitarūpo'śitādiviśeṣaḥ śubharūpaviśeṣakārakaḥ ahitarūpastvaśitādiviśeṣo 'śubharūpaviśeṣakaro bhavati tena naikarūpāt kāraṇād viruddhakāryodaya iti bhāvaḥ // 10]
children.translated_text: A specific form of what-is-eaten that has the nature of 'wholesome' produces specific good outcomes; while a specific form of what-is-eaten that has the nature of 'unwholesome' produces specific bad outcomes. Therefore, it is not from a single-natured cause that contradictory effects arise — this is the purport. // 10]

children.text: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca dṛśyante hi bhagavan hitasamākhyātam apyāhāramupayuñjānā vyādhimantaś cāgadāś ca tathaivāhitasamākhyātam evaṃ dṛṣṭe kathaṃ hitāhitopayogaviśeṣātmakaṃ śubhāśubhaviśeṣam upalabhāmaha iti // Car_1,28.6
children.translated_text: To the blessed <s>Ātreya</s> who was speaking thus, <s>Agniveśa</s> said: 'Blessed one! For it is observed that some who consume food declared to be wholesome are diseased, and some are disease-free; and likewise [some who consume food] declared to be unwholesome [are diseased and some disease-free]. This being observed, how can we ascertain that good and bad [health] outcomes are of the nature of specific wholesome and unwholesome use?' // Car_1,28.6
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: dṛśyante hi bhagavannityādau tathaivāhitasamākhyātam upayuñjānā vyādhimantaś cāgadāśceti sambandhaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: In 'For it is observed, Blessed one' etc., the connection is: '...and likewise those consuming [food] declared to be unwholesome are diseased and also disease-free.' // 1
'Of the nature of specific [use]' (<s>viśeṣātmakam</s>) means: arising from the specific [use]. // 2]

children.text:
tamuvāca bhagavānātreyo na hitāhāropayoginām agniveśa tannimittā vyādhayo jāyante na ca kevalaṃ hitāhāropayogādeva sarvavyādhibhayam atikrāntaṃ bhavati santi hy ṛte 'pyahitāhāropayogād anyā rogaprakṛtayaḥ tadyathā kālaviparyayaḥ prajñāparādhaḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhāścāsātmyā iti /
tāśca rogaprakṛtayo rasān samyagupayuñjānamapi puruṣam aśubhenopapādayanti tasmāddhitāhāropayogino'pi dṛśyante vyādhimantaḥ /
ahitāhāropayogināṃ punaḥ kāraṇato na sadyo doṣavān bhavatyapacāraḥ /
na hi sarvāṇyapathyāni tulyadoṣāṇi na ca sarve doṣāstulyabalā na ca sarvāṇi śarīrāṇi vyādhikṣamatve samarthāni bhavanti /
tadeva hy apathyaṃ deśakālasaṃyogavīryapramāṇātiyogād bhūyastaram apathyaṃ sampadyate /
children.translated_text:
The blessed <s>Ātreya</s> said to him: 'O <s>Agniveśa</s>, in those who consume wholesome food, diseases do not arise from that cause; nor is all fear of disease overcome merely by the consumption of wholesome food alone. For apart from the consumption of unwholesome food, there exist other causes of disease (<s>rogaprakṛti</s>) — namely: reversal of seasons, intellectual error (<s>prajñāparādha</s>), and sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells that are unsuitable.
And those causes of disease afflict with bad [health] outcomes even a person who properly consumes the [correct] tastes. Therefore, even consumers of wholesome food are seen to be diseased.
As for those who consume unwholesome food — their transgression does not immediately become harmful, for a reason.
For not all unwholesome [foods] produce equal [degrees of] <s>doṣa</s>-vitiation; nor are all <s>doṣas</s> of equal strength; nor are all bodies equally capable of disease-resistance.
That very unwholesome [food] — through excess of place, time, combination, potency, and measure — becomes even more unwholesome.

children.text: sa eva doṣa saṃsṛṣṭayonirviruddhopakramo gambhīrānugataś cirasthitaḥ prāṇāyatanasamuttho marmopaghātī kaṣṭatamaḥ kṣiprakāritamaśca sampadyate /
children.translated_text: That very <s>doṣa</s> — when its causes are combined, when its treatment is contradictory, when it has penetrated deep [tissues], when it is long-standing, when it arises in a vital organ, and when it damages a <s>marma</s> (vital point) — becomes most severe and most rapidly acting.

children.text: śarīrāṇi cātisthūlānyatikṛśāny aniviṣṭamāṃsaśoṇitāsthīni durbalāny asātmyāhāropacitāny alpāhārāṇy alpasattvāni ca bhavantyavyādhisahāni viparītāni punarvyādhisahāni /
children.translated_text: And bodies that are excessively corpulent or excessively thin, with loosely-set flesh, blood, and bones, that are weak, nourished on unsuitable food, of scanty food-intake, and of low vitality — these are unable to withstand disease. The opposite [types of bodies] are disease-resistant.

children.text: ebhyaś caivāpathyāhāradoṣaśarīraviśeṣebhyo vyādhayo mṛdavo dāruṇāḥ kṣiprasamutthāścirakāriṇaśca bhavanti /
children.translated_text: And from these very distinctions of unwholesome food, <s>doṣa</s>, and body — diseases become mild or severe, quick-arising or slow-developing.

children.text: eva vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ sthānaviśeṣe prakupitā vyādhiviśeṣān abhinivartayantyagniveśa // Car_1,28.7
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Agniveśa</s>, <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Kapha</s>, when vitiated in specific locations, produce specific diseases.' // Car_1,28.7
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'From that cause' (<s>tannimittā</s>) means: from the cause of wholesome food. // 1
'Not merely' (<s>na kevalam</s>) means: 'but also...' // 2
'Causes of disease' (<s>rogaprakṛtayaḥ</s>) means: causes of disease. // 3
'Of those who consume unwholesome food' and so on. // 4

children.text: kāraṇata iti nimittāntarāt pratibandhāt tacca kāraṇaṃ tadeva hy apathyam ityādivakṣyamāṇagranthaviparītaṃ boddhavyam // 5
children.translated_text: 'For a reason' (<s>kāraṇataḥ</s>) means: because of another obstructing cause. And that cause should be understood as the opposite of what will be stated in [the passage beginning] 'That very unwholesome [food]' and so on. // 5
'Immediately' (<s>sadyaḥ</s>) means: at that very time. // 6

children.text: anenāpathyasya rogajananaṃ prati kālāntaravikārakartṛtvaṃ prāyo bhavatīti darśayati anyathā sadya ityanarthakaṃ syāt kālāntare 'pi doṣākartṛtvāt // 7
children.translated_text: By this he shows that the production of disease by unwholesome [food] generally occurs after a lapse of time — otherwise 'immediately' would be meaningless, since [if it never produced disease] the word 'immediately' would be pointless because [it would be] incapable of producing <s>doṣa</s>-vitiation even later. // 7
'Harmful' (<s>doṣavān</s>) means: disease-producing. // 8

children.text: apacāra iti ahitāhāropayogaḥ ukte kāraṇamāha nahītyādi /
children.translated_text: 'Transgression' (<s>apacāra</s>) means: the consumption of unwholesome food. He states the reason for the said [delay] with 'For not...' and so on.
'Of equal <s>doṣa</s>' (<s>tulyadoṣāṇi</s>) means: producing equal [degrees of] <s>doṣa</s>-vitiation. // 9
'Disease-resistance' (<s>vyādhikṣamatva</s>) means: opposition to the strength of disease — i.e., the capacity to obstruct the production of disease. // 10
He elaborates on the equal-<s>doṣa</s> nature etc. of that very unwholesome [food] with 'That very [unwholesome food]' and so on. // 11

children.text: atra yadyapi prastutatvād apathyapratibandhakāni kāraṇāni vaktavyāni tathāpi samānanyāyatayāpathyaśaktivardhakānyucyante // 12
children.translated_text: Here, although the obstructing causes against unwholesome [food] should be stated since they are the topic at hand, nevertheless — because of following the same principle — causes that increase the power of unwholesome [food] are stated. // 12

children.text: tatra deśādīnāṃ yogāditi anuguṇadeśādiyogāt yathā vrīhiḥ pittakartṛtvenāpathyaḥ sa cānūpadeśayogādbhūyastaram apathyo bhavati dhanvadeśe tu hīnabalo bhavati tathā śaratkālasyānuguṇasya yogādbalavānbhavati hemante durbalaḥ saṃyogād yathā sa vrīhir dadhiphāṇitādiyukto balavān madhvādiyuktaśca durbalaḥ vīryād yathā sa evoṣṇīkṛto balavān śītastu durbalaḥ sa eva ca pramāṇātiyogād balī hīnamātrastvabalaḥ ityādyanusartavyam // 13
children.translated_text: There, 'through excess of place etc.' means: through conjunction with a concordant place etc. For example: rice, being <s>pitta</s>-producing, is unwholesome; and through conjunction with a marshy place, it becomes even more unwholesome; but in an arid region, its power is diminished. Likewise, through conjunction with the concordant autumn season, it becomes powerful; in winter it is weak. By combination — for example, that same rice combined with curd and jaggery becomes powerful, while combined with honey etc. it becomes weak. By potency — for example, that same [rice] when heated becomes powerful, while cold it is weak. And that same [rice], through excess of measure, becomes powerful; in diminished dose, it is powerless — and so on should be followed. // 13
He states the equal-strength of the <s>doṣa</s> with 'That very <s>doṣa</s>' and so on. // 14

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭā militā bahavo yonayaḥ kāraṇāni yasya sa tathā kiṃvā saṃsṛṣṭayonir iti anuguṇadūṣyaḥ yathā pittasya raktaṃ dūṣyam āsādya kaṣṭatvaṃ kṣiprakāritvaṃ ca bhavati // 15
children.translated_text: 'Of combined origin' (<s>saṃsṛṣṭayoni</s>) — one whose origins (causes) are many and combined. Or, '<s>saṃsṛṣṭayoni</s>' means: [a <s>doṣa</s>] with a concordant <s>dūṣya</s> (tissue to be vitiated) — as when <s>pitta</s>, having reached its concordant <s>dūṣya</s> blood, becomes severe and rapidly-acting. // 15

children.text: viruddhopakramo yathā pittaṃ mehārambhakaṃ vacanaṃ hi pittamehāḥ sarva eva yāpyāḥ viruddhopakramatvāt iti viruddhatā copakramasyātra yat pittaharaṃ madhurādi tanmehapradhānadūṣyamedaso viruddhaṃ medo'nuguṇaṃ tu kaṭvādi pitte viruddham iti // 16
children.translated_text: 'Of contradictory treatment' (<s>viruddhopakrama</s>) — for example, <s>pitta</s> producing <s>meha</s> (urinary diseases). For it is stated: 'All <s>pitta</s>-<s>mehas</s> are indeed only palliable, because of contradictory treatment.' And the contradiction of treatment here is: what destroys <s>pitta</s> — sweet etc. — is contrary to fat, the primary <s>dūṣya</s> of <s>meha</s>; while pungent etc. that is concordant with fat is contrary to <s>pitta</s>. // 16

children.text: gambhīrānugata iti gambhīramajjādidhātugataḥ vacanaṃ hi tvaṅmāṃsāśrayamuttānaṃ gambhīraṃ tv antarāśrayam iti // 17
children.translated_text: 'Having penetrated deep [tissues]' (<s>gambhīrānugata</s>) means: having entered deep tissues like marrow etc. For it is stated: 'What is located in skin and flesh is superficial; what is located internally is deep.' // 17

children.text: cirasthita iti dehe cirakālāvasthānena kṛtamūlatvāt kaṣṭasādhyaḥ // 18
children.translated_text: 'Long-standing' (<s>cirasthita</s>) means: being deeply rooted because of remaining in the body for a long time, [hence] difficult to treat. // 18
'Arising in a vital organ' (<s>prāṇāyatanasamuttha</s>) means: located in the ten vital organs beginning with the temples (<s>śaṅkha</s>), to be stated in the following chapter. // 19
'Damaging a <s>marma</s>' (<s>marmopaghātī</s>) means: causing damage to <s>marmas</s> other than the vital organs — such as <s>kṣipra</s>, <s>tala</s>, <s>hṛdaya</s>, etc. // 20

children.text: marmaghātitvenaiva marmaviśeṣaprāṇāyatanasamutthatve labdhe punastadvacanaṃ prāṇāyatanamarmāśrayiṇo viśeṣeṇa kaṣṭatvapratipādanārtham // 21
children.translated_text: Even though the quality of being located in a vital organ is already obtained by the statement of <s>marma</s>-injury (since vital organs are a type of <s>marma</s>), the separate statement of vital-organ-arising is for the purpose of demonstrating that [diseases] located in the specific <s>marmas</s> that are vital organs are especially severe. // 21
'Most severe' (<s>kaṣṭatama</s>) means: being a producer of great suffering and being incurable. // 22
'Most rapidly acting' (<s>kṣiprakāritama</s>) means: most quickly producing pathological change. // 23

children.text: cakārāt saṃsṛṣṭayonitvādihetūnām alpatvena kaṣṭakaṣṭatarakṣiprakārikṣiprakāritarādiviśeṣāś ca bhavantīti darśayati yathoktasarvahetumelake kaṣṭatamaḥ kṣiprakāritamaś ca bhavatīti jñeyaṃ kaṣṭatamatvādi ca yathāyogyatayā jñeyaṃ viruddhopakramo doṣaḥ kaṣṭa eva bhavati na kṣiprakārī // 24
children.translated_text: By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), he shows that through the lesser presence of the causes beginning with 'combined origin,' there are distinctions [in degree] — such as severe/more severe, rapid/more rapid, etc. When all the stated causes combine, [the disease] becomes most severe and most rapidly acting — this should be understood. And the severity etc. should be understood according to aptness — [for example,] a <s>doṣa</s> of contradictory treatment becomes indeed severe, but not rapidly-acting. // 24
He states bodies that are disease-intolerant with 'And bodies' and so on. // 25

children.text: aniviṣṭāni ślathāni māṃsādīni yeṣāṃ śarīriṇāṃ tāni tathā kiṃvā aniviṣṭānīti viṣamāṇi // 26
children.translated_text: '<s>Aniviṣṭa</s>' (loosely-set) — those whose flesh etc. is slack (<s>ślatha</s>). Or, '<s>aniviṣṭa</s>' means: uneven. // 26

children.text: upacitānīti saṃvardhitāni asātmyapuṣṭaṃ hi śarīraṃ bhūridoṣabhāvitameva bhavatīti bhāvaḥ // 27
children.translated_text: 'Nourished [on unsuitable food]' (<s>upacita</s>) means: grown up [on it]. For a body nourished on unsuitable food is indeed pervaded by abundant <s>doṣas</s> — this is the purport. // 27
'Opposite' (<s>viparīta</s>) means: endowed with not-excessively-corpulent-ness etc. // 28
'Disease-resistant' (<s>vyādhisahāni</s>) means: obstructive to the production of disease. // 29

children.text: etacca śarīramadhikṛtya vaiparītyaṃ vyādhisahatve udāharaṇārtham upanyastaṃ tena yathoktāpathyabalavaiparītyaṃ doṣabalavaiparītyaṃ ca na sadyo vyādhikārakaṃ bhavatītyetad apyuktaṃ boddhavyam // 30
children.translated_text: And this opposition stated with reference to the body is presented as illustration for disease-resistance. Therefore, the opposition of the stated unwholesome-strength and <s>doṣa</s>-strength too — [their being] 'not immediately disease-producing' — this too has been stated and should be understood. // 30

children.text: etad evāpathyāhāradoṣaśarīrāṇām evābalavattvabalavattvābhyāṃ lakṣaṇaviśeṣaṃ yathāyogyatayā mṛdvādivyādhikāraṇatvenopasaṃharann āha ebhyaś caivetyādi // 31
children.translated_text: He concludes by showing that these very distinctions of unwholesome food, <s>doṣa</s>, and body — by being weak or strong — are appropriately the cause of mild etc. diseases, with 'And from these very' etc. // 31

children.text: viśeṣā yathoktā uktaviparītāśca tatroktaviparītaviśeṣān mṛdavastathā cirakāriṇaśca bhavanti yathoktāpathyādiviśeṣāttu dāruṇāḥ kṣiprakāriṇaśca bhavantīti mantavyam // 32
children.translated_text: The 'distinctions' are those stated and their opposites. Among them, diseases with the stated-opposite distinctions become mild and slow-developing; while those with the stated [aggravating] distinctions of unwholesome [food] etc. become severe and rapidly-developing — this should be understood. // 32

children.text: anena prasaṅgena vātādīnāṃ rasādisthānaviśeṣeṣu kupitānāṃ ye vyādhayo bhavanti tān darśayitum āha ta evetyādi // 33]
children.translated_text: Taking advantage of this context, in order to show the diseases that arise when <s>Vāta</s> etc. are vitiated in specific locations of <s>rasa</s> etc., he says 'Those very' and so on. // 33]

children.text: tatra rasādiṣu sthāneṣu prakupitānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ yasmin sthāne ye ye vyādhayaḥ sambhavanti tāṃs tān yathāvad anuvyākhyāsyāmaḥ // Car_1,28.8
children.translated_text: Among those, we shall explain in detail the diseases that arise in each location when the <s>doṣas</s> are vitiated in the locations of <s>rasa</s> and the rest. // Car_1,28.8
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: tatra rasetyādau prakupitānāṃ doṣāṇāmiti aniyamena rase kupito vāyur vā pittaṃ vā śleṣmā vā saṃsṛṣṭā vā aśraddhādīni kurvanti // 1
children.translated_text: In 'Among those, in <s>rasa</s>' etc. — 'of the vitiated <s>doṣas</s>' means: indiscriminately — whether <s>Vāyu</s> vitiated in <s>rasa</s>, or <s>Pitta</s>, or <s>Kapha</s>, or [these] in combination — they produce loss of appetite etc. // 1

children.text: satyapi doṣabhede 'trāśrayasyābhedād āśrayaprabhāveṇaivāśraddhādayo bhavanti paraṃ doṣabhede aśraddhādāv eva vātādiliṅgaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ bhavati // 2
children.translated_text: Even though there is differentiation of <s>doṣas</s>, here — because of the non-differentiation of the substrate — through the influence of the substrate alone, loss of appetite etc. arise. But when there is <s>doṣa</s>-differentiation, specific <s>Vāta</s> etc. signs within [the conditions of] loss of appetite etc. become distinguished. // 2

children.text: kiṃvā yathāyogyatayā rasāśrayiṇā vātādinā aśraddhādikaraṇaṃ boddhavyaṃ yato na gauravaṃ vātaduṣṭarase bhavitumarhati etacca nātisundaraṃ tena pūrva eva pakṣo jyāyān // 3]
children.translated_text: Or: the production of loss of appetite etc. should be understood as [caused] by the appropriate <s>Vāta</s> etc. located in <s>rasa</s> — since heaviness cannot arise in <s>rasa</s> vitiated by <s>Vāta</s>. But this is not very elegant; therefore the first interpretation alone is better. // 3]
Loss of faith [in food], loss of appetite, distaste in the mouth, inability to perceive taste,

children.text: hṛllāso gauravaṃ tandrā sāṅgamardo jvaras tamaḥ // Car_1,28.9
children.translated_text: nausea, heaviness, drowsiness, body-ache, fever, darkness [of vision], // Car_1,28.9

children.text: pāṇḍutvaṃ srotasāṃ rodhaḥ klaibyaṃ sādaḥ kṛśāṅgatā /
children.translated_text: pallor, obstruction of channels, impotence, exhaustion, emaciation,
loss of digestive fire, untimely wrinkles, and grey hair — // Car_1,28.10
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Sūtrasthāna</s>, Chapter 28 [<s>Vividhāśitapītīya</s>]

children.text: aśraddhāyāṃ mukhapraviṣṭasyāhārasyābhyavaharaṇaṃ bhavatyeva paraṃ tv anicchā arucau tu mukhapraviṣṭaṃ nābhyavaharatīti bhedaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: In 'loss of faith' — food placed in the mouth is indeed swallowed, but with reluctance. In 'loss of appetite' (<s>aruci</s>) — food placed in the mouth is not swallowed: this is the distinction. // 1
'Distaste in the mouth' (<s>āsyavairasya</s>) means: alteration from the accustomed taste in the mouth. // 2
'Inability to perceive taste' (<s>arasajñatā</s>) means: non-apprehension of tastes. // 3
'Exhaustion' (<s>sāda</s>) means: sinking of the limbs. // 4]
These are declared to be diseases arising from vitiation of <s>rasa</s>. Now the blood-vitiation diseases will be stated:
Skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), erysipelas (<s>vīsarpa</s>), eruptions (<s>piḍakā</s>), hemorrhagic disease (<s>raktapitta</s>), menorrhagia (<s>asṛgdara</s>), // Car_1,28.11
inflammation of the anus, penis, and mouth, splenic enlargement, abdominal tumor (<s>gulma</s>), abscess (<s>vidradhi</s>),

children.text: nīlikā kāmalā vyaṅgaḥ pipplavas tilakālakāḥ // Car_1,28.12
children.translated_text: blue moles (<s>nīlikā</s>), jaundice (<s>kāmalā</s>), freckles (<s>vyaṅga</s>), port-wine stains (<s>pipplava</s>), <s>tilakālaka</s> (mole-marks), // Car_1,28.12
ringworm (<s>dadru</s>), skin-cracking (<s>carmadala</s>), leucoderma (<s>śvitra</s>), scabies (<s>pāmā</s>), urticaria (<s>koṭha</s>), and blood-circles (<s>asramaṇḍala</s>).
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: raktapradoṣajeṣu kuṣṭhagrahaṇādeva dadrvādilābhe siddhe punastadvacanaṃ viśeṣaprādurbhāvapradarśanārtham // 1
children.translated_text: Among the blood-vitiation diseases: although ringworm etc. are obtained by the inclusion of the word 'skin disease' (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) [which is a broad category], they are stated again to show their specific manifestation [as blood-vitiation diseases]. // 1
'<s>Tilakālaka</s>' means: having the shape of sesame seeds. // 2
'<s>Asramaṇḍala</s>' (blood-circles) means: red circles. // 3]
These arise from blood-vitiation. Now hear those arising from flesh-vitiation: // Car_1,28.13
Excess flesh-growth (<s>adhimāṃsa</s>), tumor (<s>arbuda</s>), hemorrhoid (<s>kali</s>), goiter (<s>galaśālūka</s>), tonsillar swelling (<s>śuṇḍikā</s>),
putrid-flesh, [nasal polyp] (<s>alajī</s>), glandular swelling (<s>gaṇḍa</s>), scrofula (<s>gaṇḍamālā</s>), and epiglottic swelling (<s>upajihvikā</s>). // Car_1,28.14
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
Here the word '<s>kīla</s>' (peg) denotes hemorrhoids (<s>arśas</s>). // 1]
Know these as flesh-tissue diseases. Now we shall declare those arising from fat-tissue:

children.text: ninditāni pramehāṇāṃ pūrvarūpāṇi yāni ca // Car_1,28.15
children.translated_text: The premonitory symptoms of <s>prameha</s> (urinary diseases), and those which are declared as 'censurable' [diseases of obesity]. // Car_1,28.15
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: ninditāni pramehapūrvarūpāṇīti keśajaṭilatvādīni teṣāmeva ninditatvāt na tv āsyavairasyamadhuratvādīni // 1
children.translated_text: 'Censurable [symptoms] and premonitory symptoms of <s>prameha</s>' — these are matted hair, etc. — since those alone are 'censurable.' Not [the symptoms] like distaste in the mouth, sweetness [of urine], etc. // 1

children.text: kiṃvā ninditānīti atisthūlagatāny āyurhrāsādīny aṣṭauninditīyoktāni teṣāṃ ca ninditatvaṃ ninditātisthūlasambaddhatvena // 2
children.translated_text: Or, 'censurable' refers to the [conditions] of the excessively corpulent — shortening of lifespan, etc. — stated in the <s>Aṣṭauninditīya</s> [chapter]. And their censurable nature is because of being connected with the censurable condition of excessive corpulence. // 2

children.text: evaṃ pūrvasminvyākhyāne yāni ca iti cakāro niyame uttaravyākhyāne tu samuccaye // 3]
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first interpretation, the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) in 'which' (<s>yāni ca</s>) is restrictive. In the latter interpretation, it is cumulative. // 3]
Supernumerary bone, supernumerary tooth, splitting-pain of teeth and bones, discoloration,
and disorders of hair, body-hair, nails, and beard — these arise from bone-vitiation. // Car_1,28.16
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
By the word '<s>adhyasthidanta</s>' (supernumerary bone-tooth), the inclusion of both supernumerary bone and supernumerary tooth [is intended].
'Pain' (<s>śūla</s>) should be understood here as pain of the bones specifically. // 1]

children.text: ruk parvaṇāṃ bhramo mūrchā darśanaṃ tamasastathā /
children.translated_text: Pain in the joints, vertigo, fainting, and also the seeing of darkness,

children.text: aruṣāṃ sthūlamūlānāṃ parvajānāṃ ca darśanam // Car_1,28.17
children.translated_text: and the appearance of boils with thick roots and those occurring at the joints — // Car_1,28.17
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Pain,' etc. — these should be understood as arising from the vitiation of marrow. // 1
'Boils' (<s>arūṃṣi</s>) means wounds/ulcers. // 2]
[These arise] from the vitiation of marrow. From the vitiation of semen [arise]: impotence and lack of sexual arousal;

children.text: rogi vā klībamalpāyur virūpaṃ vā prajāyate // Car_1,28.18
children.translated_text: or offspring that is sickly, impotent, short-lived, or deformed is born. // Car_1,28.18

children.text: na cāsya jāyate garbhaḥ patati prasravatyapi /
children.translated_text: And his wife does not conceive, or the embryo falls, or there is [excessive] discharge;

children.text: śukraṃ hi duṣṭaṃ sāpatyaṃ sadāraṃ bādhate naram // Car_1,28.19
children.translated_text: for vitiated semen afflicts a man together with his offspring and his wife. // Car_1,28.19
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
'Impotence' (<s>klaibya</s>) means the non-erection of the phallus. // 1
'Lack of arousal' (<s>aharṣaṇa</s>) means incapacity for intercourse even when erection occurs. // 2

children.text: śukraṃ hi duṣṭaṃ sāpatyaṃ sadāraṃ bādhate naramiti atrāpatyabādhā rogiklībādyapatyajanakatvena dārabādhā tu srāvigarbhādijanakatvena // 3]
children.translated_text: 'Vitiated semen afflicts a man together with his offspring and his wife' — here, the affliction regarding offspring is through producing sickly, impotent, etc. offspring; the affliction regarding the wife is through causing miscarriage, [excessive] discharge, etc. // 3]
When the waste products (<s>malas</s>), having taken resort in the sense organs, become aggravated,
they afflict the sense organs with impairment and disturbance. // Car_1,28.20
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: upaghātetyādau upaghāto vināśaḥ upatāpastu kiṃcid vaikalyam // 1]
children.translated_text: In 'impairment,' etc.: 'impairment' (<s>upaghāta</s>) means destruction; 'disturbance' (<s>upatāpa</s>) means some degree of dysfunction. // 1]
From the ligaments (<s>snāyu</s>), veins (<s>sirā</s>), and tendons (<s>kaṇḍarā</s>), when vitiated, they afflict a person
with stiffness, contraction, cramps (<s>khallī</s>), nodular growths, spasms, and numbness. // Car_1,28.21
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
'From the tendons' (<s>kaṇḍarābhyaḥ</s>) — the ablative is used in the sense of the locative. // 1
<s>Khallī</s> (cramps) means the twisting/wrenching of the hands and feet. // 2
'Nodular growth' (<s>granthi</s>) is indeed a knot in the ligaments, etc. // 3]
The <s>doṣas</s>, having taken resort in the waste products, when aggravated, cause splitting, desiccation, and corruption

children.text: doṣā malānāṃ kurvanti saṅgotsargāv atīva ca // Car_1,28.22
children.translated_text: of the waste products, and also excessive retention and excessive discharge. // Car_1,28.22
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: malānityādau bhedaśoṣapradūṣaṇam iti yathāsambhavaṃ jñeyaṃ tatra bhedaḥ purīṣasya śoṣastu viśeṣeṇa sarvamaleṣu sambhavati pradūṣaṇaṃ tu praduṣṭavarṇādiyuktatvena prākṛtavarṇādyupaghātaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: In 'waste products,' etc.: 'splitting, desiccation, and corruption' should be understood as applicable according to context. There, splitting applies to feces; desiccation can occur in all waste products in particular; corruption means being endowed with corrupted color, etc. — i.e., the impairment of natural color, etc. // 1

children.text: saṃgotsargāv atīva ceti atīva saṅgaḥ apravṛttiḥ atyutsargastu atipravṛttiḥ // 2]
children.translated_text: 'Excessive retention and excessive discharge' — excessive retention means non-evacuation; excessive discharge means excessive evacuation. // 2]
From the various foods that are eaten, drunk, licked, and chewed, that are unwholesome —

children.text: bhavantyete manuṣyāṇāṃ vikārā ya udāhṛtāḥ // Car_1,28.23
children.translated_text: these disorders arise in human beings, as have been enumerated. // Car_1,28.23
He who desires their non-arising, being wise, should always

children.text: hitānyevāśitādīni na syus tajjās tathāmayāḥ // Car_1,28.24
children.translated_text: consume only wholesome foods, etc. — then those disorders born from them will not occur. // Car_1,28.24
For disorders arising from <s>rasa</s> (nutrient fluid), the universal remedy is fasting (<s>laṅghana</s>);
the treatment for blood-born disorders has been taught by physicians in the chapter on bloodletting (<s>Vidhiśoṇitīya</s>). // Car_1,28.25
For flesh-born disorders, the [treatments are] purification, surgery (<s>śastra</s>), cauterization with alkaline substances (<s>kṣāra</s>), and cauterization with fire;
the treatment for fat-born disorders [is found] in the chapter on the Eight Blameworthy Conditions (<s>Aṣṭauninditīya</s>). // Car_1,28.26
For diseases located in the bones, the five procedures (<s>Pañcakarma</s>) are the remedy;
also enemas (<s>vasti</s>), milk, and ghee prepared with bitter substances. // Car_1,28.27
For diseases arising from marrow and semen, the remedy is food that is sweet and bitter;

children.text: annaṃ vyavāyavyāyāmau śuddhiḥ kāle ca mātrayā // Car_1,28.28
children.translated_text: sexual intercourse, physical exercise, purification at the proper time and in the proper measure. // Car_1,28.28
The pacification of diseases arising from the sense organs will be taught in the chapter <s>Trimarmīya</s>;
the alleviation of those arising from ligaments, etc. will be taught in the chapter on <s>Vāta</s>-diseases. // Car_1,28.29
In the chapter on non-suppression of natural urges (<s>Navegāndhāraṇīya</s>), a compendium of treatment has been made;

children.text: malajānāṃ vikārāṇāṃ siddhiś coktā kvacitkvacit // Car_1,28.30
children.translated_text: and the cure for disorders arising from waste products has been stated here and there. // Car_1,28.30
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: sampratyahitāhārajanitān doṣān darśayan yathākartavyam upadiśati vividhādityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, showing the disorders caused by unwholesome food, he teaches what should be done, beginning with 'from the various,' etc. // 1
'Has been taught by physicians' — the word 'stated' is to be supplied. // 2

children.text: pañcakarmāṇītyabhidhāyāpi vastaya iti vacanaṃ tiktopahitavaster viśeṣeṇa hitatvopadarśanārtham // 3
children.translated_text: Even though he has said 'the five procedures,' his [separate] statement of 'enemas' is for the purpose of showing that enemas prepared with bitter substances are especially beneficial. // 3
'Purification' means by emesis, etc. // 4
'The cure has been stated here and there' — i.e., in [the chapters on] diarrhea (<s>atīsāra</s>), <s>Grahaṇī</s> disorders, etc. // 5]
From exercise, from the sharpness of the [digestive] fire, from non-administration of the wholesome,

children.text: koṣṭhācchākhā malā yānti drutatvānmarutasya ca // Car_1,28.31
children.translated_text: the waste products go from the <s>koṣṭha</s> (visceral tract) to the <s>śākhā</s> (extremities/tissues) — and also from the rapidity of <s>Vāyu</s>. // Car_1,28.31
And those situated there sometimes linger, not being stimulated;
they do not become aggravated in an unfavorable place or time, waiting for a further causative factor. // Car_1,28.32
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: samprati rasādīnāṃ śākhārūpatvāt koṣṭhāśrayiṇo doṣā yathā śākhāṃ yānti tad āha vyāyāmetyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, since <s>rasa</s> and the rest have the form of <s>śākhā</s> (peripheral tissues), [he explains] how the <s>doṣas</s> residing in the <s>koṣṭha</s> go to the <s>śākhā</s> — this he states with 'from exercise,' etc. // 1

children.text: tatra vyāyāmakṣobhāt koṣṭhaṃ parityajya śākhāṃ malā yānti ūṣmaṇo vahnestīkṣṇatvād vilāyitā doṣāḥ śākhāṃ yānti hitasyānavacāraṇayāhitasevayātisevayātimātravṛddho doṣo jalāpūravad vṛddhaḥ svasthānamāplāvya sthānāntaraṃ yātīti yuktam // 2
children.translated_text: There, from the agitation of exercise, leaving the <s>koṣṭha</s>, the waste products go to the <s>śākhā</s>. From the sharpness of the fire — the <s>doṣas</s>, having been liquefied by the sharp [digestive] fire, go to the <s>śākhā</s>. From non-administration of the wholesome — i.e., from the use of unwholesome [substances] or their excessive use — the <s>doṣa</s>, having increased excessively, like an overflow of water, having flooded its own place, goes to another location — this is reasonable. // 2

children.text: drutatvānmārutasyeti calatvād vāyor vāyunā kṣipto yātītyarthaḥ vāyvantareṇa ca vāyor ākṣepaṇamupapannam eveti anyathā malā iti bahuvacanam asādhu // 3
children.translated_text: 'From the rapidity of <s>Vāyu</s>' — due to the mobile nature of <s>Vāyu</s>; propelled by <s>Vāyu</s>, it goes — this is the meaning. And the propulsion [of <s>doṣas</s>] by a different <s>Vāyu</s> is indeed logical; otherwise, the plural 'waste products' (<s>malāḥ</s>) would be inappropriate. // 3
Now, what do they do when they have gone to the <s>śākhā</s>? — this he states with 'those situated there,' etc. // 4

children.text: vilambante kadācid iti kadācidvyādhikaraṇe vilambaṃ kurvanti // 5
children.translated_text: 'They linger sometimes' — sometimes they cause a delay in the site of disease. // 5
Why do they linger? — he says: 'not being stimulated.' // 6

children.text: ye doṣā alpatvenābalavantaste hetvantareṇa samīritāḥ santaḥ kupyanti tathā ta eva nādeśa ityananuguṇadeśe tathā nākāla ityananuguṇakāle kupyantīti yojanā // 7
children.translated_text: Those <s>doṣas</s> which, being small in quantity and therefore weak — they, being stimulated by another cause, become aggravated; and those same [<s>doṣas</s>] do not become aggravated in an unfavorable place or at an unfavorable time — this is the construction. // 7
He states the reason for this very [fact] with 'further,' etc. // 8

children.text: yasmādbhūyo hetupratīkṣiṇas te 'lpabalā doṣāstasmādīraṇādyapekṣante etena bhūyo ye 'hetupratīkṣiṇo bhavanti balavattvānna te īraṇādyapekṣante ata evoktaṃ kadāciditi // 9]
children.translated_text: Since those weak <s>doṣas</s> 'wait for a further causative factor,' they therefore depend on stimulation, etc. By this [it is implied that] those which 'do not wait for a further [causative factor],' being powerful, do not depend on stimulation, etc. Hence the word 'sometimes' was used. // 9]
By increase, by liquefaction, by ripening, by the clearing of channel-openings,

children.text: śākhā muktvā malāḥ koṣṭhaṃ yānti vāyośca nigrahāt // Car_1,28.33
children.translated_text: the waste products, leaving the <s>śākhā</s>, go to the <s>koṣṭha</s> — and also from the restraint of <s>Vāyu</s>. // Car_1,28.33
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: samprati śākhābhyaḥ koṣṭhāgamanahetuṃ doṣāṇām āha vṛddhyetyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now he states the causes of the return of <s>doṣas</s> from the <s>śākhā</s> to the <s>koṣṭha</s>, with 'by increase,' etc. // 1

children.text: viṣyandanāditi vilayanāt vilīnaśca dravatvādeva koṣṭhe nimnaṃ yāti // 2
children.translated_text: 'By liquefaction' — by becoming dissolved; and being dissolved, due to its liquid nature, it descends to the <s>koṣṭha</s>, which is the low point. // 2

children.text: pākāditi pakvo doṣo 'baddhatvenaiva nimnaṃ koṣṭhaṃ yāti // 3
children.translated_text: 'By ripening' — the ripened <s>doṣa</s>, being in an unbound state, descends to the <s>koṣṭha</s>, the low point. // 3
'By the clearing of channel-openings' — by the removal of obstructions. // 4

children.text: vāyornigrahāditi kṣepturvāyornigrahāt prākṛtaṃ sthānaṃ koṣṭhaṃ yāti // 5]
children.translated_text: 'From the restraint of <s>Vāyu</s>' — from the restraint of the propelling <s>Vāyu</s>, [the <s>doṣa</s>] returns to the natural location, the <s>koṣṭha</s>. // 5]
For the non-arising of diseases not yet arisen, and for the removal of those already arisen —

children.text: rogāṇāṃ yo vidhirdṛṣṭaḥ sukhārthī taṃ samācaret // Car_1,28.34
children.translated_text: whatever method is prescribed, one who desires wellbeing should practice it. // Car_1,28.34
All activities of all beings are considered to be for the sake of happiness;
but due to the distinction between knowledge and ignorance, there are activities on the right and wrong paths. // Car_1,28.35
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
Now, he encapsulates in a <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism) the remedy for all diseases in brief, beginning with 'for the non-arising,' etc. // 1
'Whatever method is prescribed' — in the entire treatise. // 2

children.text: nanu yadi sukhārthā sarvaprāṇināṃ pravṛttistatkathaṃ ko 'pi amārge pravartata ityāha jñānetyādi // 3
children.translated_text: Now, if all activity of all living beings is for the sake of happiness, then how does anyone engage in the wrong path? — he answers with 'knowledge,' etc. // 3

children.text: ajñānād eva sukhasādhanamidam iti kṛtvā aparīkṣakāḥ pravartante na tu duḥkhakartṛtāsaṃdhānād iti bhāvaḥ // 4]
children.translated_text: Due to ignorance alone, thinking 'this is a means to happiness,' the undiscriminating engage [in wrong actions]; but they do not do so with the intent of causing suffering — this is the purport. // 4]
The discriminating, having thoroughly examined, pursue only what is beneficial;
but worldly people, their minds veiled by <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>moha</s> (delusion), pursue only what is pleasant. // Car_1,28.36
Learning, intelligence, memory, dexterity, steadfastness, the practice of what is beneficial,

children.text: vāgviśuddhiḥ śamo dhairyam āśrayanti parīkṣakam // Car_1,28.37
children.translated_text: purity of speech, tranquility, and fortitude — these attend upon the discriminating person. // Car_1,28.37
These qualities do not attend upon the worldly person, who is given to delusion and passion;

children.text: tanmūlā bahavo yanti rogāḥ śārīramānasāḥ // Car_1,28.38
children.translated_text: rooted in those [faults], many diseases — both physical and mental — arise. // Car_1,28.38
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: hitameveti āyativiśuddham eva tadātve duḥkhakaram api // 1
children.translated_text: 'Only what is beneficial' — that which is purely good in the long run, even if causing discomfort at present. // 1
'Only what is pleasant' — that which is comfortable at present but harmful in the long run. // 2
'Worldly people' means the undiscriminating. // 3
He praises the discriminating person with 'learning,' etc. // 4

children.text: parīkṣakamāśrayantīti parīkṣake bhavanti kiṃvā buddhyādidevatāḥ parīkṣakamāśrayante yad uktaṃ viviśur jñānadevatāḥ iti // 5
children.translated_text: 'Attend upon the discriminating person' — they exist in the discriminating person. Or, the deities of intelligence, etc. resort to the discriminating person, as stated: 'the deities of knowledge entered [him].' // 5
'Rooted in those' means rooted in <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (inertia). // 6]
Due to the error of intellect (<s>prajñāparādha</s>), one pursues five unwholesome objects;

children.text: saṃdhārayati vegāṃśca sevate sāhasāni ca // Car_1,28.39
children.translated_text: one suppresses natural urges (<s>vegas</s>) and also engages in reckless acts (<s>sāhasa</s>). // Car_1,28.39
The ignorant person becomes attached to states that bear the name 'happiness' only in the present moment;

children.text: rajyate na tu vijñātā vijñāne hy amalīkṛte // Car_1,28.40
children.translated_text: but the knowledgeable person does not become attached — for in pure knowledge [such attachment does not arise]. // Car_1,28.40
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: yathā aparīkṣake rajastamomūlā rogā bhavanti tadāha prajñāparādhād ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: How diseases rooted in <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> arise in the undiscriminating — this he states with 'due to the error of intellect,' etc. // 1
And the pursuit of unwholesome objects, etc. causes disease — this is the purport. // 2

children.text: tadātvasukheṣviti vaktavye yat sukhasaṃjñeṣu iti karoti tattadātvasukhasyāpathyasya duḥkhānubandhasukhakartṛtayā paramārthatas tadātve 'pyasukhatvaṃ darśayati yathā sukhasaṃjñakam ārogyam ityatroktam // 3
children.translated_text: Where he should say 'happiness in the present moment' (<s>tadātvasukha</s>), he says 'bearing the name happiness' (<s>sukhasaṃjña</s>) — by this he shows that unwholesome [food], which produces happiness mixed with suffering, is in the ultimate sense unhappy even in the present moment — as stated: 'health is called happiness.' // 3
'The knowledgeable' means the discriminating person. // 4]
One should not consume foods out of [mere] desire or ignorance;
having examined [what is] wholesome, one should eat — for the body indeed originates from food. // Car_1,28.41
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
'Not out of desire,' etc. // 1

children.text: ahitatvena jānann api rāgādeva kaścid duṣṭaḥ pravartate ajñānāccāhitatvājñānād eva kaściddhitādhyavasāyena pravartate etaddvayamapi niṣidhyate // 2]
children.translated_text: Even knowing something to be unwholesome, some wicked person engages [in it] out of mere desire; and out of ignorance — i.e., from not knowing it to be unwholesome — someone engages with the conviction that it is wholesome. Both of these are prohibited. // 2]
In the method of food [consumption], there are eight specific factors called 'causes';
having examined those, in the production of good and bad [health], one should employ [food]. // Car_1,28.42
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:
How should food be examined? — he answers with 'in the method of food,' etc. // 1

children.text: āhārasya vidhau vidhāne'ṣṭau viśeṣāḥ prakṛtikaraṇasaṃyogādayo rasavimāne vaktavyā hetusaṃjñakāḥ kva hetusaṃjñakā ityāha śubhetyādi // 2
children.translated_text: 'In the method of food' — in the procedure of food, the eight specific factors — natural constitution (<s>prakṛti</s>), processing (<s>karaṇa</s>), combination (<s>saṃyoga</s>), etc. — to be stated in the <s>Rasavimāna</s> — are called 'causes.' Where are they causes? — he answers with 'good,' etc. // 2

children.text: śubhāśubhasamutpattau iti te ca prakṛtyādayaḥ śubhāḥ śubhakarāḥ aśubhā aśubhakarāḥ iti jñeyam // 3]
children.translated_text: 'In the production of good and bad' — those [factors] — <s>prakṛti</s>, etc. — are 'good,' i.e., productive of good [health], and 'bad,' i.e., productive of ill [health] — this should be understood. // 3]
A man who always avoids the things to be avoided — the unwholesome —

children.text: bhavatyanṛṇatāṃ prāptaḥ sādhūnām iha paṇḍitaḥ // Car_1,28.43
children.translated_text: becomes, as it were, freed from debt, and is wise among the virtuous in this world. // Car_1,28.43
But as for the arising of disease that cannot be avoided by anyone here —

children.text: parihartuṃ na tatprāpya śocitavyaṃ manīṣibhiḥ // Car_1,28.44
children.translated_text: upon encountering that, the wise should not grieve. // Car_1,28.44
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: nanu pathyasevāyāṃ kriyamāṇāyām api balavatprāktanādharmavaśādapi vyādhayo bhavanti tat kim anena pathyasevanenetyāha parihāryāṇītyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, even when the pursuit of wholesome [practices] is being carried out, diseases also arise due to the power of strong past demerit (<s>prāktana adharma</s>). So what is the use of this pursuit of the wholesome? — he answers with 'things to be avoided,' etc. // 1

children.text: anṛṇatām iva prāpto'nṛṇatāṃ prāptaḥ etena parihāryaparihāreṇa puruṣakāre'naparādhaḥ puruṣo bhavatīti darśayati // 2
children.translated_text: 'Becomes as if freed from debt' — by this he shows that through the avoidance of what should be avoided, a person becomes free from blame regarding his own effort (<s>puruṣakāra</s>). // 2

children.text: yastu daivāgatastasya vyādhistatra sādhavo naivaṃ pathyasevinaṃ garhayanti etadevāha yattvityādi // 3
children.translated_text: But as for the disease that comes by fate — there, the virtuous do not blame the one who follows the wholesome regimen. This very [point] he states with 'but as for,' etc. // 3
'Cannot be avoided' — because it arises from powerful [past] <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning. // 4

children.text: na śocitavyam iti puruṣakārasya daivajanye 'vaśyambhāvini vyādhāv akiṃcitkaratvād ityarthaḥ // 5]
children.translated_text: 'Should not grieve' — because human effort is of no avail against disease that is inevitably destined to arise from fate — this is the meaning. // 5]
That the body originates from food, and that diseases too originate from food;
the specifics of wholesome and unwholesome, and the difference between happiness and suffering; // Car_1,28.45
the capacity and incapacity of the body and mind to endure suffering;

children.text: viśeṣo rogasaṃghāś ca dhātujā ye pṛthakpṛthak // Car_1,28.46
children.translated_text: the difference [between the wise and the worldly], the groups of diseases arising from the respective tissues; // Car_1,28.46

children.text: teṣāṃ caiva praśamanaṃ koṣṭhācchākhā upetya ca /
children.translated_text: their pacification, and how the <s>doṣas</s>, having gone from the <s>koṣṭha</s> to the <s>śākhā</s>,

children.text: doṣā yathā prakupyanti śākhābhyaḥ koṣṭhametya ca // Car_1,28.47
children.translated_text: become aggravated, and [how they do so] having gone from the <s>śākhā</s> to the <s>koṣṭha</s>; // Car_1,28.47
and the difference between the wise and the ignorant, and what is wholesome for the healthy and the sick —
all that has been illuminated in the [chapter called] <s>Vividhāśitapītīya</s>. // Car_1,28.48

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte sūtrasthāne vividhāśitapītīyo nāmāṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ // Car_1,28.49
sahatve cāsahatve cetyādinā śarīrāṇi cātisthūlāni ityādi viparītāni punar vyādhisahāni ityantaṃ granthaṃ jñāpayati // 2]

children.translated_text: [<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:

children.text: iti ha smāha bhagavān ātreyaḥ // Car_2,7.2
iha khalu pañconmādā bhavanti tadyathā vātapittakaphasannipātāgantunimittāḥ // Car_2,7.3

tatra doṣanimittāś catvāraḥ puruṣāṇām evaṃvidhānāṃ kṣipram abhinirvartante tadyathā bhīrūṇām upakliṣṭasattvānām utsannadoṣāṇāṃ samalavikṛtopahitāny anucitāny āhārajātāni vaiṣamyayuktenopayogavidhinopayuñjānānāṃ tantraprayogam api viṣamam ācaratām anyāś ca śarīraceṣṭā viṣamāḥ samācaratām atyupakṣīṇadehānāṃ vyādhivegasamudbhramitānām upahatamanasāṃ vā kāmakrodhalobhaharṣabhayamohāyāsaśokacintodvegādibhir bhūyo 'bhighātābhyāhatānāṃ vā manasy upahate buddhau ca pracalitāyām abhyudīrṇā doṣāḥ prakupitā hṛdayam upasṛtya manovahāni srotāṃsy āvṛtya janayanty unmādam // Car_2,7.4

tasyemāni pūrvarūpāṇi tadyathā śirasaḥ śūnyatā cakṣuṣor ākulatā svanaḥ karṇayoḥ ucchvāsasyādhikyam āsyasaṃsravaṇam anannābhilāṣārocakāvipākāḥ hṛdgrahaḥ dhyānāyāsasammohodvegāś cāsthāne satataṃ lomaharṣaḥ jvaraś cābhīkṣṇam unmattacittatvam udarditvam arditākṛtikaraṇaṃ ca vyādheḥ svapne cābhīkṣṇaṃ darśanaṃ bhrāntacalitānavasthitānāṃ rūpāṇām apraśastānāṃ ca tilapīḍakacakrādhirohaṇaṃ vātakuṇḍalikābhiś conmathanaṃ nimajjanaṃ ca kaluṣāṇām ambhasām āvarte cakṣuṣoś cāpasarpaṇam iti // Car_2,7.6

tatredam unmādaviśeṣavijñānaṃ bhavati tadyathā parisaraṇam ajasram akṣibhruvauṣṭāṃsahanvagrahastapādāṅgavikṣepaṇam akasmāt satatam aniyatānāṃ ca girām utsargaḥ phenāgamanam āsyāt abhīkṣṇaṃ smitahasitanṛtyagītavāditrasaṃprayogāś cāsthāne vīṇāvaṃśaśaṅkhaśamyātālaśabdānukaraṇam asāmnā yānam ayānaiḥ alaṅkaraṇam analaṅkārikair dravyaiḥ lobhaś cābhyavahāryeṣv alabdheṣu labdheṣu cāvamānas tīvramātsaryaṃ ca kārśyaṃ pāruṣyam utpiṇḍitāruṇākṣatā vātopaśayaviparyāsād anupaśayatā ca iti vātonmādaliṅgāni bhavanti /

amarṣaḥ krodhaḥ saṃrambhaś cāsthāne śastraloṣṭakaśākāṣṭhamuṣṭibhir abhihananaṃ sveṣāṃ pareṣāṃ vā abhidravaṇaṃ pracchāyaśītodakānnābhilāṣaḥ saṃtāpaś cātivelaṃ tāmrahāritahāridrasaṃrabdhākṣatā pittopaśayaviparyāsād anupaśayatā ca iti pittonmadaliṅgāni bhavanti /

sthānam ekadeśe tūṣṇīṃbhāvaḥ alpaśaś caṅkramaṇaṃ lālāśiṅghāṇakasravaṇam anannābhilāṣaḥ rahaskāmatā bībhatsatvaṃ śaucadveṣaḥ svapnanityatā śvayathur ānane śuklastimitamalopadigdhākṣatvaṃ śleṣmopaśayaviparyāsād anupaśayatā ca iti śleṣmonmādaliṅgāni bhavanti /
tridoṣaliṅgasannipāte tu sānnipātikaṃ vidyāt tam asādhyam ācakṣate kuśalāḥ // Car_2,7.7

sādhyānāṃ tu trayāṇāṃ sādhanāni snehasvedavamanavirecanāsthāpanānuvāsanopaśamanastaḥkarmadhūmadhūpanāñjanāvapīḍapradhamanābhyaṅgapradehapariṣekānulepanavadhabandhanāvarodhanavitrāsanavismāpanavismāraṇāpatarpaṇasirāvyadhanāni bhojanavidhānaṃ ca yathāsvaṃ yuktyā yac cānyad api kiṃcin nidānaviparītam auṣadhaṃ kāryaṃ tad api syād iti // Car_2,7.8
bhavati cātra unmādān doṣajān sādhyān sādhayed bhiṣaguttamaḥ /
yas tu doṣanimittebhya unmādebhyaḥ samutthānapūrvarūpaliṅgavedanopaśayaviśeṣasamanvito bhavaty unmādas tam āgantukam ācakṣate /
kecit punaḥ pūrvakṛtaṃ karmāpraśastam icchanti tasya nimittam /
tasya ca hetuḥ prajñāparādha eveti bhagavān punarvasur ātreyaḥ /

prajñāparādhād dhy ayaṃ devarṣipitṛgandharvayakṣarākṣasapiśācaguruvṛddhasiddhācāryapūjyānavamatyāhitāny ācarati anyad vā kiṃcid evaṃvidhaṃ karmāpraśastam ārabhate tam ātmanā hatam upaghnanto devādayaḥ kurvanty unmattam // Car_2,7.10

devādiprakopanimittenāgantukonmādena puraskṛtasyemāni pūrvarūpāṇi bhavanti tadyathā devagobrāhmaṇatapasvināṃ hiṃsārucitvaṃ kopanatvaṃ nṛśaṃsābhiprāyatā aratiḥ ojovarṇacchāyāvalavapuṣām upanaptiḥ svapne ca devādibhir abhibhartsanaṃ pravartanaṃ ceti tato 'nantaram unmādābhinirvṛttiḥ // Car_2,7.11

tatrāyam unmādakarāṇāṃ bhūtānām unmādayiṣyatām ārambhaviśeṣo bhavati tad yathā avalokayanto devā janayanty unmādaṃ guruvṛddhasiddhamaharṣayo 'bhiśapantaḥ pitaro darśayantaḥ spṛśanto gandharvāḥ samāviśanto yakṣāḥ rākṣasās tv ātmagandham āghrāpayantaḥ piśācāḥ punar āruhya vāhayantaḥ // Car_2,7.12
tasyemāni rūpāṇi bhavanti tad yathā atyātmabalavīryapauruṣaparākramagrahaṇadhāraṇasmaraṇajñānavacanavijñānāni aniyataś conmādakālaḥ // Car_2,7.13

unmādayiṣyatām api khalu devarṣipitṛgandharvayakṣarākṣasapiśācānāṃ guruvṛddhasiddhānāṃ vā eṣv antareṣv abhigamanīyāḥ puruṣā bhavanti tad yathā pāpasya karmaṇaḥ samārambhe pūrvakṛtasya vā karmaṇaḥ pariṇāmakāle ekasya vā śūnyagṛhavāse catuṣpathādhiṣṭhāne vā sandhyāvelāyām aprayatabhāve vā parvasandhiṣu vā mithunībhāve rajasvalābhigamane vā viguṇe vādhyayanabalimaṅgalahomaprayoge niyamavratabrahmacaryabhaṅge vā mahāhave vā deśakulapuravināśe vā mahāgrahopagamane vā striyā vā prajananakāle vividhabhūtāśubhāśucisparśane vā vamanavirecanarudhirasrāve aśucer aprayatasya vā caityadevāyatanābhigamane vā māṃsamadhutilaguḍamadyocchiṣṭe vā digvāsasi vā niśi nagaranigamacatuṣpathopavanaśmaśānāghātanābhigamane vā dvijagurusurayatipūjyābhidharṣaṇe vā dharmākhyānavyatikrame vā anyasya vā karmaṇo 'praśastasyārambhe ity abhighātakālā vyākhyātā bhavanti // Car_2,7.14

trividhaṃ tu khalūnmādakarāṇāṃ bhūtānām unmādane prayojanaṃ bhavati tad yathā hiṃsā ratiḥ abhyarcanaṃ ceti /
teṣāṃ taṃ prayojanaviśeṣam unmattācāraviśeṣalakṣaṇair vidyāt /
nidāne jñātahetvādipañcakasya cikitsopayogitayā doṣabheṣajādiviśeṣajñānam apekṣitaṃ bhavati ato vakṣyamāṇadoṣabheṣajādiviśeṣajñāpakaṃ vimānasthānaṃ brūte // 1
tatrāpi ca doṣabheṣajayoḥ prādhānyāt tadviśeṣajñāpakaṃ rasavimānaṃ prathamaṃ brūte // 2
viśeṣeṇa mīyate jñāyate doṣabheṣajādy aneneti vimānaṃ doṣabheṣajādīnāṃ prabhāvādiviśeṣa ityarthaḥ evaṃbhūtaṃvimānam abhidheyatayā yatra tiṣṭhati tad vimānasthānam // 4

iha khalu vyādhīnāṃ nimittapūrvarūparūpopaśayasaṃkhyāprādhānyavidhivikalpabalakālaviśeṣān anupraviśyānantaraṃ doṣabheṣajadeśakālabalaśarīrasārāhārasātmyasattvaprakṛtivayasāṃ mānam avahitamanasā yathāvaj jñeyaṃ bhavati bhiṣajā doṣādimānajñānāyattatvāt kriyāyāḥ /
na hy amānajño doṣādīnāṃ bhiṣag vyādhinigrahasamartho bhavati /
iha samprāptibhedasaṃkhyāprādhānyādigrahaṇenaiva samprāptim upadiśan saṃkhyādibhedena sarvaiva samprāptiḥ kathitā bhavatīti darśayati // 2
nimittādīnāṃ tu na tādṛśo bhedo 'lpagranthavaktavyo 'sti yena bhedena te 'pīha kathyeran ataste sāmānyenaivoktāḥ // 3
mānamiti prabhāvādiviśeṣaḥ etajjñāne hetum āha doṣādītyādi // 6

tatrādau rasadravyadoṣavikāraprabhāvān vakṣyāmaḥ rasāstāvatṣaṭ madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭutiktakaṣāyāḥ te samyagupayujyamānāḥ śarīraṃ yāpayanti mithyopayujyamānāstu khalu doṣaprakopāyopakalpante // Car_3,1.4

yadyapi ca doṣabheṣajetyādau doṣāpekṣatvād bheṣajasya doṣa ādau kṛtaḥ tathāpīha rasadravyarūpabheṣajasyāpekṣitarogapraśamakartṛtvena tathā doṣasyāpi ca rasadravyayoreva kāraṇatvena bheṣajaśabdasūcite rasadravye evāgre kṛte paścāttu doṣagrahaṇagṛhītau doṣavikārau // 2
prakṛṣṭo bhāvaḥ prabhāvaḥ śaktirityarthaḥ sa cehācintyaścintyaś ca grāhyaḥ // 3
yena tatra khalvanekaraseṣu ityādinā dravyavikārayoḥ prabhāvaṃ rasadvārā doṣadvārā ca cintyamapi vakṣyati // 4
te prakṛtibhūtāḥ śarīropakārakā bhavanti vikṛtimāpannāstu khalu nānāvidhair vikāraiḥ śarīram upatāpayanti // Car_3,1.5
children.translated_text: When in their natural state (<s>prakṛti</s>), they are beneficial to the body; but when they become vitiated (<s>vikṛti</s>), they afflict the body with various kinds of disorders. // Car_3,1.5
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'<s>Doṣas</s>' refers to the bodily <s>doṣas</s>. // 1
The word 'punaḥ' (again) serves to exclude the mental <s>doṣa</s>. // 2]

children.text: tatra doṣamekaikaṃ trayastrayo rasā janayanti trayas trayaś copaśamayanti /
children.translated_text: There, three tastes each generate each individual <s>doṣa</s>, and three each pacify [it].

children.text: tadyathā kaṭutiktakaṣāyā vātaṃ janayanti madhurāmlalavaṇas tv enaṃ śamayanti kaṭvamlalavaṇāḥ pittaṃ janayanti madhuratiktakaṣāyās tv enacchamayanti madhurāmlalavaṇāḥ śleṣmāṇaṃ janayanti kaṭutiktakaṣāyāstvenaṃ śamayanti // Car_3,1.6
children.translated_text: Namely: pungent, bitter, and astringent generate <s>Vāta</s>, while sweet, sour, and salty pacify it. Pungent, sour, and salty generate <s>Pitta</s>, while sweet, bitter, and astringent pacify it. Sweet, sour, and salty generate <s>Śleṣman</s> (Kapha), while pungent, bitter, and astringent pacify it. // Car_3,1.6
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states the action of unmixed tastes with 'there' etc. // 1

children.text: anena ca rasakarmopadeśena doṣāṇāmapi tattadrasotpādyatvaṃ tathā tattadrasopaśamanīyatvam uktaṃ bhavati // 2
children.translated_text: And by this teaching of the actions of tastes, it is also stated that the <s>doṣas</s> are produced by their respective tastes and are pacifiable by their respective tastes. // 2

children.text: kaṭutiktakaṣāyā vātaṃ janayantīti asati paripanthinīti jñeyaṃ tenārkāguruguḍūcyādīnāṃ tiktānāmapi vātājanakatve na doṣaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: 'Pungent, bitter, and astringent generate <s>Vāta</s>' — this should be understood [as applying only] when there is no counteracting factor (<s>paripanthin</s>). Therefore, even though <s>Arka</s>, <s>Aguru</s>, <s>Guḍūcī</s>, etc. are bitter, there is no fault in their not generating <s>Vāta</s>. // 3

children.text: tatra hy uṣṇavīryatā paripanthinī vidyate tena na te vātaṃ janayantītyādy anusaraṇīyam // 4
children.translated_text: For in those, there exists the counteracting factor of hot potency (<s>uṣṇavīrya</s>). Therefore, [the statement that] 'they do not generate <s>Vāta</s>' etc. should be followed accordingly. // 4

children.text: enam iti padena yaśca kaṭvādijo vāyustameva madhurādayaḥ sarvātmavaiparītyād viśeṣeṇa śamayantīti darśayati jāgaraṇādije hi vāyau jāgaraṇādiviparītāḥ svapnādaya eva viśeṣeṇa pathyāḥ // 5
children.translated_text: By the word 'enam' (this very one), he shows that the <s>Vāyu</s> that is produced by pungent etc. — that very one the sweet and other [tastes] pacify especially, by being completely opposite in nature. For <s>Vāyu</s> produced by wakefulness etc. is especially treatable by sleep etc. — which are the opposites of wakefulness etc. // 5

children.text: evaṃ pittaśleṣmaṇorapi enadenaṃ śabdayos tātparyaṃ darśayati // 6]
children.translated_text: Similarly, regarding <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Śleṣman</s> also, he shows the purport of the words 'enat' and 'enam.' // 6]

children.text: rasadoṣasaṃnipāte tu ye rasā yair doṣaiḥ samānaguṇāḥ samānaguṇabhūyiṣṭhā vā bhavanti te tān abhivardhayanti viparītaguṇā viparītaguṇabhūyiṣṭhā vā śamayantyabhyasyamānā iti /
children.translated_text: But when tastes and <s>doṣas</s> come together: those tastes that are of similar qualities or predominantly of similar qualities to [particular] <s>doṣas</s> augment them; while those of opposite qualities or predominantly of opposite qualities pacify them when used habitually.

children.text: etadvyavasthāhetoḥ ṣaṭtvam upadiśyate rasānāṃ paraspareṇāsaṃsṛṣṭānāṃ tritvaṃ ca doṣāṇām // Car_3,1.7
children.translated_text: For the purpose of this systematic arrangement, the sixfold nature of unmixed tastes and the threefold nature of the <s>doṣas</s> are taught. // Car_3,1.7
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: atha kayā yuktyā rasā doṣāñjanayanti śamayanti cetyāha rasadoṣetyādi // 1
