children.translated_text: Now, by what rationale do the tastes generate and pacify the <s>doṣas</s>? — he states this with 'when tastes and <s>doṣas</s>' etc. // 1
'Coming together' (<s>saṃnipāta</s>) means meeting within the body. // 2

children.text: tuśabdo viśeṣe tena viparītaguṇā eva viśeṣeṇa viparītaguṇabhūyiṣṭhāpekṣayā śamayantīti darśayati // 3
children.translated_text: The word 'tu' (but) denotes distinction; by this he shows that those of opposite qualities pacify especially — in comparison to those that are predominantly of opposite qualities. // 3

children.text: rasānāṃ tu yathā upācārādguṇā bhavanti tadabhihitaṃ guṇāguṇāśrayā noktāḥ ityādinā sūtre // 4
children.translated_text: As for how the tastes come to possess their qualities — that has been stated in the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with 'The qualities and non-qualities have not been stated as inherent' etc. // 4
'When used habitually' (<s>abhyasyamānāḥ</s>) means not when used just once. // 5

children.text: atha kasmādrasadoṣasaṃsargabhūyastvaṃ parityajya rasaṣaṭtvaṃ doṣatritvaṃ cocyate ityāha ityetadityādi // 6
children.translated_text: Now, why is the sixfold nature of tastes and the threefold nature of <s>doṣas</s> stated, instead of elaborating the multiplicity of taste-<s>doṣa</s> combinations? — he states this with 'for this purpose' etc. // 6
'Systematic arrangement' (<s>vyavasthā</s>) means the condensation of the elaboration of taste-<s>doṣa</s> combinations. // 7
The phrase 'unmixed with each other' should be connected with '<s>doṣas</s>' as well. // 8]

children.text: saṃsargavikalpavistaro hy eṣām aparisaṃkhyeyo bhavati vikalpabhedāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt // Car_3,1.8
children.translated_text: For the elaboration of combinations and permutations of these [tastes and <s>doṣas</s>] is innumerable, because the sub-divisions of permutations are innumerable. // Car_3,1.8
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states the reason for not elaborating the taste-<s>doṣa</s> combination details, with 'of combinations' etc. // 1

children.text: yasmāt saṃsargabhedavistaro 'parisaṃkhyeyas tasmāt ṣaṭtvaṃ tritvaṃ cocyate // 2
children.translated_text: Since the elaboration of combination-divisions is innumerable, therefore the sixfold and threefold [classification] is stated. // 2

children.text: vikalpabhedāparisaṃkhyeyatvād iti saṃsargavikalpasya bhedo vijātīyaprakāraḥ tasyāparisaṃkhyeyatvāt // 3
children.translated_text: 'Because the sub-divisions of permutations are innumerable' — the sub-division of a combination-permutation is a heterogeneous variety; because that is innumerable. // 3

children.text: etena yathā rasānām avāntaravyaktibhede 'pi madhuratvādisāmānyayogān madhurādivyapadeśena ṣaṭtvamucyate tathā madhurāmlamadhuralavaṇādisaṃsargāṇām api satyapyavāntarabhede sāmānyopasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā triṣaṣṭitvasaṃkhyāniyamo bhaviṣyatīti nirasyate yato madhurāmlādisaṃsarge 'pi vijātīyo madhurataramadhuratamādibhedakṛto bhedo 'parisaṃkhyeyo bhavati // 4
children.translated_text: By this, the following [objection] is refuted: just as the sixfold designation 'sweet' etc. is applied to tastes despite there being sub-varieties of individual instances — by virtue of the common property of sweetness etc. — similarly, even for combinations like sweet-sour, sweet-salty, etc., despite there being sub-varieties, one could make a generalized grouping and arrive at a fixed number of sixty-three [combinations]. [This is refuted] because even in the sweet-sour etc. combinations, the heterogeneous sub-division caused by degrees of more-sweet, most-sweet, etc. is innumerable. // 4

children.text: vacanaṃ hi rasās taratamābhyāṃ tāṃ saṃkhyām atipatanti hi iti // 5]
children.translated_text: For the statement is: 'The tastes, by [degrees of] more and most, exceed that number.' // 5]

children.text: tatra khalvanekaraseṣu dravyeṣvanekadoṣātmakeṣu ca vikāreṣu rasadoṣaprabhāvam ekaikaśyenābhisamīkṣya tato dravyavikārayoḥ prabhāvatattvaṃ vyavasyet // Car_3,1.9
children.translated_text: Therefore, in substances that have multiple tastes and in disorders that have a multi-<s>doṣa</s> nature, one should examine the influence of each taste and each <s>doṣa</s> individually, and then determine the true nature of the influence of the substance or disorder. // Car_3,1.9
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: atha kathaṃ tarhi saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca prabhāvo jñeya ityāha tatra khalvityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, how then should one know the influence of combined tastes and <s>doṣas</s>? — he states this with 'therefore' etc. // 1

children.text: tatra cānekarasadravyasyānekadoṣavikārasya ca pratyekarasadoṣaprabhāvamelakena prabhāvaṃ kathayan rasasaṃsargadoṣasaṃsargayor api tādṛśameva prabhāvaṃ kathayati yato rasadoṣasaṃsargaprabhāvāv atra dravyavikārāśrayitvād rasadoṣayor dravyavikāraprabhāvatvenocyete // 2
children.translated_text: There, by describing the influence of a multi-taste substance and a multi-<s>doṣa</s> disorder through the aggregate of the individual influences of each taste and <s>doṣa</s>, he also describes the influence of taste-combinations and <s>doṣa</s>-combinations in the same manner — since the influences of taste-combinations and <s>doṣa</s>-combinations are here stated as the influences of substances and disorders, because the tastes and <s>doṣas</s> reside in substances and disorders [respectively]. // 2

children.text: anena nyāyena sākṣādanukte'pi ekarasadravyaikadoṣavikārayor api prabhāvo 'saṃsṛṣṭarasadoṣaprabhāvakathanād ukta eva jñeyaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: By this principle, even the influence of a single-taste substance and a single-<s>doṣa</s> disorder — though not directly stated — should be understood as already stated, since the influence of unmixed tastes and <s>doṣas</s> has been described. // 3

children.text: ekaikaśyenābhisamīkṣyeti pratyekam uktarasādiprabhāveṇānekarasaṃ dravyam anekadoṣaṃ ca vikāraṃ samuditaprabhāvam abhisamīkṣya // 4]
children.translated_text: 'Having examined individually' — means having examined a multi-taste substance and a multi-<s>doṣa</s> disorder for their aggregate influence through the individually stated influence of each taste etc. // 4]
But this is not so everywhere.

children.text: na hi vikṛtiviṣamasamavetānāṃ nānātmakānāṃ paraspareṇa copahatānāmanyaiśca vikalpanair vikalpitānām avayavaprabhāvānumānenaiva samudāyaprabhāvatattvam adhyavasātuṃ śakyam // Car_3,1.10
children.translated_text: For in the case of [tastes and <s>doṣas</s>] that are combined in altered and unequal manner — that are of diverse natures, mutually counteracted, and modified by other differentiating factors — the true nature of the aggregate influence cannot be determined merely by inference from the individual component influences. // Car_3,1.10
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: ayaṃ ca rasadoṣaprabhāvadvārā dravyavikāraprabhāvaniścayo na sarvatra dravye vikāre cetyāha na tv evaṃ khalu sarvatreti // 1
children.translated_text: And this determination of the influence of substances and disorders through the medium of taste-<s>doṣa</s> influence is not [applicable] everywhere in substances and disorders — he states this with 'but this is not so everywhere.' // 1

children.text: atraiva hetum āha na hītyādinādhyavasātuṃ śakyamityantena // 2
children.translated_text: He states the reason for this very [limitation] with 'for' etc. up to 'cannot be determined.' // 2

children.text: vikṛtiviṣamasamavetānām iti vikṛtisamavetānāṃ tathā viṣamasamavetānāṃ ceti vikṛtiviṣamasamavetānām // 3
children.translated_text: 'Combined in altered and unequal manner' (<s>vikṛti-viṣama-samaveta</s>) means those combined in an altered manner and those combined in an unequal manner — [i.e.,] those that are vikṛti-samaveta and viṣama-samaveta. // 3
'Combined' (<s>samaveta</s>) means mixed — of tastes and <s>doṣas</s>. // 4

children.text: tatra rasasya vikṛtisamavāyo yathā madhure taṇḍulīyake madhuro hi prakṛtyā snehavṛṣyatvādikaraḥ taṇḍulīyake tu vikṛtisamavetatvena tanna karoti // 5
children.translated_text: The altered combination (<s>vikṛti-samavāya</s>) of a taste [is illustrated] as in <s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s> (Amaranthus), which is sweet — for sweet is naturally a producer of unctuousness, aphrodisiac properties, etc., but in <s>Taṇḍulīyaka</s>, being combined in an altered manner, it does not produce those [effects]. // 5

children.text: viṣamasamavetāstu tile kaṣāyakaṭutiktamadhurāḥ yadi hīme rasāḥ samayā mātrayā samavetāḥ syustatastilo'pi pittaśleṣmaharastridoṣaharo vā syāt pittakaphakarastvayaṃ tenātra rasānāṃ kvacit kartṛtvam akartṛtvaṃ ca kvaciditi vaiṣamyam unnīyate // 6
children.translated_text: The unequal combination (<s>viṣama-samavāya</s>) is [illustrated] in sesame (<s>tila</s>), [where] astringent, pungent, bitter, and sweet [tastes coexist]. For if these tastes were combined in equal measure, then sesame too would reduce <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>, or would reduce all three <s>doṣas</s>. But it aggravates <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Kapha</s>. Therefore, the inequality is inferred — that some tastes are operative [here] while others are not. // 6
The three reasons — 'of diverse natures' etc. — are indeed indicators of altered and unequal combination. // 7
Thus, being of diverse natures etc. gives rise to altered and unequal combination. // 8

children.text: nānātmakānāmiti nānārūpahetujanitānāṃ tena hetubhedabalādeva rasadoṣayor vikṛto viṣamo vā melako bhavatītyarthaḥ // 9
children.translated_text: 'Of diverse natures' (<s>nānātmaka</s>) means produced from causes of diverse forms; thus, by the very diversity of causes, the combination of tastes and <s>doṣas</s> becomes altered or unequal — this is the meaning. // 9
Alternatively, 'of diverse natures' means of diverse measures. // 10
And thus, being of diverse measures is the cause of unequal combination. // 11
'Mutually counteracted' means having their qualities damaged by one another. // 12

children.text: parasparaguṇopaghātastu yadyapi doṣāṇāṃ prāyo nāstyeva tathāpyadṛṣṭavaśāt kvacid bhavatīti jñeyaṃ rasānāṃ tu prabalenānyopaghāto bhavatyeva // 13
children.translated_text: And the mutual counteraction of qualities — although generally it does not [commonly] occur among <s>doṣas</s> — nevertheless, it should be understood that it occurs occasionally due to unseen [karmic] forces. But among tastes, counteraction of one by a stronger [taste] does indeed occur. // 13

children.text: anyaiśca vikalpanairiti anyaiśca bhedakaiḥ tatra rasasya bhedakāḥ svarasakalkādayaḥ ekasyaiva hi dravyasya kalpanāviśeṣeṇa guṇāntarāṇi bhavanti // 14
children.translated_text: 'And by other differentiating factors' — i.e., by other divisors. There, the differentiating factors of tastes are expressed juice (<s>svarasa</s>), paste (<s>kalka</s>), etc. For a single substance acquires different qualities through different modes of preparation. // 14
For <s>doṣas</s>, however, different tissues (<s>dūṣyas</s>) become the differentiating factors, by virtue of [the <s>doṣa</s>] acquiring different qualities [in different tissue-locations]. // 15

children.text: yaduktaṃ sa eva kupito doṣaḥ samutthānaviśeṣataḥ // 16
children.translated_text: As it has been stated: 'That very same vitiated <s>doṣa</s>, due to differences in etiology, // 16
and having gone to a different location, produces many disorders.' // 17

children.text: asminvyākhyāne rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca ya utkarṣāpakarṣakṛto viṣamasamavāyaḥ pṛthagucyate sa na yujyate yato viṣamasamavāye 'pyutkṛṣṭasya rasasya tathā doṣasya cotkṛṣṭā guṇā apakṛṣṭasya cāpakṛṣṭā guṇā bhavantīti kṛtvāvayavaprabhāvān anumānenaiva samudāyaprabhāvānumānaṃ śakyam // 18
children.translated_text: In this explanation, the unequal combination caused by the variation of more and less among tastes and <s>doṣas</s> — being stated separately — is not appropriate, because even in unequal combination, the qualities of the predominant taste or <s>doṣa</s> are predominant and those of the subordinate are subordinate; thus the aggregate influence can be inferred from the component influences. // 18

children.text: athocyate viṣamamelake rasasya doṣasya ca na ta eva guṇā utkṛṣṭā apakṛṣṭā vā bhavanti kiṃtu guṇāntarameva bhavati hanta tarhi vikṛta evāyaṃ samavāyo visadṛśakāryakāraṇatvāt // 19
children.translated_text: If it be said that in unequal mixing, a taste or <s>doṣa</s> does not have those very same qualities — predominant or subordinate — but rather acquires entirely different qualities; well then, this would itself be an altered combination, since the cause-effect relationship is dissimilar. // 19

children.text: tadevaṃ dūṣaṇadarśanād anyathā vyākhyāyate yad dvividho melako bhavati rasānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ ca prakṛtyanuguṇaḥ prakṛtyananuguṇaśca tatra yo militānāṃ prākṛtaguṇānupamardena melako bhavati sa prakṛtisamasamavāyaśabdenocyate yastu prākṛtaguṇopamardena bhavati sa vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyo 'bhidhīyate vikṛtyā hetubhūtayā viṣamaḥ prakṛtyananuguṇaḥ samavāyo vikṛtiviṣamasamavāya ityarthaḥ // 20
children.translated_text: Therefore, having seen these objections, [the text] is explained differently: the combination of tastes and <s>doṣas</s> is of two kinds — conforming to natural state (<s>prakṛti-sama-samavāya</s>) and not conforming to natural state (<s>prakṛty-ananuguna</s>). Among these, the combination that occurs without destroying the natural qualities of the mixed [components] is called 'natural-conforming combination' (<s>prakṛti-sama-samavāya</s>). But the one that occurs with destruction of natural qualities is called 'altered-unequal combination' (<s>vikṛti-viṣama-samavāya</s>) — meaning a combination that is unequal, i.e., not conforming to natural state, due to alteration (<s>vikṛti</s>) as its cause. // 20
In this very altered-unequal combination, the three reasons — being of diverse natures etc. — should be applied as already explained. // 21

children.text: ye tu vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyau pṛthag eva kurvanti viṣamasamavāyasya vaiṣamyatāratamyenātibahuprapañcitatvād viṣamāvayavaguṇānumānaṃ duḥśakam iti kṛtvā tadapi dravyavikāraprabhāveṇaiva vyapadiśanti // 22]
children.translated_text: Those who treat altered combination and unequal combination as entirely separate [concepts] — since unequal combination, due to the extensive elaboration of degrees of inequality, makes inference of the qualities of unequal components difficult — they also designate it simply as the influence of the substance or disorder [itself]. // 22]

children.text: tathāyukte hi samudaye samudāyaprabhāvatattvamevam evopalabhya tato dravyavikāraprabhāvatattvaṃ vyavasyet // Car_3,1.11
children.translated_text: In an aggregate that is so constituted, one should ascertain the true nature of the aggregate influence by [direct] observation; and from that, determine the true nature of the substance's or disorder's influence. // Car_3,1.11
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: atha kathaṃ tarhi vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyaprabhāvajñānam ityāha tathāyukte hītyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, how then is the influence of the altered-unequal combination to be known? — he states this with 'in [an aggregate] so constituted' etc. // 1
'In [an aggregate] so constituted' means in [a case of] altered-unequal combination. // 2
'The true nature of the aggregate influence' means the true nature of the influence of the combination. // 3

children.text: samadhṛte hi madhusarpiṣi sūryāvartākhye vā doṣasamudaye na saṃyujyamānamadhughṛtaguṇakramāgataṃ mārakatvaṃ na ca vātādidoṣaprabhāvagataṃ sūryavṛddhyā vardhiṣṇutvaṃ sūryāvartasya kiṃ tu saṃyogamahimakṛtam evetyarthaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: For in equal parts of honey and ghee — or in the combination of <s>doṣas</s> called <s>Sūryāvarta</s> — the lethal property does not come from the sequential [summation of] the qualities of the combined honey and ghee, nor does <s>Sūryāvarta</s>'s property of increasing with the sun come from the individual <s>doṣa</s>-influences — rather, it is produced solely by the power of the combination. // 4

children.text: yacca gatidvayaṃ doṣarasamelakasya tena prakṛtisamasamavāyarūpaṃ saṃnipātaṃ jvaranidāne doṣaliṅgamelakenaivoktavān // 5
children.translated_text: And since the combination of <s>doṣas</s> and tastes has these two courses [conforming and non-conforming], [the author] described the <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined) fever, which is of the nature-conforming type, in the chapter on the etiology of fever, through the combination of <s>doṣa</s>-characteristics alone. // 5

children.text: yaduktaṃ pṛthaguktalakṣaṇasaṃsargād dvāṃdvikam anyatamaṃ sāṃnipātikaṃ vā jvaraṃ vidyād iti // 6
children.translated_text: As it was stated: 'From the combination of the individually stated characteristics, one should know the fever as dual-<s>doṣa</s> or tri-<s>doṣa</s> (<s>sāṃnipātika</s>).' // 6

children.text: yastu vikṛtiviṣamasamavetastridoṣakṛto jvaras tasya cikitsite kṣaṇe dāhaḥ kṣaṇe śītam ityādinā lakṣaṇam uktam // 7
children.translated_text: But the tri-<s>doṣa</s> fever produced by altered-unequal combination — its characteristics are stated in the treatment section as 'at one moment burning, at another moment chill' etc. // 7

children.text: na hi śyāvaraktakoṭhotpattyādi tatroktaṃ vātādijvare kvacid asti // 8
children.translated_text: For symptoms like the eruption of blue-red welts etc. mentioned therein do not appear in any of the individual <s>Vāta</s>-fever etc. [types]. // 8

children.text: evaṃ rase'pi yatrāmrāte madhuratvaṃ prakṛtisamasamavetaṃ tatrāmrātaṃ madhuram etanmātram evoktaṃ tena madhurasāmānyaguṇāgataṃ tasya vātapittaharatvamapi labhyata eva // 9
children.translated_text: Similarly for tastes: where the sweetness in <s>Āmrāta</s> (hog-plum) is combined in a nature-conforming manner, there <s>Āmrāta</s> is stated [simply] as 'sweet' — this much only is stated. By this, its property of reducing <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s>, which follows from the general properties of sweetness, is also obtained. // 9

children.text: yatra vārtāke kaṭutiktatvena vātakaratvaṃ prāptamapi ca vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyāttanna bhavati tatrācāryeṇa vārtākaṃ vātaghnam ityuktam eva // 10
children.translated_text: But where in <s>Vārtāka</s> (eggplant), the property of aggravating <s>Vāta</s> — which should follow from its pungent-bitter [tastes] — does not occur due to altered-unequal combination, there the master has stated '<s>Vārtāka</s> alleviates <s>Vāta</s>.' // 10
'Thus' etc. — such illustrations as found throughout the treatise should be followed. // 11

children.text: yattu prakṛtisamasamavāyakṛtarasadoṣaguṇadvārā prāptamapi dravyaguṇaṃ vikāralakṣaṇaṃ ca brūte tat prakarṣārthaṃ spaṣṭārthaṃ ceti jñeyam // 12]
children.translated_text: When [the treatise] states a quality of a substance or a characteristic of a disorder that is already obtainable through the medium of the taste-<s>doṣa</s> qualities of the nature-conforming combination — that is for the purpose of emphasis and clarity — this should be understood. // 12]

children.text: tasmād rasaprabhāvataś ca dravyaprabhāvataś ca doṣaprabhāvataś ca vikāraprabhāvataś ca tattvamupadekṣyāmaḥ // Car_3,1.12
children.translated_text: Therefore, we shall teach the truth regarding the effect of <s>rasa</s> (taste), the effect of <s>dravya</s> (substance), the effect of <s>doṣa</s>, and the effect of <s>vikāra</s> (disease). // <s>Car</s>_3,1.12
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He concludes with 'Therefore' etc. // 1
'Truth' means the truth of the effects of <s>rasa</s> etc. // 2

children.text: yattu pūrvaṃ tatrādau rasadravyadoṣavikāraprabhāvān upadekṣyāmaḥ ityanena rasādiprabhāvavyākhyānapratijñānaṃ kṛtaṃ tattu rasaprabhāvānumānenaiva dravyaprabhāvakathanāt tathā doṣaprabhāveṇa ca vikāraprabhāvakathanāc caritārthaṃ syāt // 3
children.translated_text: As for what was said earlier — 'therein, first we shall teach the effects of <s>rasa</s>, <s>dravya</s>, <s>doṣa</s>, and <s>vikāra</s>' — that promise to explain the effects of <s>rasa</s> etc. is fulfilled by the statement of <s>dravya</s>-effect through inference from <s>rasa</s>-effect, and likewise by the statement of <s>vikāra</s>-effect through <s>doṣa</s>-effect. // 3

children.text: iha tu vikṛtiviṣamasamavāyātmake dravye vikāre vā rasadoṣaprabhāvānumānena na dravyavikāraprabhāvānumānam astīti kṛtvā pṛthak pṛthagrasādiprabhāvatattvābhidhānapratijñānam iti na paunaruktyam // 4
children.translated_text: Here, however, in a substance whose nature is an irregular combination of modifications, or in a disease, the effect of <s>dravya</s> and <s>vikāra</s> cannot be inferred from the effect of <s>rasa</s> and <s>doṣa</s> alone — therefore, the separate promise to state the truth of the effects of <s>rasa</s> etc. individually [is made]. Thus there is no repetition. // 4

children.text: iha dravyāṇāṃ vīryaprabhāvavipākaprabhāvau ca dravyaprabhāve rasaprabhāve vāntarbhāvanīyau // 5
children.translated_text: Here, the potency-effect (<s>vīryaprabhāva</s>) and post-digestive-effect (<s>vipākaprabhāva</s>) of substances are to be subsumed under the effect of <s>dravya</s> or the effect of <s>rasa</s>. // 5

children.text: tatra yau rasānuguṇau vīryavipākaprabhāvau tau rase yau tu rasakramoktavīryavipākaviparītau vīryavipākau tau dravyaprabhāve boddhavyau // 6
children.translated_text: Among these, potency- and post-digestive-effects that are concordant with <s>rasa</s> are [subsumed] under <s>rasa</s>-effect; but potency and post-digestive-effect that are contrary to the potency and <s>vipāka</s> stated in the sequence of <s>rasa</s> should be understood as [falling under] <s>dravya</s>-effect. // 6

children.text: upadekṣyāma iti nikhilena tantreṇa rasādiprabhāvatattvaṃ pṛthag upadekṣyāma ityarthaḥ rasādiprabhāvaḥ prapañcena nikhile tantra eva vaktavyaḥ // 7]
children.translated_text: 'We shall teach' means: we shall teach the truth of <s>rasa</s>-effect etc. separately throughout the entire treatise — the meaning is that the effect of <s>rasa</s> etc. is to be stated in detail throughout the entire treatise. // 7]
Herein, this effect of <s>rasa</s> has been taught.
Now we shall teach the effect of <s>dravya</s> (substance).
Oil, ghee, and honey are substances for the pacification of <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> [respectively]. // <s>Car</s>_3,1.13
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Showing that this itself is a summary statement, he says 'Herein, this' etc. // 1

children.text: eṣa iti rasāḥ ṣaḍ ityādinā tattvamupadekṣyāmaḥ ityantena granthenokta ityarthaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'This' means what has been stated by the text beginning with 'The six <s>rasas</s>' and ending with 'we shall teach the truth' — this is the meaning. // 2
'Has been taught' means has been stated in summary. // 3

children.text: anye tu tatraiṣa rasaprabhāva uddiṣṭo bhavati iti paṭhanti // 4
children.translated_text: Others, however, read: 'Herein, this effect of <s>rasa</s> has been indicated (<s>uddiṣṭa</s>).' // 4

children.text: asmin pakṣe dravyadoṣavikāraprabhāvo 'pi 'tra uddiṣṭaḥ so 'pi rasadvārā tena rasasyaiva prapañcābhihitatvāt tasyaivābhidhānam upasaṃharati na dravyādīnāmiti jñeyam dravyaprabhāvamityādau punariti sāmānyena dravyaprabhāvakathanāt punaḥ śṛṅgagrāhikayā tailādidravyaprabhāvaṃ kathayiṣyāma ityarthaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: In this reading, the effect of <s>dravya</s>, <s>doṣa</s>, and <s>vikāra</s> too has been indicated here — but since they were stated through <s>rasa</s>, only <s>rasa</s> has been elaborately stated, and hence only its [statement] is concluded — not that of <s>dravya</s> etc., it should be known. In 'the effect of <s>dravya</s>' etc., because <s>dravya</s>-effect has been stated generally with the word 'again' (<s>punar</s>), we shall [now] state the <s>dravya</s>-effect of oil etc. specifically — this is the meaning. // 5
'For the purpose of pacification' means having pacification as their purpose. // 6]

children.text: tatra tailaṃ snehauṣṇyagauravopapannatvād vātaṃ jayati satatamabhyasyamānaṃ vāto hi raukṣyaśaityalāghavopapanno viruddhaguṇo bhavati viruddhaguṇasaṃnipāte hi bhūyasālpam avajīyate tasmāttailaṃ vātaṃ jayati satatam abhyasyamānam /
children.translated_text: Among these, oil conquers <s>vāta</s> when used continuously, because it possesses unctuousness, heat, and heaviness. For <s>vāta</s>, being possessed of dryness, coldness, and lightness, has opposite qualities. When opposite qualities meet, the lesser is overcome by the greater. Therefore oil conquers <s>vāta</s> when used continuously.

children.text: sarpiḥ khalvevameva pittaṃ jayati mādhuryācchaityānmandatvācca pittaṃ hy amadhuram uṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Ghee likewise conquers <s>pitta</s> — because of its sweetness, coolness, and mildness. For <s>pitta</s> is non-sweet, hot, and sharp.

children.text: madhu ca śleṣmāṇaṃ jayati raukṣyāt taikṣṇyāt kaṣāyatvāc ca śleṣmā hi snigdho mando madhuraśca /
children.translated_text: And honey conquers <s>kapha</s> — because of its dryness, sharpness, and astringency. For <s>kapha</s> is unctuous, mild, and sweet.

children.text: yac cānyadapi kiṃcid dravyamevaṃ vātapittakaphebhyo guṇato viparītaṃ syāt tac caitāñjayaty abhyasyamānam // Car_3,1.14
children.translated_text: And whatever other substance also has qualities opposite to <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> — that too conquers them when used continuously. // <s>Car</s>_3,1.14
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'Used continuously' means employed without interruption. // 1
'Of opposite qualities' means having qualities opposite to those of oil. // 2
'When opposite qualities meet' means when there is a conjunction of two [things] with opposite qualities. // 3

children.text: nanu viruddhaguṇayor madhye bhūyasālpaṃ jīyate tat kathaṃ tailaṃ vātaṃ jayati na hy asya vātaṃ prati bhūyastvaṃ yuktamityāha satatam abhyasyamānam iti // 4
children.translated_text: Objection: Among two [things] with opposite qualities, the lesser is overcome by the greater — then how does oil conquer <s>vāta</s>? For it is not reasonable that it [oil] is greater than <s>vāta</s>. He answers this with 'used continuously.' // 4

children.text: satatopayogena hi tailaṃ vātād adhikaṃ bhavati tena vātaṃ jayatītyarthaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: Through continuous use, oil becomes greater than <s>vāta</s>, and thereby conquers <s>vāta</s> — this is the meaning. // 5

children.text: sarpiḥ khalvevameveti sarpirapi satatam abhyasyamānam ityarthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: 'Ghee likewise' means ghee too [conquers pitta] when used continuously — this is the meaning. // 6
'Non-sweet' means having pungent taste, which is opposite to sweet through dryness, lightness, non-aphrodisiac nature, etc. — this is the meaning. // 7

children.text: iha ca prabhāvaśabdena sāmānyena dravyaśaktir ucyate nācintyaśaktiḥ tena tailādīnāṃ snehauṣṇyādiguṇādapi vātādiśamanaṃ dravyaprabhāvādeva bhavati // 8
children.translated_text: Here, by the word '<s>prabhāva</s>' (effect), the power of a substance is spoken of in general, not the inconceivable power [alone]. Therefore, the pacification of <s>vāta</s> etc. by the qualities of unctuousness, heat, etc. in oil and the rest is indeed due to <s>dravya</s>-effect. // 8

children.text: sarpiṣi ca yadyapi madhuro rasaḥ pittapraśame vyāpriyate tathāpi mādhuryaśaityamandatvaiḥ pittaśamanaṃ sarpiḥkāryameva tena dravyaprabhāva eva vācyaḥ // 9
children.translated_text: In ghee, although the sweet taste is active in <s>pitta</s>-pacification, nevertheless the pacification of <s>pitta</s> through sweetness, coolness, and mildness is indeed a function of ghee [as a substance]. Therefore it should be called <s>dravya</s>-effect. // 9

children.text: yadā tu rasadvārā kāryaṃ dravyasya cintyate tadā rasaprabhāva iti vyapadeśo bhavati // 10
children.translated_text: When, however, the action of a substance is considered through the medium of <s>rasa</s>, then the designation '<s>rasa</s>-effect' applies. // 10

children.text: evaṃ kaṣāyānurase madhuni ca samādhānaṃ vācyam // 11
children.translated_text: The same explanation should be stated for honey, which has astringent as its secondary taste. // 11

children.text: anye tu bruvate yattailādīnāṃ vātādiśamanatvaṃ pratyacintya eva prabhāvo 'yamucyate tatra ca tailavātayor viruddhaguṇayor melake tailameva vātaṃ jayati na tu vātas tailam iti tailasyācintyaprabhāvaḥ evaṃ sarpirmadhunor api pittaśleṣmaharaṇe prabhāvājjñeye // 12
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: the pacification of <s>vāta</s> etc. by oil and the rest is indeed an inconceivable effect (<s>prabhāva</s>). And in this [view], when oil and <s>vāta</s> — having opposite qualities — meet, oil alone conquers <s>vāta</s>, but <s>vāta</s> does not [conquer] oil — this is the inconceivable effect of oil. Likewise for ghee and honey in their pacification of <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s> — it should be known as due to [their] <s>prabhāva</s>. // 12

children.text: etaccānye necchanti yatas tailādīnāṃ satatam abhyasyamānamiti padenādhikyameva vātādijayakāraṇamuktaṃ tathā yaccānyad api kiṃcid dravyam ityādigranthena dravyācintyaprabhāvaṃ parityajya sāmānyena guṇavaiparītyam evābhyāsād vātādijayahetur ucyate // 13]
children.translated_text: Others do not accept this, because the word 'used continuously' states that preponderance alone is the cause of conquering <s>vāta</s> etc. Likewise, by the text 'and whatever other substance' etc., rejecting the inconceivable effect of specific substances, the opposition of qualities in general, through habitual use, is stated as the cause of conquering <s>vāta</s> etc. // 13]

children.text: atha khalu trīṇi dravyāṇi nātyupayuñjītādhikam anyebhyo dravyebhyaḥ tadyathāpippalī kṣāraḥ lavaṇamiti // Car_3,1.15
children.translated_text: Now then, three substances should not be used in excess more than other substances — namely, <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>kṣāra</s> (alkali), and <s>lavaṇa</s> (salt). // <s>Car</s>_3,1.15
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Having stated a substance to be used habitually as an example of [<s>dravya</s>-]effect, he states what should not be used habitually with 'Now then' etc. // 1

children.text: adhikamanyebhya iti vacanādanyadapi citrakabhallātakādyevaṃjātīyaṃ nātyupayoktavyaṃ pippalyādidravyaṃ tv anyebhyo 'pyadhikam atyupayoge varjanīyamiti darśayati // 2]
children.translated_text: By the expression 'more than other [substances],' it is shown that other things too — <s>citraka</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and the like — should not be used excessively; but <s>pippalī</s> etc. are to be avoided in excess even more than those others. // 2]

children.text: pippalyo hi kaṭukāḥ satyo madhuravipākā gurvyo nātyarthaṃ snigdhoṣṇāḥ prakledinyo bheṣajābhimatāś ca tāḥ sadyaḥ śubhāśubhakāriṇyo bhavanti āpātabhadrāḥ prayogasamasādguṇyāt doṣasaṃcayānubandhāḥ satatam upayujyamānā hi guruprakleditvācchleṣmāṇam utkleśayanti auṣṇyāt pittaṃ na ca vātapraśamanāyopakalpante 'lpasnehoṣṇabhāvāt yogavāhinyastu khalu bhavanti tasmātpippalīr nātyupayuñjīta // Car_3,1.16
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalīs</s> (long peppers) are pungent in taste yet sweet in post-digestive effect (<s>vipāka</s>), heavy, not excessively unctuous-hot, moistening, and valued as medicine. They produce both good and bad effects immediately — [they are] 'attractive at first contact' (<s>āpātabhadra</s>), excellent in moderate use, [but] accompanied by accumulation of <s>doṣas</s> [when overused]. For when used continuously, they disturb <s>kapha</s> because of heaviness and moistening quality, [and] <s>pitta</s> because of heat — and they do not serve for the pacification of <s>vāta</s> because of their insufficient unctuousness and heat. They are, however, <s>yogavāhinī</s> (carriers of [other therapeutic] combinations). Therefore one should not use <s>pippalīs</s> excessively. // <s>Car</s>_3,1.16
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: kaṭukāḥ satyo madhuravipākāḥ ityādi pippalīguṇakathanam anabhyāsaprayoge doṣavaiparītyena doṣapraśamanopadarśanārthaṃ tathā atyabhyāse guruprakleditvācchleṣmāṇam utkleśayanti ityādigranthavaktavyadoṣakaraṇayogyatopadarśanārthaṃ ca // 1
children.translated_text: The statement of the qualities of <s>pippalī</s> — 'pungent in taste, sweet in <s>vipāka</s>' etc. — is for showing that in non-habitual use, [<s>pippalī</s>] pacifies <s>doṣas</s> by the opposition of qualities; and for showing its capacity to produce the faults stated in the text 'when used continuously, they disturb <s>kapha</s> because of heaviness and moistening' etc. // 1
The break is: 'valued as medicine, and immediately.' // 2
'Immediately' means when not used habitually. // 3

children.text: śubhāśubhakāriṇyo bhavantīti sadyaḥ śubhakāriṇyaḥ atyabhyāsaprayoge tv aśubhakāriṇyaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: 'Produce both good and bad effects' means: they produce good effects immediately [in non-habitual use], but produce bad effects when used excessively habitually. // 4
He shows this very production of good and bad effects with 'attractive at first contact' etc. // 5

children.text: prayogasamasādguṇyād iti samasya prayogasya sadguṇatvāt same 'lpakāle alpamātre ca pippalyādiprayoge sadguṇā bhavantītyarthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: 'Because of the excellence of moderate use' means: because moderate use — that is, use for a short time and in small quantity — of <s>pippalī</s> etc. is excellent, they are beneficial — this is the meaning. // 6
'Those whose excessive use is accompanied by accumulation of <s>doṣas</s>' — [the compound means:] those for which excessive use brings about accumulation of <s>doṣas</s>. // 7
He elaborates this very 'accompaniment by <s>doṣa</s>-accumulation' with 'when used continuously' etc. // 8

children.text: pippalīdharmakathanaprastāvād guṇāntaram āha yogavāhinyas tv ityādi // 9
children.translated_text: In the context of stating the properties of <s>pippalī</s>, he states another quality with 'but they are <s>yogavāhinī</s>' etc. // 9

children.text: yogavāhitvena kaṭukānāmapi pippalīnāṃ vṛṣyaprayogeṣu yogaḥ tathā jvaragulmakuṣṭhaharādiprayogeṣu jvarādīn hanti pippalī // 10
children.translated_text: By virtue of being <s>yogavāhinī</s>, even pungent <s>pippalīs</s> are employed in aphrodisiac preparations; likewise in treatments for fever, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), etc. — <s>pippalī</s> destroys fevers and the like. // 10
And this prohibition against excessive use of <s>pippalī</s> should be understood as excluding the exceptions (<s>apavāda</s>). // 11

children.text: tena pippalīrasāyanaprayogas tathā gulmādiṣu ca pippalīvardhamānakaprayogo na virodham āvahati // 12
children.translated_text: Therefore, the use of <s>pippalī</s> in rejuvenation preparations (<s>rasāyana</s>), and the use of <s>pippalī</s> in gradually increasing doses for <s>gulma</s> and the like, does not entail contradiction. // 12

children.text: ukte hi viṣaye yathoktavidhānena nirdoṣā eva pippalya iti ṛṣivacanād unnīyate /
children.translated_text: For it is inferred from the words of the sages that in the stated contexts, <s>pippalīs</s> used according to the prescribed method are indeed harmless.

children.text: anye tu annasaṃskaraṇe pippalyādīnām atiprayogo na tu svātantryeṇeti bruvate /
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: the prohibition of excessive use of <s>pippalī</s> etc. [applies] in seasoning food, but not [when used] independently [as medicine].

children.text: satatamupayujyamānā iti atimātratvena tathā satataprayogeṇa ceti jñeyam // 13]
children.translated_text: 'Used continuously' should be understood as [meaning both] in excessive quantity and through continuous use. // 13]

children.text: kṣāraḥ punar auṣṇyataikṣṇyalāghavopapannaḥ kledayatyādau paścādviśoṣayati sa pacanadahanabhedanārtham upayujyate so 'tiprayujyamānaḥ keśākṣihṛdayapuṃstvopaghātakaraḥ saṃpadyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣāra</s> (alkali), possessing heat, sharpness, and lightness, moistens initially and afterwards desiccates. It is employed for the purposes of digestion, burning, and splitting. When used excessively, it produces damage to hair, eyes, heart, and virility.

children.text: ye hy enaṃ grāmanagaranigamajanapadāḥ satatam upayuñjate ta āndhyaṣāṇḍhyakhālityapālityabhājo hṛdayāpakartinaśca bhavanti tadyathā prācyāś cīnāśca tasmātkṣāraṃ nātyupayuñjīta // Car_3,1.17
children.translated_text: Those villages, cities, market-towns, and regions that use it continuously become afflicted with blindness, eunuchism, baldness, and premature graying, and suffer heart-pain — for example, the eastern peoples and the <s>Cīnas</s> (Chinese). Therefore one should not use <s>kṣāra</s> excessively. // <s>Car</s>_3,1.17
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'Suffering heart-pain' means having a cutting type of pain in the heart. // 1]

children.text:
lavaṇaṃ punarauṣṇyataikṣṇyopapannam anatiguru anatisnigdham upakledi visraṃsanasamartham annadravyarucikaram āpātabhadraṃ prayogasamasādguṇyāt doṣasaṃcayānubandhaṃ tad rocanapācanopakledanavisraṃsanārtham upayujyate /
tad atyartham upayujyamānaṃ glāniśaithilyadaurbalyābhinirvṛttikaraṃ śarīrasya bhavati /
ye hy enad grāmanagaranigamajanapadāḥ satatamupayuñjate te bhūyiṣṭhaṃ glāsnavaḥ śithilamāṃsaśoṇitā aparikleśasahāś ca bhavanti /
children.translated_text: <s>Lavaṇa</s> (salt), possessing heat and sharpness, neither excessively heavy nor excessively unctuous, moistening, capable of causing loosening [of tissues], producing relish for food-substances — [it is] 'attractive at first contact,' excellent in moderate use, [but] accompanied by accumulation of <s>doṣas</s> [when overused]. It is employed for the purposes of appetizing, digesting, moistening, and loosening. When used excessively, it produces lassitude, flaccidity, and weakness in the body. Those villages, cities, market-towns, and regions that use it continuously become mostly languid, with flaccid flesh and blood, and unable to endure exertion.

children.text: tadyathā vāhlīkasaurāṣṭrikasaindhavasauvīrakāḥ te hi payasāpi saha lavaṇam aśnanti /
children.translated_text: For example, the <s>Vāhlīkas</s>, the people of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>, the <s>Saindhavas</s>, and the <s>Sauvīras</s> — for they eat salt even with milk.

children.text: ye 'pīha bhūmer atyūṣarā deśāsteṣvoṣadhivīrudvanaspativānaspatyā na jāyante'lpatejaso vā bhavanti lavaṇopahatatvāt /
children.translated_text: And those lands here that are excessively saline — in them, herbs, shrubs, fruit-bearing trees, and flower-bearing trees either do not grow or have little vitality, because they are damaged by salt.
Therefore one should not use salt excessively.

children.text: ye hy atilavaṇasātmyāḥ puruṣāsteṣāmapi khālityapālityāni valayaścākāle bhavanti // Car_3,1.18
children.translated_text: Those persons who are habituated to excessive salt — even they develop baldness, premature graying, and wrinkles before their time. // <s>Car</s>_3,1.18
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'Lassitude' (<s>glāni</s>) means wasting of flesh, or loss of thrilling sensation. // 1

children.text: na kevalaṃ lavaṇātiyogaḥ śarīropaghātakaraḥ kiṃtu bhūmer apyupaghātakara ityāha ye 'pīhetyādi // 2
children.translated_text: Not only is excessive use of salt harmful to the body, but it is harmful even to the earth — he states this with 'And those [lands] here' etc. // 2
'Saline' (<s>ūṣara</s>) means having salt as predominant. // 3

children.text: lavaṇaṃ nātyupayuñjīteti nātimātraṃ lavaṇaṃ satatam upayuñjīta annadravyasaṃskārakaṃ tu stokamātram abhyāsenāpyupayojanīyam eva // 4
children.translated_text: 'One should not use salt excessively' means one should not use excessive quantities of salt continuously. However, a small amount as a seasoning for food-substances should be used even habitually. // 4

children.text: vāhlīkādivyatirikte 'pi deśe ye 'tilavaṇam aśnanti teṣāmapi doṣānāha ye hītyādi // 5
children.translated_text: He states the faults even for those in regions other than <s>Vāhlīka</s> etc. who consume excessive salt, with 'Those who' etc. // 5

children.text: etena cānyatrāpi deśe 'timātralavaṇasātmyānāṃ lavaṇātyupayogakṛta eva śaithilyādidoṣa unnīyate na deśasvabhāvakṛtaḥ // 6]
children.translated_text: And by this it is inferred that in other regions too, the faults of flaccidity etc. in those habituated to excessive salt are caused by excessive use of salt alone, not by the nature of the region. // 6]
Therefore, for them, gradual withdrawal from that habituation is beneficial.

children.text: sātmyamapi hi krameṇopanivartyamānam adoṣam alpadoṣaṃ vā bhavati // Car_3,1.19
children.translated_text: For even a habituation, when gradually discontinued, produces either no harm or very little harm. // <s>Car</s>_3,1.19
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'For them' means for those habituated to excessive <s>kṣāra</s> and excessive <s>lavaṇa</s>. // 1

children.text: tatsātmyata iti atimātrakṣārād atimātralavaṇāc ca sātmyāt // 2
children.translated_text: 'From that habituation' means from the habituation to excessive <s>kṣāra</s> and excessive <s>lavaṇa</s>. // 2
'Gradually' means not suddenly — [but rather] by the method of abandoning habituation stated in [the section on] what should be restrained. // 3
And here, by the word 'habituation' (<s>sātmya</s>), habituation through familiarity (<s>okasātmya</s>) is intended. // 4

children.text: alpadoṣam adoṣaṃ veti pakṣadvaye 'tyarthasātmyam alpadoṣaṃ bhavati anyattvadoṣam iti vyavasthā // 5]
children.translated_text: In the two alternatives — 'of little harm' or 'of no harm' — excessive habituation is of little harm, and the other is [simply] the harm [of the substance itself] — this is the determination. // 5]

children.text: sātmyaṃ nāma tad yad ātmanyupaśete sātmyārtho hy upaśayārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Sātmya</s> (habituation) is that which is agreeable to oneself; for the meaning of <s>sātmya</s> is the meaning of <s>upaśaya</s> (that which is beneficial).

children.text: tattrividhaṃ pravarāvaramadhyavibhāgena saptavidhaṃ tu rasaikaikatvena sarvarasopayogācca /
children.translated_text: It is of three kinds — by the division into best, worst, and middling — and of seven kinds — by [habituation to] each single taste and by the use of all tastes.

children.text: tatra sarvarasaṃ pravaram avaramekarasaṃ madhyaṃ tu pravarāvaramadhyastham /
children.translated_text: Among these, [habituation to] all tastes is the best; [habituation to] a single taste is the worst; and the middling is between the best and the worst.

children.text: tatrāvaramadhyābhyāṃ sātmyābhyāṃ krameṇaiva pravaram upapādayet sātmyam /
children.translated_text: One should gradually bring a person from the worst and middling habituations to the best habituation.

children.text: sarvarasamapi ca sātmyam upapannaḥ prakṛtyādyupayoktraṣṭamāni sarvāṇyāhāravidhiviśeṣāyatanānyabhisamīkṣya hitam evānurudhyeta // Car_3,1.20
children.translated_text: And even one who has attained the habituation to all tastes should, having examined all eight factors of dietary regimen — beginning with natural quality (<s>prakṛti</s>) and ending with the consumer (<s>upayoktṛ</s>) — follow only what is beneficial. // Car_3,1.20
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'<s>Sātmya</s>' — the meaning is: <s>oka-sātmya</s> (habituation through repeated use). // 1
'From <s>oka</s>' means from habitual practice. // 2
'The meaning of <s>upaśaya</s>' means that which is denoted by the word <s>upaśaya</s>. // 3
'That' refers to <s>oka-sātmya</s>. // 4
'Of three kinds' — by the division into best, worst, and middling. // 5

children.text: saptavidhaṃ tu ekaikarasena ṣaṭ saṃsṛṣṭarasopayogāccaikam evaṃ saptavidham // 6
children.translated_text: 'Of seven kinds' — six by [habituation to] each single taste, and one by the use of mixed tastes — thus seven. // 6
By the word 'mixed' (<s>saṃsṛṣṭa</s>), [combinations of] two tastes etc. up to six tastes are included. // 7
'Between the best and the worst' — [habituation to] two tastes etc. up to five tastes. // 8
'The person characterized by the worst and middling [habituations]' — // 9
'Best' means [habituation to] all tastes. // 10
'Should bring about the habituation' means should practice it. // 11
'Gradually' means by the sequence of practice as stated. // 12

children.text: upapāditasarvarasasātmyenāpi cāhāraḥ praśastaprakṛtyādisampanna eva kartavya ityāha sarvarasam ityādi // 13
children.translated_text: Even one who has attained habituation to all tastes should still take food that is endowed with praiseworthy natural constitution etc. — he states this with 'all tastes' etc. // 13
'Having examined' means having considered with respect to what is wholesome and unwholesome. // 14

children.text: hitameveti padena yadeva prakṛtyādinā hitaṃ tad evānurudhyeta sevetetyarthaḥ // 15]
children.translated_text: By the phrase 'only what is beneficial' — whatever is beneficial according to natural constitution etc., one should follow that alone, i.e., practice it — this is the meaning. // 15]

children.text: tatra khalvimānyaṣṭāv āhāravidhiviśeṣāyatanāni bhavanti tadyathā prakṛtikaraṇasaṃyogarāśideśakālopayogasaṃsthopayoktraṣṭamāni bhavanti // Car_3,1.21
children.translated_text: Now, there are these eight factors of dietary regimen (<s>āhāravidhiviśeṣāyatana</s>), namely: natural quality (<s>prakṛti</s>), preparation (<s>karaṇa</s>), combination (<s>saṃyoga</s>), quantity (<s>rāśi</s>), place (<s>deśa</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), rules of intake (<s>upayogasaṃsthā</s>), and the consumer (<s>upayoktṛ</s>) as the eighth. // Car_3,1.21
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: āhārasya vidhiḥ prakāro vidhānaṃ vā ityāhāravidhiḥ tasya viśeṣo hitatvamahitatvaṃ ca tasyāyatanāni hetūn ity āhāravidhiviśeṣāyatanāni // 1
children.translated_text: 'The method of food' — i.e., the manner or mode of food — is <s>āhāra-vidhi</s>. Its 'specifics' (<s>viśeṣa</s>) are its wholesomeness and unwholesomeness. The 'bases' (<s>āyatana</s>) of those are the causes — thus '<s>āhāra-vidhi-viśeṣa-āyatanāni</s>' (the bases of the specifics of dietary method). // 1
The meaning is: the wholesomeness and unwholesomeness of the dietary method are caused by natural quality (<s>prakṛti</s>) etc. // 2
'Those of which the consumer is the eighth' — [these are called] <s>upayoktr-aṣṭama</s> (having the consumer as eighth). // 3]

children.text: tatra prakṛtir ucyate svabhāvo yaḥ sa punarāhārauṣadhadravyāṇāṃ svābhāviko gurvādiguṇayogaḥ tadyathā maṣamudgayoḥ śūkaraiṇayośca /
children.translated_text: There, 'natural quality' (<s>prakṛti</s>) refers to the inherent nature — which is the natural connection with qualities such as heaviness etc. belonging to food and medicinal substances. For example, [the natural qualities of] black gram (<s>māṣa</s>) and green gram (<s>mudga</s>), or of pork and deer meat.
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He elaborates on [the factors] beginning with natural quality with 'there' etc. // 1
'Inherent' means not produced by preparation etc. // 2

children.text: māṣamudgayor iti prakṛtyā māṣe gurutvaṃ mudge ca laghutvaṃ śūkare gurutvam eṇe ca laghutvam // 3]
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>Māṣa</s> and <s>Mudga</s>' — by nature, <s>Māṣa</s> (black gram) is heavy and <s>Mudga</s> (green gram) is light; pork is heavy and deer meat (<s>eṇa</s>) is light. // 3]
'Preparation' (<s>karaṇa</s>) is the processing of naturally-constituted substances.
For <s>saṃskāra</s> (processing) is defined as the imparting of different qualities.

Those qualities are imparted through contact with water, fire, cleansing, churning, place, time, infusion (<s>vāsana</s>), trituration (<s>bhāvana</s>), etc., and through passage of time, vessel, etc.
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: dravyāṇām iti vaktavye svābhāvikānām iti yat karoti tenotpattikāle janakabhūtaiḥ svaguṇāropaṇaṃ saṃskārastūtpannasyaiva toyādinā guṇāntarādhānamiti darśayati // 1
children.translated_text: Where he should have said [simply] 'of substances,' by saying 'of naturally-constituted [substances]' he shows that at the time of origin, the imputation of innate qualities by the generative [causes] is [the natural quality], whereas processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is the imparting of different qualities to an already-produced [substance] by water etc. // 1

children.text: tacca prākṛtaguṇopamardenaiva kriyate yathā toyāgnisaṃnikarṣaśaucais taṇḍulasthaṃ gauravam upahatya lāghavam anne kriyate // 2
children.translated_text: And this [processing] is done precisely by destroying the natural qualities — just as by contact with water, fire, and cleansing, the heaviness present in rice grains is destroyed and lightness is produced in the cooked food. // 2

children.text: yaduktaṃ sudhautaḥ prasrutaḥ svinnaḥ saṃtaptaś caudano laghuḥ // 3
children.translated_text: As it has been stated: 'Well-washed, drained, steamed, and heated rice (<s>odana</s>) is light.' // 3
Similarly, even the lightness of naturally light <s>Raktaśāli</s> etc. is increased by contact with fire etc. // 4

children.text: manthanādguṇādhānaṃ yathā śothakṛd dadhi śothaghnaṃ sasnehamapi manthanāt iti // 5
children.translated_text: The imparting of qualities by churning — as in: 'Yogurt causes swelling, [but] even with its unctuousness, through churning [i.e., as buttermilk] it alleviates swelling.' // 5

children.text: deśena yathā bhasmarāśer adhaḥ sthāpayet ityādau // 6
children.translated_text: By place — as in 'one should place [it] beneath a heap of ashes' etc. // 6
The imparting of qualities by infusion (<s>vāsana</s>) — as when water acquires fragrance through infusion with lotus (<s>utpala</s>) etc. // 7

children.text: bhāvanayā ca svarasādikṛtayā sthitasyaivāmalakāder guṇasyotkarṣo bhavati // 8
children.translated_text: And by trituration (<s>bhāvana</s>) with expressed juice etc., the quality of an already existing [substance] like <s>Āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) etc. is enhanced. // 8
By passage of time — as in 'one should drink [it] after a fortnight when the <s>rasa</s> (fermented juice) has developed' etc. // 9

children.text: bhājanena yathā traiphalenāyasīṃ pātrīṃ kalkenālepayet ityādau // 10
children.translated_text: By vessel — as in 'one should coat an iron vessel with the paste of <s>Triphala</s>' etc. // 10
By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), grinding (<s>peṣaṇa</s>), consecration with mantras (<s>abhimantraṇa</s>), etc. are included. // 11

children.text: nanu saṃskārādheyena guṇena kathaṃ svābhāvikaguṇanāśaḥ kriyate yataḥ svabhāvo niṣpratikriyaḥ ityuktaṃ yadi hi saṃskāreṇa svābhāvikagurutvaṃ pratikriyate tadā svabhāvo niṣpratikriyaḥ iti kathaṃ brūmaḥ svabhāvo niṣpratikriyaḥ iti svabhāvo bhāvānām utpattau nānyathā kriyate // 12
children.translated_text: Objection: How can a quality imparted by processing destroy the natural quality? For it has been stated that 'nature is irremediable' (<s>svabhāvo niṣpratikriyaḥ</s>). If natural heaviness is counteracted by processing, then how can we say 'nature is irremediable'? [Reply:] 'Nature is irremediable' means that the nature of things at the time of their origination cannot be made otherwise. // 12

children.text: tena jātipratibaddhaṃ māṣādīnāṃ gurutvaṃ na tajjātau sphoṭayituṃ pāryate saṃskāreṇa tu tadanyathākaraṇamanumatameva dṛṣṭatvāt // 13
children.translated_text: Thus, the heaviness of <s>Māṣa</s> etc. that is bound to the species cannot be eliminated within that species by processing. But the alteration of it [in a particular instance] by processing is indeed accepted, since it is observed. // 13

children.text: kaścit tu guṇo dravyāṇāṃ saṃskārādināpi nānyathā kriyate yathā vahner auṣṇyaṃ vāyoścalatvaṃ tailasya sneha ityādi // 14
children.translated_text: Some quality of substances, however, cannot be made otherwise even by processing etc. — such as the heat of fire, the mobility of wind, the unctuousness of oil, etc. // 14
For these are qualities that exist as long as the substance exists. // 15
But heaviness and the like — since their departure is observed even in old grain etc. — do not exist as long as the substance exists. // 16

children.text: uktaṃ hi guṇo dravyavināśād vā vināśam upagacchati // 17
children.translated_text: For it has been stated: 'A quality perishes either from the destruction of the substance, // 17
or from the imposition of a different quality.' // 18

children.text: yatra tu saṃskāreṇa vrīherlājalakṣaṇaṃ dravyāntarameva janyate tatra guṇāntarotpādaḥ suṣṭhveva // 19]
children.translated_text: But where processing produces an entirely different substance — as when rice becomes puffed rice (<s>lāja</s>) — there the production of different qualities is quite proper. // 19]

children.text: saṃyogaḥ punar dvayor bahūnāṃ vā dravyāṇāṃ saṃhatībhāvaḥ sa viśeṣamārabhate yaṃ punar naikaikaśo dravyāṇyārabhante tad yathā madhusarpiṣoḥ madhumatsyapayasāṃ ca saṃyogaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Combination' (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the union of two or more substances. It initiates a special [effect] that the individual substances do not initiate singly. For example, the combination of honey and ghee, or the combination of honey, fish, and milk.
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states combination with 'combination' etc. // 1

children.text: sa viśeṣamārabhata iti saṃyujyamānadravyaikadeśe 'dṛṣṭaṃ kāryam ārabhata ityarthaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'It initiates a special [effect]' — meaning it initiates an unseen effect in some portion of the combined substances. // 2

children.text: yaṃ naikaikaśa iti yaṃ viśeṣaṃ pratyekasaṃyujyamānāni dravyāṇi nārabhanta ityarthaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: 'Which [effect] the individual [substances] do not [initiate] singly' — meaning which special [effect] the individually combined substances do not initiate. // 3

children.text: madhusarpiṣī hi pratyekamamārake milite tu mārake bhavataḥ kṣīramatsyādisaṃyogaśca kuṣṭhādikaro bhavati // 4
children.translated_text: For honey and ghee individually are not lethal, but when combined [in equal parts] they become lethal. And the combination of milk, fish, etc. produces skin diseases (<s>kuṣṭha</s>) etc. // 4

children.text: saṃyogas tv iha prādhānyenaivopalabhyamānadravyamelako vivakṣitas tena bhāvanādiṣvapi yadyapi saṃyogo 'sti tathāpi tatra bhāvanādravyāṇāṃ prādhānyenānupalabdher na saṃyogena grahaṇam // 5]
children.translated_text: Here, 'combination' is intended as the mixing of substances that are primarily perceptible. Therefore, even though there is combination in trituration (<s>bhāvana</s>) etc., since the trituration-substances are not primarily perceptible [in the result], they are not included under 'combination.' // 5]
'Quantity' (<s>rāśi</s>) consists of the total aggregate and the individual component [measures], for the purpose of determining the effects of correct and incorrect amounts.

children.text: tatra sarvasyāhārasya pramāṇagrahaṇam ekapiṇḍena sarvagrahaḥ parigrahaḥ punaḥ pramāṇagrahaṇam ekaikaśyenāhāradravyāṇām /
children.translated_text: There, the total aggregate (<s>sarvagraha</s>) is the measure of the entirety of food taken as a single mass; the individual component (<s>parigraha</s>) is the measure of each food substance individually.

children.text: sarvasya hi grahaḥ sarvagrahaḥ sarvataśca grahaḥ parigraha ucyate /
children.translated_text: For the measure of the whole is the 'total aggregate,' and the measure from all sides [i.e., of each component] is called the 'individual component.'
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'Quantity' (<s>rāśi</s>) means measure. // 1

children.text: mātrāmātraphalaviniścayārtha iti mātrāvadāhārauṣadhasya ca yat phalaṃ śubham amātrasya hīnasyātiriktasya vā yat phalam aśubham // 2
children.translated_text: 'For the purpose of determining the effects of correct and incorrect amounts' — the good result of food and medicine in correct amount, and the bad result of incorrect amount — whether deficient or excessive. // 2

children.text: yaduktaṃ tasya jñānārtham ucitapramāṇam anucitapramāṇaṃ ca rāśisaṃjñaṃ bhavati // 3
children.translated_text: As it has been stated: 'For the knowledge of that, the appropriate measure and the inappropriate measure are called <s>rāśi</s>.' // 3
He elaborates the total aggregate with 'there' etc. // 4
'Of the entirety' — the measure of the mixed [food] — rice, meat, soup, etc. — as a single mass. // 5
He elaborates the individual component with 'the individual component' etc. // 6

children.text: ekaikaśyeneti annasya kuḍavaḥ sūpasya palaṃ māṃsasya dvipalamityādyavayavamānapūrvakaṃ samudāyamānam // 7
children.translated_text: 'Individually' — the aggregate measure [determined] through the prior measure of each component — a <s>kuḍava</s> of rice, a <s>pala</s> of soup, two <s>palas</s> of meat, etc. // 7

children.text: sarvagrahe pratyavayavamānaniyamo nāsti tena yena kenacid āhāreṇa pratyekamaniyatamānena sampūrṇāhāramātrāniyamanaṃ sarvagrahaḥ // 8
children.translated_text: In the total aggregate, there is no restriction of the measure of each component; thus the total aggregate is the determination of the total food-amount through any food whatever, without a fixed measure for each [component]. // 8
He shows this very [point] through etymology with 'for [the measure] of the whole' etc. // 9
'From all sides' (<s>sarvataḥ</s>) means from the side of each individual component. // 10]

children.text: deśaḥ punaḥ sthānaṃ sa dravyāṇāmutpattipracārau deśasātmyaṃ cācaṣṭe /
children.translated_text: 'Place' (<s>deśa</s>) means location. It indicates the origin and habitat of substances, as well as regional habituation (<s>deśa-sātmya</s>).
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He elaborates place with 'place' etc. // 1
By the word 'location' (<s>sthāna</s>), he indicates the location of both the food substance and the consumer. // 2
'It indicates' — it serves as a means of knowing the qualities [acquired] through the origin, habitat, etc. of the substance. // 3

children.text: tatrotpattyā himavati jātaṃ guṇavadbhavati marau jātaṃ laghu bhavati ityādi // 4
children.translated_text: There, by origin — [a substance] produced in the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas) is of superior quality; produced in a desert, it is light — and so on. // 4

children.text: pracāreṇa laghu bhakṣyāṇāṃ prāṇināṃ tathā dhanvapracāriṇāṃ bahukriyāṇāṃ ca lāghavaṃ viparyaye ca gauravaṃ gṛhyate // 5
children.translated_text: By habitat — the lightness of animals that eat light food, that range in arid regions, and that are very active is understood; and heaviness in the contrary [case]. // 5

children.text: deśasāmyena ca deśaviparītaguṇaṃ sātmyaṃ gṛhyate yathānūpe uṣṇarūkṣādi dhanvani ca śītasnigdhādi // 6
children.translated_text: By regional suitability — habituation to qualities opposite to those of the region is understood — as in marshy regions (<s>anūpa</s>), [habituation to] hot and dry [substances] etc.; and in arid regions (<s>dhanvan</s>), [habituation to] cold and unctuous [substances] etc. // 6
But <s>oka-sātmya</s> (personal habituation) is included under the factor of the 'consumer' (<s>upayoktṛ</s>). // 7]

children.text: kālo hi nityagaś cāvasthikaśca tatrāvasthiko vikāramapekṣate nityagastu ṛtusātmyāpekṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Time' (<s>kāla</s>) is both perpetual (<s>nityaga</s>) and conditional (<s>āvasthika</s>). Among these, the conditional depends on the [current] disorder; while the perpetual depends on seasonal habituation (<s>ṛtu-sātmya</s>).
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'Perpetual' means of the form of the day-night [cycle] etc. // 1
'Conditional' means characterized by specific conditions such as being diseased, childhood, etc. // 2

children.text: vikāramapekṣata iti bālyādikṛtaṃ tu śleṣmavikāraṃ jvarādikaṃ cāhāraniyamārthamapekṣata ityarthaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: 'Depends on the disorder' — it depends on <s>Kapha</s>-disorders etc. caused by childhood etc. and on fevers etc. — for the purpose of dietary regulation. // 3
'Seasonal habituation' means it depends on the season — thus it 'depends on seasonal habituation.' // 4]
'Rules of intake' (<s>upayoga-saṃsthā</s>) means the regulation of use. It depends on the signs of digestion.
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: evamāhāropayogaḥ kartavya evaṃ na kartavya ityupayoganiyamaḥ sa jīrṇalakṣaṇāpekṣa iti prādhānyenoktaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: 'The regulation of use' — i.e., food should be taken in this manner and not in that manner — this regulation of use depends on the signs of digestion, as stated principally. // 1

children.text: teneha ajalpann ahasan nātidrutaṃ nātivilambitam ityādyupayoganiyamamapyapekṣata eva ajīrṇabhojane tu mahāṃstridoṣakopalakṣaṇo doṣo bhavatītyayam evodāhṛtaḥ // 2]
children.translated_text: By this, it also depends on the regulations of intake such as 'not talking, not laughing, not too fast, not too slow' etc. But since in eating before [complete] digestion, a great fault characterized by the aggravation of all three <s>doṣas</s> occurs, this [sign of digestion] alone is cited [as the primary rule]. // 2]
'The consumer' (<s>upayoktṛ</s>) is the one who takes that food — [the factor] upon which <s>oka-sātmya</s> (personal habituation) depends.
Thus the eight factors of dietary regimen have been explained. // Car_3,1.22
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: yadāyattam okasātmyam iti bhoktṛpuruṣāpekṣaṃ hy abhyāsasātmyaṃ bhavati kasyaciddhi kiṃcid evābhyāsāt pathyamapathyaṃ vā sātmyaṃ bhavati // 1]
children.translated_text: 'Upon which <s>oka-sātmya</s> depends' — for habituation through repeated use depends on the individual consumer. For something becomes habitual to someone — whether wholesome or unwholesome — [precisely] through that person's repeated use. // 1]

children.text: eṣāṃ viśeṣāḥ śubhāśubhaphalāḥ parasparopakārakā bhavanti tān bubhutseta buddhvā ca hitepsureva syāt na ca mohāt pramādādvā priyam ahitam asukhodarkam upasevyam āhārajātam anyadvā kiṃcit // Car_3,1.23
children.translated_text: The specific applications of these [eight factors] produce good and bad results, and they are mutually supportive. One should seek to understand them, and having understood them, one who desires well-being should follow only what is beneficial — and should never, through delusion or negligence, partake of food or anything else that is pleasant but unwholesome and of unpleasant consequence. // Car_3,1.23
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: eṣāmityādau śubhaphalā viśeṣā aśubhaphalāśca parasparopakārakā bhavantīti jñeyam // 1
children.translated_text: In 'of these' etc., the specific applications that produce good results and those that produce bad results are mutually supportive — this should be understood. // 1

children.text: tatra prakṛtyā lāghavādiḥ śubhaphalaḥ gurvādiś cāśubhaphalaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: There, lightness etc. by natural quality is a good-result-producing [application]; heaviness etc. is a bad-result-producing [one]. // 2
The specific application imparted by preparation etc. — if prescribed in the treatise, it is auspicious; if prohibited, it is inauspicious. // 3
Regional unsuitability, being produced in a condemned region, etc. is a bad-result [factor] for the substance. // 4

children.text: evaṃ kālāsātmyamaśubhaphalaṃ cājīrṇabhojanādi tathā okāsātmyaṃ cāśubhamaśubhaphalamiti jñeyaṃ viparītaṃ tu śubhaphalam // 5
children.translated_text: Similarly, seasonal unsuitability is a bad-result [factor]; and eating before [complete] digestion etc. — and personal unsuitability — are also bad-result-producing and inauspicious. The opposite [of each] produces good results. // 5

children.text: mohāditi ajñānāt pramādāditi jñātvāpi rāgād ityarthaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: 'Through delusion' means through ignorance; 'through negligence' means through desire even after knowing — this is the meaning. // 6
'Pleasant' means pleasing only in the immediate [moment]. // 7
'Unwholesome' — 'of unpleasant consequence' is the elaboration of this. // 8

children.text: asukhaṃ duḥkharūpam udarka uttarakālīnaṃ phalaṃ yasya sa tathā // 9
children.translated_text: That which has an unpleasant, painful result (<s>udarka</s>) in the future is called such. [9]
"Other" refers to medicine, regimen, etc. [10]

children.text: tatredamāhāravidhividhānamarogāṇāmāturāṇāṃ cāpi keṣāṃcit kāle prakṛtyaiva hitatamaṃ bhuñjānānāṃ bhavati uṣṇaṃ snigdhaṃ mātrāvat jīrṇe vīryāviruddham iṣṭe deśe iṣṭasarvopakaraṇaṃ nātidrutaṃ nātivilambitam ajalpan ahasan tanmanā bhuñjīta ātmānamabhisamīkṣya samyak // Car_3,1.24
children.translated_text: Here is the rule regarding the method of diet (<s>āhāravidhividhāna</s>), which is most beneficial for the healthy and also for certain patients who eat at the proper time and in accordance with their natural constitution: one should eat warm, unctuous, in proper quantity, after the previous meal has been digested, with non-antagonistic potencies, in a pleasant place, with all desired accessories, not too quickly, not too slowly, without talking, without laughing, with full attention, having properly considered oneself. [Car 3.1.24]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
In "here" etc., "this" refers to what is about to be stated. [1]

<s>Āhāravidhi</s> (dietary rule) is that by which one is regulated — namely the forthcoming instructions about warm, unctuous food, etc.; this is the <s>āhāravidhividhāna</s> (method of dietary rules). [2]

children.text: āturāṇāṃ ca keṣāṃciditi padena raktapittināṃ śītameva kapharogiṇāṃ rūkṣameva hitamityādiviparyayaṃ darśayati // 3
children.translated_text: By the phrase "and also for certain patients," he shows the exception: for those with <s>raktapitta</s> (bleeding disorders), only cold food is beneficial; for those with <s>kapha</s> diseases, only dry food is beneficial — and so on in reverse. [3]

children.text: keṣāṃcidbhuñjānānām idam āhāravidhividhānaṃ hitatamaṃ bhavatīti yojanā // 4
children.translated_text: The construction is: this method of dietary rules is most beneficial for certain people who eat thus. [4]

children.text: prakṛtyaiveti svabhāvenaiva hitatamaṃ hitatamam ityuktaṃ tena yat prakṛtyā hitaṃ tat kadācideva kaṃcideva puruṣam āsādyāhitaṃ bhavati tacca kādācitkatvād anādṛtaṃ tena prāyikatvādenaṃ hitatamaṃ vakṣyāma iti bhāvaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: "By nature" means by its own inherent character it is most beneficial. By saying "most beneficial," he implies that what is naturally beneficial may occasionally become harmful for a particular person under particular circumstances; but since this is only occasional, it is disregarded. Therefore, the sense is: we shall declare this as most beneficial on the basis of general applicability. [5]
In "warm" etc., the word "properly" (<s>samyak</s>) should be read as a separate clause. [6]

children.text: tasya sādguṇyam upadekṣyāma uṣṇam aśnīyād uṣṇaṃ hi bhujyamānaṃ svadate bhuktaṃ cāgnim audaryam udīrayati kṣipraṃ jarāṃ gacchati vātam anulomayati śleṣmāṇaṃ ca parihrāsayati tasmāduṣṇam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: We shall explain the excellence of these qualities. One should eat warm food, for warm food when being eaten is relishing, and once eaten it stimulates the digestive fire (<s>agni</s>) in the stomach, is quickly digested, propels <s>Vāta</s> downward, and diminishes <s>Śleṣman</s> (Kapha). Therefore one should eat warm food.

children.text: snigdhamaśnīyāt snigdhaṃ hi bhujyamānaṃ svadate bhuktaṃ cānudīrṇam agnim udīrayati kṣipraṃ jarāṃ gacchati vātamanulomayati śarīramupacinoti dṛḍhīkarotīndriyāṇi balābhivṛddhim upajanayati varṇaprasādaṃ cābhinirvartayati tasmāt snigdhamaśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should eat unctuous food, for unctuous food when being eaten is relishing, and once eaten it stimulates the digestive fire without disturbing it, is quickly digested, propels <s>Vāta</s> downward, nourishes the body, strengthens it, fortifies the sense organs, generates increase of strength, and produces clarity of complexion. Therefore one should eat unctuous food.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
"Of that" means of food possessing the qualities of warmth, unctuousness, etc. [1]
<s>Sādguṇya</s> means the state of possessing excellent qualities. [2]
"Diminishes" (<s>parihrāsayati</s>) means it breaks up the accumulated mass. [3]

children.text: mātrāvadaśnīyāt mātrāvaddhi bhuktaṃ vātapittakaphān apīḍayad āyur eva vivardhayati kevalaṃ sukhaṃ gudam anuparyeti na coṣmāṇamupahanti avyathaṃ ca paripākameti tasmānmātrāvad aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should eat in proper quantity, for food eaten in proper quantity does not aggravate <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, or <s>Kapha</s>, but rather promotes longevity alone; it passes comfortably through the rectum, does not impair the digestive fire, and is digested without distress. Therefore one should eat in proper quantity.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: mātrāvaditi praśaṃsāyāṃ matup tena praśastamātram ityarthaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: <s>Mātrāvat</s> — the possessive suffix -mat is used in the sense of praise, so the meaning is "having a commendable quantity." [1]

children.text: apīḍayaditi anatimātratvena svasthānasthitaṃ sadvātādīn sthānāpīḍanād aprakopayat // 2
children.translated_text: "Without aggravating" means that, by not being excessive in quantity, the <s>doṣas</s> remain in their proper places and are not provoked by displacement from their seats. [2]
"Passes through the rectum" means that once digested, it exits in a manner appropriate to its nature. [3]
<s>Ūṣman</s> refers to the digestive fire (<s>vahni</s>). [4]

children.text: jīrṇe 'śnīyāt ajīrṇe hi bhuñjānasyābhyavahṛtam āhārajātaṃ pūrvasyāhārasya rasam apariṇatam uttareṇāhārarasenopasṛjat sarvān doṣān prakopayatyāśu jīrṇe tu bhuñjānasya svasthānastheṣu doṣeṣvagnau codīrṇe jātāyāṃ ca bubhukṣāyāṃ vivṛteṣu ca srotasāṃ mukheṣu viśuddhe codgāre hṛdaye viśuddhe vātānulomye visṛṣṭeṣu ca vātamūtrapurīṣavegeṣvabhyavahṛtam āhārajātaṃ sarvaśarīradhātūn apradūṣayad āyur evābhivardhayati kevalaṃ tasmājjīrṇe 'śnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should eat only after the previous meal has been digested, for if one eats while the previous meal is undigested, the newly ingested food, mixing its juice with the incompletely transformed juice of the previous meal, quickly provokes all the <s>doṣas</s>. But when one eats after digestion is complete — when the <s>doṣas</s> are settled in their proper places, when the digestive fire is kindled, when hunger has arisen, when the openings of the channels (<s>srotas</s>) are clear, when the eructation is pure, when the heart is clear, when <s>Vāta</s> moves downward, and when the urges of flatus, urine, and feces have been properly released — then the ingested food, without corrupting any bodily tissue (<s>dhātu</s>), promotes longevity alone. Therefore one should eat only after digestion is complete.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
"Of the previous" refers to what was eaten on the preceding day. [1]
"Incompletely transformed" means not properly developed. [2]

children.text: āhāraraseneti āhārapariṇāmagatena madhurādinā kiṃvā āhārajena rasena // 3
children.translated_text: "With the juice of food" means with the sweet and other <s>rasas</s> produced during the transformation of food; alternatively, with the <s>rasa</s> (nutrient fluid) generated from food. [3]
"When the <s>doṣas</s> are settled in their proper places" and so on — this describes the signs that the previous meal has been digested. [4]

children.text: vīryāviruddham aśnīyāt aviruddhavīryam aśnan hi viruddhavīryāhārajairvikārair nopasṛjyate tasmād vīryāviruddham aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should eat food with non-antagonistic potencies (<s>vīryāviruddha</s>), for one who eats food of non-antagonistic potency is not afflicted by disorders arising from food of antagonistic potencies. Therefore one should eat food with non-antagonistic potencies.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

"Disorders arising from food of antagonistic potencies" refers to <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases), blindness, <s>visarpa</s> (erysipelas), and others mentioned in the chapter called <s>Ātreyabhadrakāpyīya</s>. [1]

children.text: iṣṭe deśe iṣṭasarvopakaraṇaṃ cāśnīyāt iṣṭe hi deśe bhuñjāno nāniṣṭadeśajairmanovighātakarair bhāvair manovighātaṃ prāpnoti tathaiveṣṭaiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ tasmādiṣṭe deśe tatheṣṭasarvopakaraṇaṃ cāśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should eat in a pleasant place and with all desired accessories, for one who eats in a pleasant place does not suffer mental disturbance from the factors that cause mental disturbance which arise in an unpleasant place; likewise with desired accessories. Therefore one should eat in a pleasant place and with all desired accessories.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: manovighātakarairbhāvairiti trividhakukṣīye vakṣyamāṇaiḥ kāmādibhiś cittopatāpakaraiś cittavikārair ityarthaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: "Factors that cause mental disturbance" refers to desire (<s>kāma</s>) and other emotional afflictions that cause mental distress, which will be described in the <s>Trividhakukṣīya</s> chapter — meaning mental disorders. [1]

children.text: tatheṣṭaiśca sarvopakaraṇair bhuñjāno manovighātaṃ na prāpnotīti yojanā aniṣṭabhojanāder manovighāto bhavati // 2]
children.translated_text: The construction is: likewise, one who eats with desired accessories does not suffer mental disturbance; undesired food and such cause mental disturbance. [2]

children.text: nātidrutamaśnīyāt atidrutaṃ hi bhuñjānasyotsnehanamavasādanaṃ bhojanasyāpratiṣṭhānaṃ ca bhojyadoṣasādguṇyopalabdhiś ca na niyatā tasmānnātidrutam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should not eat too quickly, for one who eats too quickly experiences displacement of food, depression, improper settling of the food, and the defects and good qualities of the food are not reliably perceived. Therefore one should not eat too quickly.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
<s>Utsnehana</s> means going by the wrong path. [1]
<s>Avasādana</s> means sinking down. [2]
"Improper settling" means failure to enter the stomach (<s>koṣṭha</s>), remaining stuck at the level of the chest. [3]

children.text: bhojyagatānāṃ doṣāṇāṃ keśādīnāṃ sādguṇyasya ca svādutvādeḥ upalabdhir na niyatā bhavati kadācidupalabhyate kadācin neti // 4
children.translated_text: The perception of defects such as hair in the food and of good qualities such as pleasant taste is not reliable — sometimes they are perceived, sometimes not. [4]

children.text: tatra doṣānupalabdhyā sadoṣasyaiva bhakṣaṇaṃ sādguṇyānupalabdhyā ca prītyabhāvaḥ // 5]
children.translated_text: Here, from the failure to perceive defects comes the eating of defective food, and from the failure to perceive good qualities comes the absence of satisfaction. [5]

children.text: nātivilambitam aśnīyāt ativilambitaṃ hi bhuñjāno na tṛptim adhigacchati bahu bhuṅkte śītībhavaty āhārajātaṃ viṣamaṃ ca pacyate tasmānnātivilambitam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should not eat too slowly, for one who eats too slowly does not achieve satisfaction, eats excessively, the food becomes cold, and it is digested unevenly. Therefore one should not eat too slowly.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: viṣamaṃ ca pacyata iti cirakālabhojanenāgnisambandhasya vaiṣamyāditi bhāvaḥ // 1]
children.translated_text: "Digested unevenly" — the sense is that due to the irregular contact with the digestive fire caused by eating over a prolonged period. [1]

children.text: ajalpannahasan tanmanā jalpato hasato 'nyamanasa vā bhuñjānasya ta eva hi doṣā bhavanti ya evātidrutam aśnataḥ tasmād ajalpannahasaṃstanmanā bhuñjīta /
children.translated_text: One should eat without talking, without laughing, and with full attention; for one who eats while talking, laughing, or with a distracted mind incurs the very same defects as one who eats too quickly. Therefore one should eat without talking, without laughing, and with full attention.
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: ya evātidrutam aśnato doṣā iti utsnehanādayaḥ // 1]
children.translated_text: "The same defects as eating too quickly" refers to displacement of food and the others. [1]

children.text: ātmānam abhisamīkṣya bhuñjīta samyag idaṃ mamopaśete idaṃ nopaśeta ityevaṃ viditaṃ hy asyātmana ātmasātmyaṃ bhavati tasmādātmānamabhisamīkṣya bhuñjīta samyagiti // Car_3,1.25
children.translated_text: One should eat having properly considered oneself — "this agrees with me, this does not agree with me" — for thus what is wholesome to one's own constitution (<s>ātmasātmya</s>) becomes known to oneself. Therefore one should eat having properly considered oneself. [Car 3.1.25]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: nopaśeta itītyatra itiśabdena sātmyāsātmyavidhānopadarśakena vicāraphalamokasātmyasevanaṃ darśayati // 1
children.translated_text: In "does not agree with me" etc., by the word "thus" (<s>iti</s>), which indicates the method of determining what is wholesome and unwholesome, he shows that the fruit of such deliberation is the practice of what is habituated to oneself (<s>okasātmya</s>). [1]

children.text: ātmana iti padenātmanaivātmasātmyaṃ pratipuruṣaṃ jñāyate na śāstropadeśeneti darśayati // 2]
children.translated_text: By the word "oneself" (<s>ātmana</s>), he shows that one's own constitutional compatibility (<s>ātmasātmya</s>) is known by oneself for each individual person, not through textual instruction. [2]
He who knows the <s>rasas</s> (tastes), substances, <s>doṣas</s>, and diseases along with their effects,

children.text: veda yo deśakālau ca śarīraṃ ca sa no bhiṣak // Car_3,1.26
children.translated_text: as well as place, time, and the body — he is our physician. [Car 3.1.26]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
He praises the knowledge of <s>rasa</s>, effects, and other topics taught in this chapter with "<s>rasas</s>" and so on.

children.text: sa no bhiṣagiti no 'smākaṃ saṃmata ityarthaḥ // 1]
children.translated_text: "He is our physician" — "our" means approved by us. [1]
The subject of this <s>Vimāna</s> (chapter of specific determination) is <s>rasas</s> (tastes), substances, <s>doṣas</s>, diseases, and their effects;

children.text: dravyāṇi nātisevyāni trividhaṃ sātmyameva ca // Car_3,1.27
children.translated_text: substances that should not be used excessively; and the threefold <s>sātmya</s> (habituation). [Car 3.1.27]
The eight factors governing diet (<s>āhārāyatana</s>), and the excellence of food qualities —
all this has been elucidated in the <s>Vimāna</s> chapter entitled <s>Rasasaṃkhyā</s> (Enumeration of Tastes). [Car 3.1.28]

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte vimānasthāne rasavimānaṃ nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ // Car_3,1.29
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, called <s>Rasavimāna</s> (Specific Determination of Tastes), in the <s>Vimānasthāna</s> (Section on Specific Determination) of the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and revised by <s>Caraka</s>. [Car 3.1.29]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]

children.text: doṣavikārau ca yadyapi trividhakukṣīye prabhāvavistāreṇa vaktavyau tathāpīha saṃkṣepeṇoktāv eva tena doṣavikāraprabhāvāv apyuktāv iti yaducyate saṃgrahe tat sādhu // 1
children.translated_text: Although the <s>doṣas</s> and diseases will be discussed in detail along with their effects in the <s>Trividhakukṣīya</s> chapter, they have already been mentioned here in brief. Therefore, since the effects of the <s>doṣas</s> and diseases have indeed been stated, what is said in the summary is correct. [1]

children.text: tailādidravyatrayakathanaṃ ca dravyaprabhāvagṛhītamiti kṛtvā na pṛthak saṃgrahe paṭhitam // 2]
children.translated_text: The mention of the three substances such as oil (<s>taila</s>) is subsumed under the topic of the effects of substances, and therefore is not listed separately in the summary. [2]
Now we shall expound the chapter on the body entitled <s>Katidhāpuruṣīya</s> ("In How Many Ways is the Person Constituted"). [Car 5.1.1]

children.text: iti ha smāha bhagavān ātreyaḥ // Car_5,1.2
children.translated_text: Thus indeed spoke the blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. [Car 5.1.2]
