O wise one, in how many ways is the <s>puruṣa</s> (person) divided according to the division of <s>dhātus</s> (constituents)?

children.text: puruṣaḥ kāraṇaṃ kasmāt prabhavaḥ puruṣasya kaḥ // Car_5,1.3
children.translated_text: Is the <s>puruṣa</s> the cause, or what is the origin of the <s>puruṣa</s>? [Car 5.1.3]

children.text: kim ajño jñaḥ sa nityaḥ kiṃ kim anityo nidarśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Is the self unknowing or knowing? Is it eternal or has it been shown to be non-eternal?

children.text: prakṛtiḥ kā vikārāḥ ke kiṃ liṅgaṃ puruṣasya ca // Car_5,1.4
children.translated_text: What is <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)? What are the <s>vikāras</s> (modifications)? And what is the characteristic mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the <s>puruṣa</s>? [Car 5.1.4]

children.text: niṣkriyaṃ ca svatantraṃ ca vaśinaṃ sarvagaṃ vibhum /
children.translated_text: Those who know the self (<s>ātmajña</s>) declare the <s>Ātman</s> (self) to be without action, independent, self-controlled, all-pervading, omnipresent,

children.text: vadanty ātmānam ātmajñāḥ kṣetrajñaṃ sākṣiṇaṃ tathā // Car_5,1.5
children.translated_text: the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), and the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>). [Car 5.1.5]

children.text: niṣkriyasya kriyā tasya bhagavan vidyate katham /
children.translated_text: O Blessed One, if it is without action, how can it have any activity?

children.text: svatantraś ced aniṣṭāsu kathaṃ yoniṣu jāyate // Car_5,1.6
children.translated_text: If it is independent, why is it born in undesirable wombs? [Car 5.1.6]

children.text: vaśī yady asukhaiḥ kasmād bhāvair ākramyate balāt /
children.translated_text: If it is self-controlled, why is it forcibly overcome by unpleasant states?

children.text: sarvāḥ sarvagatatvāc ca vedanāḥ kiṃ na vetti saḥ // Car_5,1.7
children.translated_text: And if it is all-pervading, why does it not know all sensations? [Car 5.1.7]
If it is omnipresent, why does it not see what is hidden behind a rock or a wall?

children.text: kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetram athavā kiṃ pūrvam iti saṃśayaḥ // Car_5,1.8
children.translated_text: Or is the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) or the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) prior? — this is the doubt. [Car 5.1.8]

children.text: jñeyaṃ kṣetraṃ vinā pūrvaṃ kṣetrajño hi na yujyate /
children.translated_text: Without a field to be known, the knower of the field cannot logically exist first;

children.text: kṣetraṃ ca yadi pūrvaṃ syāt kṣetrajñaḥ syād aśāśvataḥ // Car_5,1.9
children.translated_text: and if the field existed first, then the knower of the field would be non-eternal. [Car 5.1.9]

children.text: sākṣibhūtaś ca kasyāyaṃ kartā hy anyo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And as witness — witness to whom? For no other agent is found.

children.text: syāt kathaṃ cāvikārasya viśeṣo vedanākṛtaḥ // Car_5,1.10
children.translated_text: And how can there be a distinction produced by sensation in something that is without modification? [Car 5.1.10]

children.text: atha cārtasya bhagavaṃs tisṛṇāṃ kāṃ cikitsati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, O Blessed One, when a person is afflicted, which of the three does the physician treat —

children.text: atītāṃ vedanāṃ vaidyo vartamānāṃ bhaviṣyatīm // Car_5,1.11
children.translated_text: the past sensation, the present one, or the future one? [Car 5.1.11]
The future sensation has not yet arrived; the past one does not return;

children.text: sāṃpratikyā api sthānaṃ nāsty arteḥ saṃśayo hy ataḥ // Car_5,1.12
children.translated_text: and even the present one has no stable locus — hence there is doubt about suffering. [Car 5.1.12]

children.text: kāraṇaṃ vedanānāṃ kiṃ kim adhiṣṭhānam ucyate /
children.translated_text: What is the cause of sensations? What is said to be their substratum?

children.text: kva caitā vedanāḥ sarvā nivṛttiṃ yānty aśeṣataḥ // Car_5,1.13
children.translated_text: And where do all these sensations completely cease? [Car 5.1.13]
The all-knowing one, who has renounced everything, who has emerged from all contact,

children.text: ekaḥ praśānto bhūtātmā kair liṅgair upalabhyate // Car_5,1.14
children.translated_text: the one, the tranquil <s>Bhūtātman</s> (elemental self) — by what marks is it perceived? [Car 5.1.14]

children.text: ity agniveśasya vacaḥ śrutvā matimatāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of <s>Agniveśa</s>, the best among the wise,

children.text: sarvaṃ yathāvat provāca praśāntātmā punarvasuḥ // Car_5,1.15
children.translated_text: <s>Punarvasu</s>, whose mind was perfectly tranquil, spoke everything as it truly is. [Car 5.1.15]
The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) is declared to be the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) beginning with <s>Kha</s> (space/ether) with consciousness (<s>cetanā</s>) as the sixth.

children.text: cetanādhātur apy ekaḥ smṛtaḥ puruṣasaṃjñakaḥ // Car_5,1.16
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the single conscious element alone is also declared to bear the designation <s>puruṣa</s>. [Car 5.1.16]
Again, according to the division of constituents, the <s>puruṣa</s> is declared to consist of twenty-four:

children.text: mano daśendriyāṇy arthāḥ prakṛtiś cāṣṭadhātukī // Car_5,1.17
children.translated_text: mind (<s>manas</s>), the ten sense organs (<s>indriya</s>), the sense objects (<s>artha</s>), and <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) comprising the eight-fold <s>dhātu</s>. [Car 5.1.17]

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ manaso jñānasyābhāvo bhāva eva ca /
children.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>manas</s> (mind) is the absence and presence of cognition (<s>jñāna</s>);

children.text: sati hy ātmendriyārthānāṃ sannikarṣe na vartate // Car_5,1.18
children.translated_text: for even when there is conjunction of the self, sense organs, and their objects, cognition does not occur [Car 5.1.18]

children.text: vaivṛttyān manaso jñānaṃ sānnidhyāt tac ca vartate /
children.translated_text: due to the turning away of the mind; and cognition occurs when it is present.

children.text: aṇutvam atha caikatvaṃ dvau guṇau manasaḥ smṛtau // Car_5,1.19
children.translated_text: Atomicity (<s>aṇutva</s>) and singularity (<s>ekatva</s>) are declared to be the two qualities of <s>manas</s> (mind). [Car 5.1.19]

children.text: cintyaṃ vicāryam ūhyaṃ ca dhyeyaṃ saṃkalpyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: That which is to be thought upon (<s>cintya</s>), deliberated upon (<s>vicārya</s>), conjectured (<s>ūhya</s>), meditated upon (<s>dhyeya</s>), and resolved upon (<s>saṃkalpya</s>) —

children.text: yat kiṃcin manaso jñeyaṃ tat sarvaṃ hy arthasaṃjñakam // Car_5,1.20
children.translated_text: whatever is to be cognized by the mind, all of that is designated as <s>artha</s> (object). [Car 5.1.20]
The action of the mind is the restraint of the sense organs and the control of itself;

children.text: ūho vicāraś ca tataḥ paraṃ buddhiḥ pravartate // Car_5,1.21
children.translated_text: from conjecture and deliberation, thereafter the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) proceeds to act. [Car 5.1.21]
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}]
Having stated the qualities of <s>manas</s> (mind), he now states its objects with "that which is to be thought upon" and so on. [1]

children.text: cintyaṃ kartavyatayā akartavyatayā vā yanmanasā cintyate // 2
children.translated_text: <s>Cintya</s> (that which is to be thought upon) is what is thought about by the mind in terms of what should be done or what should not be done. [2]
<s>Vicārya</s> (that which is to be deliberated upon) is what is examined through reasoning about its logical validity or invalidity. [3]

children.text: ūhyaṃ ca yat sambhāvanayā ūhyate evametadbhaviṣyati iti // 4
children.translated_text: <s>Ūhya</s> (that which is to be conjectured) is what is conjectured through estimation — "it will be thus." [4]
<s>Dhyeya</s> (that which is to be meditated upon) has as its domain the knowledge arising from contemplative practice (<s>bhāvanā</s>). [5]
<s>Saṃkalpya</s> (that which is to be resolved upon) has as its domain the determination of something as possessing merit or possessing fault. [6]
By 'whatever,' subjects not [explicitly] mentioned such as pleasure etc. are included. // 7
'Knowable by the mind' means graspable by the mind independently of the sense organs. // 8

children.text: ete ca mano'rthāḥ śabdādirūpā eva tena ṣaṣṭhārthakalpanayā na caturviṃśatisaṃkhyātirekaḥ // 9
children.translated_text: And these objects of the mind are indeed of the nature of sound etc. [i.e., sensory objects]. Therefore, by the postulation of a sixth [sense-]object, the number twenty-four is not exceeded. // 9

children.text: sukhādayas tu śabdādivyatiriktā mano'rthā buddhibhedagrahaṇenaiva grāhyāḥ // 10
children.translated_text: But pleasure and the like, which are objects of the mind distinct from sound etc., are to be grasped only through the apprehension of distinctions in cognition (<s>buddhibheda</s>). // 10
Having stated the object of the mind, he states the function of the mind with 'the sense organ' etc. // 11

children.text: indriyābhigrahaḥ indriyādhiṣṭhānaṃ manasaḥ karma tathā svasya nigraho manasaḥ karma mano hy aniṣṭaviṣayaprasṛtaṃ manasaiva niyamyate manaśca guṇāntarayuktaṃ sadviṣayāntarān niyamayati ityāhureke // 12
children.translated_text: The governance of the sense organs (<s>indriyābhigraha</s>) — i.e., the superintendence of the sense organs — is a function of the mind. Likewise, self-restraint is a function of the mind. For the mind, when directed toward an undesirable object, is restrained by the mind itself. And the mind, when endowed with a different quality, restrains [itself] from another object — thus some say. // 12
As it is stated: 'The mind, inclined toward sense-objects, cannot be restrained // 13

children.text: niyantum ahitād arthād dhṛtirhi niyamātmikā iti // 14
children.translated_text: from harmful objects when <s>dhṛti</s> (steadfastness) is lost — for <s>dhṛti</s> is of the nature of restraint.' // 14

children.text: tena dhṛtyā kāraṇabhūtayā ātmānaṃ niyamayatīti na svātmani kriyāvirodhaḥ // 15
children.translated_text: Therefore, by means of <s>dhṛti</s> as the [instrumental] cause, it restrains itself — thus there is no contradiction of action upon one's own self. // 15
He states another function of the mind with '<s>ūha</s> (deliberation) and <s>vicāra</s> (discernment).' // 16

children.text: atroha ālocanajñānaṃ nirvikalpakam vicāro heyopādeyatayā vikalpanam // 17
children.translated_text: Here, <s>ūha</s> is non-conceptual apprehension (<s>ālocanajñāna</s>); <s>vicāra</s> is conceptualization in terms of what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted. // 17

children.text: caturvidhaṃ hi vikalpakāraṇaṃ sāṃkhyā manyante tatra bāhyam indriyarūpam ābhyantaraṃ tu mano'haṃkāro buddhiśceti tritayam // 18
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> hold that the cause of conceptualization is fourfold. Among these, the external [cause] is in the form of the sense organs; the internal [causes] are three — the mind, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), and <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). // 18

children.text: tatrendriyāṇyālocayanti nirvikalpena gṛhṇantītyarthaḥ manastu saṃkalpayati heyopādeyatayā kalpayatītyarthaḥ ahaṃkāro 'bhimanyate mamedamahamatrādhikṛta iti manyata ityarthaḥ buddhir adhyavasyati tyajāmyenaṃ doṣavantam upādadāmyenaṃ guṇavantam ityadhyavasāyaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // 19
children.translated_text: Among these, the sense organs apprehend — meaning they grasp non-conceptually. The mind conceives — meaning it conceptualizes in terms of what is to be rejected and accepted. <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> appropriates — meaning it thinks 'this is mine, I am concerned with this.' <s>Buddhi</s> determines — meaning it makes the determination 'I shall discard this which is defective, I shall take this which is meritorious.' // 19

children.text: ūhas tu yadyapi bāhyacakṣurādikarma tathāpi tatrāpi mano'dhiṣṭhānam astīti manaḥkarmatayoktaḥ // 20
children.translated_text: Although <s>ūha</s> (deliberation) is actually a function of the external eye etc., still, because the mind's superintendence is present there too, it is stated as a function of the mind. // 20

children.text: vacanaṃ hi sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayam avagāhate yasmāt // 21
children.translated_text: For the statement is: 'The intellect accompanied by the internal organ apprehends every object; // 21

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi iti // 22
children.translated_text: therefore the [internal] instrument is threefold — the gate, while the rest are doors.' // 22

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ buddhiḥ pravartata iti ūhavicārānantaraṃ buddhir adhyavasāyaṃ karotītyarthaḥ // 23
children.translated_text: 'Then afterwards <s>buddhi</s> operates' — means that after <s>ūha</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, <s>buddhi</s> makes the determination — this is the meaning. // 23

children.text: ahaṃkāravyāpāraś cābhimananam ihānukto 'pi buddhivyāpāreṇaiva sūcito jñeyaḥ // 24
children.translated_text: And the function of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — namely, self-appropriation (<s>abhimanana</s>) — though not mentioned here, should be understood as indicated by the function of <s>buddhi</s> itself. // 24

children.text: buddhirhi tyajāmyenamupādadāmīti vādhyavasāyaṃ kurvatī ahaṃkārābhimata eva viṣaye bhavati tena buddhivyāpāreṇaivāhaṃkāravyāpāro 'pi gṛhyate // 25
children.translated_text: For <s>buddhi</s>, in making the determination 'I shall discard this' or 'I shall take this,' operates only upon an object that has [already] been appropriated by <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. Therefore, through the function of <s>buddhi</s> itself, the function of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> too is grasped. // 25
For in <s>buddhi</s>, the functions of all the instruments are deposited. // 26
As it is stated: 'These quality-distinctions, resembling lamps, mutually different from one another,
having illuminated the entire purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s>, present [it] to <s>buddhi</s>.' // 27]
A sense-object is grasped by the sense organ when accompanied by the mind;

children.text: kalpyate manasā tūrdhvaṃ guṇato doṣato'thavā // Car_5,1.22
children.translated_text: but thereafter it is conceptualized by the mind — in terms of merit or fault. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.22
That cognition which arises in that object, which is of the nature of determination —

children.text: vyavasyati tayā vaktuṃ kartuṃ vā buddhipūrvakam // Car_5,1.23
children.translated_text: by that [determination], one resolves to speak or to act, preceded by intellect. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.23
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He elaborates this very fact that <s>buddhi</s> is preceded by <s>ūha</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, with 'by the sense organ' etc. // 1
'Is grasped' means is grasped by mere <s>ūha</s>, non-conceptually. // 2
'In terms of merit' means as what is to be accepted. // 3
'In terms of fault' means as what is to be rejected. // 4
He elaborates the determination of <s>buddhi</s> with 'arises' etc. // 5
'In that object' means in the object conceptualized by the mind. // 6
'Of the nature of determination' means of firm nature, i.e., of the nature of <s>adhyavasāya</s> (resolution). // 7

children.text: vyavasyatīti anuṣṭhānaṃ karoti udyukto bhavatītyarthaḥ buddhyadhyavasitamarthaṃ vaktuṃ kartuṃ vānutiṣṭhatīti yāvat // 8
children.translated_text: 'Resolves' means undertakes action, becomes engaged — the meaning is that one proceeds to speak or act upon the object determined by <s>buddhi</s>. // 8

children.text: buddhipūrvakamityanena yadeva buddhipūrvakam anuṣṭhānaṃ tad evaivaṃvidhaṃ bhavati nonmattādyanuṣṭhānamiti darśayati // 9]
children.translated_text: By [saying] 'preceded by intellect,' he shows that only action preceded by intellect is of this kind — not the action of a madman etc. // 9]
The sense organs [of cognition] — pertaining to space etc. — are five, each endowed with one additional [element],

children.text: pañca karmānumeyāni yebhyo buddhiḥ pravartate // Car_5,1.24
children.translated_text: inferrable from their functions, from which <s>buddhi</s> (cognition) arises. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.24
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: mano'bhidhāyendriyāṇyabhidhatte tatrāpi jyāyastvād buddhīndriyāṇi prāgāha ekaiketyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Having described the mind, he describes the sense organs. Among them, because of their pre-eminence, he first states the cognitive sense organs with 'each with one additional' etc. // 1

children.text: khādīnāṃ madhye ekaikenādhikena bhūtena yuktānīndriyāṇi pañca cakṣurādīni ekaikādhikapadena pañcāpi pāñcabhautikāni paraṃ cakṣuṣi tejo'dhikamityādyuktaṃ sūcayati // 2
children.translated_text: Among space etc., sense organs endowed with one additional element in each [successive one] are five — namely the eye and the rest. By the expression 'one additional,' he indicates that all five are composed of all five elements, but in the eye, fire predominates — and so on as stated. // 2
'Inferrable from their functions' means inferrable from their effects — the effects being visual cognition etc. // 3

children.text: yebhyo buddhiḥ pravartata iti yāni buddhīndriyāṇi tānīmāni pañceti darśayati // 4
children.translated_text: 'From which <s>buddhi</s> arises' — he shows that these five are the cognitive sense organs (<s>buddhīndriya</s>). // 4

children.text: yadyapi ca sāṃkhye āhaṃkārikāṇīndriyāṇi yaduktaṃ sāttvika ekādaśakaḥ pravartate vaikṛtād ahaṃkārād iti tathāpi matabhedādbhautikatvam indriyāṇāṃ jñeyaṃ kiṃvā aupacārikam etadbhautikatvam indriyāṇāṃ jñeyam upacārabījaṃ ca yad guṇabhūyiṣṭhaṃ yad indriyaṃ gṛhṇāti tattadbhūyiṣṭham ityucyate cakṣustejo gṛhṇāti tena taijasam ucyate ityādi jñeyam // 5]
children.translated_text: Although in <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the sense organs are products of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — as stated: 'The <s>sāttvika</s> group of eleven arises from the modified <s>ahaṃkāra</s>' — nevertheless, due to difference of doctrine, the sense organs should be understood as elemental (<s>bhautika</s>). Or, this elemental nature of the sense organs should be understood as figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>). The basis for the figurative usage is that whichever element predominates in what a sense organ grasps, that [organ] is said to be predominantly of that [element]. The eye grasps light (<s>tejas</s>), therefore it is called 'fiery' — and so on should be understood. // 5]
The hands, feet, anus, genitals, and the organ of speech —
these are the five motor organs (<s>karmendriya</s>). The feet are for the function of locomotion. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.25
The anus and genitals are for excretion; the hands for grasping and holding.

children.text: jihvāvāgindriyaṃ vāk ca satyā jyotistamo'nṛtā // Car_5,1.26
children.translated_text: The tongue is the organ of speech; and speech is either true — [like] light — or dark — [like] falsehood. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.26
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Now he states the motor organs with 'the hands' etc. // 1
The two hands are one [organ] and the two feet are one organ — because they perform a single type of function. // 2
The anus and genitals are each separate [organs]. // 3
To show the classification of speech for the purpose of acceptance and rejection, he says 'and speech' etc. // 4

children.text: jyotiriva jyotiḥ dharmakartṛtvenobhayalokaprakāśakāritvāt etadviparyayeṇa tamaḥ anṛtā // 5]
children.translated_text: 'Light' (<s>jyotis</s>) — [speech] is like light, because it illuminates both worlds by producing <s>dharma</s>. In the opposite case, it is 'darkness' — falsehood. // 5]

children.text: mahābhūtāni khaṃ vāyur agnir āpaḥ kṣitistathā /
children.translated_text: The great elements are: space, air, fire, water, and earth.

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaśca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhaśca tadguṇāḥ // Car_5,1.27
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell are their [respective] qualities. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.27
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: sampratyuddeśakramānurodhādarthe 'bhidhātavye 'rthānāṃ prakṛtigrahaṇagṛhītapañcabhūtaguṇatayā parādhīnatvād aṣṭadhātuprakṛtigṛhītāni bhūtānyeva tāvadāha mahābhūtānītyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, following the order of enumeration, when the objects (<s>artha</s>) are to be described — since the objects, by virtue of their five-element quality as grasped by the inclusion in <s>prakṛti</s>, are dependent [on elements] — he first states the elements themselves, which are included in the eight-<s>dhātu</s> <s>prakṛti</s>, with 'the great elements' etc. // 1

children.text: śabdādayo yathāsaṃkhyaṃ khādīnāṃ naisargikā guṇā jñeyāḥ // 2
children.translated_text: Sound etc. should be understood as the natural qualities of space etc. in their respective order. // 2

children.text: yastu guṇotkarṣo 'bhidhātavyaḥ sa hi anupraviṣṭabhūtasambandhād eva // 3
children.translated_text: The augmentation of qualities that is to be stated [later] is indeed due to the entry of other elements. // 3

children.text: tena pṛthivyāṃ caturbhūtapraveśāt pañcaguṇatvam evaṃ jalādāv api caturguṇatvādi jñeyam // 4]
children.translated_text: Therefore, in earth, because of the entry of [the other] four elements, there are five qualities. Likewise in water etc., there are four qualities and so on — this should be understood. // 4]
Among these, the first [element] has one quality; in each successive one the qualities increase.

children.text: pūrvaḥ pūrvaguṇaścaiva kramaśo guṇiṣu smṛtaḥ // Car_5,1.28
children.translated_text: The prior quality of the prior [element] is also [present] successively in [each later] substance — thus it is recorded. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.28
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: naisargikaṃ guṇamabhidhāya bhūtāntarapraveśakṛtaṃ guṇam āha teṣām ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Having stated the natural quality, he states the quality produced by the entry of other elements, with 'of these' etc. // 1

children.text: ekaguṇaḥ pūrva iti pūrvo dhātuḥ kharūpaḥ śabdaikaguṇaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'The first has one quality' — the first substance, in the form of space, has only one quality — sound. // 2

children.text: puṃliṅgatā ca khādīnāṃ dhāturūpatābuddhisthīkṛtatvāt uktaṃ hi khādayaś cetanāṣaṣṭhā dhātavaḥ iti // 3
children.translated_text: And the masculine gender [applied to space etc.] is because their being conceived as substances (<s>dhātu</s>) has become fixed in the mind. For it is stated: 'Space and the rest, with consciousness as the sixth, are the substances (<s>dhātus</s>).' // 3

children.text: yathā yathā ca paratvaṃ tathā tathā ca guṇavṛddhir yathāsaṃkhyam // 4
children.translated_text: As each [element] is successively later, so is there successive increase of qualities — in corresponding order. // 4

children.text: nanu etāvatā 'py ekaguṇatvadviguṇatvādi na niyamena jñāyate ko guṇaḥ kva bhūte ityāha pūrva ityādi // 5
children.translated_text: Objection: Even by this much, the one-quality-ness, two-quality-ness, etc. are not determinately known — [i.e.,] which quality [resides] in which element. He answers with 'the prior' etc. // 5

children.text: guṇiṣu khādiṣu dhātuṣu pūrvo guṇaḥ krameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ vartate na kevalaṃ pūrvaḥ kiṃtu pūrvasyāpi yo guṇaḥ sa ca pūrvaguṇa uttare bhūte vartate // 6
children.translated_text: In the substances (<s>guṇins</s>) — the elements space etc. — the prior quality is present successively in corresponding order. Not only the prior [quality], but also the quality of the prior [element] — that prior-quality is [also] present in the later element. // 6

children.text: tena khe pūrve pūrvaḥ śabdaguṇo vartate vāyau tu sparśaḥ kramaprāptaḥ pūrvo bhavati pūrvaguṇaśca śabda iti dviguṇatvam evamagnyādau ca jñeyam // 7
children.translated_text: Therefore, in space — the first [element] — the prior quality, sound, is present. In air, however, touch — obtained by sequence — is the prior [natural quality], and the prior-quality — sound — [is also present]. Thus there are two qualities. Likewise in fire etc. this should be understood. // 7

children.text: gandhas tūttaraguṇāntarābhāvānna pūrvo bhavati tathāpi gandhaś ca tadguṇāḥ iti granthe tadguṇā itipadāpekṣayā gandhasya pūrvatvaṃ kalpanīyaṃ kiṃvā pūrva iti chattriṇo gacchantīti nyāyenoktaṃ tenāpūrvo 'pi gandhaḥ kramāgataḥ pṛthivyāṃ jñeyaḥ // 8]
children.translated_text: Smell, however, because there is no further subsequent quality, is not 'prior' [in the same sense]. Nevertheless, in the text 'smell — and those are their qualities,' with reference to the word 'their qualities,' the priority of smell should be construed [as belonging to earth]. Or, 'the prior' is said by the maxim of 'the umbrella-holders are walking' — therefore smell too, though not [technically] prior, should be understood as reaching earth by sequence. // 8]
Hardness, liquidity, mobility, and heat — [these are the distinguishing marks] of earth, water, air, and fire [respectively].
Non-resistance [is that] of space. [This is] the visible mark, in due order. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.29
All this distinguishing mark is within the range of the tactile sense organ.
For touch — together with its absence — is knowable by the tactile sense organ. // <s>Car</s>_5,1.30
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
He states the distinctive mark of the elements that is not shared [with other elements], with 'hardness' etc. // 1

children.text: apratīghātaḥ apratihananam asparśatvam iti yāvat sparśavaddhi gativighātakaṃ bhavati nākāśaḥ asparśavattvāt // 2
children.translated_text: 'Non-resistance' (<s>apratīghāta</s>) means non-obstruction, i.e., the absence of touch. For what possesses touch obstructs movement, but not space — because it is devoid of touch. // 2
'All this' means hardness etc. // 3
'Within the range of the tactile sense organ' means knowable by the tactile sense organ. // 4
How is all this knowable by the tactile sense organ? He answers with 'for touch' etc. // 5
'Together with its absence' (<s>saviparyaya</s>) means the absence of touch — this is the meaning. // 6

children.text: yad indriyaṃ yadgṛhṇāti tattasyābhāvamapi gṛhṇāti tena ākāśasyāsparśatvam api sparśanendriyagrāhyam iti yuktam // 7
children.translated_text: Whatever sense organ grasps something also grasps its absence. Therefore, the touchlessness of space too is graspable by the tactile sense organ — this is reasonable. // 7

children.text: dravatvaṃ calatvaṃ ca sāṃkhyamate sparśanagrāhyatvāt sthūlabhūtavātadharmaḥ sparśa eva yaddhi sparśanena gṛhyate tat sarvaṃ mahābhūtavātapariṇāma eva // 8
children.translated_text: Liquidity and mobility, in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view, being graspable by touch, are a form of touch itself — a property of the gross element air. For whatever is grasped by the tactile sense, all of that is indeed a modification of the great element air. // 8

children.text: etāni ca khādīni sūkṣmāṇi tanmātrarūpāṇi jñeyāni sthūlabhūtāni tu khādīni vikāratayā tatroktāni // 9
children.translated_text: And these [elements] — space etc. — should be understood as subtle, in the form of <s>tanmātras</s>. The gross elements — space etc. — are stated there [in <s>Sāṃkhya</s>] as modifications. // 9
In the <s>prakṛti</s>-group, the subtle forms — the <s>tanmātras</s> — are stated. // 10

children.text: vacanaṃ hi tanmātrāṇyaviśeṣās tebhyo bhūtāni pañca pañcabhyaḥ // 11
children.translated_text: For the statement is: 'The <s>tanmātras</s> are the non-specifics; from them [arise] the five elements, from the five [elements] // 11

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorāśca mūḍhāśca iti tenehāpi khādīni tanmātraśabdoktāni sūkṣmāṇi boddhavyāni // 12]
children.translated_text: these are known as the specifics — quiescent, violent, and stupefying.' Therefore here too, space etc. designated by the term <s>tanmātra</s> should be understood as subtle. // 12]
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Śārīrasthāna</s>, 1
Now we shall expound the section on rejuvenation (<s>rasāyana</s>) called <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s>. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.1
Thus indeed spoke the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.2
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: pūrvasthānoktalakṣaṇābhāvenāvadhāritāyuṣmadbhāvena cikitsā dharmārthayaśaskarī kartavyetyanantaraṃ cikitsābhidhāyakaṃ sthānam ucyate // 1
children.translated_text: After ascertaining the nature of a person possessing longevity through the absence of [fatal] signs described in the previous sections, the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s> (Section on Therapeutics) — which produces <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and fame — is stated next [on the principle that] treatment should be undertaken. // 1

children.text: rasāyanavājīkaraṇasādhanamapi yathā cikitsocyate tathānantaram eva vakṣyati // 2
children.translated_text: That the means of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (virilification) too are called 'treatment' (<s>cikitsā</s>) — that will be stated immediately after. // 2
Among these, before the treatment of fever etc., <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> are stated first because of their great benefit. // 3

children.text: tayorapi ca rasāyanameva varṣasahasrāyuṣṭvādikāraṇatayā mahāphalam iti tad abhidhīyate tatrāpi cābhayāmalakīyaś cikitsāsthānārthasūtrābhidhāyakatayāgre 'bhidhīyate // 4]
children.translated_text: And between these two, <s>rasāyana</s> alone is of great benefit because it causes a lifespan of a thousand years etc. — therefore it is described [first]. And among [the <s>rasāyana</s> chapters], the <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s> is described first because it states the essential purport of the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>. // 4]
Treatment, disease-removal, the wholesome, the means, medicine,
atonement, pacification, restoration to natural state, the beneficial — [these are synonyms of <s>cikitsā</s>]. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, 1 [<s>Rasāyanādhyāya</s>]

children.text: tatrādau vyavahārārthaṃ sthānābhidheyasya bheṣajasya paryāyānāha cikitsitam ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: First, for the purpose of common usage, he states the synonyms of medicine (<s>bheṣaja</s>) — the subject matter of this section — with 'treatment' etc. // 1
And he makes such a statement of synonyms of the principal subject at the beginning — just as in the <s>Nidānasthāna</s>, the synonyms 'cause, form' etc. are stated. // 2

children.text: etacca paryāyābhidhānaṃ prādhānyena catuṣpādasyaiva bheṣajasya yaduktaṃ catuṣpādaṃ ṣoḍaśakalaṃ bheṣajamiti bhiṣajo bhāṣante iti // 3
children.translated_text: And this statement of synonyms primarily refers to medicine as having four limbs — as stated: 'Physicians say that medicine has four limbs and sixteen components.' // 3

children.text: evaṃbhūtabheṣajāṅgarūpatayā tu sthāvarajaṅgamadravyarūpasya bheṣajasya bheṣajatvamevāntaravyavahārakṛtaṃ jñeyam // 4
children.translated_text: However, as having the nature of medicine-charcoal, the medicinality of medicine — which is in the form of plant and animal substances — should be known as established merely by conventional usage. // 4
'Atonement' (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) is a name for medicine — because, like atonement, medicine removes diseases which are the effects of unrighteous action. // 5]

children.text: vidyād bheṣajanāmāni bheṣajaṃ dvividhaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: One should know the names of medicines; and that medicine is of two kinds:
some promote vigor in the healthy, and some destroy diseases in the afflicted. // Car_6,1.4
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He elaborates the twofold division with 'of the healthy' etc. // 1
'Some' means: not all [do both]. // 2

children.text: svasthatvena vyavahriyamāṇasya puṃso jarādisvābhāvikavyādhiharatvena tathāpraharṣavyayāyakṣayitvānucitaśukratvādyapraśastaśārīrabhāvaharatvena ūrjaḥ praśastaṃ bhāvam ādadhātīti svasthasyorjaskaram // 3
children.translated_text: 'Promoting vigor in the healthy' — for a person conventionally designated as healthy, [medicine] removes natural diseases such as aging etc., and also removes undesirable bodily states such as lack of exhilaration, loss from exertion, wasting, and improper semen etc. — thus it bestows <s>ūrjas</s> (vigor), meaning an excellent state, upon the healthy. // 3
'Destroying disease in the afflicted' — by this qualification, [it means] removing fever etc. from one afflicted by fever etc. // 4

children.text: roganud iti vacanenaivārtaviśeṣitāyāṃ labdhāyāṃ yad ārtasya iti karoti tena sahajajarādikṛtāṃ pīḍām anudvejikāṃ parityajya jvarādināsvābhāvikena rogeṇa pīḍitasyeti darśayati // 5]
children.translated_text: Since by the expression 'destroying disease' itself the qualification 'afflicted' is already obtained — why does he say 'of the afflicted'? By this he shows: setting aside the non-distressing affliction caused by natural aging etc., [it means] one who is afflicted by non-natural disease such as fever etc. // 5]
And non-medicine too is of two kinds: [merely] harming, and harming with after-effects.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
In the context of medicine, he states the twofold division of non-medicine with 'non-medicine' etc. // 1
'Harming' (<s>bādhana</s>) here means causing harm only temporarily — like a small [amount of] unwholesome [food]. // 2
'With after-effects' (<s>sānubādhana</s>) means producing diseases of long duration like <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) etc. // 3]
That which promotes vigor in the healthy — that is <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac), that is <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation). // Car_6,1.5

children.text: prāyaḥ prāyeṇa rogāṇāṃ dvitīyaṃ praśame matam /
children.translated_text: The second [type] is generally considered for the pacification of diseases.

children.text: prāyaḥśabdo viśeṣārtho hy ubhayaṃ hy ubhayārthakṛt // Car_6,1.6
children.translated_text: The word 'generally' is for the purpose of [indicating] predominance — for both [types] accomplish both purposes. // Car_6,1.6
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He divides the twofold medicine already stated, with 'of the healthy' etc. // 1
The break is: 'that is <s>vṛṣya</s>, that is <s>rasāyana</s>, generally.' // 2

children.text: yadvṛṣyaṃ prāyo bhavati tathā rasāyanaṃ yat prāyo bhavati ārtasya rogaharaṃ yadbāhulyena tat svasthorjaskaram ucyate yattu dvitīyam ārtarogaharaṃ tat prāyeṇa jvarādiśamanaṃ rasāyanaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ ca bhavati yathākṣatakṣīṇoktaṃ sarpirguḍādi rasāyanaṃ vṛṣyaṃ ca bhavati tathā pāṇḍurogokto yogarājo rasāyanatvenoktaḥ tathā kāsādhikāre 'gastyaharītakī rasāyanatvenoktetyādy anusaraṇīyam // 3
children.translated_text: That which is predominantly <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac) and that which is predominantly <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) — what is primarily disease-removing for the afflicted is called 'promoting vigor in the healthy.' And the second — that which is disease-removing for the afflicted — generally serves also as disease-pacifying, rejuvenative, and aphrodisiac. For example, the ghee-and-jaggery preparation mentioned for <s>kṣatakṣīṇa</s> (consumptive wounds) is both rejuvenative and aphrodisiac; likewise <s>Yogarāja</s> mentioned in the context of <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> (anemia) is stated as rejuvenative; similarly in the section on cough, <s>Agastyaharītakī</s> is stated as rejuvenative — and such [examples] should be followed. // 3

children.text: rasāyanoktānāṃ ca jvarādiharatvam atra suvyaktameva rasāyanagrantheṣu // 4
children.translated_text: And the fever-removing etc. property of those stated as rejuvenatives is quite evident in the <s>rasāyana</s> texts themselves. // 4

children.text: anye tu bruvate yad vyādhimātraharaṃ na tad rasāyanaṃ kiṃtu śarīrasaṃyogadārḍhyād dīrghāyuḥkartṛtvasādhāraṇadharmayogād upacaritavyādhiharaṃ rasāyanam ihocyata iti // 5
children.translated_text: Others, however, say: what merely removes disease is not <s>rasāyana</s>; rather, what is called <s>rasāyana</s> here is [that which] incidentally removes disease through its general property of strengthening bodily composition and producing longevity. // 5

children.text: nanu yadi svasthorjaskaramapi vyādhiharaṃ vyādhiharaṃ ca svasthorjaskaraṃ tatkiṃ kiṃciditi padena bheṣajakarmavyavasthādarśakena kriyate brūmaḥ bāhulyena svasthorjaskaratvaṃ vyādhiharatvaṃ ca vyavasthāpyate na ceha sarvārtarogaharasya svasthorjaskaratvamiti pratijñāyate yena pāṭhāsaptaparṇādīnām api rasāyanatvaṃ sādhanīyaśaktitvād ārtarogaharatvena yaducyate tadapi rasāyanaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ ca bhavatīti lavamātropadarśanaṃ kriyate tat svasthārtayor ubhayārthakartṛtvam // 6
children.translated_text: Objection: if what promotes vigor in the healthy also removes disease, and what removes disease also promotes vigor in the healthy, then what is accomplished by the word 'some' which shows a distinction in medicinal action? We reply: the distinction is established by predominance — [one is predominantly] vigor-promoting for the healthy, [the other predominantly] disease-removing. And here it is not claimed that everything that removes disease in the afflicted promotes vigor in the healthy — so that one would have to make even <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>saptaparṇa</s>, etc. into rejuvenatives. Since they have the power to accomplish [only their specific task], what is said — that which removes disease in the afflicted is also rejuvenative and aphrodisiac — is merely a partial illustration. The point is that both serve both purposes for both the healthy and the afflicted. // 6
He explains the purport of the word 'generally' with 'generally' etc. // 7
'For the purpose of predominance' means: for the purpose of [indicating] preponderance — this is the meaning. // 8]
Long life, memory, intelligence, health, youthful age,
excellence of radiance, complexion, and voice, bodily and sensory strength supreme, // Car_6,1.7

children.text: vāksiddhiṃ praṇatiṃ kāntiṃ labhate nā rasāyanāt /
children.translated_text: fulfillment of speech, respectability, beauty — one obtains [all these] through <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: lābhopāyo hi śastānāṃ rasādīnāṃ rasāyanam // Car_6,1.8
children.translated_text: For <s>rasāyana</s> is the means of obtaining the excellent <s>rasas</s> (vital essences) and other [tissues]. // Car_6,1.8
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He states the effects of <s>rasāyana</s> with 'long' etc. // 1
'Excellence' (<s>audārya</s>) should be connected with the three — radiance, complexion, and voice. // 2

children.text: vāksiddhiḥ yad ucyate tad avaśyaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: 'Fulfillment of speech' (<s>vāksiddhi</s>) means: what is spoken necessarily comes to pass — this is the meaning. // 3
'Respectability' (<s>praṇati</s>) means: being honored by the world. // 4

children.text: katham etad rasāyanena kriyata ityāha lābhetyādi rasādigrahaṇena smṛtyādayo 'pi gṛhyante // 5]
children.translated_text: How is this accomplished by <s>rasāyana</s>? — he answers with 'means of obtaining' etc. By the word '<s>rasa</s> etc.,' memory and the rest are also included. // 5]
That which produces a lineage of offspring, which gives immediate exhilaration,
by which one goes to women with excessive strength like a stallion, unobstructed; // Car_6,1.9
by which one becomes most dear to women, by which one is nourished;
by which even in old age the semen appears inexhaustible and fruitful; // Car_6,1.10

children.text: prabhūtaśākhaḥ śākhīva yena caityo yathā mahān /
children.translated_text: by which, like a tree with abundant branches, like a great sacred tree,
one becomes venerable, highly esteemed among people, with very many offspring; // Car_6,1.11
by which one obtains here the root of lineage, and hereafter infinity —

children.text: yaśaḥ śriyaṃ balaṃ puṣṭiṃ vājīkaraṇameva tat // Car_6,1.12
children.translated_text: fame, fortune, strength, and nourishment — that is verily <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (aphrodisiac therapy). // Car_6,1.12
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He states the effects of <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> with 'offspring' etc. // 1

children.text: apatyasaṃtānaḥ apatyaparamparā tena putrapautrakaram ityarthaḥ vājīkaraṇajanitācchukrāj jātaḥ putraḥ putrajananasamartho bhavatītyarthaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'Lineage of offspring' (<s>apatyasaṃtāna</s>) means a succession of offspring — thus it means producing sons and grandsons. The meaning is: a son born from semen generated by <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> becomes capable of producing [his own] sons. // 2
And the 'being most dear' here is because, having abundant semen, one engages in uninterrupted intercourse — as it is said:
Kings desire even an ugly warrior as servant;
women [desire] a husband who is sexually vigorous, foolish, and bold. // 3
Thus. // 4
'Is nourished' (<s>upacīyate</s>) means: attains robustness. // 5
'Inexhaustible' means: as if inexhaustible. // 6
'Fruitful' (<s>phalavat</s>) means: capable of producing conception. // 7
'Sacred tree' (<s>caitya</s>) means: a temple or sacred shrine. // 8
'Venerable' (<s>arcya</s>) means: worthy of worship. // 9
'Infinity' means: as if infinite — meaning a long lineage: this is the sense. // 10]

children.text: svasthasyorjaskaraṃ tv etad dvividhaṃ proktam auṣadham /
children.translated_text: This medicine promoting vigor in the healthy has been declared twofold.
That which causes the extirpation of diseases will be taught in [the section on] therapeutics. // Car_6,1.13
The purpose of therapeutics is just this much — that which is medicine for disorders,
and the method of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) first, and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (aphrodisiac therapy) also. // Car_6,1.14
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'In therapeutics' means: in the therapeutics of fever etc. // 1

children.text: nanu rasāyanavājīkaraṇe api jvarādicikitsite eva tat kiṃ viśiṣyocyate vakṣyate taccikitsite ityāha cikitsitārtha ityādi // 2
children.translated_text: Objection: since <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> too are included in the therapeutics of fever etc. [by virtue of treating disease], why is it separately said 'will be taught in therapeutics'? — he answers with 'the purpose of therapeutics' etc. // 2

children.text: satyaṃ rasāyanaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ ca jvarādivyādhiharatvāc cikitsitaśabdenocyata ityarthaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: True — <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> are indeed called by the term 'therapeutics' because of their fever-removing etc. property — this is the meaning. // 3

children.text: atha vyādhiharatvāccikitsite vaktavyatvācca rasāyanavājīkaraṇe kva nu vaktavye ityāha rasāyanetyādi // 4
children.translated_text: Now, since they are to be stated in therapeutics because of their disease-removing property — where then should <s>rasāyana</s> and <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> be taught? — he answers with '<s>rasāyana</s>' etc. // 4
'Method' (<s>vidhi</s>) means procedure — meaning the exposition of <s>rasāyana</s>. // 5
'First' (<s>agre</s>) means: immediately after [the disease-therapeutics]. // 6
'And <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> first' — the remainder is: will be expounded hereafter. // 7]
That which is contrary to medicine should be known as non-medicine.

children.text: tadasevyaṃ niṣevyaṃ tu pravakṣyāmi yadauṣadham // Car_6,1.15
children.translated_text: That is not to be used; but I shall teach the medicine that is to be employed. // Car_6,1.15
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He elaborates the non-medicine mentioned earlier with 'non-medicine' etc. // 1
'Contrary' means: producing disease-generating effects. // 2]
The sages know two modes of applying <s>rasāyanas</s>:
the <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> (indoor/hut-entry method) and the <s>vātātapika</s> (outdoor/wind-and-sun method). // Car_6,1.16
The procedure of the <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> (hut-entry) method shall first be instructed —
[it is] for kings, physicians, twice-born, virtuous persons of meritorious deeds. // Car_6,1.17
In a safe, excellent, well-equipped city,

children.text: diśi pūrvottarasyāṃ ca subhūmau kārayetkuṭīm // Car_6,1.18
children.translated_text: in the northeast direction, on good ground, one should have a hut constructed — // Car_6,1.18
endowed with adequate breadth and height, having three inner chambers, with small windows,
with thick walls, comfortable in all seasons, well-finished, and pleasing to the mind; // Car_6,1.19
inaccessible to undesirable sounds and other [stimuli], free from women,
equipped with desired provisions, with physicians, medicines, and Brahmins ready at hand. // Car_6,1.20
Then, during the northern course [of the sun], in the bright fortnight, on a day honored by [auspicious] <s>tithi</s> and <s>nakṣatra</s>,
at an auspicious time with favorable planetary configuration, having had [his hair] shaved, // Car_6,1.21
having established fortitude, memory, and strength, with faith, concentrated,

children.text: vidhūya mānasāndoṣān maitrīṃ bhūteṣu cintayan // Car_6,1.22
children.translated_text: having dispelled mental faults, contemplating friendliness toward all beings, // Car_6,1.22
having first worshipped the deities and circumambulated the twice-born,

children.text: devagobrāhmaṇān kṛtvā tatas tāṃ praviśet kuṭīm // Car_6,1.23
children.translated_text: having honored gods, cows, and Brahmins — then he should enter that hut. // Car_6,1.23

children.text: tasyāṃ saṃśodhanaiḥ śuddhaḥ sukhī jātabalaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: In that [hut], purified by cleansing procedures, comfortable, having regained strength,
he should employ the <s>rasāyana</s>. I shall now teach that purification [procedure]. // Car_6,1.24
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'<s>Kuṭīprāveśika</s>' means: that which is performed by entering a hut. // 1
'<s>Vātātapika</s>' means: that which is performed even while exposed to wind and sun. // 2

children.text: trigarbhāṃ prathamamekaṃ gṛhaṃ tasyābhyantare dvitīyam evaṃ trigarbhāstrayo garbhā antarāṇi yasyāṃ sā trigarbhāmiti antas triprakoṣṭhām // 3
children.translated_text: 'Having three inner chambers' (<s>trigarbhā</s>) — the first is one room, within that a second, [and within that a third] — thus 'three chambers' means three inner compartments within it — meaning having three inner enclosures. // 3
'With small windows' (<s>sūkṣmalocanā</s>) means: with small door-apertures and lattice-windows. // 4
'In the bright [fortnight]' (<s>śukle</s>) means: in the bright half of the month. // 5
'With physicians etc. ready at hand' means: [a hut] in which physicians etc. are prepared — so described. // 6
'Honored by <s>tithi</s> and <s>nakṣatra</s>' means: honored on account of the conjunction of auspicious <s>tithi</s> and <s>nakṣatra</s>. // 7
'Having had [hair] shaved' (<s>kṛtavāpana</s>) means: having had the tonsure performed. // 8
'Mental faults' means: desire, anger, and the like. // 9
'By cleansing procedures' means: by emesis, purgation, enema, and nasal purgation. // 10
'Comfortable' (<s>sukhī</s>) means: free from disease. // 11

children.text: jātabala iti saṃśodhanāpahṛtamalatayā saṃsarjanādikrameṇa punar jātabalaḥ // 12
children.translated_text: 'Having regained strength' (<s>jātabala</s>) means: having strength restored through the <s>saṃsarjana</s> (graduated diet) regimen after the impurities were removed by purification. // 12

children.text: yadyapīha saṃśodhanair iti bahuvacanaprayogāt sarvāṇyeva saṃśodhanāni saṃmatāni tathāpīha rasāyane viśeṣeṇa yaugikatvāddharītakyādiprayoga evoktaḥ anye tu harītakyādiprayogeṇaiva paraṃ saṃśodhanaṃ kartavyam ityāhuḥ saṃśodhanair iti bahuvacanaṃ punar yāvacchuddher harītakyādiprayogasyaiva karaṇaṃ darśayati // 13]
children.translated_text: Although here the plural 'by cleansing procedures' admits all purification methods, nevertheless in the context of <s>rasāyana</s> specifically, because of its appropriateness, only the use of <s>harītakī</s> etc. is prescribed. Others, however, say: the supreme purification should be done only through the use of <s>harītakī</s> etc. The plural 'by cleansing procedures' indicates that the application of <s>harītakī</s> etc. should be repeated until complete purification [is achieved]. // 13]
Powders of <s>harītakīs</s>, rock-salt, <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry), jaggery,

children.text: vacāṃ viḍaṅgaṃ rajanīṃ pippalīṃ viśvabheṣajam // Car_6,1.25
children.translated_text: <s>vacā</s> (calamus), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric), <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), and <s>viśvabheṣaja</s> (dry ginger) — // Car_6,1.25
the person should drink with warm water, having been prepared with oleation and sudation.
Then, for [the person] whose body has been purified, and for whom the <s>saṃsarjana</s> (graduated diet) has been completed — // Car_6,1.26

children.text: trirātraṃ yāvakaṃ dadyāt pañcāhaṃ vāpi sarpiṣā /
children.translated_text: one should give barley-gruel for three days, or for five days with ghee,

children.text: saptāhaṃ vā purāṇasya yāvacchuddhestu varcasaḥ // Car_6,1.27
children.translated_text: or for seven days with aged [ghee] — until the feces are purified. // Car_6,1.27
Then, knowing him to be of purified bowels, one should administer the <s>rasāyana</s>,
knowing [his] age, constitution, and habitual suitability — whichever [<s>rasāyana</s>] is appropriate for whomever. // Car_6,1.28
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Barley-gruel' (<s>yāvaka</s>) means: food made of barley. // 1
The three alternatives of three days etc. correspond to mild, moderate, and strong purification respectively. // 2]
One should know <s>harītakī</s> — possessed of five tastes, hot, free from saltiness, auspicious,
<s>doṣa</s>-regulating, light, appetizing, and digestive; // Car_6,1.29

children.text: āyuṣyāṃ pauṣṭikīṃ dhanyāṃ vayasaḥ sthāpanīṃ parām /
children.translated_text: promoting longevity, nourishing, auspicious, supremely age-preserving,
pacifying all diseases, bestowing intelligence, sensory strength, and power; // Car_6,1.30
<s>Kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of gases), <s>śoṣa</s> (consumption), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), <s>mada</s> (intoxication),
<s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>grahaṇīdoṣa</s> (malabsorption), chronic intermittent fever, // Car_6,1.31
heart disease with headache, chronic diarrhea, loss of appetite,

children.text: kāsaṃ pramehamānāhaṃ plīhānam udaraṃ navam // Car_6,1.32
children.translated_text: cough, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), distension, splenic disease, fresh abdominal disease, // Car_6,1.32
excessive <s>kapha</s> secretion, hoarseness, discoloration, jaundice, worms,
edema, <s>tamaka</s> (asthma), vomiting, impotence, and bodily lassitude, // Car_6,1.33
various obstructions of channels, coating upon the heart and chest,
and confusion of memory and intellect — one conquers quickly [all these] with <s>harītakī</s>. // Car_6,1.34
Those with indigestion, those eating dry food, those emaciated by women, wine, or poison —

children.text: severan nābhayām ete kṣuttṛṣṇoṣṇārditāś ca ye // Car_6,1.35
children.translated_text: and those afflicted by hunger, thirst, and heat [should use them] applied at the navel. // Car_6,1.35
One should know the same qualities and actions in <s>āmalakī</s> (emblic myrobalan)

children.text: yānyuktāni harītakyā vīryasya tu viparyayaḥ // Car_6,1.36
children.translated_text: as were stated for <s>harītakī</s>, but with opposite <s>vīrya</s> (potency). // Car_6,1.36
Therefore, by such actions [which are] like the nectar of immortality,
the physician should consider <s>harītakī</s> and <s>āmalaka</s> as the most excellent among [all fruits]. // Car_6,1.37
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: yadyapi dravyāntarāṇi daśavarṣaśatāyuṣkararasāyanādhikṛtāni santi tathāpi harītakyāmalake eva rogaharatvāyuṣkaratvarūpobhayadharmayogād adhyāyādau guṇakarmabhyāmucyete tatrāpi yadyapi āmalakaṃ vayaḥsthāpanānām ityuktaṃ tathāpi rogaharatve harītakī prakarṣavatīti kṛtvā harītaky agre 'bhihitā // 1
children.translated_text: Although other substances are mentioned in the context of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenation) that bestow a lifespan of a thousand years, nonetheless <s>harītakī</s> and <s>āmalaka</s> alone — possessing both properties of curing diseases and promoting longevity — are praised at the beginning of the chapter for their qualities and actions. Moreover, although <s>āmalaka</s> is said to be foremost among '<s>vayaḥsthāpana</s>' (age-stabilizing) substances, <s>harītakī</s> is mentioned first because it excels in disease-removal. // 1

children.text: harītakyādiṣu pañcarasatvādyutpādo 'dṛṣṭavaśād bhūtasaṃniveśaviśeṣaprabhāvakṛtaḥ tena nātropapattayaḥ kramante // 2
children.translated_text: The production of five <s>rasas</s> (tastes) etc. in <s>harītakī</s> and other [fruits] is due to the power of a special configuration of elements through unseen [karmic] forces; therefore, rational explanations do not apply here. // 2
'<s>Śivā</s>' means auspicious, because it possesses excellent qualities. // 3
'Alleviating all diseases' — through combination, processing, etc. // 4
Even after declaring [it] to be a destroyer of all diseases, stating that it destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) etc. is to show that it especially destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> etc. // 5

children.text: pravartakatve 'pyatīsāragrahaṇīharatvaṃ vibaddhadoṣapravartakatayā jñeyaṃ yaduktaṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ vibaddhaṃ vā saśūlaṃ yo 'tisāryete // 6
children.translated_text: Although it is a purgative, its ability to cure <s>atīsāra</s> (diarrhea) and <s>grahaṇī</s> (malabsorption) should be understood as being through the purgation of obstructed <s>doṣas</s>. As has been stated: 'One who passes stool little by little, or [stool that is] obstructed, with pain — // 6
him one should purge with pastes of <s>Abhayā</s> (harītakī) and <s>pippalī</s>, [administered] comfortably warm.' // 7
Even after stating that it bestows intelligence and memory, mentioning that it cures confusion of memory and intelligence is to show its specific power therein. // 8

children.text: vīryasya tu viparyaya ityanenāmalakasya śītavīryatvam uktam // 9
children.translated_text: 'But with opposite <s>vīrya</s>' — by this, the cold <s>vīrya</s> (potency) of <s>āmalaka</s> is stated. // 9
'Most excellent' (<s>śasyāni</s>) means the fruits that are without stones. // 10]
The <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas), the best of mountains, is the supreme land of medicinal herbs.
Therefore, one should gather the fruits produced there, and only those that ripen in their proper season, // Car_6,1.38
filled with <s>rasa</s> (juice) and <s>vīrya</s> (potency) in their respective seasons, according to the proper method,
and nourished by sun, wind, shade, and water, // Car_6,1.39
which are uneaten [by insects], not putrid, free from blemishes, and free from poison.

children.text: teṣāṃ prayogaṃ vakṣyāmi phalānāṃ karma cottamam // Car_6,1.40
children.translated_text: I shall now describe the application and the supreme actions of these fruits. // Car_6,1.40
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: yadyapi himavān auṣadhabhūmīnām ityuktaṃ tathāpi rasāyane himavatprabhavāṇyeva bheṣajāni grāhyāṇīti darśayitum auṣadhīnām ityāhābhidhānam // 1
children.translated_text: Although [the general statement] '<s>Himavat</s> is [the best] among the lands of herbs' has been stated, to show that specifically for <s>rasāyana</s>, medicines originating from <s>Himavat</s> alone should be gathered, the statement 'of herbs' is made. // 1
'In their respective seasons' means at the time of the ripening of the fruits — this is the meaning. // 2

children.text: yathāvidhīti yathā bheṣajagrahaṇaṃ maṅgaladevatārcanādipūrvakaṃ syāt tathāvaśyaṃ rasāyane kartavyam // 3
children.translated_text: 'According to the proper method' means that just as the gathering of medicines should be preceded by auspicious rites, worship of deities, etc., so it must certainly be done in [the context of] <s>rasāyana</s>. // 3
'Free from poison' (<s>agadāni</s>) — by this he shows that the fruit should be free from defects [caused by] wind, fire, etc. // 4]
Portions of ten <s>palas</s> each of the five <s>pañcamūlas</s> (five groups of five roots),
and a thousand <s>harītakī</s> [fruits], and three times that amount of fresh <s>āmalaka</s>, // Car_6,1.41
<s>Vidārīgandhā</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Nidigdhikā</s>,
one should know the group beginning with <s>Vidārīgandhā</s> and ending with <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s> as the fifth, // Car_6,1.42
<s>Bilva</s>, <s>Agnimantha</s>, <s>Śyonāka</s>, <s>Kāśmarya</s>, and <s>Pāṭalā</s>,

children.text: punarnavāṃ śūrpaparṇyau balām eraṇḍameva ca // Car_6,1.43
children.translated_text: <s>Punarnavā</s>, two <s>Śūrpaparṇīs</s>, <s>Balā</s>, and <s>Eraṇḍa</s> as well, // Car_6,1.43
<s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, and <s>Śatāvarī</s>,
and the roots of <s>Śara</s>, <s>Ikṣu</s>, <s>Darbha</s>, <s>Kāśa</s>, and <s>Śāli</s> rice. // Car_6,1.44
Thus, one should prepare portions of these five groups of five roots as stated,
and cook everything in ten times [its quantity of] water. // Car_6,1.45
When reduced to one-tenth, strain and collect that decoction,

children.text: harītakīśca tāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāṇyāmalakāni ca // Car_6,1.46
children.translated_text: and add all those <s>harītakīs</s> and all those <s>āmalakas</s>. // Car_6,1.46
All those fruits, with stones removed, should be crushed with pestles,
immersed in that decoction, and the following powders should be added: // Car_6,1.47
of <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> (Centella), <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper), <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>Plava</s>,
<s>Musta</s> with <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood) and <s>Aguru</s> (aloe wood), // Car_6,1.48
<s>Madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>Haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>Vacā</s> (calamus), and <s>Kanaka</s> (nāgakeśara),

children.text: bhāgāṃś catuṣpalān kṛtvā sūkṣmailāyās tvacas tathā // Car_6,1.49
children.translated_text: portions of four <s>palas</s> each, along with fine <s>Elā</s> (cardamom) and <s>Tvak</s> (cinnamon bark). // Car_6,1.49
A thousand [<s>palas</s>] of <s>Sitopalā</s> (rock sugar), powdered, with one <s>tulā</s> (hundred <s>palas</s>) extra,

children.text: tailasya hy āḍhakaṃ tatra dadyāt trīṇi ca sarpiṣaḥ // Car_6,1.50
children.translated_text: and one <s>āḍhaka</s> (a measure) of oil should be added, and three [<s>āḍhakas</s>] of ghee. // Car_6,1.50
All of that should be cooked in a vessel of <s>Udumbara</s> (fig wood / copper) over gentle fire,

children.text: jñātvā lehyamadagdhaṃ ca śītaṃ kṣaudreṇa saṃsṛjet // Car_6,1.51
children.translated_text: and when it is known to be a [proper] linctus and unburnt, it should be cooled and mixed with honey. // Car_6,1.51
The measure of honey should be half the [total] fats. All of that, in a ghee-coated vessel,

children.text: tiṣṭhet saṃmūrchitaṃ tasya mātrāṃ kāle prayojayet // Car_6,1.52
children.translated_text: should be set aside after thorough blending. The dose should be administered at the proper time, // Car_6,1.52
a dose being such that it does not obstruct one's [single] meal with regard to digestion.

children.text: ṣaṣṭikaḥ payasā cātra jīrṇe bhojanamiṣyate // Car_6,1.53
children.translated_text: When digested, <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk is the prescribed food. // Car_6,1.53
The <s>Vaikhānasas</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, and other ascetics rich in <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
having consumed this <s>rasāyana</s>, became possessed of limitless lifespans. // Car_6,1.54
Casting off their aged bodies, they attained supreme youthful age,
free from drowsiness, fatigue, and breathlessness, without illness, and with concentrated minds. // Car_6,1.55
Endowed with intellect, memory, and strength, the ascetics rich in <s>tapas</s>,
pursued sacred study, austerity, and celibacy with utmost dedication. // Car_6,1.56
One who desires longevity should employ this <s>Brāhma Rasāyana</s> (divine rejuvenation),

children.text: dīrgham āyur vayaś cāgryaṃ kāmāṃśceṣṭān samaśnute // Car_6,1.57
children.translated_text: and attains long life, supreme youth, and all desired objects. // Car_6,1.57
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: pañcānām ityādau pratidravyaṃ daśapalabhāgagrahaṇam uktaṃ hi jātūkarṇe iti pañca pañcamūlāni teṣāṃ pratidravyaṃ daśapalāni iti // 1
children.translated_text: In 'of the five' etc. — the taking of a ten-<s>pala</s> portion per substance is stated. As said by <s>Jātūkarṇa</s>: 'Five groups of five roots — of these, ten <s>palas</s> of each substance.' // 1
'A thousand <s>harītakīs</s>' means a thousand <s>harītakī</s> fruits. // 2
'<s>Śūrpaparṇīs</s>' are <s>Mudgaparṇī</s> and <s>Māṣaparṇī</s>. // 3
'<s>Vīrā</s>' is the plant called <s>Jālandhara</s>. // 4
'Pestle' (<s>kūrcana</s>) means an instrument for crushing — such as a stone slab, mortar, etc. // 5
'Having immersed' (<s>vinīya</s>) means having placed into. // 6
'<s>Plava</s>' is <s>Kaivartamustaka</s> (a type of sedge). // 7
'<s>Kanaka</s>' is <s>Nāgakeśara</s> (Mesua ferrea). // 8
'<s>Tvak</s>' (bark) is <s>Guḍatvak</s> (cinnamon bark). // 9
'Of <s>Udumbara</s>' means made of copper. // 10
'Half the fats' means half the [combined quantity of] ghee and oil. // 11
'One' [meal] means one afternoon meal. // 12]

children.text: yathoktaguṇānām āmalakānāṃ sahasraṃ piṣṭasvedanavidhinā payasa ūṣmaṇā susvinnamanātapaśuṣkamanasthi cūrṇayet /
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>āmalakas</s> of the aforementioned qualities should be steamed by the method of steaming pressed [cakes] — [i.e.,] by placing them on grass etc. over a pot filled with water and steaming with the heat of milk — dried without sun-exposure, de-stoned, and powdered.

children.text: tadāmalakasahasrasvarasaparipītaṃ sthirāpunarnavājīvantīnāgabalābrahmasuvarcalāmaṇḍūkaparṇīśatāvarīśaṅkhapuṣpīpippalīvacāviḍaṅgasvayaṅguptāmṛtā candanāgurumadhukamadhūkapuṣpotpalapadmamālatīyuvatīyūthikācūrṇāṣṭabhāgasaṃyuktaṃ punar nāgabalāsahasrapalasvarasaparipītam anātapaśuṣkaṃ dviguṇitasarpiṣā kṣaudrasarpiṣā vā kṣudraguḍākṛtiṃ kṛtvā śucau dṛḍhe ghṛtabhāvite kumbhe bhasmarāśer adhaḥ sthāpayed antarbhūmeḥ pakṣaṃ kṛtarakṣāvidhānam atharvavedavidā pakṣātyaye coddhṛtya kanakarajatatāmrapravālakālāyasacūrṇāṣṭabhāgasaṃyuktam ardhakarṣavṛddhyā yathoktena vidhinā prātaḥ prātaḥ prayuñjāno 'gnibalam abhisamīkṣya jīrṇe ca ṣaṣṭikaṃ payasā sasarpiṣkam upasevamāno yathoktān guṇān samaśnuta iti // Car_6,1.58
children.translated_text: That [powder], saturated with the juice of those thousand <s>āmalakas</s>, combined with an eighth part of the powders of <s>Sthirā</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Nāgabalā</s>, <s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s>, <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Svayaṅguptā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Aguru</s>, <s>Madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>Madhūka</s> flowers, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Yuvatī</s>, and <s>Yūthikā</s>, and again saturated with the juice of a thousand <s>palas</s> of <s>Nāgabalā</s>, dried without sun-exposure, [mixed] with twice [the amount of] ghee — or with honey and ghee — made into the form of small <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery balls), and placed in a clean, strong, ghee-anointed jar underground beneath a heap of ashes for a fortnight, with protective rites performed by one versed in the <s>Atharvaveda</s>. At the end of the fortnight, having taken it out and combined it with an eighth part of the powders of gold, silver, copper, coral, and iron, [the dose] should be administered each morning with increments of half a <s>karṣa</s>, by the prescribed method, after assessing one's digestive strength; and when digested, one should take <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee — [by this method] one attains the aforementioned qualities. // Car_6,1.58
This divine <s>Brāhma Rasāyana</s>, served by the great sages —
the one who employs it becomes free from disease, long-lived, and supremely strong. // Car_6,1.59
Beloved of the people, successful in all aims, with radiance equal to the sun and moon,

children.text: śrutaṃ dhārayate sattvamārṣaṃ cāsya pravartate // Car_6,1.60
children.translated_text: he retains learning and memory, and a disposition of the sages arises in him. // Car_6,1.60
With the essence of mountains for his body, and vigor equal to the wind,

children.text: sa bhavatyaviṣaṃ cāsya gātre saṃpadyate viṣam // Car_6,1.61
children.translated_text: he becomes [invulnerable] — poison touching his body becomes non-toxic. // Car_6,1.61
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: piṣṭasvedanavidhineti yathā piṣṭakaṃ toyaparipūritapātroparidattatṛṇādisaṃsthitaṃ svedyate tathā tat svedanīyam ityarthaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: 'By the method of steaming pressed [cakes]' — just as a pressed cake placed on grass etc. over a pot filled with water is steamed, so that [<s>āmalaka</s>] should be steamed — this is the meaning. // 1
'Saturated with its own juice' means processed (bhāvita) with its own juice. // 2
<s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s> and other herbs will be described in the <s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s> [chapter]. // 3
'<s>Yuvatī</s>' is <s>Navamālikā</s> (jasmine). // 4
'An eighth part' — one-eighth is the eighth part. // 5
'In the form of small <s>guḍa</s>' means in the form of <s>phāṇita</s> (inspissated juice). // 6
'With increments of half a <s>karṣa</s>' — one should increase starting from half a <s>karṣa</s>. // 7
'By the prescribed method' means by the method of entering the rejuvenation hut (<s>kuṭīprāveśika</s>). // 8
'The aforementioned qualities' means those qualities recited in the preceding passage on the results [of the practice]. // 9

children.text: dharaṇīdharasāra iti uṣṭramukhavat tena dharaṇīdharāḥ parvatās teṣāṃ sāro lauhaṃ tadvatsāra ityarthaḥ // 10
children.translated_text: 'With the essence of mountains' — like a camel's face [i.e., a compound reading]: mountains (<s>dharaṇīdharas</s>) are the peaks, their essence is iron; having an essence like that — this is the meaning. // 10
'Non-toxic' (<s>aviṣam</s>) — poison becomes non-transforming. // 11]
<s>Bilva</s>, <s>Agnimantha</s>, <s>Śyonāka</s>, <s>Kāśmarya</s>, <s>Pāṭalī</s>, <s>Balā</s>,

children.text: parṇyaś catasraḥ pippalyaḥ śvadaṃṣṭrā bṛhatīdvayam // Car_6,1.62
children.translated_text: four <s>Parṇīs</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Śvadaṃṣṭrā</s>, and two <s>Bṛhatīs</s>, // Car_6,1.62
<s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Tāmalakī</s>, <s>Drākṣā</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Aguru</s>,

children.text: abhayā cāmṛtā ṛddhir jīvakarṣabhakau śaṭī // Car_6,1.63
children.translated_text: <s>Abhayā</s> (harītakī), <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, <s>Śaṭī</s>, // Car_6,1.63
<s>Musta</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Śailā</s>, <s>Candana</s>, <s>Utpala</s>,
<s>Vidārī</s>, <s>Vṛṣa</s> roots, <s>Kākolī</s>, and <s>Kākanāsikā</s>, // Car_6,1.64
one <s>pala</s> each of these, and five hundred [fruits] of <s>āmalaka</s>.
One should add them all together and cook in a <s>droṇa</s> (large measure) of water. // Car_6,1.65
When these herbs are known to have yielded their essence, then that decoction
and those <s>āmalakas</s>, having been removed and de-stoned, [should be processed] with oil and ghee — // Car_6,1.66
twelve <s>palas</s> [of oil and ghee combined] — fried, and then adding half a <s>tulā</s>
of purified <s>Matsyaṇḍikā</s> (sugar candy), the physician should cook it properly like a linctus. // Car_6,1.67
Six <s>palas</s> of honey should be added when the preparation has cooled,
and four <s>palas</s> of <s>Tugākṣīrī</s> (bamboo manna), and two <s>palas</s> of <s>Pippalī</s>, // Car_6,1.68
and one <s>pala</s> of <s>Tvak</s> (cinnamon), <s>Elā</s> (cardamom), <s>Pattra</s> (bay leaf), and <s>Kesara</s> (saffron/stamens).
This is the <s>Cyavanaprāśa</s>, declared to be the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>. // Car_6,1.69
It is specifically taught as the destroyer of <s>kāsa</s> (cough) and <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea),
and as a body-builder for the emaciated, the injured, the elderly, and children. // Car_6,1.70
It removes loss of voice, chest diseases, heart diseases, <s>vātaśoṇita</s> (gout),
thirst, and disorders of <s>śukra</s> (semen). // Car_6,1.71
The dose should be that which does not obstruct one's food intake.
By the use of this, <s>Cyavana</s>, though very aged, became young again. // Car_6,1.72
Intellect, memory, bodily lustre, freedom from disease, excellence of lifespan, strength of the senses,

children.text: strīṣu praharṣaṃ paramagnivṛddhiṃ varṇaprasādaṃ pavanānulomyam // Car_6,1.73
children.translated_text: delight with women, supreme increase of digestive fire, fair complexion, and the downward movement of <s>Vāta</s> — // Car_6,1.73

children.text: rasāyanasyāsya naraḥ prayogāl labheta jīrṇo 'pi kuṭīpraveśāt /
children.translated_text: these a man obtains from the use of this <s>rasāyana</s>, even when aged, through entering the rejuvenation hut;

children.text: jarākṛtaṃ rūpamapāsya sarvaṃ bibharti rūpaṃ navayauvanasya // Car_6,1.74
children.translated_text: casting off all the form wrought by old age, he bears the form of fresh youth. // Car_6,1.74
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: parṇyaś catasra iti śālaparṇī pṛśniparṇī mudgaparṇī māṣaparṇī ca // 1
children.translated_text: 'Four <s>Parṇīs</s>' are <s>Śālaparṇī</s>, <s>Pṛśniparṇī</s>, <s>Mudgaparṇī</s>, and <s>Māṣaparṇī</s>. // 1
'<s>Tāmalakī</s>' is <s>Bhūmyāmalakī</s> (Phyllanthus). // 2
'<s>Kākanāsā</s>' is <s>Nāsāphalā</s>; others [say] <s>Kākatuṇḍaka</s>. // 3
'Having yielded their essence' — this occurs here when the water is reduced to one-fourth. // 4
'De-stoned' (<s>niṣkulam</s>) means having the stones removed. // 5

children.text: tailasarpiṣoriti samāsanirdeśād ubhābhyāmeva dvādaśapalāni na pṛthak pṛthak // 6
children.translated_text: 'Of oil and ghee' — since stated as a compound, twelve <s>palas</s> [is the total] of both together, not twelve <s>palas</s> of each separately. // 6
'<s>Matsyaṇḍikā</s>' is a mass of <s>khaṇḍa</s> (crystallized sugar). // 7
Here, even though honey and ghee are in equal [six-<s>pala</s>] measures, because they are combined with other substances, there is no [dietary] incompatibility. // 8]

children.text: athāmalakaharītakīnām āmalakavibhītakānāṃ harītakīvibhītakānām āmalakaharītakīvibhītakānāṃ vā palāśatvagavanaddhānāṃ mṛdāvaliptānāṃ kukūlasvinnānām akulakānāṃ palasahasramulūkhale saṃpothya dadhighṛtamadhupalalatailaśarkarāsaṃyuktaṃ bhakṣayed anannabhug yathoktena vidhinā tasyānte yavāgvādibhiḥ pratyavasthāpanam abhyaṅgotsādanaṃ sarpiṣā yavacūrṇaiśca ayaṃca rasāyanaprayogaprakarṣo dvistāvadagnibalam abhisamīkṣya pratibhojanaṃ yūṣeṇa payasā vā ṣaṣṭikaḥ sasarpiṣkaḥ ataḥ paraṃ yathāsukhavihāraḥ kāmabhakṣyaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Then, [taking] <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Harītakī</s>, or <s>Āmalaka</s> and <s>Vibhītaka</s>, or <s>Harītakī</s> and <s>Vibhītaka</s>, or <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Harītakī</s>, and <s>Vibhītaka</s> — wrapped in the bark of <s>Palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa), coated with clay, slow-roasted over cow-dung fire, with the stones removed — one should pound a thousand <s>palas</s> [of them] in a mortar and eat [the preparation] mixed with yogurt, ghee, honey, sesame powder (<s>palala</s>), oil, and sugar, taking no other food, following the prescribed method. At the end [of this course], gradual dietary resumption (<s>pratyavasthāpana</s>) should be done with thin gruel (<s>yavāgū</s>) etc. Massage and rubbing (<s>utsādana</s>) with ghee and barley flour [should be performed]. And this is the maximum duration of the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen — twice [the initial duration], having assessed the digestive strength. At each meal, <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with ghee, accompanied by soup or milk. After that, one may live comfortably and eat as one pleases.

children.text: anena prayogeṇarṣayaḥ punar yuvatvam avāpur babhūvuś cānekavarṣaśatajīvino nirvikārāḥ paraśarīrabuddhīndriyabalasamuditāś ceruś cātyantaniṣṭhayā tapaḥ // Car_6,1.75
children.translated_text: By this regimen, the sages regained youth, lived for many hundreds of years free from disease, endowed with supreme bodily, mental, and sensory strength, and practiced austerities with utmost steadfastness. // Car_6,1.75
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'<s>Kukūlaka</s>' is cow-dung fire. // 1
'Without stones' (<s>akulaka</s>) means without seeds. // 2

children.text: dravyādīnāmatra mānaṃ noktaṃ tena pradhānasya cūrṇasya dadhyādibhir militaiḥ samānamānatvaṃ kiṃvā pratyekameva dadhyādīnāṃ cūrṇasamatvam // 3
children.translated_text: The measure of the ingredients is not stated here; therefore, the principal powder is equal in measure to the combined yogurt etc., or alternatively, each of yogurt etc. is equal to the powder individually. // 3
'<s>Palala</s>' is sesame powder. // 4
The word 'eat' (<s>bhakṣayet</s>) is appropriate even for an electuary, since it refers merely to the act of consuming a small quantity. // 5
'Taking no other food' means not eating any other food whatsoever. // 6
'At its end' means at the time of discontinuing this regimen. // 7

children.text: pratyavasthāpanamiti yavāgvādikramaviśeṣaṇaṃ tena prayogānte yadā annasaṃsarjanaṃ kartavyaṃ tadā yavāgvādikrameṇety uktasyārthasya pratyavasthāpanaṃ kriyata ityarthaḥ // 8
children.translated_text: 'Gradual dietary resumption' (<s>pratyavasthāpana</s>) qualifies 'with gruel etc.' — thus when dietary resumption is to be done at the end of the regimen, it is done in the sequence of gruel etc. — this is the meaning. // 8
'With soup or milk' — the alternative depends on the digestive strength. // 9]

children.text: harītakyāmalakavibhītakapañcapañcamūlaniryūhe pippalīmadhukamadhūkakākolīkṣīrakākolyātmaguptājīvakarṣabhakakṣīraśuklākalkasamprayuktena vidārīsvarasena kṣīrāṣṭaguṇasamprayuktena ca sarpiṣaḥ kumbhaṃ sādhayitvā prayuñjāno 'gnibalasamāṃ mātrāṃ jīrṇe ca kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ śāliṣaṣṭikam uṣṇodakānupānam aśnañjarāvyādhipāpābhicāravyapagatabhayaḥ śarīrendriyabuddhibalam atulam upalabhyāpratihatasarvārambhaḥ paramāyur avāpnuyāt // Car_6,1.76
children.translated_text: In a decoction of <s>Harītakī</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Vibhītaka</s>, and the five groups of five roots (<s>pañcapañcamūla</s>), one should prepare a <s>kumbha</s>-measure of ghee combined with a paste of <s>Pippalī</s>, <s>Madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>Madhūka</s> (Mahua), <s>Kākolī</s>, <s>Kṣīrakākolī</s>, <s>Ātmaguptā</s> (Mucuna), <s>Jīvaka</s>, <s>Ṛṣabhaka</s>, and <s>Kṣīraśuklā</s> (milk <s>Vidārī</s>), with the juice of <s>Vidārī</s> (Pueraria), and combined with eight parts of milk. Taking this [ghee] in a dose proportionate to one's digestive fire, and after digestion eating <s>Śāli</s> or <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee, followed by warm water — one becomes free from fear of aging, disease, sin, and sorcery, attains incomparable bodily, sensory, and mental strength, succeeds in all undertakings without obstruction, and attains the maximum lifespan. // Car_6,1.76
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
Here, among the <s>Harītakī</s> etc. [ingredients], '<s>Kṣīraśuklā</s>' is the milk <s>Vidārī</s> (Ipomoea digitata). // 1

children.text: atra harītakyādikvāthasya tv eko bhāgaḥ kṣīrasyāṣṭau bhāgāḥ sarpiṣa eko bhāgaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: Here, one part of the <s>Harītakī</s> etc. decoction, eight parts of milk, [and] one part of ghee [are the proportions]. // 2
A '<s>kumbha</s>' is two <s>droṇas</s>. // 3

children.text: vacanaṃ hi droṇastu dviguṇaḥ śūrpo vijñeyaḥ kumbha eva ca iti // 4]
children.translated_text: For the statement is: 'A <s>droṇa</s> doubled is to be known as a <s>śūrpa</s>, which is indeed a <s>kumbha</s>.' // 4]

children.text: harītakyāmalakavibhītakaharidrāsthirābalāviḍaṅgāmṛtavallīviśvabheṣajamadhukapippalīsomavalkasiddhena kṣīrasarpiṣā madhuśarkarābhyāmapi ca saṃnīyāmalakasvarasaśataparipītam āmalakacūrṇam ayaścūrṇacaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ pāṇitalamātraṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ prāśya yathoktena vidhinā sāyaṃ mudgayūṣeṇa payasā vā sasarpiṣkaṃ śāliṣaṣṭikānnam aśnīyāt trivarṣaprayogādasya varṣaśatam ajaraṃ vayas tiṣṭhati śrutam avatiṣṭhate sarvāmayāḥ praśāmyanti viṣamaviṣaṃ bhavati gātre gātram aśmavat sthirībhavati adhṛṣyo bhūtānāṃ bhavati // Car_6,1.77
children.translated_text: Ghee prepared with milk [and] the [decoction of] <s>Harītakī</s>, <s>Āmalaka</s>, <s>Vibhītaka</s>, <s>Haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>Sthirā</s>, <s>Balā</s>, <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Amṛtavallī</s> (<s>Guḍūcī</s>), <s>Viśvabheṣaja</s> (ginger), <s>Madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>Pippalī</s>, and <s>Somavalkā</s> — combined with honey and sugar, and <s>Āmalaka</s> powder soaked a hundred times in <s>Āmalaka</s> juice, mixed with one-fourth part of iron powder — a palm-measure of this should be taken every morning. Following the prescribed method, in the evening one should eat <s>Śāli</s> or <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with ghee and <s>Mudga</s> (green gram) soup or milk. By using this for three years, one's lifespan remains a hundred years without aging, learning is retained, all diseases are pacified, poison becomes ineffective on the body, the body becomes firm as stone, and one becomes invincible to supernatural beings. // Car_6,1.77
Just as <s>Amṛta</s> (ambrosia) is for the immortals, just as <s>Sudhā</s> (nectar) is for the serpents (<s>Bhogavat</s>),
so was the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen for the great sages of old. // Car_6,1.78

children.text: na jarāṃ na ca daurbalyaṃ nāturyaṃ nidhanaṃ na ca /
children.translated_text: Neither aging, nor weakness, nor haste, nor death
did those devoted to <s>rasāyana</s> in ancient times encounter, [even over] thousands of years. // Car_6,1.79

children.text: na kevalaṃ dīrghamihāyuraśnute rasāyanaṃ yo vidhivanniṣevate /
children.translated_text: Not only does one who follows the <s>rasāyana</s> according to the prescribed method attain long life here,

children.text: gatiṃ sa devarṣiniṣevitāṃ śubhāṃ prapadyate brahma tatheti cākṣayam // Car_6,1.80
children.translated_text: but he also reaches the auspicious path frequented by divine sages, and likewise the imperishable <s>Brahman</s>. // Car_6,1.80

children.text:
[{Āyurvedadīpikā}
  amṛtavallī guḍūcī /
  somavalkaḥ viṭkhadiraḥ /
  kṣīrasarpiḥ kṣīrasamutthitasarpiḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:] '<s>Amṛtavallī</s>' is <s>Guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora cordifolia). '<s>Somavalkā</s>' is <s>Viṭkhadira</s> (cutch). '<s>Kṣīra-sarpiḥ</s>' is ghee derived from milk.

children.text: ayaścūrṇasya caturtho bhāgaḥ yata etadayaścūrṇaṃ caturthabhāgamata ekasmin prayoge jātūkarṇena ayaścūrṇapādayuktam iti kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'One-fourth part of iron powder' — i.e., this iron powder is one-fourth in proportion. Thus in a single preparation, <s>Jātūkarṇa</s> has specified 'combined with one-fourth iron powder.' // [continued]

children.text: amarāṇāmamṛtaṃ jarādiharaṃ nāgānāṃ ca sudhā jarāmaraṇaharī ityubhayopādānaṃ dṛṣṭānte /
children.translated_text: '<s>Amṛta</s> of the immortals' removes aging etc., and '<s>Sudhā</s> of the serpents' removes aging and death — thus both [are adduced] as illustrations. // [continued]
'<s>Brahman</s>' means liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). // [continued]
And the <s>rasāyana</s>'s capacity to [lead to] liberation is stated here by virtue of its purifying the <s>sattva</s> (mind/essence). // 1]
In this <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s> [section], six formulations have been declared —

children.text: rasāyanānāṃ siddhānām āyur yair anuvartate // Car_6,1.81
children.translated_text: of accomplished <s>rasāyanas</s>, by which life is maintained. // Car_6,1.81

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne rasāyanādhyāye 'bhayāmalakīyo nāma rasāyanapādaḥ prathamaḥ // Car_6,1.82
children.translated_text: Thus in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>Rasāyana</s>, [ends] the first quarter called <s>Abhayāmalakīya</s>. // Car_6,1.82
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
With '<s>Abhaya</s>' etc., he shows the number of formulations stated, for the purpose of removing doubt. // [continued]
Similarly, the enumeration of numbers at the end should be understood in other [chapters] as well. // 1]
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Now we shall expound the quarter on <s>Rasāyana</s> called <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s> (for those who desire life). // Car_6,2.1

children.text: iti ha smāha bhagavān ātreyaḥ // Car_6,2.2
children.translated_text: Thus said the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car_6,2.2
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: pūrvapāde hy āmalakarasāyanānyuktāni ihāpyāmalakarasāyanāni santīti prāṇakāmīyam anantaram ucyate // 1
