children.translated_text: In the previous quarter, <s>Āmalaka</s>-based <s>rasāyanas</s> were stated; since there are <s>Āmalaka</s>-based <s>rasāyanas</s> here as well, the <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s> is stated next [in sequence]. // 1
'<s>Prāṇakāmīya</s>' — so named because it is composed with reference to the word '<s>prāṇakāma</s>' (one who desires life). // 2]

children.text: prāṇakāmāḥ śuśrūṣadhvam idam ucyamānam amṛtam ivāparam aditisutahitakaram acintyādbhutaprabhāvam āyuṣyam ārogyakaraṃ vayasaḥ sthāpanaṃ nidrātandrāśramaklamālasyadaurbalyāpaharam anilakaphapittasāmyakaraṃ sthairyakaram abaddhamāṃsaharam antaragnisaṃdhukṣaṇaṃ prabhāvarṇasvarottamakaraṃ rasāyanavidhānam /
children.translated_text: O you who desire life! Listen to this that is being declared — a <s>rasāyana</s> regimen like another <s>Amṛta</s> (ambrosia), beneficial to the sons of <s>Aditi</s> (the gods), of inconceivable and wondrous potency, promoting longevity, producing health, stabilizing age, removing sleep, drowsiness, fatigue, exhaustion, lassitude, and weakness, bringing equilibrium of <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Kapha</s>, and <s>Pitta</s>, bestowing firmness, removing loose flesh, kindling the internal fire, producing the best of luster, complexion, and voice.

children.text: anena cyavanādayo maharṣayaḥ punaryuvatvam āpur nārīṇāṃ ceṣṭatamā babhūvuḥ sthirasamasuvibhaktamāṃsāḥ susaṃhatasthiraśarīrāḥ suprasannabalavarṇendriyāḥ sarvatrāpratihataparākramāḥ kleśasahāś ca /
children.translated_text: By this [regimen], <s>Cyavana</s> and other great sages regained youth, became most desired by women, had firm, well-proportioned, and well-distributed flesh, had compact and stable bodies, had clear strength, complexion, and sense-organs, had unobstructed prowess everywhere, and were able to endure hardship.

children.text: sarve śarīradoṣā bhavanti grāmyāhārād amlatvalavaṇakaṭukakṣāraśukraśākamāṃsatilapalalapiṣṭānnabhojināṃ virūḍhanavaśūkaśamīdhānyaviruddhāsātmyarūkṣakṣārābhiṣyandibhojināṃ klinnagurupūtiparyuṣitabhojināṃ viṣamādhyaśanaprāyāṇāṃ divāsvapnastrīmadyanityānāṃ viṣamātimātravyāyāmasaṃkṣobhitaśarīrāṇāṃ bhayakrodhaśokalobhamohāyāsabahulānām atonimittaṃ hi śithilībhavanti māṃsāni vimucyante saṃdhayaḥ vidahyate raktaṃ viṣyandate cānalpaṃ medaḥ na saṃdhīyate 'sthiṣu majjā śukraṃ na pravartate kṣayamupaityojaḥ sa evaṃbhūte glāyati sīdati nidrātandrālasyasamanvito nirutsāhaḥ śvasiti asamarthaśceṣṭānāṃ śārīramānasīnāṃ naṣṭasmṛtibuddhicchāyo rogāṇām adhiṣṭhānabhūto na sarvamāyuravāpnoti /
children.translated_text: All bodily defects arise from the diet of village-dwellers (<s>grāmyāhāra</s>) — of those who eat sour, salty, pungent, alkaline, semen-diminishing, greens, meat, sesame, sesame powder, and food made of flour; of those who eat sprouted, fresh, husked and leguminous grains, incompatible, unsuitable, dry, alkaline, and exudate-producing foods; of those who eat moist, heavy, putrid, and stale food; of those who mostly eat irregularly and in excess; of those habituated to daytime sleep, women, and wine; of those whose bodies are agitated by irregular or excessive exercise. [These defects also arise] in those dominated by fear, anger, grief, greed, delusion, and exertion. For because of these causes, the flesh becomes flaccid, the joints become loose, the blood is burnt, abundant fat oozes out, marrow does not deposit in the bones, semen does not form, <s>Ojas</s> (vital essence) undergoes depletion. Such a person becomes languid, dejected, afflicted with sleep, drowsiness, and lassitude, without enthusiasm, breathless, and incapable of physical and mental activities — with diminished memory, intellect, and complexion — becomes a locus for diseases, and does not attain the full lifespan.

children.text: tasmādetāndoṣānavekṣamāṇaḥ sarvān yathoktān ahitān apāsyāhāravihārān rasāyanāni prayoktumarhatītyuktvā bhagavān punarvasur ātreya uvāca // Car_6,2.3
children.translated_text: Therefore, having observed all these defects, one should abandon all the unwholesome foods and habits as stated, and undertake <s>rasāyana</s> [therapy] — having said this, the venerable <s>Punarvasu</s> <s>Ātreya</s> spoke: // Car_6,2.3
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: nidrāharatvaṃ rasāyanasya vaikārikanidrāharatvena kiṃvā devavatsarvadā prabuddho nidrārahito bhavati // 1
children.translated_text: The <s>rasāyana</s>'s 'removal of sleep' should be understood as removal of pathological sleep; or [it means that], like the gods, one becomes always awake and free from [the need for] sleep. // 1
The definition of drowsiness (<s>tandrā</s>) in another treatise:
'Non-perception of sense objects, heaviness, yawning, exhaustion —

children.text: nidrārtasyeva yasyaite tasya tandrāṃ vinirdiśet iti // 2
children.translated_text: when these [symptoms] are present as if in one who is sleepy, one should diagnose drowsiness (<s>tandrā</s>).' // 2
'Loose flesh' (<s>abaddha-māṃsa</s>) means non-compact flesh. // 3
'Producing the best of luster etc.' means it makes luster and the rest excellent. // 4

children.text: evaṃjātīyaś ca pūrvanipātāniyamo 'pratibandhena carake'sti sa mayūravyaṃsakādipāṭhād draṣṭavyaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: And such [grammatical] irregularity of word-order is found in <s>Caraka</s> without restriction — it should be understood from readings like '<s>mayūra-vyaṃsaka</s>' etc. // 5

children.text: anena hītyādinā purāvṛttakathanena rasāyanāni vakṣyamāṇāni pravṛttyarthaṃ stauti // 6
children.translated_text: With 'by this' etc., by narrating past events, he praises the <s>rasāyanas</s> that are about to be stated, for the purpose of motivating [their use]. // 6

children.text: rasāyanaprayoge varjanīyaṃ grāmyāhārādi dūṣaṇatvena nirdiśannāha sarve ityādi // 7
children.translated_text: Indicating the village diet etc. as corrupting factors that should be avoided during <s>rasāyana</s> practice, he says 'all' etc. // 7
'<s>Tila</s>' (sesame) means un-powdered sesame; '<s>palala</s>' is sesame powder. // 8
'Because of these causes' — means caused by the village diet etc. // 9

children.text: śukraṃ na pravartata iti notpadyate śukramityarthaḥ // 10]
children.translated_text: 'Semen does not form' means semen is not produced — this is the meaning. // 10]

children.text: āmalakānāṃ subhūmijānāṃ kālajānām anupahatagandhavarṇarasānām āpūrṇasapramāṇavīryāṇāṃ svarasena punarnavākalkapādasamprayuktena sarpiṣaḥ sādhayedāḍhakam ataḥ paraṃ vidārīsvarasena jīvantīkalkasamprayuktena ataḥ paraṃ caturguṇena payasā balātibalākaṣāyeṇa śatāvarīkalkasaṃyuktena anena krameṇaikaikaṃ śatapākaṃ sahasrapākaṃ vā śarkarākṣaudracaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ sauvarṇe rājate mārttike vā śucau dṛḍhe ghṛtabhāvite kumbhe sthāpayet tadyathoktena vidhinā yathāgni prātaḥ prātaḥ prayojayet jīrṇe ca kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ śāliṣaṣṭikam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: One should prepare a <s>āḍhaka</s>-measure of ghee with the juice of <s>Āmalakas</s> — grown in good soil, ripened in season, with unimpaired smell, color, and taste, full-sized and of full potency — combined with one-fourth part of <s>Punarnavā</s> paste. Then [a second preparation] with the juice of <s>Vidārī</s> combined with <s>Jīvantī</s> paste. Then [a third preparation] with four parts of milk combined with the decoction of <s>Balā</s> and <s>Atibalā</s> and <s>Śatāvarī</s> paste. By this sequence, each [preparation] should be cooked a hundred times or a thousand times. Combined with one-fourth part of sugar and honey, it should be stored in a clean, strong vessel — of gold, silver, or clay — seasoned with ghee. This should be administered every morning according to the prescribed method, in a dose proportionate to the digestive fire. After digestion, one should eat <s>Śāli</s> or <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.

children.text: asya prayogādvarṣaśataṃ vayo'jaraṃ tiṣṭhati śrutamavatiṣṭhate sarvāmayāḥ praśāmyanti apratihatagatiḥ strīṣu apatyavān bhavatīti // Car_6,2.4
children.translated_text: By using this, one's lifespan remains a hundred years without aging, learning is retained, all diseases are pacified, one's movements are unobstructed, one becomes potent with women and blessed with offspring. // Car_6,2.4
[One attains] a large body with the strength of mountain-ore, firm sense organs and exceedingly strong sense organs,
invincible by others, of supremely beautiful form, and possessed of a mind [blessed with] fame, honor, and happiness. // Car_6,2.5
Great strength, foremost purity of complexion, a voice resembling the thunder of dense clouds —

children.text: bhavatyapatyaṃ vipulaṃ sthiraṃ ca samaśnato yogamimaṃ narasya // Car_6,2.6
children.translated_text: and abundant, stable offspring — [these accrue] to the man who properly takes this formulation. // Car_6,2.6
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
[Each preparation should be cooked] a hundred times individually — this is the meaning. // 1

children.text: ekaikapākasādhanaṃ pṛthak kartavyaṃ tena triśatadhā pāko bhavati // 2
children.translated_text: The preparation of each individual cooking should be done separately; thus the cooking amounts to three hundred [total]. // 2

children.text: atra ca kalkopalepādi nopakṣīṇamapi yadavaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati tadeva grāhyaṃ vacanabalāt // 3
children.translated_text: And here, even the paste-coating etc. that has diminished [during cooking] — whatever remains, that alone should be taken, by the force of the textual instruction. // 3

children.text: sauvarṇādipātreṣu yathāpūrvaṃ varaguṇatvam anyathā samānaguṇatve sarveṣāṃ mṛtpātrasya sulabhatvenātidurlabhataraṃ sauvarṇapātraṃ nopadeśam arhati // 4
children.translated_text: Among gold etc. vessels, the superiority of qualities is in the stated order. Otherwise, if they were of equal quality, the gold vessel — being far more difficult to obtain than an earthen vessel — would not merit mention [in the instruction]. // 4
'According to the prescribed method' means by the <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> (entering-the-hut) method. // 5
'Mountain-ore' (<s>girisāra</s>) means iron. // 6]

children.text: āmalakasahasraṃ pippalīsahasrasamprayuktaṃ palāśataruṇakṣārodakottaraṃ tiṣṭhet tadanugatakṣārodakam anātapaśuṣkam anasthi cūrṇīkṛtaṃ caturguṇābhyāṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ saṃnīya śarkarācūrṇacaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ ghṛtabhājanasthaṃ ṣaṇmāsān sthāpayedantarbhūmeḥ /
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>Āmalakas</s> combined with a thousand <s>Pippalīs</s> should be soaked in alkaline water [prepared with] young <s>Palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) [leaves/ash]. [Then] the alkaline water having permeated [them] should be drained off, [the fruits] dried without sun-exposure, pitted, and powdered. Combined with four parts of honey and ghee, mixed with one-fourth part of sugar powder, stored in a ghee-seasoned vessel, it should be kept underground for six months.

children.text: tasyottarakālamagnibalasamāṃ mātrāṃ khādet paurvāhṇikaḥ prayogo nāparāhṇikaḥ sātmyāpekṣaścāhāravidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: After that period, one should consume a dose proportionate to one's digestive fire. The use should be in the forenoon, not in the afternoon. The dietary regimen should be based on personal habituation (<s>sātmya</s>).

children.text: asya prayogād varṣaśatamajaraṃ vayas tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.7
children.translated_text: By using this, one's lifespan remains a hundred years without aging — the rest is the same as before. // Car_6,2.7
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'Young <s>Palāśa</s>' means <s>Palāśa</s> that is young [i.e., in its middle stage]. By this, [the use of] immature and old <s>Palāśa</s> is excluded. // 1

children.text: kṣārodakottaramiti yathā kṣārodakaṃ bhāvyādupari bhavati tathā kartavyamiti darśayati // 2
children.translated_text: 'Covered with alkaline water' — [means] one should ensure that the alkaline water is above the items being soaked. // 2
'One-fourth part' means a quarter [of the total measure]. // 3
'The same as the previous' — by the statement of the result of the previous formula, this too is appropriate: such is the meaning. // 4]

children.text: āmalakacūrṇāḍhakam ekaviṃśatirātram āmalakasvarasaparipītaṃ madhughṛtāḍhakābhyāṃ dvābhyāmekīkṛtam aṣṭabhāgapippalīkaṃ śarkarācūrṇacaturbhāgasamprayuktaṃ ghṛtabhājanasthaṃ prāvṛṣi bhasmarāśau nidadhyāt tadvarṣānte sātmyapathyāśī prayojayet asya prayogād varṣaśatam ajaram āyus tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.8
children.translated_text: One <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure) of <s>āmalaka</s> (Indian gooseberry) powder, soaked for twenty-one nights in <s>āmalaka</s> juice, combined with one <s>āḍhaka</s> each of honey and ghee, with <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper) as one-eighth part, mixed with one-fourth part of sugar powder, placed in a ghee-coated vessel — one should store it during the rainy season in an ash-heap. At the end of the rainy season, eating suitable wholesome food, one should employ it. By its use, one's lifespan remains free from aging for a hundred years — the same as the previous [formula]. // Car_6,2.8

children.text: viḍaṅgataṇḍulacūrṇānām āḍhakamāḍhakaṃ pippalītaṇḍulānām adhyardhāḍhakaṃ sitopalāyāḥ sarpistailamadhvāḍhakaiḥ ṣaḍbhir ekīkṛtaṃ ghṛtabhājanasthaṃ prāvṛṣi bhasmarāśāv iti sarvaṃ samānaṃ pūrveṇa yāvad āśīḥ // Car_6,2.9
children.translated_text: One <s>āḍhaka</s> each of <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes) seed powder, one and a half <s>āḍhakas</s> of <s>pippalī</s> seeds, [one and a half āḍhakas] of rock sugar — combined with six <s>āḍhakas</s> of ghee, oil, and honey, placed in a ghee-coated vessel, [stored] during the rainy season in an ash-heap — everything is the same as the previous [formula] up to the benediction. // Car_6,2.9
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: yāvad āśīr iti āśīḥ phalaśrutiḥ tena tadvarṣānte ityādi granthoktavidhividhānaṃ darśayati // 1]
children.translated_text: 'Up to the benediction' — the benediction is the statement of the result (<s>phalaśruti</s>). By this he indicates the procedure stated in the text beginning with 'at the end of the rainy season.' // 1]

children.text: yathoktaguṇānāmāmalakānāṃ sahasramārdrapalāśadroṇyāṃ sapidhānāyāṃ bāṣpam anudvamantyām āraṇyagomayāgnibhir upasvedayet tāni susvinnaśītāny uddhṛtakulakāny āpothyāḍhakena pippalīcūrṇānāmāḍhakena ca viḍaṅgataṇḍulacūrṇānām adhyardhena cāḍhakena śarkarāyā dvābhyāṃ dvābhyām āḍhakābhyāṃ tailasya madhunaḥ sarpiṣaśca saṃyojya śucau dṛḍhe ghṛtabhāvite kumbhe sthāpayed ekaviṃśatirātram ata ūrdhvaṃ prayogaḥ asya prayogādvarṣaśatam ajaram āyus tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.10
children.translated_text: One thousand <s>āmalakas</s> of the qualities described above — one should steam them in a fresh <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) trough with a lid, not allowing steam to escape, using forest cow-dung fires. Those [fruits], well-steamed and cooled, with their seeds removed, should be pounded and combined with one <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>pippalī</s> powder, one <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>viḍaṅga</s> seed powder, one and a half <s>āḍhakas</s> of sugar, and two <s>āḍhakas</s> each of oil, honey, and ghee. [This should be] stored in a clean, strong, ghee-seasoned pot for twenty-one nights. Thereafter it is for use. By its use, one's lifespan remains free from aging for a hundred years — the same as the previous [formula]. // Car_6,2.10
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'The same as the previous' means: this is the same as the previous formula up to the statement of the result — such is the meaning. // 1]

children.text: dhanvani kuśāstīrṇe snigdhakṛṣṇamadhuramṛttike suvarṇavarṇamṛttike vā vyapagataviṣaśvāpadapavanasalilāgnidoṣe karṣaṇavalmīkaśmaśānacaityoṣarāvasathavarjite deśe yathartusukhapavanasalilādityasevite jātāny anupahatāny anadhyārūḍhāny abālāny ajīrṇāny adhigatavīryāṇi śīrṇapurāṇaparṇāny asaṃjātāny aparṇāni tapasi tapasye vā māse śuciḥ prayataḥ kṛtadevārcanaḥ svasti vācayitvā dvijātīn cale sumuhūrte nāgabalāmūlāny uddharet teṣāṃ suprakṣālitānāṃ tvakpiṇḍam āmramātram akṣamātraṃ vā ślakṣṇapiṣṭamāloḍya payasā prātaḥ prayojayet cūrṇīkṛtāni vā pibet payasā madhusarpirbhyāṃ vā saṃyojya bhakṣayet jīrṇe ca kṣīrasarpirbhyāṃ śāliṣaṣṭikam aśnīyāt /
children.translated_text: In arid land, strewn with <s>kuśa</s> grass, with unctuous, black, sweet soil — or with golden-colored soil — free from the defects of poison, wild beasts, wind, water, and fire; avoiding plowed land, anthills, cremation grounds, sacred trees, saline soil, and dwellings; enjoying seasonally comfortable wind, water, and sun — [plants] that have grown [there], undamaged, not overgrown [by other trees], neither too young nor too old, having attained full potency, with old leaves fallen and new leaves not yet sprouted — in the month of <s>Tapas</s> (Māgha) or <s>Tapasya</s> (Phālguna), one who is pure, self-restrained, having performed worship of the gods, having had the twice-born recite benedictions, at a moving [i.e., <s>Indra</s>] auspicious moment, should dig up the roots of <s>Nāgabalā</s>. Those, well-washed, [made into] a bark-paste the size of a mango [fruit] or the size of an <s>akṣa</s> (berry), finely ground, should be stirred into milk and employed in the morning. Or, made into powder, one should drink it with milk, or combine it with honey and ghee and eat it. When digested, one should eat <s>śāli</s> or <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee.

children.text: saṃvatsaraprayogādasya varṣaśatamajaraṃ vayastiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.11
children.translated_text: By use for one year, one's lifespan remains free from aging for a hundred years — the same as the previous [formula]. // Car_6,2.11
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'In arid land' means: in a <s>jāṅgala</s> (dry/arid) region.
'Plowing' (<s>karṣaṇa</s>) means: [land worked] by plow and the like.
'Not overgrown' (<s>anadhyārūḍha</s>) means: not encroached upon by a large neighboring tree.
'<s>Tapas</s>' means the month of <s>Māgha</s> (January-February). // 1
'<s>Tapasya</s>' means <s>Phālguna</s> (February-March).
'At a moving auspicious moment' (<s>cale sumuhūrte</s>) means: at the <s>Indra muhūrta</s>.
'The size of a mango' (<s>āmramātra</s>) means: the measure of one <s>pala</s>. // 2]

The juices of <s>Balā</s>, <s>Atibalā</s>, sandalwood, <s>aguru</s> (aloewood), <s>dhava</s>, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>khadira</s> (catechu), <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood), and <s>āsana</s> — and ten herbs ending with <s>Punarnavā</s> — are explained [in the same manner] as <s>Nāgabalā</s>.

children.text: svarasānāmalābhe tv ayaṃ svarasavidhiś cūrṇānām āḍhakam āḍhakam udakasyāhorātrāsthitaṃ mṛditapūtaṃ svarasavat prayojyam // Car_6,2.12
children.translated_text: When the juices of these are unavailable, this is the substitute procedure for juices: one <s>āḍhaka</s> of powder soaked in water for a day and night, pressed and filtered, should be employed like juice. // Car_6,2.12
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: punarnavāntā daśa ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīye amṛtābhayā dhātrī yuktā śreyasī śvetātirasā maṇḍūkaparṇī sthirā punarnavā iti sarvā vayaḥsthāpanoktāḥ // 1
children.translated_text: The ten [herbs] ending with <s>Punarnavā</s> — in the <s>Ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīya</s> [chapter they are listed]: <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Abhayā</s>, <s>Dhātrī</s>, <s>Yuktā</s>, <s>Śreyasī</s>, <s>Śvetā</s>, <s>Atirasā</s>, <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>Sthirā</s>, and <s>Punarnavā</s> — all of which are stated [there] as age-preserving. // 1
'Explained as <s>Nāgabalā</s>' means: the application of these too is the same as for <s>Nāgabalā</s>. // 2
The procedure for <s>Balā</s> and the rest is with juice only. // 3
The diet etc. should be understood as [the same] as for <s>Nāgabalā</s>. // 4
When juices are unavailable, he states the substitute with 'of juices' etc. // 5]

children.text:
bhallātakāny anupahatāny anāmayāny āpūrṇarasapramāṇavīryāṇi pakvajāmbavaprakāśāni śucau śukre vā māse saṃgṛhya yavapalle māṣapalle vā nidhāpayet tāni caturmāsasthitāni sahasi sahasye vā māse prayoktum ārabheta śītasnigdhamadhuropaskṛtaśarīraḥ /
pūrvaṃ daśabhallātakānyāpothyāṣṭaguṇenāmbhasā sādhu sādhayet teṣāṃ rasamaṣṭabhāgāvaśeṣaṃ pūtaṃ sapayaskaṃ pibet sarpiṣāntar mukham abhyajya /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhallātakas</s> (marking nuts) that are undamaged, free from disease, filled with complete juice, potency, and measure, resembling ripe <s>jāmbu</s> (Syzygium) fruits in appearance — collected in the month of <s>Śuci</s> (Jyeṣṭha) or <s>Śukra</s> (Āṣāḍha), one should store them in barley chaff or black gram chaff. After four months' storage, in the month of <s>Sahas</s> (Āgrahāyaṇa) or <s>Sahasya</s> (Pauṣa), one should begin their use, having prepared the body with cold, unctuous, and sweet [substances]. First, ten <s>bhallātakas</s> should be pounded and well-cooked in eight times [their volume of] water. Their decoction, reduced to one-eighth, filtered, mixed with milk, should be drunk — having anointed the interior of the mouth with ghee.

children.text: tāny ekaikabhallātakotkarṣāpakarṣeṇa daśabhallātakāny ā triṃśataḥ prayojyāni nātaḥ paramutkarṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: These should be employed with an increase and decrease of one <s>bhallātaka</s> at a time, [starting from] ten <s>bhallātakas</s> up to thirty. Beyond that there is no further increase.
By the method of application, the <s>bhallātaka</s> course is limited to one thousand [total].

children.text: jīrṇe ca sasarpiṣā payasā śāliṣaṣṭikāśanam upacāraḥ prayogānte ca dvis tāvat payasaivopacāraḥ /
children.translated_text: When digested, the regimen is eating <s>śāli</s> or <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with ghee and milk. At the end of the course, the regimen with milk alone [continues for] twice as long.

children.text: tatprayogādvarṣaśatamajaraṃ vayas tiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.13
children.translated_text: By this application, one's lifespan remains free from aging for a hundred years — the same as the previous [formula]. // Car_6,2.13
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: śuciḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ śukrastu āṣāḍhaḥ saha āgrahāyaṇaḥ sahasyaḥ pauṣaḥ // 1
children.translated_text: '<s>Śuci</s>' is <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> (May-June); '<s>Śukra</s>' is <s>Āṣāḍha</s> (June-July); '<s>Sahas</s>' is <s>Āgrahāyaṇa</s> (November-December); '<s>Sahasya</s>' is <s>Pauṣa</s> (December-January). // 1

children.text: etacca bhallātakaṃ māsacatuṣṭayasthitaṃ yavapallādau uddhṛtamātraṃ na prayojyaṃ kiṃtu yathokta eva kāle śītaguṇayukte // 2
children.translated_text: These <s>bhallātakas</s> stored for four months in barley chaff etc. should not be used immediately upon removal — rather, only at the prescribed time when endowed with cold qualities. // 2
'Having anointed the interior of the mouth with ghee' is for the purpose of preventing burning of the mouth. // 3

children.text: nātaḥ paramiti triṃśataḥ pareṇa prayogo na bhallātakasya // 4
children.translated_text: 'Beyond that there is no [further increase]' means: beyond thirty, there is no application of <s>bhallātaka</s>. // 4

children.text: sahasraparo bhallātakaprayoga iti upayuktabhallātakasaṃpiṇḍanayā yadā sahasraṃ pūryate tadaivoparamaḥ kartavyaḥ sahasrādarvāgapi ca prayogaparityāgaḥ prakṛtyādyapekṣayā bhavatyeva // 5
children.translated_text: 'The <s>bhallātaka</s> course is limited to one thousand' means: when, by aggregating the <s>bhallātakas</s> used [over the whole course], a thousand is reached, then alone should cessation be done. And cessation of the course before [reaching] a thousand also occurs depending on constitution etc. // 5

children.text: sahasrasaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ cehaikena vardhanahrāsakrameṇa na bhavati tena punar āvṛttyā ca triṃśatparyantaṃ prayogaḥ kartavyaḥ yathā hi bhallātakaprayogābhyāsena sahasrasaṃkhyāpūraṇaṃ bhavati tathā kṛtvā parityāgaḥ kartavyaḥ // 6
children.translated_text: The completion of one thousand in number does not happen here by a single cycle of increasing and decreasing [from 10 to 30 and back]; therefore the course up to thirty should be repeated. In whatever manner the completion of one thousand <s>bhallātakas</s> is achieved through repeated courses of application, having done so, cessation should be made. // 6

children.text: anye tv atra suśrute arśaścikitsitoktaśataparyantaṃ bhallātakaprayogeṇa samaṃ virodhaṃ paśyantaḥ suśrutaprayogasyāpyanyathā vyākhyānena triṃśatkamātraṃ prayogamicchanti tacca vyākhyānaṃ nātisaṃgatam // 7
children.translated_text: Others, however, seeing a contradiction here with the <s>bhallātaka</s> course of up to one hundred stated in <s>Suśruta</s>'s therapeutics of hemorrhoids, wish [to limit] the application to only thirty by an alternative interpretation of <s>Suśruta</s>'s course — but that interpretation is not very coherent. // 7

children.text: kiṃca sahasradvayasya tatropayogo vihitaḥ atra sahasraparyantaḥ prayogaḥ tena vyādhiviṣayo'nya eva sa prayogaḥ ayaṃ tu rasāyanaviṣayaḥ // 8]
children.translated_text: Moreover, there [in <s>Suśruta</s>] the use of two thousand is prescribed; here the course is limited to one thousand. Therefore that course has a different [therapeutic] scope relating to disease, while this one pertains to <s>rasāyana</s>. // 8]

children.text: bhallātakānāṃ jarjarīkṛtānāṃ piṣṭasvedanaṃ pūrayitvā bhūmāv ākaṇṭhaṃ nikhātasya snehabhāvitasya dṛḍhasyopari kumbhasyāropyoḍupenāpidhāya kṛṣṇamṛttikāvaliptaṃ gomayāgnibhir upasvedayet teṣāṃ yaḥ svarasaḥ kumbhaṃ prapadyeta tam aṣṭabhāgamadhusamprayuktaṃ dviguṇaghṛtam adyāt tatprayogādvarṣaśatamajaraṃ vayastiṣṭhatīti samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.14
children.translated_text: Crushed <s>bhallātakas</s>, filling a steaming vessel (<s>piṣṭasvedana</s>), [placed] upon a strong, ghee-seasoned pot buried in the ground up to the neck, covered on top with a lid (<s>uḍupa</s>), smeared with black clay — one should steam [them] with cow-dung fires. Whatever juice of those [<s>bhallātakas</s>] descends into the pot — that, mixed with one-eighth part of honey and with twice [the amount of] ghee, one should consume. By this application, one's lifespan remains free from aging for a hundred years — the same as the previous [formula]. // Car_6,2.14
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: piṣṭasvedanaṃ tat yatrasthaṃ piṣṭakam upasvedyate tadupari yat pidhānapātraṃ tacceha sacchidraṃ grāhyam anyathoparisthabhallātakatāpāc cyutaḥ sneho nādho yāti // 1]
children.translated_text: 'Steaming vessel' (<s>piṣṭasvedana</s>) means: that in which the paste is steamed — the covering vessel on top should here be taken as having holes [in it]; otherwise the oil released by the heat of the <s>bhallātakas</s> above would not descend below. // 1]

children.text: bhallātakatailapātraṃ sapayaskaṃ madhukena kalkenākṣamātreṇa śatapākaṃ kuryāditi samānaṃ pūrveṇa // Car_6,2.15
children.translated_text: <s>Bhallātaka</s> oil in a vessel, mixed with milk, with a paste (<s>kalka</s>) of <s>madhuka</s> (licorice) the size of an <s>akṣa</s> (berry) — one should cook it a hundred times — the same as the previous [formula]. // Car_6,2.15
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'<s>Bhallātaka</s> oil' means: the <s>bhallātaka</s> fat obtained by the method just described. // 1]

children.text: bhallātakasarpiḥ bhallātakakṣīraṃ bhallātakakṣaudraṃ guḍabhallātakaṃ bhallātakayūṣaḥ bhallātakatailaṃ bhallātakapalalaṃ bhallātakasaktavaḥ bhallātakalavaṇaṃ bhallātakatarpaṇam iti bhallātakavidhānamuktaṃ bhavati // Car_6,2.16
children.translated_text: <s>Bhallātaka</s>-ghee, <s>bhallātaka</s>-milk, <s>bhallātaka</s>-honey, jaggery-<s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>-broth, <s>bhallātaka</s>-oil, <s>bhallātaka</s>-cake, <s>bhallātaka</s>-roasted-grain, <s>bhallātaka</s>-salt, <s>bhallātaka</s>-gruel — thus the <s>bhallātaka</s> procedures are declared complete. // Car_6,2.16
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'<s>Bhallātaka</s>-ghee' and the rest — these are ten preparations. // 1

children.text: atra ca yathāyogyatayā bhallātakena sarpirādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ saṃyogaśca jñeyaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: And here, the processing (<s>saṃskāra</s>) or combination (<s>saṃyoga</s>) of ghee etc. with <s>bhallātaka</s> should be understood as appropriate. // 2
As stated in [the chapter of] <s>Jatūkarṇa</s>: 'Ghee, milk, honey, jaggery, broth, oil, cake, roasted grain, salt, and gruel — processed with or combined with <s>bhallātaka</s>.' // 3

children.text: evaṃ ca sarpiḥkṣīrayūṣatailānāṃ saṃskāro yathānyāyaṃ bhallātakena kṣaudrapalalasaktutarpaṇānāṃ bhallātakena yogaḥ guḍalavaṇayostu saṃskāraḥ saṃyogo vā // 4
children.translated_text: Thus: for ghee, milk, broth, and oil — processing with <s>bhallātaka</s> as appropriate; for honey, cake, roasted grain, and gruel — combination with <s>bhallātaka</s>; for jaggery and salt — either processing or combination. // 4

children.text: lavaṇe saṃskārapakṣe hi lavaṇasamaṃ bhallātakam antardhūmadagdhaṃ grāhyam // 5
children.translated_text: In the case of salt being processed — <s>bhallātaka</s> equal [in quantity] to the salt should be taken, burned in contained smoke. // 5

children.text: anye tu sarpirādīnāṃ sarveṣāmeva bhallātakena saṃskāraṃ vyākhyānayanti // 6
children.translated_text: Others, however, explain the processing of all [items] from ghee onward with <s>bhallātaka</s>. // 6
Here, the roasted-grain preparation, being predominantly non-liquid, should be distinguished by non-specific action. // 7]
<s>Bhallātakas</s> are sharp, ripening, and equal to fire;
they become like ambrosia when employed according to proper method. // Car_6,2.17
These ten modes of their application have been proclaimed;
one who knows the disease, constitution, and habitual suitability should devise these applications. // Car_6,2.18

children.text: kaphajo na sa rogo'sti na vibandho'sti kaścana /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>kapha</s>-born disease, no constipation whatsoever,

children.text: yaṃ na bhallātakaṃ hanyācchīghraṃ medhāgnivardhanam // Car_6,2.19
children.translated_text: that <s>bhallātaka</s> cannot quickly destroy — it enhances intellect and digestive fire. // Car_6,2.19
Formerly, life-desiring sages such as <s>Cyavana</s> and others, though aged,

children.text: rasāyanaiḥ śivair etair babhūvur amitāyuṣaḥ // Car_6,2.20
children.translated_text: became of immeasurable lifespan through these auspicious <s>rasāyanas</s>. // Car_6,2.20
Sacred knowledge, austerity, celibacy, and meditation on the Self —

children.text: dīrghāyuṣo yathākāmaṃ saṃbhṛtya tridivaṃ gatāḥ // Car_6,2.21
children.translated_text: [these] they cultivated at will with their long life, and [then] went to heaven. // Car_6,2.21
Therefore, for the purpose of extending life, those who desire life and seek happiness
should employ the method of <s>rasāyana</s> properly, with full concentration. // Car_6,2.22
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Equal to fire' (<s>agnisamāna</s>) means: by virtue of causing burning and blistering. // 1
'Having cultivated' (<s>saṃbhṛtya</s>) means: having accomplished. // 2]
The combinations of <s>rasāyanas</s> proven [effective], by [<s>Ātreya</s>] who desires the welfare of beings,
have been declared in the <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s> [section] — thirty-seven [combinations in all], by the great sage. // Car_6,2.23

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne rasāyanādhyāye prāṇakāmīyo nāma rasāyanapādo dvitīyaḥ // Car_6,2.24
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s>, revised by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>Rasāyana</s>, the second quarter named <s>Prāṇakāmīya</s> [is complete]. // Car_6,2.24
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: pādānusaṃgrahe saptatriṃśatprayogā uktāḥ tatra balādibhiraṣṭābhiḥ punarnavāntaiśca daśabhiraṣṭādaśaprayogāḥ apare tu vyāhṛtā vyaktā eva // 1]
children.translated_text: In the chapter-summary, thirty-seven preparations are stated. Among these, eighteen preparations are from the eight [beginning with] <s>Balā</s> and the ten ending with <s>Punarnavā</s>. The remaining ones are manifestly stated. // 1]
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, 2 [Second quarter of the <s>Rasāyana</s> chapter]
Now we shall expound the <s>Karapracitīya</s> (hand-gathered) <s>rasāyana</s> quarter. // Car_6,1.3.1
Thus indeed spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car_6,1.3.2
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
Because of the similarity in being an <s>āmalaka</s>-<s>rasāyana</s>, the <s>Karapracitīya</s> is stated immediately after. // 1]

children.text: karapracitānāṃ yathoktaguṇānām āmalakānāmuddhṛtāsthnāṃ śuṣkacūrṇitānāṃ punarmāghe phālgune vā māse triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ svarasaparipītānāṃ punaḥ śuṣkacūrṇīkṛtānām āḍhakam ekaṃ grāhayet atha jīvanīyānāṃ bṛṃhaṇīyānāṃ stanyajananānāṃ śukrajananānāṃ vayaḥsthāpanānāṃ ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīyoktānām auṣadhagaṇānāṃ candanāgurudhavatiniśakhadiraśiṃśapāsanasārāṇāṃ cāṇuśaḥ kṛttānām abhayāvibhītakapippalīvacācavyacitrakaviḍaṅgānāṃ ca samastānāmāḍhakamekaṃ daśaguṇenāmbhasā sādhayet tasminnāḍhakāvaśeṣe rase supūte tāny āmalakacūrṇāni dattvā gomayāgnibhir vaṃśavidalaśaratejanāgnibhir vā sādhayed yāvad apanayādrasasya tam anupadagdham upahṛtyāyasīṣu pātrīṣvāstīrya śoṣayet suśuṣkaṃ tat kṛṣṇājinasyopari dṛṣadi ślakṣṇapiṣṭam ayaḥsthālyāṃ nidhāpayet samyak taccūrṇam ayaś cūrṇāṣṭabhāgasamprayuktaṃ madhusarpirbhyām agnibalam abhisamīkṣya prayojayediti // Car_6,1.3.3
children.translated_text: One should take one <s>āḍhaka</s> (measure) of <s>āmalakas</s> that are hand-picked, possessing the stated qualities, with seeds removed, dried and powdered — then again, in the month of <s>Māgha</s> or <s>Phālguna</s>, soaked twenty-one times in their own juice, then again dried and powdered. Then, one <s>āḍhaka</s> of all the following combined — the medicinal groups of the <s>Jīvanīya</s> (life-promoting), <s>Bṛṃhaṇīya</s> (nourishing), <s>Stanyajanana</s> (milk-generating), <s>Śukrajanana</s> (semen-generating), and <s>Vayaḥsthāpana</s> (age-preserving) groups as stated in the <s>Ṣaḍvirecanaśatāśritīya</s>, together with candana, <s>aguru</s>, <s>dhava</s>, <s>tiniśa</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>śiṃśapā</s>, <s>āsana</s>, and <s>sāra</s> cut into fine pieces, and <s>abhayā</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>cavya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s> — should be boiled in ten times [their quantity of] water. When one <s>āḍhaka</s> of decoction remains, well-strained, those <s>āmalaka</s> powders should be added and cooked over cow-dung fires or fires of bamboo, <s>vidala</s>, <s>śara</s>, and <s>tejana</s> until the liquid is removed. That [preparation], unburnt, should be removed and spread in iron vessels to dry. When well-dried, it should be ground smooth on a stone placed on a black antelope skin, and stored in an iron pot. That powder, combined with one-eighth part of iron [powder], should be administered with honey and ghee after assessing the digestive strength. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.3
This <s>rasāyana</s> was formerly [used by] <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
<s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and others like them. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.4
Having used it with diligence, they were freed from fatigue, disease, and the fear of old age;
they performed austerities as long as they wished, endowed with great strength through its power. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.5
This <s>rasāyana</s> was created by <s>Brahmā</s> for [a lifespan of] a thousand years,
pacifying old age and disease, bestowing intellect, sensory strength, and power. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.6
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
The word 'hand-picked' (<s>karapracita</s>) prohibits [the use of] those that have fallen by themselves. // 1

children.text: māghe phālgune vetigrahaṇavacanāt tathaiva gṛhītānāmadhikāra ityāgamādunnīyate // 2
children.translated_text: From the instruction 'in <s>Māgha</s> or <s>Phālguna</s>,' it is inferred from tradition that the rule applies to those picked at that same [time]. // 2
The 'juice' here is that of <s>āmalaka</s> alone, because of the [governing] topic. // 3
'<s>Śāka</s>' is a large-leaved tree. // 4
'Cut' (<s>kṛtta</s>) means chopped. // 5

children.text: iha gomayāgnyādyupakaraṇaniyamenaiva śaktyutkarṣo bhavatīti ṛṣivacanād unnīyate // 6
children.translated_text: Here, it is inferred from the sage's words that the superiority of potency arises precisely from the restriction to cow-dung fire etc. as instruments. // 6

children.text: yaduktam ṛṣayas tv eva jānanti yogasaṃyogajaṃ phalam iti // 7
children.translated_text: As stated: 'Only the sages know the result born of [specific] combinations and conjunctions.' // 7
Likewise elsewhere too, the restriction of procedural details should be explained [in this way]. // 8
'Of black antelope skin' (<s>kṛṣṇājina</s>) means the hide of the black antelope. // 9]
Through austerity, celibacy, meditation, and tranquility,
and through the method of <s>rasāyana</s>, with a life-span joined to [proper] time — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.7

children.text: sthitā maharṣayaḥ pūrvaṃ nahi kiṃcid rasāyanam /
children.translated_text: the great sages of old remained [long-lived]. For no <s>rasāyana</s>
succeeds for those who are attached to worldly life, engaged in other pursuits, and lacking self-discipline. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.8
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: samprati rasāyanasya tapobrahmacaryadhyānādiyuktasyaiva mahāphalatvaṃ bhavatīti darśayannāha tapasetyādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, showing that the <s>rasāyana</s> yields great fruit only when accompanied by austerity, celibacy, meditation, etc., he says 'through austerity' etc. // 1

children.text: kālayuktena cāyuṣeti aniyatakālayuktena cāyuṣetyarthaḥ niyatakālāyuṣaṃ prati tu na rasāyanaṃ phalavadityuktam eva // 2
children.translated_text: 'With a life-span joined to time' means with an indefinite life-span — the meaning is that <s>rasāyana</s> is not effective for one whose lifespan is fixed [by fate]. This has been stated already. // 2
'Remained' means lived for a long time. // 3

children.text: viparyayeṇa tapaḥprabhṛtivirahe rasāyanasyāphalatām āha na hītyādi // 4]
children.translated_text: Conversely, he states the ineffectiveness of <s>rasāyana</s> in the absence of austerity etc. with 'for no' etc. // 4]
Living on milk for a year, dwelling always among cows,

children.text: sāvitrīṃ manasā dhyāyan brahmacārī yatendriyaḥ // Car_6,1.3.9
children.translated_text: meditating on the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra] mentally, celibate, with senses restrained — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.9

children.text: saṃvatsarānte pauṣīṃ vā māghīṃ vā phālgunīṃ tithim /
children.translated_text: at the year's end, on the <s>Pauṣī</s>, <s>Māghī</s>, or <s>Phālgunī</s> full-moon day,
having fasted for three days during the bright fortnight, entering an <s>āmalaka</s> grove — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.10
climbing a tree rich with large fruits, [and taking] a fruit on the branch,
grasping [it] with the hand, one should remain chanting <s>Brahma</s> [mantras] until the descent of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar). // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.11
For then, inevitably, <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) dwells in the <s>āmalaka</s> for a moment.
[The fruits] become like rock-sugar and honey, unctuous, and soft. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.12
Through the contact with <s>amṛta</s>, however many of those [fruits] one eats,
one lives that many thousands of years, with youth restored. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.13
Having eaten them to satisfaction, one becomes like an immortal.

children.text: svayaṃ cāsyopatiṣṭhante śrīr vedā vākca rūpiṇī // Car_6,1.3.14
children.translated_text: And of their own accord, <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), the <s>Vedas</s>, and <s>Vāk</s> (Speech) in embodied form attend upon him. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.14
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
Although restraint of the senses has been obtained through celibacy, the connection with the word 'with senses restrained' is for showing the excellence of sensory restraint. // 1
The 'year's end' in <s>Pauṣa</s> etc. should be understood as the completion of a year from the day of undertaking the discipline. // 2
After '<s>Phālgunī</s>,' the completion is 'having reached.' // 3

children.text: na drumamārohet ityasyeha āruhya drumamiti vacanenāpavādaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: The [general] rule 'one should not climb a tree' is here overridden by the specific statement 'climbing a tree.' // 4
'Chanting <s>Brahma</s>' means chanting the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>. // 5
'Until the descent of <s>amṛta</s>' means until the arrival of <s>amṛta</s>. // 6
'Eating them to satisfaction' — the sixth [case-ending] is used in the instrumental sense. // 7
'Speech in embodied form' (<s>vāg rūpiṇī</s>) means the presiding deity of speech. // 8]

children.text: triphalāyā rase mūtre gavāṃ kṣāre ca lāvaṇe /
children.translated_text: In the juice of <s>triphalā</s>, in cow's urine, in saline alkali,

children.text: krameṇa ceṅgudīkṣāre kiṃśukakṣāra eva ca // Car_6,1.3.15
children.translated_text: then successively in <s>iṅgudī</s>-alkali and in <s>kiṃśuka</s>-alkali — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.15
one should temper plates of sharp iron, fire-colored,
four fingers long and as thin as a sesame seed. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.16
When they are known to be collyrium-colored, one should have them made into fine powder.

children.text: tāni cūrṇāni madhunā rasenāmalakasya ca // Car_6,1.3.17
children.translated_text: Those powders, with honey and with the juice of <s>āmalaka</s> — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.17
combined in the form of a confection (<s>leha</s>), placed in a pot treated with ghee,

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ nidheyāni yavapalle tathaiva ca // Car_6,1.3.18
children.translated_text: should be stored for a year — and likewise in a pit of barley. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.18
The wise one should stir it once a month, stirring throughout [the vessel].
After the passage of a year, it is to be used with honey and ghee — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.19

children.text: prātaḥ prātarbalāpekṣī sātmyaṃ jīrṇe ca bhojanam /
children.translated_text: each morning, gauging one's strength, and wholesome food [should be taken] when [the previous dose is] digested.

children.text: eṣa eva ca lauhānāṃ prayogaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ // Car_6,1.3.20
children.translated_text: And this same is declared as the method of use for all iron [preparations]. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.20
He would not be assailable by injuries, diseases, old age, or death;

children.text: sa dhṛṣyaḥ syādgajaprāṇaḥ sadā cātibalendriyaḥ // Car_6,1.3.21
children.translated_text: he would have the vital force of an elephant and always exceedingly powerful senses. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.21
Intelligent, renowned, accomplished in speech, retentive of learning, and greatly wealthy —
such would a man become who uses the iron <s>rasāyana</s> for one year. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.22
By this very method, for gold and silver too,
the proven preparation that extends life and removes all diseases [is to be made]. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.23
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'In alkali' means in filtered alkali-water. // 1
'In saline alkali' means in the alkali of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> (Celastrus paniculatus). // 2
'One should temper' means one should quench [the heated iron in the liquid]. // 3

children.text: lauhānāmityanenaiva lohāntarniviṣṭayoḥ suvarṇarajatayor grahaṇe siddhe punas tayor vacanaṃ tayor viśeṣeṇādaropadarśanārtham // 4
children.translated_text: Although the inclusion of gold and silver among 'iron [preparations]' is already established by the word 'all iron [preparations],' the separate mention of those two is to show special regard for them. // 4
The attainment of great wealth should be understood as due to the power of <s>rasāyana</s> itself. // 5]
<s>Aindrī</s>, the one called <s>Matsyākhyaka</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Vacā</s> (calamus), <s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s>,

children.text: pippalyo lavaṇaṃ hema śaṅkhapuṣpī viṣaṃ ghṛtam // Car_6,1.3.24
children.translated_text: <s>Pippalī</s> (long pepper), salt, gold, <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, poison, and ghee — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.24
of these, [take] three-<s>yava</s> measures of each, excluding gold, ghee, and poison;

children.text: dvau yavau tatra hemnastu tilaṃ dadyādviṣasya ca // Car_6,1.3.25
children.translated_text: of gold, give two <s>yavas</s>; and of poison, [give] a <s>tila</s> (sesame-seed [measure]). // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.25
And give one <s>pala</s> of ghee. One should employ all these together;

children.text: ghṛtaprabhūtaṃ sakṣaudraṃ jīrṇe cānnaṃ praśasyate // Car_6,1.3.26
children.translated_text: food rich in ghee, with honey, is recommended when [the medicine is] digested. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.26
It pacifies old age and disease, is supremely productive of memory and intellect,
promotes longevity, is nourishing, auspicious, and clarifies the voice and complexion. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.27
And this <s>Aindra</s> <s>rasāyana</s>, when perfected, is supremely productive of <s>ojas</s>;

children.text: nainat prasahate kṛtyā nālakṣmīrna viṣaṃ na ruk // Car_6,1.3.28
children.translated_text: neither sorcery, nor misfortune, nor poison, nor disease can overpower it. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.28

children.text: śvitraṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ jaṭharāṇi gulmāḥ plīhā purāṇo viṣamajvaraśca /
children.translated_text: Vitiligo, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease), abdominal disorders, <s>gulmas</s> (tumors), chronic splenic disease, intermittent fever,
diseases that impair intellect, memory, and knowledge, and exceedingly powerful <s>vāta</s> disorders — all are pacified by this. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.29
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: matsyākhyako macchu iti loke khyātaḥ anye tu aindrībhedaṃ matsyākhyakam āhuḥ // 1
children.translated_text: '<s>Matsyākhyaka</s>' is what is known in common parlance as '<s>macchu</s>.' Others, however, say that <s>Matsyākhyaka</s> is a variety of <s>Aindrī</s>. // 1
'Three-<s>yava</s> measures' means in the measure of three <s>yavas</s>. // 2
'Rich in ghee' qualifies the food. // 3
'Sorcery' (<s>kṛtyā</s>) means black magic. // 4]

children.text: maṇḍūkaparṇyāḥ svarasaḥ prayojyaḥ kṣīreṇa yaṣṭīmadhukasya cūrṇam /
children.translated_text: The juice of <s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s> should be used; the powder of <s>Yaṣṭīmadhuka</s> (licorice) with milk;

children.text: raso guḍūcyāstu samūlapuṣpyāḥ kalkaḥ prayojyaḥ khalu śaṅkhapuṣpyāḥ // Car_6,1.3.30
children.translated_text: the juice of <s>Guḍūcī</s> with root and flower; and the paste of <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> indeed. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.30
These are life-giving, disease-destroying, enhancing strength, digestive fire, complexion, and voice,

children.text: medhyāni caitāni rasāyanāni medhyā viśeṣeṇa ca śaṅkhapuṣpī // Car_6,1.3.31
children.translated_text: and are intellect-promoting <s>rasāyanas</s>. And <s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> especially promotes intellect. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.31
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]
'<s>Maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>' etc. — these are four formulations. // 1]
Five, eight, seven, or ten <s>pippalīs</s> with honey and ghee —
one seeking the benefits of <s>rasāyana</s> should use [them] for one year. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.32
Three by three in the forenoon, having eaten before a meal,
<s>pippalīs</s> treated with <s>kiṃśuka</s>-alkali and fried in ghee — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.33
should be used mixed with sugar by one desiring the benefits of <s>rasāyana</s>,

children.text: jetuṃ kāsaṃ kṣayaṃ śoṣaṃ śvāsaṃ hikkāṃ galāmayān // Car_6,1.3.34
children.translated_text: to conquer cough, consumption, <s>śoṣa</s> (wasting), dyspnea, hiccup, throat diseases, // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.34
hemorrhoids, malabsorption, anemia, intermittent fever,

children.text: vaisvaryaṃ pīnasaṃ śophaṃ gulmaṃ vātabalāsakam // Car_6,1.3.35
children.translated_text: hoarseness, nasal congestion, edema, <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), and <s>vātabalāsaka</s>. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.35
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>]

children.text: pañcetyādau saṃkhyāvyatikrameṇānuktasaṃkhyānām api pippalīnām upayogaṃ sūcayati // 1
children.translated_text: In 'five' etc., by transgressing the [stated] numbers, the use of <s>pippalīs</s> in unstated numbers too is indicated. // 1

children.text: yadāpi trīṇi dravyāṇi nātyupayuñjīta pippalīṃ kṣāraṃ lavaṇam ityuktaṃ tathāpīha dravyāntarasaṃyuktānāṃ pippalīnām abhyāso na viruddhaḥ kiṃvā uktapippalīrasāyanavyatirekeṇotsargāpavādanyāyāt sa niṣedho jñeyaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: Although it was said 'three substances should not be used excessively — <s>pippalī</s>, <s>kṣāra</s>, and <s>lavaṇa</s>' — nevertheless here the habitual use of <s>pippalīs</s> combined with other substances is not contradictory. Or, by the principle of general rule and exception (<s>utsargāpavāda-nyāya</s>), that prohibition should be understood as excluding the stated <s>pippalī</s> <s>rasāyana</s>. // 2
'<s>Kiṃśuka</s>' is <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma). // 3]
Increasing by increments of ten for ten days — [reaching] ten-<s>pippalī</s> [per] day —

children.text: vardhayet payasā sārdhaṃ tathaivāpanayet punaḥ // Car_6,1.3.36
children.translated_text: one should increase [the dose] along with milk, and likewise decrease it again. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.36

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe ca bhuñjīta ṣaṣṭikaṃ kṣīrasarpiṣā /
children.translated_text: And when each [dose] is digested, one should eat <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> (sixty-day rice) with milk and ghee.
This is the use of one thousand <s>pippalīs</s> — [it is a] <s>rasāyana</s>. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.37

children.text: piṣṭās tā balibhiḥ sevyāḥ śṛtā madhyabalair naraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of strong [constitution] should take them ground into paste; those of moderate strength, cooked;

children.text: cūrṇīkṛtā hrasvabalair yojyā doṣāmayān prati // Car_6,1.3.38
children.translated_text: those of low strength should use them powdered — [all] for <s>doṣas</s> and diseases. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.38
The ten-<s>pippalī</s> [regimen] is best; six is declared middling;

children.text: prayogo yas triparyantaḥ sa kanīyān sa cābalaiḥ // Car_6,1.3.39
children.translated_text: the regimen ending at three is the least — and that is for the weak. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.39
The <s>pippalī</s> <s>rasāyana</s> is nourishing, voice-promoting, life-extending, destructive of splenic disease and abdominal enlargement,

children.text: vayasaḥ sthāpanaṃ medhyaṃ pippalīnāṃ rasāyanam // Car_6,1.3.40
children.translated_text: age-preserving, and intellect-promoting. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.40
At the end of digestion, one <s>abhayā</s> (<s>harītakī</s>); before food, two <s>vibhītakas</s>;

children.text: bhuktvā tu madhusarpirbhyāṃ catvāryāmalakāni ca // Car_6,1.3.41
children.translated_text: and after food, four <s>āmalakas</s> with honey and ghee — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.41
using [this] for one year — [this is] the <s>rasāyana</s> of <s>triphalā</s>.

children.text: jīved varṣaśataṃ pūrṇam ajaro 'vyādhireva ca // Car_6,1.3.42
children.translated_text: One lives a full hundred years, free from old age and disease. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.42
With the paste of <s>triphalā</s>, one should coat a new iron vessel.

children.text: tam ahorātrikaṃ lepaṃ pibet kṣaudrodakāplutam // Car_6,1.3.43
children.translated_text: That coating, [left for] a day and night, one should drink soaked in honey-water. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.43
Food rich in unctuous [substances] is recommended when [the medicine is] digested.

children.text: ajaro 'ruk samābhyāsāj jīvec caiva samāḥ śatam // Car_6,1.3.44
children.translated_text: Free from old age and disease, through continuous use for years, one lives a hundred years. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.44
With <s>madhuka</s> (licorice), <s>tugākṣīrī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, honey, and ghee,

children.text: triphalā sitayā cāpi yuktā siddhaṃ rasāyanam // Car_6,1.3.45
children.translated_text: and <s>triphalā</s> with sugar — [when] combined, [it is] a perfected <s>rasāyana</s>. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.45
With all [types of] iron, gold, <s>vacā</s> (calamus), honey and ghee,

children.text: viḍaṅgapippalībhyāṃ ca triphalā lavaṇena ca // Car_6,1.3.46
children.translated_text: <s>viḍaṅga</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and <s>triphalā</s> with salt — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.46
through use for one year, [it] bestows intellect, memory, and strength,
becomes life-giving, auspicious, and destructive of old age and disease. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.47

children.text: anamlaṃ ca kaṣāyaṃ ca kaṭu pāke śilājatu /
children.translated_text: <s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch) is non-sour, astringent, and pungent in post-digestive effect;
neither excessively hot nor cold; its origin is from four minerals — // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.48
gold, silver, copper, and iron.

children.text: rasāyanaṃ tadvidhibhistad vṛṣyaṃ tacca roganut // Car_6,1.3.49
children.translated_text: That [<s>śilājatu</s>] is a <s>rasāyana</s> according to its [respective] methods, an aphrodisiac, and disease-removing. // <s>Car</s>_6,1.3.49
and [<s>Śilājatu</s>] processed with decoctions that alleviate <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Pitta</s>, and <s>Kapha</s>,

children.text: vīryotkarṣaṃ paraṃ yāti sarvairekaikaśo 'pi vā // Car_6,1.3.50
children.translated_text: attains supreme excellence of potency — [whether processed] with all [decoctions] or with each one individually. // Car_6,1.3.50
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: śilājaturasāyanaṃ darśayituṃ śilājatuno 'bhyarhitasya guṇāneva tāvadāha anamlam ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: In order to present the <s>Śilājatu</s> <s>rasāyana</s>, he first states the qualities of the highly esteemed <s>Śilājatu</s> with 'non-sour' etc. // 1
'<s>Vara</s>' means the best. // 2

children.text: suśrute yadyapi trapusīsambhavaṃ prakṣipya ṣaḍvidhaśilājatu sāmānyena roge rasāyanādhikāre coktaṃ tathāpīha rasāyanādhikāre tadadhikṛtacaturvidham evoktam // 3]
children.translated_text: Although in <s>Suśruta</s>, by adding those derived from tin and lead, sixfold <s>Śilājatu</s> is stated generally in both the [chapters on] disease and <s>rasāyana</s>, here in the <s>rasāyana</s> context only the fourfold [classification] appropriate to that context is stated. // 3]

children.text: prakṣiptoddhṛtam apy enat punas tat prakṣiped rase /
children.translated_text: Having immersed and then removed it, one should again immerse that [<s>Śilājatu</s>] in the warm decoction.

children.text: koṣṇe saptāhametena vidhinā tasya bhāvanā // Car_6,1.3.51
children.translated_text: For seven days — by this method is its processing (<s>bhāvanā</s>). // Car_6,1.3.51
By the previously stated method, together with the powdered metals,

children.text: tatpītaṃ payasā dadyād dīrghamāyuḥ sukhānvitam // Car_6,1.3.52
children.translated_text: that [<s>Śilājatu</s>], consumed with milk, bestows long life accompanied by well-being. // Car_6,1.3.52
It pacifies old age and disease, is supremely body-strengthening,
promotes intellect and memory, is auspicious — one who takes milk as diet should employ it. // Car_6,1.3.53
The course [of use is]: seven groups of seven [days] (49 days), three groups of seven (21 days), and one group of seven (7 days) —
thus a threefold course is prescribed: the best, middle, and lowest respectively. // Car_6,1.3.54

children.text: palamardhapalaṃ karṣo mātrā tasya tridhā matā /
children.translated_text: The dose is considered threefold: one <s>pala</s>, half a <s>pala</s>, and one <s>karṣa</s>.
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states the method of processing <s>Śilājatu</s> with 'having immersed' etc. // 1
'Immersed and [then] removed' means removed immediately after immersion — this is '<s>prakṣiptoddhṛtam</s>.' // 2
'Together with the metals' — in the absence of a specified proportion, the <s>Śilājatu</s> should be equal in portion to the metals. // 3

children.text: prayogaḥ saptasaptāhā iti saptasaptāhavyāpakaprayoga ityarthaḥ evaṃ trayaś caikaśca saptaka ityatrāpi boddhavyam // 4]
children.translated_text: 'The course is seven groups of seven' — meaning a course extending over seven groups of seven days. Similarly, 'three [groups] and one group of seven' should also be understood. // 4]

children.text: jāterviśeṣaṃ savidhiṃ tasya vakṣyāmyataḥ param // Car_6,1.3.55
children.translated_text: I shall now describe the specific varieties of <s>Śilājatu</s>, along with [their] methods. // Car_6,1.3.55
The mineral ores of mountains — beginning with gold — when heated by the sun, exude [a substance].

children.text: jatvābhaṃ mṛdu mṛtsnācchaṃ yanmalaṃ tacchilājatu // Car_6,1.3.56
children.translated_text: That impurity which resembles lac, is soft, ite, and smooth — that is <s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch). // Car_6,1.3.56
That which is sweet with a bitter [aftertaste], resembling the <s>Japā</s> (hibiscus) flower [in color],

children.text: kaṭurvipāke śītaśca sa suvarṇasya nisravaḥ // Car_6,1.3.57
children.translated_text: pungent in <s>vipāka</s> (post-digestive effect), and cold [in potency] — that is the exudate of gold. // Car_6,1.3.57

children.text: rūpyasya kaṭukaḥ śvetaḥ śītaḥ svādu vipacyate /
children.translated_text: That from silver is pungent, white, cold, and matures into sweet <s>vipāka</s>.
That from copper is like the throat of a peacock [in color], bitter, hot, and matures into pungent <s>vipāka</s>. // Car_6,1.3.58
That which resembles <s>Guggulu</s> (bdellium) in appearance, is bitter with a salty taste,

children.text: kaṭurvipāke śītaśca sarvaśreṣṭhaḥ sa cāyasaḥ // Car_6,1.3.59
children.translated_text: pungent in <s>vipāka</s>, and cold [in potency] — that is the best of all, being derived from iron. // Car_6,1.3.59
All [varieties] have the smell of cow's urine and are applicable in all treatments,
but in <s>rasāyana</s> applications, the last one (iron-derived) is specially commended. // Car_6,1.3.60
In order: for <s>Vāta</s>-<s>Pitta</s>, <s>Śleṣman</s> (Kapha)-<s>Pitta</s>, <s>Kapha</s>, and [all] three [<s>doṣas</s>] —
the exudates from ores of gold etc. are especially praised, respectively. // Car_6,1.3.61
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'With methods' means accompanied by procedures. // 1

children.text: śilājatuvidhānaṃ ca yathākramaṃ vātapitte ityādigranthena vaktavyam // 2
children.translated_text: And the method of [using] <s>Śilājatu</s> will be stated by the passage 'in order, for <s>Vāta</s>-<s>Pitta</s>' etc. // 2

children.text: hemādiśabdeneha hemādisambhavasthānabhūtaśilocyate yato na sākṣāt suvarṇādibhya eva śilājatu sravati // 3
children.translated_text: By the word 'gold etc.,' the rocks that are the source-locations of gold etc. are referred to, since <s>Śilājatu</s> does not exude directly from gold etc. themselves. // 3
'<s>Mṛtsna</s>' means smooth; '<s>accha</s>' means clear. // 4

children.text: yastu rūpyabhave kaṭurase viruddhaḥ svāduḥ pāka uktaḥ sa utsargāpavādanyāyena jñeyaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: The sweet <s>vipāka</s> stated for the silver-derived [<s>Śilājatu</s>], which contradicts its pungent <s>rasa</s>, should be understood through the principle of general rule and exception. // 5

children.text: vīryaṃ tu tāmrabhavasyoṣṇasya tathā trayāṇāṃ ca śītatvayuktānām atyuṣṇaśītavīryatāyā avakāśo nāsti ataḥ sāmānyaguṇakathane nātyuṣṇaśītam itipadena uṣṇasya śītasya ca vīryasya prakarṣo niṣidhyate tenānuṣṇāśītatvaṃ vidhīyate tataśca śilājatuni vīryaṃ śītam uṣṇaṃ vābhihitamapi na balavadbhavatīti labhyate // 6]
children.translated_text: As for the <s>vīrya</s> (potency): the copper-derived one is hot, and three [others] are cold — yet there is no scope for extreme heat or coldness, since in the general description [of <s>Śilājatu</s>] the phrase 'neither too hot nor too cold' prohibits an extreme of hot or cold <s>vīrya</s>; thereby a temperate quality (<s>anūṣṇāśītatva</s>) is prescribed. Thus it is understood that even though hot or cold <s>vīrya</s> is stated for <s>Śilājatu</s>, it is not strongly predominant. // 6]
During the use of <s>Śilājatu</s>, one should avoid foods that cause burning (<s>vidāhin</s>) and are heavy,
and at all times one should avoid <s>Kulattha</s> (horse gram). // Car_6,1.3.62

children.text: te hy atyantaviruddhatvād aśmano bhedanāḥ param /
children.translated_text: For they, being extremely incompatible, are observed in the world to be supreme stone-breakers (lithogenic),
therefore their use is prohibited [during <s>Śilājatu</s> therapy]. // Car_6,1.3.63

children.text: payāṃsi takrāṇi rasāḥ sayūṣās toyaṃ samūtrā vividhāḥ kaṣāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Milk, buttermilk, meat juices, broths, water, various urines, and decoctions

children.text: āloḍanārthaṃ girijasya śastās te te prayojyāḥ prasamīkṣya kāryam // Car_6,1.3.64
children.translated_text: are recommended for mixing with <s>Śilājatu</s> (the mountain-born substance); they should be employed after considering the purpose. // Car_6,1.3.64

children.text: na so 'sti rogo bhuvi sādhyarūpaḥ śilāhvayaṃ yaṃ na jayet prasahya /
children.translated_text: There is no curable disease on earth that <s>Śilājatu</s> cannot conquer forcefully.

children.text: tat kālayogairvidhibhiḥ prayuktaṃ svasthasya corjāṃ vipulāṃ dadāti // Car_6,1.3.65
children.translated_text: And when employed at the right time and by the proper methods, it bestows abundant vigor even on the healthy. // Car_6,1.3.65

children.text: karapracitike pāde daśa ṣaṭ ca maharṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Karapracitīya</s> quarter, sixteen
formulations of accomplished <s>rasāyanas</s> have been declared by the great sage. // Car_6,1.3.66

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsāsthāne rasāyanādhyāye karapracitīyo nāma rasāyanapādastṛtīyaḥ // Car_6,1.3.67
children.translated_text: Thus in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s> and redacted by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>Rasāyana</s>, [ends] the third quarter called <s>Karapracitīya</s>. // Car_6,1.3.67
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'During the uses of <s>Śilājatu</s>' — the plural indicates different uses distinguished by [different] mixing vehicles etc. This should be understood. // 1
Although heavy [foods] are prohibited during <s>Śilājatu</s> use, the use of milk etc. [as adjuvants] is [permitted] by force of special instruction. // 2
'At all times' means as long as the qualities beneficial for the <s>rasāyana</s> [regimen] persist. // 3

children.text: kecit tu yāvajjīvaṃ kulatthavarjanam āhuḥ yaduktaṃ suśrute tadbhāvitaḥ kapotāṃśca kulatthāṃśca vivarjayet iti // 4
children.translated_text: Some, however, say <s>Kulattha</s> should be avoided for life, as stated in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'One who has consumed [<s>Śilājatu</s>] should avoid pigeons and <s>Kulattha</s>.' // 4
He praises the use of <s>Śilājatu</s> with 'there is no [curable disease]' etc. // 5]
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, 1 [<s>Rasāyanādhyāya</s>], 3 [<s>Karapracitīya</s>]
Now we shall expound the quarter on <s>Rasāyana</s> called <s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s> (the origin of <s>Āyurveda</s>). // Car_6,1.4.1
Thus said the venerable <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car_6,1.4.2
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: āyurvedasamutthānīyo nāma rasāyanapādaḥ pāriśeṣyād ucyate āyurvedasamutthānam asminn astīti matvarthīyacchapratyayeṇāyurvedasamutthānīyaḥ // 1]
children.translated_text: The quarter called <s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s> is so named by residual determination: '<s>Āyurvedasamutthāna</s> (the origin of <s>Āyurveda</s>) is [described] in this' — [formed] with the <s>-īya</s> suffix in the sense of 'possessing.' // 1]

children.text: ṛṣayaḥ khalu kadācicchālīnā yāyāvarāśca grāmyauṣadhyāhārāḥ santaḥ sāmpannikā mandaceṣṭā nātikalyāśca prāyeṇa babhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: Once, the sages — both the sedentary (<s>śālīna</s>) and the itinerant (<s>yāyāvara</s>) — subsisting on village herbs and food, had generally become moderately affluent, sluggish in activity, and not fully healthy.

children.text: te sarvāsām itikartavyatānām asamarthāḥ santo grāmyavāsakṛtamātmadoṣaṃ matvā pūrvanivāsam apagatagrāmyadoṣaṃ śivaṃ puṇyam udāraṃ medhyam agamyam asukṛtibhir gaṅgāprabhavam amaragandharvakiṃnarānucaritam anekaratnanicayamacintyādbhutaprabhāvaṃ brahmarṣisiddhacāraṇānucaritaṃ divyatīrthauṣadhiprabhavam atiśaraṇyaṃ himavantam amarādhipatiguptaṃ jagmur bhṛgvaṅgiro'trivasiṣṭhakaśyapāgastyapulastyavāmadevāsitagautamaprabhṛtayo maharṣayaḥ // Car_6,1.4.3
children.translated_text: Finding themselves incapable of all their duties, considering the deterioration of self to be caused by village-dwelling, they went to their former abode, free from the defects of village life — auspicious, meritorious, noble, sacred, unattainable by those lacking merit, originating from the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, frequented by gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, filled with heaps of many gems, of inconceivable and wondrous power, frequented by <s>Brahmarṣis</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>, the source of divine sacred sites and medicinal herbs, supremely refuge-giving — [namely] <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalayas), guarded by the lord of the immortals. [They were] the great sages <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Asita</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and others. // Car_6,1.4.3
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
The sages' being '<s>śālīna</s>' (sedentary) and '<s>yāyāvara</s>' (itinerant) is due to their adoption of different modes of religious practice. // 1
'<s>Sāmpannika</s>' means those who use whatever is available (<s>sampannam</s>). // 2
'Not fully healthy' means not entirely free from disease. // 3
'Duties' (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) means activities. // 4

The mention of <s>Indra</s> as a synonym [for the lord of the immortals] is for the purpose of praise, and this praise is [appropriate] because <s>Indra</s> was the one who disseminated <s>Āyurveda</s>. // 5]

children.text: tān indraḥ sahasradṛg amaragurur abravītsvāgataṃ brahmavidāṃ jñānatapodhanānāṃ brahmarṣīṇām /
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, the thousand-eyed one, the preceptor of the immortals, said to them: 'Welcome to the <s>Brahmarṣis</s> rich in knowledge and <s>tapas</s> (austerity), knowers of <s>Brahman</s>!

children.text: asti nanu vo glānir aprabhāvatvaṃ vaisvaryaṃ vaivarṇyaṃ ca grāmyavāsakṛtam asukham asukhānubandhaṃ ca grāmyo hi vāso mūlam aśastānāṃ tat kṛtaḥ puṇyakṛdbhir anugrahaḥ prajānāṃ svaśarīramavekṣituṃ kālaḥ kālaścāyamāyurvedopadeśasya brahmarṣīṇām ātmanaḥ prajānāṃ cānugrahārtham āyurvedamaśvinau mahyaṃ prāyacchatāṃ prajāpatiraśvibhyāṃ prajāpataye brahmā prajānām alpam āyur jarāvyādhibahulam asukham asukhānubandham alpatvād alpatapodamaniyamadānādhyayanasaṃcayaṃ matvā puṇyatamam āyuḥprakarṣakaraṃ jarāvyādhipraśamanam ūrjaskaram amṛtaṃ śivaṃ śaraṇyamudāraṃ bhavanto mattaḥ śrotumarhatāthopadhārayituṃ prakāśayituṃ ca prajānugrahārthamārṣaṃ brahma ca prati maitrīṃ kāruṇyam ātmanaś cānuttamaṃ puṇyamudāraṃ brāhmamakṣayaṃ karmeti // Car_6,1.4.4
children.translated_text: Surely you have languor, loss of vigor, loss of mastery, and loss of complexion — [all] caused by village-dwelling — which is suffering and leads to further suffering. For village-dwelling is the root of all misfortune. But you, doers of merit, have bestowed benefit upon the people. Now it is time to attend to one's own body. And this is the time for instruction in <s>Āyurveda</s>. For the benefit of the <s>Brahmarṣis</s> themselves and of all people — the <s>Aśvins</s> gave <s>Āyurveda</s> to me, <s>Prajāpati</s> to the <s>Aśvins</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Prajāpati</s>. Seeing that the lifespan of beings is short, beset with old age and disease, full of suffering and leading to further suffering — and because of its shortness, [allowing] only little accumulation of austerity, self-control, restraint, charity, study, and merit — [<s>Brahmā</s> taught this] most sacred [science] that extends lifespan, pacifies old age and disease, bestows strength, is immortal, auspicious, a supreme refuge, and noble. You are worthy to hear it from me, and then to retain it, disseminate it, and benefit the people — [an act of] friendship and compassion toward the sages' <s>Brahman</s> and toward the people, and for yourselves the most excellent, noble, sacred, and imperishable work of <s>Brahmā</s>.' // Car_6,1.4.4

children.text: tacchrutvā vibudhapativacanam ṛṣayaḥ sarva evāmaravaram ṛgbhis tuṣṭuvuḥ prahṛṣṭāśca tadvacanamabhinananduśceti // Car_6,1.4.5
children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the lord of the gods, all the sages praised the foremost of the immortals with <s>Ṛg</s> verses, and delighted, they applauded his words. // Car_6,1.4.5
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'Leading to further suffering' — meaning it brings in its wake disease-form suffering. // 1
'Root' means cause. // 2

children.text: kṛtaḥ prajānāmanugraha iti grāme sthitvā āyurvedoktārogyasādhanadharmādiprakāśanena prajānugrahaḥ kṛta evetyarthaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: 'Benefit upon the people has been bestowed' — means that by dwelling in the village and teaching the means of health, <s>Dharma</s>, etc. as prescribed by <s>Āyurveda</s>, the benefit of the people has indeed been accomplished. // 3
The word 'this' should be connected with both [occurrences of] the word 'time.' // 4
The analysis is: 'to <s>Prajāpati</s> — <s>Brahmā</s> [gave it].' // 5
The construction is: 'Having considered the lifespan of beings to be short etc.' // 6
'Because of its shortness' — supply: 'of the lifespan.' // 7

children.text: alpastapaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ saṃcayo'smin alpe āyuṣi tat tathā // 8
children.translated_text: 'Little is the accumulation of austerity etc. in this short lifespan' — thus [the compound is formed]. // 8
The word '<s>prati</s>' connects individually with 'friendship' and each of the following [virtues]. // 9
The word '<s>atha</s>' indicates the commencement [of a new topic]. // 10

children.text: tena maitrīkāruṇyādīnyadhikṛtya yaṃ brahmā prajāpataye'dāt tamanuśrotum arhateti yojanā // 11
children.translated_text: Thus the construction is: 'With reference to friendship, compassion, etc. — you are worthy to hear from me that which <s>Brahmā</s> gave to <s>Prajāpati</s>.' // 11

children.text: yadyapi ca ṛṣayo bharadvājadvārā indrādadhigatāyurvedāḥ tathāpi grāmyavāsakṛtamanoglānyā na tathā sphuṭārtho vartata iti śaṅkayā punarindras tānupadiśati // 12]
children.translated_text: Although the sages had already received <s>Āyurveda</s> from <s>Indra</s> through [the intermediary] <s>Bharadvāja</s>, nonetheless, because their mental capacity was not clear due to the languor caused by village-dwelling, <s>Indra</s> instructs them again, apprehending [this difficulty]. // 12]

children.text: athendras tadāyurvedāmṛtam ṛṣibhyaḥ saṃkramyovāca etatsarvamanuṣṭheyam ayaṃ ca śivaḥ kālo rasāyanānāṃ divyāścauṣadhayo himavatprabhavāḥ prāptavīryāḥ tadyathā aindrī brāhmī payasyā kṣīrapuṣpī śrāvaṇī mahāśrāvaṇī śatāvarī vidārī jīvantī punarnavā nāgabalā sthirā vacā chattrā aticchatrā medā mahāmedā jīvanīyāścānyāḥ payasā prayuktāḥ ṣaṇmāsāt paramāyurvayaśca taruṇamanāmayatvaṃ svaravarṇasampadam upacayaṃ medhāṃ smṛtimuttamabalam iṣṭāṃścāparān bhāvān āvahanti siddhāḥ // Car_6,1.4.6
children.translated_text: Then <s>Indra</s>, having transmitted that nectar of <s>Āyurveda</s> to the sages, said: 'All this should be practiced, and this is the auspicious time for <s>rasāyanas</s>. The divine herbs originating from the <s>Himavat</s> have attained [full] potency — namely: <s>Aindrī</s>, <s>Brāhmī</s>, <s>Payasyā</s>, <s>Kṣīrapuṣpī</s>, <s>Śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>Mahāśrāvaṇī</s>, <s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Vidārī</s>, <s>Jīvantī</s>, <s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>Nāgabalā</s>, <s>Sthirā</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, <s>Cchatrā</s>, <s>Aticchatrā</s>, <s>Medā</s>, <s>Mahāmedā</s>, and other <s>Jīvanīya</s> (life-giving) herbs. These, when employed with milk and accomplished [through proper preparation], within six months bring supreme longevity, youthful age, freedom from disease, excellence of voice and complexion, bodily growth, intellect, memory, supreme strength, and other desired benefits.' // Car_6,1.4.6
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'<s>Mahāśrāvaṇī</s>' is <s>Alambuṣā</s>. // 1
'<s>Aticchatrā</s>' is <s>Madhurikā</s>. // 2]

children.text: brahmasuvarcalā nāmauṣadhir yā hiraṇyakṣīrā puṣkarasadṛśapattrā ādityaparṇī nāmauṣadhiryā sūryakāntā iti vijñāyate suvarṇakṣīrā sūryamaṇḍalākārapuṣpā ca nārīnāmauṣadhiḥ aśvabalā iti vijñāyate yā bilvajasadṛśapattrā kāṣṭhagodhā nāmauṣadhir godhākārā sarpānāmauṣadhiḥ sarpākārā somo nāmauṣadhirājaḥ pañcadaśaparvā sa soma iva hīyate vardhate ca padmā nāmauṣadhiḥ padmākārā padmaraktā padmagandhā ca ajānām auṣadhiḥ ajaśṛṅgī iti vijñāyate nīlā nāmauṣadhistu nīlakṣīrā nīlapuṣpā latāpratānabahuleti āsāmoṣadhīnāṃ yāṃ yāmevopalabheta tasyās tasyāḥ svarasasya sauhityaṃ gatvā snehabhāvitāyām ārdrapalāśadroṇyāṃ sapidhānāyāṃ digvāsāḥ śayīta tatra pralīyate ṣaṇmāsena punaḥ sambhavati tasyājaṃ payaḥ pratyavasthāpanaṃ ṣaṇmāsena devatānukārī bhavati vayovarṇasvarākṛtibalaprabhābhiḥ svayaṃ cāsya sarvavācogatāni prādurbhavanti divyaṃ cāsya cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ca bhavati gatir yojanasahasraṃ daśavarṣasahasrāṇy āyur anupadravaṃ ceti // Car_6,1.4.7
children.translated_text: The herb called <s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s> has golden sap and leaves resembling lotus. The herb called <s>Ādityaparṇī</s> — known as '<s>Sūryakāntā</s>' — has golden sap and flowers shaped like the sun's disc. The herb called <s>Nārī</s> — known as '<s>Aśvabalā</s>' — has leaves resembling <s>Bilva</s> (wood-apple) seeds. The herb called <s>Kāṣṭhagodhā</s> is shaped like a monitor lizard. The herb called '<s>Sarpa</s>' is snake-shaped. The king of herbs is <s>Soma</s>, having fifteen joints — it wanes and waxes like the moon. The herb called <s>Padmā</s> is lotus-shaped, lotus-colored, and lotus-scented. The herb of goats — known as '<s>Ajaśṛṅgī</s>' (goat's horn). The herb called <s>Nīlā</s> has blue sap, blue flowers, and abundant creeping tendrils. Whichever of these herbs one obtains, having drunk to satiety of its juice, one should lie naked in a trough of fresh <s>Palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) wood seasoned with ghee, with a lid. There [in the trough], one dissolves in six months and is reborn. Goat's milk is used for gradual dietary restoration. Within six months, one becomes like a god in age, complexion, voice, form, strength, and radiance. All forms of speech spontaneously manifest in him, and he gains divine sight and hearing. His range of movement extends a thousand <s>yojanas</s>, and his lifespan is ten thousand years, free from affliction. // Car_6,1.4.7
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
<s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s> and the other herbs of the described characteristics are divine herbs and not widely known. // 1
Some describe '<s>Ādityaparṇī</s>' as <s>Sūryāvarta</s> itself, grown in a special region. // 2

children.text: aśvabaleti jñāyata iti ṛṣibhirevānena nāmnā jñāyate nalaukikaiḥ lokāprasiddhatvāt // 3
children.translated_text: 'Known as <s>Aśvabalā</s>' — it is known by this name among the sages alone, not among common people, because of its not being well-known in the world. // 3

children.text: soma iva vardhate hīyata iti yathāsomavṛddhikṣayau tathā tatkālameva tasya vṛddhikṣayau bhavataḥ // 4
children.translated_text: 'It waxes and wanes like <s>Soma</s> (the moon)' — just as the moon waxes and wanes, so its waxing and waning occur at that very same time. // 4

children.text: pralīyata iti druto bhavati anye tu mūrchatīti varṇayanti // 5
children.translated_text: 'Dissolves' (<s>pralīyate</s>) means liquefies. Others, however, describe it as 'one faints.' // 5
'Gradual dietary restoration' (<s>pratyavasthāpana</s>) should be understood as applicable to the resumption of food. // 6
'All forms of speech' (<s>sarva-vāco-gata</s>) means all particular types of utterance. // 7]
The potency of divine herbs can be endured by those like you [sages],
but it cannot be endured by those who have not cultivated themselves spiritually. // Car_6,1.4.8

children.text: oṣadhīnāṃ prabhāveṇa tiṣṭhatāṃ sve ca karmaṇi /
children.translated_text: By the power of the herbs and by abiding in your own [spiritual] practice,
all complete well-being will come to pass for you. // Car_6,1.4.9
These herbs, born in their proper regions, can indeed be used

children.text: śakyā oṣadhayo hy etāḥ sevituṃ viṣayābhijāḥ // Car_6,1.4.10
children.translated_text: by forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprastha</s>) and householders (<s>gṛhastha</s>) who are purified and self-controlled. // Car_6,1.4.10
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: etaddivyaṃ rasāyanamṛṣibhistadvidhair vā sevyam iti darśayann āha divyānām ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Showing that this divine <s>rasāyana</s> is to be used by sages or those of similar [spiritual attainment], he says 'of divine [herbs]' etc. // 1

children.text: viṣayābhijā iti svocitapuṇyadeśe jātā ityarthaḥ apuṇye tu deśe divyauṣadhijanmaiva na bhavati bhavantyo 'pi nirvāryā bhavantīti bhāvaḥ // 2]
children.translated_text: 'Born in their proper regions' (<s>viṣayābhijāḥ</s>) means born in holy regions appropriate to them. In an unholy region, divine herbs are not even born; and if born [there], they are ineffective — this is the import. // 2]
But those [herbs] that are of milder potency due to the qualities of the terrain

children.text: mṛduvīryatarās tāsāṃ vidhirjñeyaḥ sa eva tu // Car_6,1.4.11
children.translated_text: and due to the middling practice [of the users] — for them, the same method should be known [as applicable]. // Car_6,1.4.11

children.text: paryeṣṭuṃ tāḥ prayoktuṃ vā ye 'samarthāḥ sukhārthinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those seekers of well-being who are unable to find or to use those [divine herbs],
this other <s>rasāyana</s> method is recommended for them. // Car_6,1.4.12
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: samprati brahmasuvarcalādīnāṃ yathā mṛduvīryatvaṃ bhavati tadāha yās tv ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now he states how <s>Brahmasuvarcalā</s> etc. come to have milder potency, with 'but those' etc. // 1
'Due to the qualities of the terrain' — i.e., due to the properties of terrain other than the praised regions like the Himalayas etc. // 2
'Of them' — of forest-dwellers etc. who are other than the sages. // 3

children.text: madhyamena ca karmaṇeti asamyakprayogeṇa kiṃvā anatimahatādṛṣṭena // 4]
children.translated_text: 'Due to middling practice' — due to improper application, or alternatively, due to unseen [karmic] merit that is not very great. // 4]

children.text: balyānāṃ jīvanīyānāṃ bṛṃhaṇīyāś ca yā daśa /
children.translated_text: Of the ten groups [called] strengthening (<s>balya</s>), vitalizing (<s>jīvanīya</s>), and bulk-promoting (<s>bṛṃhaṇīya</s>),

children.text: vayasaḥ sthāpanānāṃ ca khadirasyāsanasya ca // Car_6,1.4.13
children.translated_text: and of the age-stabilizing [group], and of <s>Khadira</s> and <s>Āsana</s>,
and of <s>Kharjūra</s> (dates), <s>Madhūka</s> (Mahua), <s>Mustā</s>, and <s>Utpala</s> (blue lotus),
and of <s>Mṛdvīkā</s> (grapes), <s>Viḍaṅga</s>, <s>Vacā</s>, and <s>Citraka</s>,
and of <s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>Payasyā</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>, and <s>Joṅgaka</s>,

children.text: ṛddhyā nāgabalāyāśca dvāradāyā dhavasya ca // Car_6,1.4.15
children.translated_text: and of <s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Nāgabalā</s>, <s>Dvāradā</s>, and <s>Dhava</s>,
and of <s>Triphalā</s> and <s>Kaṇṭakārī</s>, and of <s>Vidārī</s> and <s>Candana</s> (sandalwood),
and of sugarcane, <s>Śara</s>-root, <s>Śrīparṇī</s>, and <s>Tiniśa</s> —

children.text: rasāḥ pṛthak pṛthag grāhyāḥ palāśakṣāra eva ca /
children.translated_text: the juices should be taken individually, and also <s>Palāśa</s> alkali-water.

children.text: eṣāṃ palonmitān bhāgān payo gavyaṃ caturguṇam // Car_6,1.4.17
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s>-weight portions of each of these, [combined with] four parts of cow's milk,

children.text: dve pātre tilatailasya dve ca gavyasya sarpiṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: two <s>pātras</s> of sesame oil and two of cow's ghee —

children.text: tat sādhyaṃ sarvam ekatra susiddhaṃ snehamuddharet // Car_6,1.4.18
children.translated_text: all this should be cooked together; when well-prepared, the fat should be extracted. // Car_6,1.4.17-18
Into that, an <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>Āmalaka</s> powder soaked a hundred times
in its own juice should be added, along with fresh honey,
and one <s>prastha</s> of sugar powder should be added,

children.text: tugākṣīryāḥ sapippalyāḥ sthāpyaṃ saṃmūrchitaṃ ca tat // Car_6,1.4.20
children.translated_text: along with <s>Tugākṣīrī</s> (bamboo-manna) and <s>Pippalī</s>. The [preparation] should be blended and stored
