in a clean earthen vessel seasoned with ghee, for half a month.

children.text: mātrāmagnisamāṃ tasya tata ūrdhvaṃ prayojayet // Car_6,1.4.21
children.translated_text: After that, one should use it in a dose proportionate to one's digestive fire. // Car_6,1.4.19-21
Of gold, copper, coral, iron, and crystal,
and of pearl, <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), conch, and silver —
adding one-sixteenth measure of their powders, and avoiding exertion and sexual intercourse,

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe ca bhuñjīta ṣaṣṭikaṃ kṣīrasarpiṣā // Car_6,1.4.23
children.translated_text: one should eat <s>Ṣaṣṭika</s> rice with milk and ghee after each digestion. // Car_6,1.4.22-23
This [preparation] pacifies all diseases, is aphrodisiac, supremely life-promoting,
bestowing strength of <s>sattva</s> (mind), memory, body, digestive fire, intellect, senses, and [overall] strength.
It is supremely vigor-producing, and produces [excellent] complexion and voice.
It pacifies poison and misfortune, and bestows mastery of all forms of speech.

children.text: siddhārthatāṃ cābhinavaṃ vayaśca prajāpriyatvaṃ ca yaśaśca loke /
children.translated_text: Those who desire fulfillment of aims, renewed youth, love of progeny, and fame in the world

children.text: prayojyam icchadbhiridaṃ yathāvad rasāyanaṃ brāhmamudāravīryam // Car_6,1.4.26
children.translated_text: should use this <s>Brāhma</s> (divine) <s>rasāyana</s> of noble potency according to the proper method. // Car_6,1.4.24-26
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
In [the verse beginning with] 'strengthening' etc. — '<s>Joṅgaka</s>' is <s>Aguru</s> (aloeswood). // 1
'<s>Dvāradā</s>' is the <s>Śāka</s> tree (teak), or alternatively <s>Kapikacchu</s> (Mucuna). // 2
'<s>Śrīparṇī</s>' is <s>Gambhārī</s> (Gmelina arborea). // 3
'<s>Palāśa</s> alkali' means <s>Palāśa</s> alkali-water. // 4
'<s>Sucaukṣe</s>' means very clean. // 5
'A dose proportionate to the fire' means a dose appropriate to one's digestive capacity. // 6

children.text: ṣoḍaśīṃ mātrāmiti āmalakādicūrṇayuktaghṛtāpekṣayā ṣoḍaśabhāgo hemādicūrṇād grāhyaḥ // 7]
children.translated_text: 'One-sixteenth measure' — with respect to the <s>Āmalaka</s> etc. powder-combined ghee, one-sixteenth should be taken of the gold etc. powders. // 7]
The <s>kuṭīprāveśa</s> (entering-the-hut) [method] is beneficial for those who are capable, free from disease, wise, self-controlled,
of auspicious time, and possessed of [requisite] provisions. // Car_6,1.4.27

children.text: ato'nyathā tu ye teṣāṃ sauryamārutiko vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: But for those who are otherwise, the <s>saurya-mārutika</s> (sun-and-wind) method [is recommended].

children.text: tayoḥ śreṣṭhataraḥ pūrvo vidhiḥ sa tu suduṣkaraḥ // Car_6,1.4.28
children.translated_text: Of the two, the former method is superior, but it is very difficult to perform. // Car_6,1.4.28
If diseases arise from a lapse in the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen,

children.text: yathāsvamauṣadhaṃ teṣāṃ kāryaṃ muktvā rasāyanam // Car_6,1.4.29
children.translated_text: the appropriate medicine for each [disease] should be administered, setting aside the <s>rasāyana</s>. // Car_6,1.4.29
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: kuṭīprāveśikarasāyanaviṣayān vātātapikarasāyanaviṣayāṃśca puruṣān āha samarthānām ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: He describes the persons suitable for the <s>kuṭīprāveśika</s> <s>rasāyana</s> and those suitable for the <s>vātātapika</s> <s>rasāyana</s> with 'of those who are capable' etc. // 1
'Of auspicious time' (<s>kṣaṇin</s>) means those who have [chosen] an auspicious moment. // 2
'<s>Sauryamārutika</s>' — so called because it is performed with exposure to sun and wind. // 3]
One who speaks truth, who is free from anger, who has renounced wine and sexual intercourse,
who is non-violent, who avoids exertion, who is tranquil, who speaks pleasantly, // Car_6,1.4.30
who is devoted to prayer and purity, who is steadfast, who is always generous, who is austere,
who delights in worshiping gods, cows, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, preceptors, teachers, and elders, // Car_6,1.4.31
who is always compassionate, who is always aware of mercy,
who has balanced waking and sleeping, who always eats milk and ghee, // Car_6,1.4.32
who knows place, time, and measure, who knows propriety, who is free from egotism,
who follows praiseworthy conduct, who is of unmixed [diet], whose senses are inclined toward the inner self, // Car_6,1.4.33
who attends upon elders, believers, and those who have conquered themselves —
one should know such a man, devoted to the scriptures of <s>Dharma</s>, as a perpetual <s>rasāyana</s>. // Car_6,1.4.34

children.text: guṇair etaiḥ samuditaiḥ prayuṅkte yo rasāyanam /
children.translated_text: One who, endowed with all these qualities combined, undertakes <s>rasāyana</s>

children.text: rasāyanaguṇān sarvān yathoktān sa samaśnute // Car_6,1.4.35
children.translated_text: attains all the stated benefits of <s>rasāyana</s>. // Car_6,1.4.35
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states in general the qualities of the person suitable for <s>rasāyana</s> with 'one who speaks truth' etc. // 1
'One who is aware of mercy' (<s>karuṇavedin</s>) means one who perceives beings with compassion. // 2
'Of unmixed [diet]' (<s>asaṃkīrṇa</s>) means one who eats unmixed food [i.e., does not eat promiscuously]. // 3
'Perpetual <s>rasāyana</s>' (<s>nitya-rasāyana</s>) — one whose <s>rasāyana</s> practice is constant. // 4]
A being never attains the benefits of <s>rasāyana</s> without first expelling

children.text: rasāyanaguṇair jantur yujyate na kadācana // Car_6,1.4.36
children.translated_text: the bodily and mental <s>doṣas</s>, at least in a general manner. // Car_6,1.4.36
For the formulations aimed at extending lifespan and destroying aging and disease
succeed [only] for those of purified mind and body who are self-disciplined. // Car_6,1.4.37
This [teaching] should not be imparted at all to those who are spiritually fallen,

children.text: arujebhyo 'dvijātibhyaḥ śuśrūṣā yeṣu nāsti ca // Car_6,1.4.38
children.translated_text: to non-<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are without disease, and to those in whom there is no desire to learn. // Car_6,1.4.38
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: manaḥśuddhyaiva prayatātmatāyāṃ labdhāyāṃ punas tadabhidhānam itaramānasaguṇeṣu prayatātmatāyā abhyarhitatopadarśanārtham // 1
children.translated_text: Even though self-discipline is already obtained when mental purity is attained, its re-statement is for the purpose of showing its special importance among the other mental qualities. // 1

children.text: arujebhyo 'dvijātibhyo yeṣu ca puruṣeṣu śuśrūṣā nāsti teṣu caitan na vācyamiti yojanā // 2]
children.translated_text: 'To non-<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are without disease, and to those in whom there is no desire to learn' — the construction is: this should not be imparted to such persons. // 2]
The <s>rasāyana</s> formulations, the aphrodisiac formulations that are recognized,
and all medicine for disorders — all these depend on the physician. // Car_6,1.4.39
Therefore, a wise person should honor the physician — the teacher of life (<s>prāṇācārya</s>), who is intelligent and well-versed in the <s>Vedas</s> —

children.text: aśvināv iva devendraḥ pūjayed atiśaktitaḥ // Car_6,1.4.40
children.translated_text: with the utmost of one's ability, just as <s>Indra</s> honored the <s>Aśvins</s>. // Car_6,1.4.40
The <s>Aśvins</s>, the divine physicians, are remembered as the bearers of the sacrifice.

children.text: yajñasya hi śiraśchinnaṃ punastābhyāṃ samāhitam // Car_6,1.4.41
children.translated_text: For the head of the sacrifice, once severed, was restored by those two. // Car_6,1.4.41

children.text: praśīrṇā daśanāḥ pūṣṇo netre naṣṭe bhagasya ca /
children.translated_text: The shattered teeth of <s>Pūṣan</s>, and the lost eyes of <s>Bhaga</s>,
and the paralysis of the arm of the thunderbolt-wielder (<s>Indra</s>) — were all treated by those two. // Car_6,1.4.42
And the cool-rayed one (the Moon), seized by <s>rājayakṣman</s> (consumption), was treated,
and <s>Candra</s> (the Moon), who had fallen from <s>Soma</s> [worship], was made happy again by those two. // Car_6,1.4.43

children.text: bhārgavaścyavanaḥ kāmī vṛddhaḥ san vikṛtiṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Cyavana</s> of the <s>Bhārgava</s> lineage, desirous [of youth], having become old and disfigured,
devoid of complexion and voice — was made young again by those two. // Car_6,1.4.44
By these and many other deeds, those two supreme physicians
became greatly revered by <s>Indra</s> and other noble [gods]. // Car_6,1.4.45

children.text: grahāḥ stotrāṇi mantrāṇi tathā nānāhavīṃṣi ca /
children.translated_text: Planetary offerings, hymns of praise, <s>mantras</s>, and various oblations,
and sacrificial animals with smoke-offerings — are prescribed for those two by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // Car_6,1.4.46
And at the morning pressing, <s>Indra</s> drinks the <s>Soma</s> together with the <s>Aśvins</s>,

children.text: sautrāmaṇyāṃ ca bhagavānaśvibhyāṃ saha modate // Car_6,1.4.47
children.translated_text: and at the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> sacrifice, the venerable [<s>Indra</s>] rejoices together with the <s>Aśvins</s>. // Car_6,1.4.47

children.text: indrāgnī cāśvinau caiva stūyante prāyaśo dvijaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and the <s>Aśvins</s> are mostly praised by the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;

children.text: stūyante vedavākyeṣu na tathānyā hi devatāḥ // Car_6,1.4.48
children.translated_text: they are praised in the Vedic passages — not so the other deities. // Car_6,1.4.48
By the ageless, immortal, wise gods, together with their lords, who are eternal —
by those reverent ones, the <s>Aśvins</s> are thus [honored as] physicians. // Car_6,1.4.49
By mortals — subject to death, disease, and aging, whose lives are mostly suffering, who desire happiness —

children.text: kiṃ punarbhiṣajo martyaiḥ pūjyāḥ syur nātiśaktitaḥ // Car_6,1.4.50
children.translated_text: how much more should physicians be honored with the utmost of one's ability! // Car_6,1.4.50
A physician who is virtuous, intelligent, skilled, twice-born, and well-versed in the treatises

children.text: prāṇibhirguruvatpūjyaḥ prāṇācāryaḥ sa hi smṛtaḥ // Car_6,1.4.51
children.translated_text: should be honored like a teacher by living beings — for he is remembered as the teacher of life (<s>prāṇācārya</s>). // Car_6,1.4.51
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: samprati rasāyanādisiddhir vaidyādhīnā tena vaidyastutim ārabhate ya ityādi // 1
children.translated_text: Now, since the success of <s>rasāyana</s> etc. depends on the physician, he commences the praise of the physician with 'the [formulations]' etc. // 1

children.text: prāṇācāryamityatra prāṇivaryam iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatra prāṇināṃ varyaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prāṇivaryaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇācārya</s>' (teacher of life) — alternatively, the reading is '<s>prāṇivarya</s>' (best among living beings); there, 'the best of beings' (<s>prāṇīnāṃ varyaḥ</s>) is '<s>prāṇivarya</s>.' // 2
'Those who carry the sacrifice' — thus they are '<s>yajñavāhas</s>' (bearers of sacrifice). // 3
He illustrates this very role as bearers of sacrifice with 'of <s>Dakṣa</s>' etc. // 4
'<s>Pūṣan</s>' is a [form of] the Sun; '<s>Bhaga</s>' is also a variety of the Sun. // 5

children.text: somābhipatita iti somābhipatanayogena pīḍita ityarthaḥ somātipacita iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatrāpyatipacanena somapānātiyogaṃ darśayati // 6
children.translated_text: 'Afflicted by <s>Soma</s>' (<s>somābhipatita</s>) means: afflicted by the conjunction with <s>Soma</s>-fall — that is the meaning. Or the reading is '<s>somātipatita</s>' — there too, by excessive cooking, it shows the excessive use of <s>Soma</s>-drinking. // 6
'<s>Grahas</s>' means: the drinking vessels for <s>Soma</s>. // 7

children.text: stotrāṇi stavāḥ stāvakavācaḥ śastrāṇīti kecit saṃśasyate 'neneti kṛtvā sāmaṛgvyatiriktaṃ stotramāhuḥ śastrāṇi astrāṇyeva vaṣaḍyuktāni śastrāṇi ca yajñe kalpyanta eva // 8
children.translated_text: '<s>Stotras</s>' means: praises, laudatory words. Some say — since 'that by which one praises' [is the etymology] — <s>stotras</s> mean hymns other than <s>Sāman</s> and <s>Ṛc</s>. '<s>Śastras</s>' means: weapons indeed — [those] accompanied by the <s>vaṣaṭ</s> call; both <s>śastras</s> and [weapons] are employed in the sacrifice. // 8

children.text: dhūmrāś ca paśava iti dhūmravarṇapaśavaḥ evaṃvarṇāś ca paśavaḥ śreṣṭhā bhavanti // 9
children.translated_text: 'And smoky animals' (<s>dhūmrāś ca paśavaḥ</s>) means: animals of smoky color. Animals of such color are the most excellent. // 9
'<s>Savana</s>' means: at the place of sacrifice. // 10
'<s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>' is a particular type of sacrifice. // 11
'Exceedingly powerful' (<s>atiśaktita</s>) means: even beyond one's own natural power. // 12]
Upon completion of learning, the second birth of the physician is declared;

children.text: aśnute vaidyaśabdaṃ hi na vaidyaḥ pūrvajanmanā // Car_6,1.4.52
children.translated_text: for one attains the title 'physician' — one is not a physician by [mere] prior birth. // Car_6,1.4.52
Upon completion of learning, either the <s>Brāhma</s> (divine) spirit or the <s>Ārṣa</s> (seer's) spirit

children.text: dhruvam āviśati jñānāttasmād vaidyo dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ // Car_6,1.4.53
children.translated_text: certainly enters [the physician] through knowledge — therefore the physician is called 'twice-born.' // Car_6,1.4.53
No wise person should maliciously think of, revile, or conduct himself harmfully toward

children.text: prāṇācāryaṃ budhaḥ kaścid icchann āyur anitvaram // Car_6,1.4.54
children.translated_text: the physician who is the teacher of life — [not] one who desires unimpeded longevity. // Car_6,1.4.54
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He states the basis for the application of the terms 'physician' and 'twice-born' with 'learning' etc. // 1

children.text: tena vidyāyogād vaidyatvaṃ tathā vidyāsamāptilakṣaṇajanmanā dvijatvaṃ bhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati // 2
children.translated_text: Thus it is stated: physician-hood comes from the connection with learning, and twice-born-hood comes from the birth characterized by the completion of learning. // 2

children.text: brāhmaṃ vā ārṣaṃ vā iti vikalpo vaidyaviśeṣābhiprāyād bhavati tayor yo naiṣṭhikacikitsārthastasya brāhmam itarasya tu lokānugrāhiṇa ārṣamiti vyavasthā // 3]
children.translated_text: The alternative 'either <s>Brāhma</s> or <s>Ārṣa</s>' is based on the distinction among physicians: for one whose purpose is ultimate liberation, [it is] the <s>Brāhma</s> [spirit]; for the other, who benefits the world, [it is] the <s>Ārṣa</s> — such is the distinction. // 3]
But a person who, having heard the [rules of] therapeutics — or even without having heard them —

children.text: nopākaroti vaidyāya nāsti tasyeha niṣkṛtiḥ // Car_6,1.4.55
children.translated_text: does not render service to the physician — for him there is no atonement in this world. // Car_6,1.4.55
The physician too, with effort, should protect all patients like his own sons

children.text: ābādhebhyo hi saṃrakṣed icchan dharmam anuttamam // Car_6,1.4.56
children.translated_text: from afflictions — desiring the supreme <s>dharma</s>. // Car_6,1.4.56
<s>Āyurveda</s> was revealed by the great sages, devoted to <s>dharma</s>,
for the purposes of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (prosperity), and <s>kāma</s> (pleasure) — by those desiring the imperishable abode. // Car_6,1.4.57
One who engages in healing not for the sake of wealth, not for the sake of pleasure,

children.text: vartate yaścikitsāyāṃ sa sarvam ativartate // Car_6,1.4.58
children.translated_text: but out of compassion for living beings — he surpasses all. // Car_6,1.4.58
Those who make the practice of healing a commodity for sale for the sake of livelihood —

children.text: te hitvā kāñcanaṃ rāśiṃ pāṃśurāśimupāsate // Car_6,1.4.59
children.translated_text: they, abandoning a heap of gold, attend upon a heap of dust. // Car_6,1.4.59
To those being dragged by terrible diseases toward the abode of <s>Vaivasvata</s> (Death),

children.text: chittvā vaivasvatān pāśān jīvitaṃ yaḥ prayacchati // Car_6,1.4.60
children.translated_text: he who, cutting <s>Vaivasvata</s>'s nooses, gives back life — // Car_6,1.4.60
no one comparable to that giver of <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> is found in this world;

children.text: na hi jīvitadānāddhi dānam anyad viśiṣyate // Car_6,1.4.61
children.translated_text: for no other gift is superior to the gift of life. // Car_6,1.4.61

children.text: paro bhūtadayā dharma iti matvā cikitsayā /
children.translated_text: Knowing that compassion for beings is the supreme <s>dharma</s>, he who

children.text: vartate yaḥ sa siddhārthaḥ sukham atyantam aśnute // Car_6,1.4.62
children.translated_text: engages in healing — he has accomplished his purpose and attains ultimate happiness. // Car_6,1.4.62
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Having heard' (<s>saṃśrutya</s>) means: having promised. // 1
'The practice of healing as a commodity' (<s>cikitsāpaṇya</s>) means: healing itself is the commodity to be sold. // 2

children.text: te hitvetyādau dharmārthaṃ kriyamāṇacikitsā mahāphalatvena kāñcanarāśitulyā itarā tv asārakalpā pāṃśurāśitulyā // 3
children.translated_text: In 'they, abandoning' etc.: healing practiced for the sake of <s>dharma</s> is like a heap of gold because of its great fruit; the other [healing for profit] is like a heap of dust because it is devoid of essence. // 3
'The abode of <s>Vaivasvata</s>' means: the house of <s>Yama</s> (Death). // 4]
The auspicious method of divine medicines, arising from <s>Āyurveda</s>,
having qualities barely inferior to ambrosia — the proven jewel-<s>rasāyana</s>; // Car_6,1.4.63
that which the Lord of the Immortals (<s>Indra</s>) declared to the accomplished celibate students —
all that has been fully revealed in [this section on] the origin of <s>Āyurveda</s>. // Car_6,1.4.64

children.text: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte cikitsitasthāne rasāyanādhyāye āyurvedasamutthānīyo nāma rasāyanapādaścaturthaḥ // Car_6,1.4.65
children.translated_text: Thus, in the treatise composed by <s>Agniveśa</s>, revised by <s>Caraka</s>, in the <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, in the chapter on <s>Rasāyana</s>, the fourth <s>rasāyana</s> quarter named <s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s> [is complete]. // Car_6,1.4.65
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
'Jewel-<s>rasāyana</s>' (<s>ratnarasāyana</s>) in the summary means: <s>rasāyana</s> combined with gems such as gold etc. // 1

children.text: āyurvedasamutthāne prakāśitatayā divyauṣadhividhyādi yaduvāca brahmacāribhyo'mareśvaraḥ tat saṃprakāśitam iti yojanā // 2]
children.translated_text: The construction is: that which the Lord of the Immortals declared to the celibate students regarding the origin of <s>Āyurveda</s> — the method of divine medicines etc. — all that has been fully revealed. // 2]
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, 1 [<s>Rasāyanādhyāya</s>], 4 [<s>Āyurvedasamutthānīya</s>]
Now we shall expound the <s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s> quarter of <s>Vājīkaraṇa</s> (aphrodisiac therapy). // Car_6,2.1.1
Thus indeed spoke the Blessed <s>Ātreya</s>. // Car_6,2.1.2
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: svasthorjaskaratvasāmānyāt rasāyanamanu vājīkaraṇaṃ vācyaṃ tatrāpi vājīkaraṇe pravṛttyupadarśakaprakaraṇayuktatvād ādau saṃyogaśaramūlīya ucyate /
children.translated_text: Because of the commonality in promoting vigor for the healthy, <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> is to be taught after <s>rasāyana</s>. And within <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> itself, the <s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s> is stated first because it appropriately contains the introductory topic showing the motivation [for the subject].
'<s>Saṃyogaśaramūlīya</s>' means: that in which there is 'the combination of <s>śaramūlas</s> (sugarcane roots).' // 1]
A self-controlled man should always seek <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> (aphrodisiac therapy),

children.text: tadāyattau hi dharmārthau prītiśca yaśa eva ca // Car_6,2.1.3
children.translated_text: for <s>dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> depend upon it, as do pleasure and fame. // Car_6,2.1.3
For this [<s>vājīkaraṇa</s>] is the foundation of [having] a son, and these virtues are dependent on offspring.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: avājī vājīvātyarthaṃ maithune śaktaḥ kriyate yena tad vājīkaraṇam // 1
children.translated_text: '<s>Vājīkaraṇa</s>' means: that by which one who is impotent (<s>avājī</s>) or one [already potent] is made capable of exceedingly powerful intercourse like a stallion (<s>vājī</s>). // 1

children.text: uktaṃ hi vājīvātibalo yena yātyapratihataḥ striyam ityādi // 2
children.translated_text: For it has been said: 'by which one goes to women with excessive strength like a stallion, unobstructed' etc. // 2

children.text: anvicchediti rasāyanānmahāphalāt tadapekṣayālpaphalaṃ vājīkaraṇaṃ paścād icchet // 3
children.translated_text: 'Should seek' — after <s>rasāyana</s>, which is of great fruit, one should seek <s>vājīkaraṇa</s>, which is of relatively lesser fruit, afterwards. // 3

children.text: puruṣa iti padena taruṇapuruṣagrāhiṇā bālavṛddhau niṣiddhavyavāyau nirākaroti // 4
children.translated_text: By the word 'man' (<s>puruṣa</s>), which takes [only] a young adult man, he excludes the boy and the old — for whom sexual intercourse is prohibited. // 4
For it has been said:
A very young boy, whose tissues are not yet fully formed, going to women,
would suddenly be damaged — like a small pond [drained] by irrigation. // 5

children.text: śuṣkaṃ rūkṣaṃ yathā kāṣṭhaṃ jantujagdhaṃ vijarjaram /
children.translated_text: Like dry, rough wood, eaten by insects, decayed —

children.text: spṛṣṭamāśu viśīryeta tathā vṛddhaḥ striyo vrajan iti // 6
children.translated_text: which crumbles when touched — so too an old man going to women. // 6

children.text: nityamityanena na rasāyanavat saṃprayogo vṛṣyasya kiṃtv āhāravat sarvadoṣayoga iti darśayati // 7
children.translated_text: By the word 'always' (<s>nitya</s>), he shows that <s>vṛṣya</s> (aphrodisiac) [use] is not [restricted] like <s>rasāyana</s> [to special courses], but rather, like food, is for constant application regarding all <s>doṣas</s>. // 7

children.text: ātmavānityanena durātmano vṛṣyakaraṇaṃ niṣedhati sa hi vṛṣyopayogādupacitadhātuḥ sann agamyāgamanamapi kuryāt // 8
children.translated_text: By 'self-controlled' (<s>ātmavān</s>), he prohibits the making of aphrodisiacs for the wicked; for he, having built up his tissues through aphrodisiac use, might even resort to illicit women. // 8

children.text: dharmādayo vṛṣyāyattā eva yathā bhavanti tadāha putrasyetyādi // 9
children.translated_text: He states how <s>dharma</s> etc. are indeed dependent on <s>vṛṣya</s> [therapy] with 'of a son' etc. // 9
'Foundation' (<s>āyatana</s>) means: cause. // 10

children.text: ete guṇā iti dharmādayaḥ vṛṣyaprayogajanitaḥ putro dharmādīn pituḥ sampādayatītyarthaḥ // 11
children.translated_text: 'These virtues' means: <s>dharma</s> etc. — a son born from <s>vṛṣya</s> application accomplishes <s>dharma</s> etc. for the father: this is the meaning. // 11

children.text: vājīkaraṇasevayā ceha yuktayaiva ṛtukāle ca maithunaṃ prādhānyenābhipretaṃ tena tisraiṣaṇīye traya upastambhāḥ ityādigranthena brahmacaryaṃ yaduktaṃ tad ṛtukāle yathāvidhikṛtamaithunāpratiṣedhakam iti na virodhaḥ // 12]
children.translated_text: And here, by <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> practice, intercourse primarily at the proper season [for procreation] is intended. Therefore there is no contradiction with the statement 'the three supports are: [celibacy]' etc. in the <s>Tisraiṣaṇīya</s> chapter, where celibacy is enjoined — for that [celibacy teaching] does not prohibit properly regulated intercourse at the appropriate season. // 12]

children.text: vājīkaraṇam agryaṃ ca kṣetraṃ strī yā praharṣiṇī // Car_6,2.1.4
children.translated_text: And the foremost <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> is a woman who is the 'field,' who is stimulating. // Car_6,2.1.4

children.text: iṣṭā hy ekaikaśo 'py arthāḥ paraṃ prītikarāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: For even individually, desired objects [of the senses] are considered supremely pleasure-giving;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ strīśarīre ye saṃghātena pratiṣṭhitāḥ // Car_6,2.1.5
children.translated_text: how much more so when they are established together in the body of a woman! // Car_6,2.1.5
For the aggregate of sense-objects exists in women and nowhere else.
That sense-object which is dependent on women produces pleasure exceedingly;

children.text: strīṣu prītirviśeṣeṇa strīṣv apatyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam // Car_6,2.1.6
children.translated_text: pleasure is especially in women; offspring is established in women. // Car_6,2.1.6

children.text: dharmārthau strīṣu lakṣmīśca strīṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> are in women; fortune (<s>lakṣmī</s>) is in women; the worlds are established in women.

children.text: surūpā yauvanasthā yā lakṣaṇairyā vibhūṣitā // Car_6,2.1.7
children.translated_text: She who is beautiful, in the bloom of youth, adorned with [auspicious] marks, // Car_6,2.1.7

children.text: yā vaśyā śikṣitā yā ca sā strī vṛṣyatamā matā /
children.translated_text: she who is submissive and well-trained — that woman is considered the most aphrodisiac.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
He states the foremost form of <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> among all aphrodisiacs with '<s>vājī</s>' etc. // 1
'Field' (<s>kṣetra</s>) means: like a field — because therein the seed in the form of semen sprouts. // 2

children.text: arthā iti śabdādayaḥ te ca strīgatādhararasakalaviṅkarutarūpādayaḥ prasiddhā eva // 3
children.translated_text: 'Objects' means: sounds etc. — and those are well known as the sounds of the lips, the voice of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, beautiful forms, etc. [all present in women]. // 3

children.text: dharmārthau strīṣviti sahaiva patnyā dharmaścarya ityādyupadeśād dharmaḥ tathānuraktā gṛhiṇī artharakṣaṇādi karotītyartha ityarthaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: '<s>Dharma</s> and <s>artha</s> are in women' — because of the teaching 'with his wife alone should one practice <s>dharma</s>' etc., [there is] <s>dharma</s>; likewise, a devoted wife manages wealth-protection etc. — that is <s>artha</s>: this is the meaning. // 4

children.text: striyā lakṣmyāḥ saṃyoge dhanasampad bhavatīti strīṣu lakṣmīḥ pratiṣṭhitetyarthaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: 'Fortune is in women' means: through the conjunction with <s>Lakṣmī</s> (the goddess of fortune) [in the form of a wife], prosperity of wealth occurs — this is the meaning. // 5
'Submissive' (<s>vaśyā</s>) means: obedient. // 6
'Well-trained' (<s>śikṣitā</s>) means: trained in the sixty-four arts such as singing, playing instruments, dancing, etc. as stated in the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s>. // 7]

children.text: nānābhaktyā tu lokasya daivayogācca yoṣitām // Car_6,2.1.8
children.translated_text: Due to the diverse inclinations of people and the providential conjunction of women, // Car_6,2.1.8

children.text: taṃ taṃ prāpya vivardhante naraṃ rūpādayo guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: upon attaining a particular man, qualities such as beauty etc. increase [in him].
She who — by age, beauty, speech, and gestures — is for someone the supreme woman, // Car_6,2.1.9

children.text: praviśatyāśu hṛdayaṃ daivād vā karmaṇo 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: who enters his heart quickly, whether by fate or by [ritual] action;
she who is in the form of the heart's delight, who shares the same desire of mind, // Car_6,2.1.10

children.text: samānasattvā yā vaśyā yā yasya prīyate priyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: who is of the same temperament, who is submissive, who delights in what he finds pleasing;

children.text: yā pāśabhūtā sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ parairguṇaiḥ // Car_6,2.1.11
children.translated_text: she who is a snare for all the senses through her supreme qualities; // Car_6,2.1.11

children.text: yayā viyukto nistrīkam aratir manyate jagat /
children.translated_text: separated from whom he considers the world joyless and devoid of women;

children.text: yasyā ṛte śarīraṃ nā dhatte śūnyam ivendriyaiḥ // Car_6,2.1.12
children.translated_text: without whom the body feels as if empty of its senses; // Car_6,2.1.12
seeing whom one is not overcome by grief, anxiety, displeasure, or fear;

children.text: yāti yāṃ prāpya visrambhaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣyatyatīva yām // Car_6,2.1.13
children.translated_text: attaining whom one reaches confidence; seeing whom one is exceedingly delighted; // Car_6,2.1.13
whom one approaches as if [she were] ever-new, always with an excess of passionate excitement;

children.text: gatvā gatvāpi bahuśo yāṃ tṛptiṃ naiva gacchati // Car_6,2.1.14
children.translated_text: with whom, even after going again and again many times, one never reaches satiety — // Car_6,2.1.14

children.text: sā strī vṛṣyatamā tasya nānābhāvā hi mānavāḥ /
children.translated_text: that woman is the most aphrodisiac for that man — for human beings are of diverse natures.

children.text: atulyagotrāṃ vṛṣyāṃ ca prahṛṣṭāṃ nirupadravām // Car_6,2.1.15
children.translated_text: One desirous of offspring, free from disease, should approach a woman of different <s>gotra</s> (lineage), who is aphrodisiac, delighted, and free from defects, // Car_6,2.1.15
who has bathed purely.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

children.text: rūpādivyatirekeṇāpi kācit kasyacit karmavaśādvṛṣyā strī bhavatīti darśayannāha nānetyādi // 1
children.translated_text: He states that even apart from beauty etc., some woman becomes aphrodisiac for some man by force of [past] karma — with 'diverse' etc. // 1
'By providential conjunction' (<s>daivayogāt</s>) means: by force of actions in a past life. // 2
'Increase' (<s>vivardhante</s>) means: they produce the aphrodisiac effect. // 3
'Gestures' (<s>hāva</s>) means: particular erotic gestures of women toward a man. // 4

children.text: uktaṃ ca bharatena prakāśarūpakaṃ sattvaṃ sattvotplavāḥ samudgatāḥ // 5
children.translated_text: And it has been stated by <s>Bharata</s>: 'The manifest form of <s>sattva</s> (temperament), the surges of <s>sattva</s>, are the emergences;
from these arise <s>hāva</s> (gestures) etc.' — so say the supreme sages. // 6
'By fate' (<s>daivāt</s>) means: from actions of a past life. // 7
'By action' (<s>karmaṇaḥ</s>) means: from actions in this life, such as attraction rituals etc. // 8
'Desire of mind' (<s>manaḥśaya</s>) means: passion. // 9
'A snare' (<s>pāśabhūtā</s>) means: because of being the cause of binding the mind and senses. // 10

children.text: nānābhāvā hi mānavāḥ ityanena rūpādiguṇayogena sarvapuruṣān prati strīṇāṃ priyatvamiti darśayati // 11]
children.translated_text: 'For human beings are of diverse natures' — by this he shows that through the conjunction of beauty and other qualities, a woman's dearness [varies] for all men. // 11]

children.text: acchāyaś caikaśākhaś ca niṣphalaśca yathā drumaḥ // Car_6,2.1.16
children.translated_text: Like a tree without shade, with a single branch, and fruitless, // Car_6,2.1.16
of unpleasant smell, and alone — so is a man without offspring.

children.text: citradīpaḥ saraḥ śuṣkam adhātur dhātusaṃnibhaḥ // Car_6,2.1.17
children.translated_text: A painted lamp, a dried-up lake, tissue-less [yet] resembling one with tissues — // Car_6,2.1.17
without progeny, [like] a bundle of straw — such should be considered a man-shaped [being].
Without foundation, naked, empty, and with only one sense-organ — // Car_6,2.1.18
and devoid of action — such should be considered one who has no offspring.
Having many forms, many faces, many arrays, many activities, // Car_6,2.1.19
many eyes, much knowledge, and many selves — [such is] one with many offspring.

children.text: maṅgalyo'yaṃ praśasyo'yaṃ dhanyo'yaṃ vīryavān ayam // Car_6,2.1.20
children.translated_text: 'This one is auspicious, this one is praiseworthy, this one is blessed, this one is powerful, // Car_6,2.1.20
this one has many branches' — thus is praised a man with many offspring.

children.text: prītirbalaṃ sukhaṃ vṛttir vistāro vipulaṃ kulam // Car_6,2.1.21
children.translated_text: Pleasure, strength, happiness, livelihood, expansion, an extensive family, // Car_6,2.1.21
fame, worlds of happy consequence, and satisfaction — all depend on offspring.
Therefore, one desiring offspring and the virtues dependent on offspring // Car_6,2.1.22
should be devoted to <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> — and also desiring the pleasures of love.
The proven <s>vājīkaraṇa</s> combinations — delightful for enjoyment, enhancing virility and offspring — // Car_6,2.1.23
I shall hereafter declare.
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}

[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: jñānetyādau jñānaṃ tattvajñānaṃ praśamaḥ śāntiḥ tapaḥ cāndrāyaṇādi // 1
children.translated_text: In 'knowledge' etc. — 'knowledge' means knowledge of truth; 'tranquility' means peacefulness; 'austerity' means practices like the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> fast. // 1

children.text: cikitsitaṃ cikitsāvidhāyako granthaḥ nidānādyabhidhānaṃ ca cikitsārthameva nidānādijñānapūrvakatvāc cikitsāyāḥ // 2
children.translated_text: 'Treatment' means the text that prescribes the therapeutic method. And the description of etiology (<s>nidāna</s>) etc. is also for the purpose of treatment, since treatment is preceded by knowledge of etiology etc. // 2

children.text: pañcānāmiti vacanena pañcānāmapi cikitsāviṣayatvaṃ darśayati nahi kāsaśvāsavadasyāsādhyatvaṃ kasyāścid atretyarthaḥ tathā suśrutoktātiriktatṛṣṇādvayāntarbhāvaṃ pañcasveva sūcayati // 3
children.translated_text: By the word 'five,' he shows that all five [types] are treatable — for unlike cough and dyspnea, no [type of thirst] is incurable here. Similarly, he indicates that the two additional [types of] thirst mentioned by <s>Suśruta</s> are included within these five. // 3

children.text: uktaṃ hi suśrute tisraḥ smṛtāstāḥ kṣatajā caturthī kṣayāttathā hy āmasamudbhavā ca // 4
children.translated_text: For it is stated in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'Three are remembered; the fourth is from blood loss; likewise from depletion; and the fifth arises from <s>āma</s> (undigested material); // 4
the seventh arises from food.' // 5]
From agitation, fear, exertion, grief, anger, fasting, and wine,
from the use of alkaline, sour, salty, pungent, hot, dry, and desiccated food, // Car_6,22.4
from tissue depletion, disease, emaciation, excessive use of emesis etc., and the heat of the sun —

children.text: pittānilau pravṛddhau saumyān dhātūṃś ca śoṣayataḥ // Car_6,22.5
children.translated_text: <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, aggravated [by these], desiccate the watery (<s>saumya</s>) tissues. // Car_6,22.5
Drying up the <s>rasa</s>-carrying channels, the root of the tongue, the throat, the palate, and the <s>kloman</s> (respiratory organ),

children.text: saṃśoṣya nṛṇāṃ dehe kurutastṛṣṇāṃ mahābalāvetau // Car_6,22.6
children.translated_text: these two [<s>doṣas</s>], of great power, produce thirst in the human body. // Car_6,22.6

children.text: pītaṃ pītaṃ hi jalaṃ śoṣayatastāvato na yāti śamam /
children.translated_text: For they desiccate each successive [quantity of] water that is drunk, and therefore [the thirst] does not subside.
In those emaciated by severe disease, it arises as a complication. // Car_6,22.7
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]

children.text: kṣobhād ityādyuktanidānasya yathāyogyatayā vātakartṛtvaṃ vātapittakartṛtvaṃ conneyam // 1
children.translated_text: Among the etiological factors stated beginning with 'agitation' etc., the agency of <s>Vāta</s> or the agency of <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s> [together] should be inferred as appropriate. // 1
'<s>Pitta</s> and <s>Vāta</s>' etc. is the text [describing] the pathogenesis (<s>samprāpti</s>) common to all [types of] thirst. // 2
'Watery tissues' (<s>saumya dhātus</s>) means <s>Kapha</s>, <s>rasa</s> (plasma), and water — which are predominant in the qualities of <s>Soma</s> (the moon/water). // 3
'Corrupt' — i.e., they vitiate through desiccation. // 4
'<s>Kloman</s>' — is in the accusative plural. // 5

children.text: dehe ityanena etāsāṃ tṛṣṇānāṃ śarīratvaṃ darśayati // 6
children.translated_text: By [the word] 'in the body,' he shows that these [types of] thirst are bodily [in origin]. // 6

children.text: yā hi mānasī tṛṣṇā sā śarīre icchādveṣātmikā tṛṣṇā sukhaduḥkhāt pravartate ityādāv uktā iyaṃ tu dehāśrayadoṣakāraṇā satī dehajaiveti bhāvaḥ // 7
children.translated_text: For the mental thirst — which is of the nature of desire and aversion in the body — has been stated in 'thirst arises from pleasure and pain' etc. But this [thirst] is bodily, being caused by the <s>doṣas</s> residing in the body — this is the import. // 7

children.text: svābhāvikatṛṣṇāyām api vātapitte ārambhake eva tat kiṃ sāpyatra na gṛhyate // 8
children.translated_text: Even in natural thirst, <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s> are indeed the initiators. Then why is it not included here? // 8

children.text: maivaṃ tasyā ucitadravapānenaivābhipretena praśamād iha asvābhāvikavyādhiprakaraṇe nādhikāra iti hṛdi kṛtvā // 9
children.translated_text: It should not be so [included], because natural thirst is pacified simply by drinking the desired liquid. Since this is a section on unnatural diseases, it has no place here — keeping this in mind. // 9

children.text: svābhāvikatṛṣṇākaravātapittābhyāṃ vakṣyamāṇatṛṣṇārambhakavātapittayor viśeṣamāha pītaṃ pītam ityādi // 10
children.translated_text: He states the distinction between the <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s> that cause natural thirst and the <s>Vāta</s> and <s>Pitta</s> that initiate the thirst to be described, with 'each successive [quantity of water] drunk' etc. // 10

children.text: prakṛtatṛṣṇārambhakau pittavātau pītaṃ pītaṃ jalaṃ śoṣayataḥ ato jalaśoṣaṇatvāddhetor na śamaṃ yāti puruṣaḥ svābhāvikyāṃ jalaṃ pītvā śāntimadhigacchatīti bhāvaḥ // 11
children.translated_text: The <s>Pitta</s> and <s>Vāta</s> that initiate the [pathological] thirst under discussion desiccate each successive [quantity of] water that is drunk; therefore, because they desiccate water, the person does not attain relief. In natural thirst, however, one attains peace upon drinking water — this is the import. // 11
He states the arising of thirst as a complication with 'severe' etc. // 12
'As a complication' (<s>upasargabhūtā</s>) means in the form of a secondary affliction. // 13]
The premonitory sign [of thirst] is dryness of the mouth; the defining characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is constant craving for water.
[The premonitory stage shows] mildness of the symptoms of all types of thirst — [this is] the disappearance [i.e., the subsiding toward relief]. // Car_6,22.8
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states the premonitory sign of thirst with 'premonitory sign' etc. // 1

children.text: prāgrūpakathane eva madhye tṛṣṇānāmavyabhicārilakṣaṇam āha svalakṣaṇam ityādi // 2
children.translated_text: While stating the premonitory sign itself, he states in between the invariable characteristic of thirst with 'defining characteristic' etc. // 2

children.text: svalakṣaṇam iti avyabhicārilakṣaṇaṃ yathā jvarasya saṃtāpaḥ śvayathor utsedhaḥ // 3
children.translated_text: 'Defining characteristic' (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) means the invariable characteristic — just as fever's [characteristic] is heat, and swelling's is elevation. // 3

children.text: punaḥ prakṛtaṃ prāgrūpam āha liṅgānāṃ lāghavamapāya iti // 4
children.translated_text: He then returns to the topic of premonitory signs with 'mildness of the symptoms is the disappearance' etc. // 4

children.text: liṅgānāṃ vakṣyamāṇavātādijatṛṣṇāliṅgānāṃ lāghavam alpatvaṃ keṣāṃcic cābhāvaḥ pūrvarūpaṃ tṛṣṇānām ityarthaḥ // 5
children.translated_text: 'Mildness of the symptoms' — the smallness, and of some the absence, of the symptoms of <s>Vāta</s>-originated etc. thirst that will be described — constitutes the premonitory sign of thirst. // 5

children.text: tena pūrvarūpāvasthāyāṃ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāni kānicin na bhavantyeva yāni ca bhavanti tānyalpatayāsphuṭāni bhavanti // 6
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the premonitory stage, some of the symptoms to be described do not appear at all, and those that do appear are indistinct due to their mildness. // 6

children.text: uktaṃ ca avyaktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tasya pūrvarūpam iti smṛtam iti // 7
children.translated_text: And it has been stated: 'The indistinct [form of] the symptom is remembered as the premonitory sign.' // 7

children.text: kiṃvā yadetat prāgrūpaṃ mukhaśoṣaḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadāmbukāmitvam etat prāgrūpaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ ca tṛṣṇānāṃ tena mukhaśoṣāmbukāmitve svalakṣaṇe tathā pūrvarūpe ca bhavataḥ pūrvarūpāvasthāyāṃ tv aprabale mukhaśoṣāmbukāmitve jñeye // 8
children.translated_text: Alternatively: 'The premonitory sign is dryness of the mouth; the defining characteristic is constant craving for water' — these are both the premonitory sign and the defining characteristic of thirst. Thus, dryness of the mouth and craving for water are both the defining characteristic and the premonitory sign. In the premonitory stage, however, the dryness of the mouth and craving for water should be understood as not fully manifested. // 8

children.text: ye tu prāgrūpaṃ mukhaśoṣaḥ svarakṣayaḥ sarvadāmbukāmitvam iti paṭhanti teṣāṃ mate tṛṣṇāyāḥ svalakṣaṇaṃ noktaṃ syāt // 9
children.translated_text: Those who read 'premonitory sign is dryness of the mouth, loss of voice, constant craving for water' — in their view, the defining characteristic of thirst would not have been stated. // 9

children.text: uktaṃ ca hārīte'pi tṛṣṇāsvalakṣaṇaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ tu tṛṣṇānāṃ sarvadāmbupipāsitā iti // 10
children.translated_text: And it is stated in <s>Hārīta</s> too regarding the defining characteristic of thirst: 'The defining characteristic of thirst is constant craving for water.' // 10

children.text: kiṃvā mukhaśoṣasvarakṣaye eva pūrvarūpaṃ sarvadāmbukāmitvaṃ ca svalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgānāṃ ca lāghavaṃ rogarūpāyās tṛṣṇāyā apāyo gamanamityarthaḥ ayameva tṛṣṇāvyuparamo yad vakṣyamāṇaliṅgānām alpatvaṃ sarvathocchedo hi tṛṣṇālakṣaṇānāṃ na bhavatyeva sahajatṛṣṇāgrastatvenaitallakṣaṇānām alpamātratayāvasthānāt // 11
children.translated_text: Alternatively: dryness of the mouth and loss of voice are the premonitory sign; constant craving for water is the defining characteristic; and 'mildness of the symptoms' is the abatement (<s>apāya</s>) — i.e., the subsidence — of the thirst as a disease. This subsidence of thirst is precisely the diminution of the symptoms to be described, for the complete cessation of the characteristics of thirst never occurs, since one is always subject to natural thirst and these characteristics persist in a mild degree. // 11

children.text: kaiścit tu liṅgānāṃ lāghavam āśūtpādaḥ sa ca apāyo maraṇam iti kṛtvā tṛṣṇānāmasādhyatālakṣaṇamidamucyate tannātimanoharam // 12]
children.translated_text: Some [commentators], however, [interpret] 'mildness of symptoms' as 'rapid onset' and that (<s>apāya</s>) as 'death' — making this the characteristic of incurability of thirst. But that is not very satisfying. // 12]
Dryness of the mouth, cracking of the voice, dizziness, burning sensation, delirium, and stupor,
roughness of the palate, lips, throat, and tongue, and mental disorientation — // Car_6,22.9
protrusion of the tongue, loss of taste, deafness, pain in the vital points (<s>marma</s>), and exhaustion (<s>sāda</s>) —

children.text: tṛṣṇodbhūtā kurute pañcavidhāṃ liṅgataḥ śṛṇu tām // Car_6,22.10
children.translated_text: thirst, when fully manifest, produces [these]. It is fivefold by its characteristics — hear about it. // Car_6,22.10
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
He states the complications of all [types of] thirst with 'dryness of the mouth' etc. // 1
'Fully manifest' (<s>udbhūtā</s>) means aggravated. // 2

children.text: ye tu mukhaśoṣādīni lakṣaṇānyāhustanmate tṛṣṇopadravānām abhidhānaṃ na syāt upadravāścādhyāyasaṃgrahe saṃgṛhītāḥ tenātiśayavṛddhā mukhaśoṣādaya upadravāḥ vṛddhāstu liṅgam iti vyavasthā // 3]
children.translated_text: Those who consider dryness of the mouth etc. as characteristics — in their view, the complications of thirst would not have been stated, though the complications are included in the chapter summary. Therefore, when excessively aggravated, dryness of the mouth etc. are complications; when [merely] aggravated, they are symptoms — this is the determination. // 3]

children.text: abdhātuṃ dehasthaṃ kupitaḥ pavano yadā viśoṣayati /
children.translated_text: When the aggravated wind (<s>Pavana</s>) desiccates the water-element present in the body,
when that [water-element] is dried up, the weak person dries up and then becomes thirsty while drying up. // Car_6,22.11
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
With 'the water-element' etc., he states the pathogenesis etc. of the five [types]. // 1
'Present in the body' means existing in the body in the form of various [substances such as] <s>rasa</s> (plasma) etc. // 2
'When the water-element is dried up, [the person] dries up' — this is the construction. // 3]

children.text: nidrānāśaḥ śiraso bhramastathā śuṣkavirasamukhatā ca sroto'varodha iti ca syālliṅgaṃ vātatṛṣṇāyāḥ // Car_6,22.12
children.translated_text: Loss of sleep, dizziness of the head, dryness and tastelessness of the mouth, and obstruction of the channels — these are the symptoms of <s>Vāta</s>-thirst. // Car_6,22.12
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
'Obstruction of the channels' means excessive damage [to the channels]. // 1]

children.text: pittaṃ matamāgneyaṃ kupitaṃ cet tāpayaty apāṃ dhātum /
children.translated_text: <s>Pitta</s>, which is considered to be of fiery nature — when aggravated, it heats up the water-element.

children.text: saṃtaptaḥ sa hi janayettṛṣṇāṃ dāholbaṇāṃ nṛṇām // Car_6,22.13
children.translated_text: That [water-element], being scorched, generates in humans a thirst dominated by burning sensation. // Car_6,22.13
Bitterness of the mouth, burning of the head, desire for cold, fainting,
and yellowness of the eyes, urine, and feces — this is the presentation of <s>Pitta</s>-thirst. // Car_6,22.14
[<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s> commentary:]
With '<s>Pitta</s>' etc., he states the <s>Pitta</s>-originated [thirst]. // 1

children.text: śarīrasaṃkhyāśarīre pittamāpyam uktaṃ yad dravasarasnigdhamandamṛdupicchilaṃ rasarudhiravasākaphapittasvedādi tad āpyaṃ raso rasanaṃ ca ityanena tathā tatraiva yat pittasya yo yā ca śarīre bhāḥ tat sarvam āgneyam ityanena dvayātmakatvaṃ pittasya yadyapyuktaṃ tathāpyāgneyākāratvād bāhulyāt pittam āgneyam eveti darśayannāha pittaṃ matam āgneyam iti dvayātmakatve 'pi ca pittasyāgneyāṃśaprādhānyād anyatrāpi saumyāgneyavāyavyavikārabhede paittikavikārā āgneyatvena gṛhītā eva // 2
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śārīrasaṃkhyāśārīra</s> [chapter], <s>pitta</s> has been said to be watery (<s>āpya</s>) — [as stated]: 'That which is liquid, flowing, unctuous, mild, soft, and viscous — [namely] <s>rasa</s> (plasma), blood, fat, <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, sweat, etc. — that is watery.' By the statement '<s>rasa</s> [is plasma] and <s>rasana</s> [is taste]' etc. [it is watery]. Likewise, in that same [chapter]: 'Whatever radiance of <s>pitta</s> is in the body — all that is fiery' — by this the dual nature of <s>pitta</s> has been stated. Nevertheless, because of its predominantly fiery appearance, he shows that <s>pitta</s> is indeed fiery, saying '<s>pitta</s> is considered fiery.' And even though <s>pitta</s> has a dual nature, because of the predominance of the fiery component, elsewhere too, in the classification of disorders into <s>saumya</s> (watery), <s>āgneya</s> (fiery), and <s>vāyavya</s> (airy) varieties, <s>paittika</s> (bilious) disorders are indeed subsumed under the fiery category. // 2
'It being heated' (<s>saṃtaptaḥ sa hi</s>) — the water element being heated. // 3

children.text: saṃtaptaṃ hi iti pāṭhapakṣe pittameva janayediti yojyam // 4
children.translated_text: In the variant reading '<s>saṃtaptaṃ hi</s>' — the construction should be: '[the heated water element] would generate <s>pitta</s> itself.' // 4

children.text: yadābdhātur janayati tadā pittasaṃtapta eva janayatīti pittasyaiva kartṛtvam // 5]
children.translated_text: When the water element generates [thirst], it generates [it] only when heated by <s>pitta</s> — thus the agency belongs to <s>pitta</s> alone. // 5]
The thirst that arises from <s>āma</s> (undigested material) — that too is fiery, being generated by <s>āma</s>-[obstructed] <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: liṅgaṃ tasyāś cārucir ādhmānakaphaprasekau ca // Car_6,22.15
children.translated_text: Its signs are: loss of taste, distension, and excessive <s>kapha</s> secretion. // Car_6,22.15
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
With 'thirst' etc., he states the <s>āma</s>-born [type]. // 1

children.text: āmaśabdena ceha lakṣaṇayā āmasamānacikitsita āmasamānalakṣaṇaś ca kapho 'pi gṛhyate // 2
children.translated_text: And here, by the word '<s>āma</s>' — by secondary designation — <s>kapha</s> too is included, as it shares the same treatment and symptoms as <s>āma</s>. // 2

children.text: tenāmaprabhavāyā vyutpādanena kaphajāpi suśrutoktā gṛhītaiveha sāpyāgneyetyanena pūrvaparijñātaṃ sarvāsāṃ vātapittajanyatvaṃ samunnayati // 3
children.translated_text: Therefore, by the derivation '<s>āma</s>-born,' the <s>kapha</s>-born [thirst] stated by <s>Suśruta</s> is also included here. By 'that too is fiery,' he extends the previously established [principle] that all [types of thirst] are produced by <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>. // 3

children.text: vātaśca tṛṣṇākāraṇatvenokto'pyatrāpradhānaṃ pittameva ye pradhānam itīha vātākathanād unnīyate // 4
children.translated_text: And <s>vāta</s>, though stated as a cause of thirst, is here secondary — <s>pitta</s> alone is primary: this is inferred from the non-mention of <s>vāta</s> here. // 4
Elsewhere too it has been said: 'Vision, digestion, heat, hunger, thirst, softness of body,
radiance, clarity, intellect — these are the non-pathological actions of <s>pitta</s>.' // 6
'Being generated by <s>āma</s>-<s>pitta</s>' means: being generated by <s>pitta</s> that has increased due to obstruction by <s>āma</s> — this is the meaning. // 7]

children.text: deho rasajo'mbubhavo rasaśca tasya kṣayācca tṛṣyeddhi /
children.translated_text: The body is born from <s>rasa</s> (plasma/nutrient fluid), [which is] born from water; and <s>rasa</s> [is the source].
From its depletion one indeed thirsts — with feeble voice, fainting, with dried-up heart, throat, and palate. // Car_6,22.16
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
With 'the body is born from <s>rasa</s>' etc., he states the depletion-born [type]. // 1

children.text: āhārarasāt sarvadhātupoṣako dhāturasa utpadyate sa ca raso dehapoṣako 'mbubhava iti āpya ityarthaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: From the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of food, the tissue-<s>rasa</s> that nourishes all tissues is produced; and that <s>rasa</s>, which nourishes the body, is '<s>ambubhava</s>' — meaning watery (<s>āpya</s>): this is the meaning. // 2

children.text: tasya kṣayāditi rasakṣayāt tṛṣyate rasakṣayād ambukṣayo bhavati tena cāmbukṣayeṇa puruṣaḥ pānīyaprārthanārūpatṛṣṇayā yukto bhavatīti yuktam iti darśayati // 3
children.translated_text: 'From its depletion' means: from the depletion of <s>rasa</s>, one thirsts. From the depletion of <s>rasa</s>, depletion of water occurs; and by that depletion of water, the person becomes afflicted with thirst in the form of craving for drink — thus it is reasonable: this he shows. // 3

children.text: uktaṃ hi suśrute doṣadhātumalakṣīṇo balakṣīṇo'pi mānavaḥ // 4
children.translated_text: For it has been said in <s>Suśruta</s>: 'A person depleted in <s>doṣas</s>, tissues, and wastes, or depleted in strength, // 4

children.text: svayonivardhanaṃ yat tad annapānaṃ prakāṅkṣati iti ihāpi coktaṃ tasya kṣayācca tṛṣyeddhi iti // 5]
children.translated_text: desires food and drink that augments its own source.' And here too it has been said: 'from its depletion one indeed thirsts.' // 5]

children.text: bhavati khalu yopasargāttṛṣṇā sā śoṣiṇī kaṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The thirst that arises as a complication (<s>upasarga</s>) — that is desiccating and severe,
[arising] in those whose bodies are afflicted by fever, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disorders), consumption, wasting, dyspnea, and the like. // Car_6,22.17
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
With 'arises' etc., he states the complication-born [type]. // 1
'From complication' (<s>upasargāt</s>) means: from complications of fever etc. — [it arises] in the form of a complication of fever etc.: so much is meant. // 2
'Severe' (<s>kaṣṭā</s>) means: difficult to treat. // 3

children.text: evaṃ prāksūtritavātapittāmāmbukṣayopasargātmikāḥ pañca tṛṣṇā vyāhṛtāḥ atraiva suśrutoktā kaphajā āmajāyām avaruddhā kṣatajā upasargātmikāyām avaruddhā annajā cāmajāyām evāntarbhāvanīyā // 4]
children.translated_text: Thus the five types of thirst — born from <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>āma</s>, water-depletion, and complications — have been previously stated in sūtra form. Here, the <s>kapha</s>-born [type] stated by <s>Suśruta</s> is included in the <s>āma</s>-born; the injury-born (<s>kṣataja</s>) is included in the complication-born; and the food-born (<s>annaja</s>) should also be included in the <s>āma</s>-born. // 4]
But all [types of thirst], when excessively persistent in those emaciated by disease and those with persistent vomiting,
accompanied by severe complications — such thirsts should be known as [leading] to death. // Car_6,22.18
[{<s>Āyurvedadīpikā</s>}
Now he states the characteristics of incurability of the thirsts with 'but all' etc.
'Accompanied by severe complications' means: having distressing complications. // 1]
<s>Carakasaṃhitā</s>, <s>Cikitsāsthāna</s>, 22 [Treatment of Thirst (<s>Tṛṣṇācikitsita</s>)]
